review:
Been playing since KF1 back in the day. KF3 feels more like a tech demo than an actual polished KF title. It feels like this game was designed for 10 year olds with immediate access to their parents wallets and who lack the critical thinking to care about the little things that make games great, or overall quality of finished products. 

The textures make everything look plastic like the guns, environment, even the zeds. The crafting feature is a bit unnecessary. The enemy designs are pretty cool as a plus, but they feel like you're getting Temu Horzine, not OG pants-crapping Killing Floor zeds. 

I also had to turn the character voices to mute because the in-game announcer excruciatingly annoying and the character lines are generic and stale. The microtransactions that plagued the end of KF2 have been given the president treatment here and they are front and center on in-game menus, truly cancerous. Anyone who pushed for these features shouldn't be working in the gaming industry, you are a plague on this earth. 

This is a solid 5/10 with some room to be a 6 or 7 in a year. It is unmistakably a DOWNGRADE from KF2, which I didn't know was possible. This is not the good old Tripwire or Killing Floor I remember. Wait for a $5 sale, that's more reflective of the quality you're getting with this game, even $20 on sale is a scam.

I don’t understand how such a game can be released in 2025! I don’t know how the developers can think that their product is fun. I was looking for fun but it’s nowhere to be found. 
Kf3 is just a plain horde mode like you know it from zombie from call of duty black ops from 15 years ago. They didn’t add any objectives to the gameplay. You just run and mow down zombies. 
The gunplay is weak at best. You didn’t get any feedback if you hit or miss. The enemies don’t flinch and don’t stumble when you hit them so you get the feeling you’re shooting in the air. The bigger enemies are just bullet sponges. 
The progression is a joke. You get 60 points for finishing a level but you need 100 for upgrading the skills. It takes forever to unlock the skills and to upgrade them. 
Each class has to be levels individually. Especially at the beginning when you’re not sure what classes to play you start always with a class at lvl 1. in order to play other levels it’s recommended to play to first level to level them a bit because on the other maps you don’t stand a chance. 
I tried the game solo and i tried the game in Multiplayer. 
There is no fun to be found.

- Si el usuario no dispone un ordenador muy moderno, el tiempo promedio para entrar al juego es de 5-10 minutos para cargar todos los recursos del mismo, en caso contrario inicia rápidamente.

- Prácticamente es un juego como si se encontrase en fase beta (o gamma si existiera) pues tiene innumerables bugs que afectan al gameplay. De entre los errores del amplio abanico que he tenido el placer de encontrar, destacan los siguientes: expulsión de la partida por conexión con el servidor o por el anti cheat, el mapa se vuelve oscuro o no deja de temblar, el boss final de la partida no spawnea, no spawnear con el arma inicial en el multijugador, colisiones imperfectas al compartir dinero con otros jugadores tras lanzarlo al suelo (a veces atraviesa a los jugadores y ellos mismos tienen que pasar por encima para recogerlo), T pose de personajes u otras entidades en momentos determinados. 

- Las partidas en general son monótonas, solo hay 8 mapas y 3 jefes finales. El sistema del dinero destaca por ser lo más ávaro posible, al completar la ronda la ganancia de dinero es muy justa o deficiente para poder comprar armas, armaduras, herramientas, etc. lo que incrementa significativamente la dificultad del juego por el desbalanceo de puntos de vida que tiene los enemigos y el daño de las armas con las que tienes que sobrevivir sin comprar otras mejores.

- Existe 3 dificultades en el juego: normal, difícil e infernal. Si juegas en difícil, si no juegas con otros jugadores es muy complicado ganar la partida; todos los jefes tienen un daño tan alto que con 2 golpes te pueden tumbar. No he tenido aun el privilegio de probar la dificultad infernal, pues tener el nivel 18 (de 30 máximos) no es suficiente para ganar la partida de forma individual en modo difícil.

- Hay muy pocos jugadores online, muchas partidas juegas solo o, en el mejor de los casos, los jugadores comienzan a unirse una vez comenzada.

En conclusión, no recomiendo comprar este juego por el precio sugerido, le doy 7 euros tal y como está el producto actualmente, le falta muchas actualizaciones, contenido y mejoras de mecánicas para que cumplan las expectativas de un juego de la saga Killing Floor.

review: FIX BUG FIRST
name: Killing Floor 3

review:
Dear Tripwire Team,

I’m writing because I’ve been a Killing Floor fan for years — from the mod days through KF2 — and because I genuinely care about this series. My brother and I have over 100 hours each in KF3 and countless more in KF2. We wanted to love this game. But right now, KF3 doesn’t feel like Killing Floor anymore.

1. You Took Away the Heart of the Game
Where is Kevin Clamely? Where’s the weird, dark humor and atmosphere that gave the series personality? KF3 feels sterile — the identity has been stripped out.

The biggest problem: the game revolves entirely around getting a Vulkan. Every perk, every build, every decision feels secondary to that one goal. It’s terrible design. The individuality of perks — the soul of the series — is gone. Ironically, there are essentially no perks in the game; it’s just whichever perk has the better stats on the Vulkan.

Each perk has no clearly defined role anymore, partly because of the weapon-focus meta. There need to be clear trash killers and large zed killers. Right now, each perk has enough hybrid skills that let them do both too well, making perk choice meaningless. For example, there’s no need for a Combat Medic because the buffs they provide aren’t strong enough to justify their presence — they don’t kill anything better than any other perk. And since everyone can use a Medic Pistol with purple darts, the Medic heals no better than anyone else either.

A simple fix: boost perk-specific weapon bonuses to make staying within your perk’s arsenal worth it again. Each perk should feel like an expert with their weapons — just like in KF1 and KF2, where you reloaded faster and did more damage with your perk guns. That gave perks identity and mastery. Right now, it’s often better for a Sharpshooter to use an explosive shotgun or the Vulkan than to use their own arsenals. Bass ackwards.

And please, bring back perk passives. Those small, intrinsic upgrades tied your identity to your class and gave each one a rhythm of growth. Losing them makes leveling feel hollow. The current passives are not acknowledgeable.

2. Encumbrance and Strategic Choice Are Gone
One of the most elegant systems in KF2 was encumbrance. It created genuine strategy and mid-match decision-making — choosing between a powerful but heavy weapon or a flexible loadout with utility.

That ebb and flow between waves — picking mid-tier weapons between levels 2–4, deciding whether to switch loadouts before a boss — mattered. It gave every game personality.

Now, encumbrance is gone, and so are those choices. Every match just becomes a race to the Vulkan, and once you get it, your decisions are over. That’s not progression — it’s monotony.

3. Gameplay Bugs and RNG Madness
We got the Queen Crawler five games in a row.
At a 33% chance per boss, that’s a 1 in 40,000 event. Probably a bug, but it killed morale. My brother and I even made a bet: if it happened again, we’d uninstall. You can guess what spawned next.

And where is Suicidal difficulty? “Hard” is too easy, “Hell on Earth” is a wall. Suicidal was that perfect middle ground — the natural home for players who’d mastered the basics but didn’t want every match to be a punishment.

4. Balance and Combat Feel
Combat feels wrong across the board:

Scrakes are pure bullet sponges now, even with top-end weapons like the Vulkan. The classic KF dynamic — explosives for Fleshpounds, bullets for Scrakes — is gone. It used to reward tactical coordination.

Sharpshooter is borderline useless. Zeds bob and weave too much to land headshots consistently, especially when you’re overwhelmed. Even if you do, the Sharpshooter’s weapons hit like peashooters compared to other perks’ explosive or area-damage options. They should be the fastest at killing large zeds with precision — that’s their purpose — but right now, they get outpaced by nearly everyone. The Engineer’s Ifrit can kill a Fleshpound in three bolts, and the Firebug’s Vulkan can burn one down in two full charges.

Perk roles don’t matter. Every perk can do everything decently well. The lack of specialization makes team composition meaningless.

Why make Scrakes weak to cut damage, then cover them in Zedtech armor that resists cut damage? It’s confusing and counterintuitive.

KF used to reward coordinated play — now it rewards whichever perk can abuse the current meta weapon.

Suggestion: Bring back static perk-specific stats like in KF1 and KF2. Tie reload, damage, and weapon handling bonuses to perk weapons only. That would naturally restore balance and bring back the satisfaction of mastering your role.

And while we’re here — take sidearms away or rework them. The extra slot feels clunky and pointless. Just have two weapon slots and buff pistols to make them viable secondaries instead of filler. Right now, having two primaries bound to one slot just adds frustration.

5. Technical and Interface Frustrations
KF3 runs poorly on every system I’ve tried. It’s visually fine, but the optimization is abysmal for what’s on screen.

And the menus and interface make the experience worse:

The crafting material pool doesn’t appear on the crafting page. You have to back out through several menus just to check your totals.

The weapon part crafting system feels awful. Please make it so we can choose the tier 3 ability instead of grinding endlessly for perfect rolls. The parts make a huge difference in weapon power, and the current system feels more punishing than rewarding.

Sentry activation is inconsistent — sometimes a tap of “E,” sometimes a hold.

The operational budget isn’t visible outside of a match. If I want to test upgrades, I literally have to open a live game or do math by hand. Just add a loadout sandbox in the menu for preplanning.

Add a “Teleport to Chopper” button in the menus. It’s a small quality-of-life thing, but running back to the chopper every single time is tedious.

KF2’s menus were clunky but functional. KF3’s feel like work.

6. Character Writing and Tone
The voicelines are rough. KF2 had charm — personality mixed with grim humor. KF3’s dialogue sounds tone-deaf, especially the Engineer, who lectures about “improving zeds” as scientific projects in a post-apocalyptic world. It breaks immersion completely — why would the protagonists be suggesting improvements to the monsters they’re fighting to survive against?

7. The Grind and Progression
Something changed under the hood, because the XP grind has slowed dramatically.
At launch, I leveled Assault and Engineer to 30 in about 15–20 hours each. Now, after 50 hours of Firebug, I’m still not 30. It feels like progress got throttled silently, and it kills long-term motivation.

The game shouldn’t be about the grind to level 30 — the game should start once you reach it. The fun begins when perks are fully unlocked and team synergy shines. Please make XP gain faster so players can get to the real experience sooner.

8. The One Thing You Got Right
KF3 finally lets me queue privately with my friends. That’s a huge improvement over KF2, where randoms could join mid-match — even on the last wave — beg for dosh, and ruin the boss prep because nobody could armor up or reload properly.

You also stopped low-level players from dropping into high-wave lobbies, which used to break pacing and team balance. Credit where it’s due — this feature is one of the best quality-of-life changes in the entire franchise.

9. Final Thoughts
All of this comes from a place of love and deep familiarity with Killing Floor.
KF1 and KF2 still pull thousands of players daily because they feel cohesive — perks have personality, teamwork matters, and the experience flows.

KF3 stripped that away and replaced it with an unfocused weapon-upgrade grind that undermines the very things that made Killing Floor special.

Please, give perks their meaning back. Restore encumbrance and strategic choice. Fix the boss RNG, rebalance the combat roles, and optimize the engine.

The series deserves better than this.

review:
Don't even kid yourself with this game, even after this 'big' update that's come out recently, this game is a spit in the face of anybody who had any attachment to the series and an insult to newcomers.

The cosmetics have both been made worse and uglier - the hi-tech theme was poorly received in KF2, so obviously we'll theme the third game entirely around it! Rather than letting the player to mix and match their cosmetics (or expanding on it) we just got a body slot and a head slot, cosmetics are exclusively tied to the new passes (no special themed rewards from weeklys, vosh crates or random drops) but, that doesn't even matter much when each character is just not that interesting, not real amusing lines, flat personalities that were clearly written with the perk tied character design in mind and a VA change for Foster, which makes me think Scully will have the same. We didn't even get the brit vets of the voicing from the previous games making a return.

But hey, this is all cosmetic, maybe the gameplay saves it? Of course not. If you enjoyed Berserker, you'll be happy to know that it feels worse than it did in the first game, with enemies having their attacks coming out before their animations would suggest (gorefasts being the most frustrating), parrying just feels incredibly awkward and there's only 2 dedicated melee weapons (3 counting the kunai) 1 being a katana and the second being 2 katanas - complete joke. 

This is a good segway though, because why would you use melee on the class that appears to be melee oriented when you can just spec into bleed damage and have some of the highest, no effort global damage boost around! Class identity? What's that? let's just make it so all classes can use everything and have practically 0 reason to ever specialise, it's not like the perks were made for that reason, they were just a vague suggestion clearly. All of the skills feel next to useless minus the few meta ones - why add more if they're all garbage? 3 trees and yet most of them are not even worth looking at.

Core gameplay changes were done, such as removing the weight and thus the inventory system entirely, which helped balancing out the powerful weapons and gave you a reason to think about what you took (on top of choosing things that your perk actually benefited from - but whatever...) wave lengths are gone, now it's always 6 wave, no 4/7/10 anymore - Endless? Objective?(not that I cared for it, but usually sequels should probably have more in it) all MIA. Healing? limited to a certain usage based on skills however this means that battles of attrition will always end in failure since you're limited on how much damage you can take, this also means healing others is exclusively medic weapons now for darts, I don't get this change - why attempt to fix what wasn't broken?

Weapons feel weak and without any real buffs coming from the perks, they stay weak, maybe to push you in the direction of grinding mats for the purpose of applying and upgrading attachments on them to slightly buff their damage numbers and their cost to buy from the trader - I'm not really opposed to this idea, but I dislike how weak everything feels except for a handful of them *cough* vulcan *cough* Either damage tuning needs to be made, or enemy HP needs to be slashed across the board, way too much of the game is spent just backpedalling away from everything - which feels weird, since holding a lane or being Han Solo popping heads in the previous games were great, but feels far less of an option in this one.

Graphically, colours are all washed out, nothing really pops and things can blend together, I don't mind the visual changes on the zeds, but I hate how grey everything appears, it's completely lifeless.

Map design is probably the only thing I don't hate, the maps all feel nice and somebody even remade them in KF2 which lets you enjoy them without the drag of having to play them in their original state.

I should also note that I had 0 ability to finish a multiplayer match because community servers are gone and so are dedicated servers, because we still live in 2007 apparently and I kept disconnecting before any match could even finish. So all my playtime was done solo, which led me thinking that maybe weapons feel so horrible because zed hp isn't scaled, but even then, that means they still feel like shit with multiple players. Community stuff in general is completely absent, I don't think we'll see community skins make a return - mutators are out and goodbye to custom maps I guess. Will they return? who knows and who cares, something tells me this game won't have anybody developing for it anyway.

While there's certainly more to expand on, I'm trying to keep my complaining brief - but last thing I need to touch on is the bosses. They're boring and they have 0 personality. No voice lines, they're just ugly abominations, which is like - yea, fine. But it's just an odd departure from the rest, they're also subject to the same tanky nonsense as the rest of the cast, so it's spent just backpedalling and slowly plinking away their health and hoping they don't smack you around because you have limit healing charges! and to make it even better, you're slow as molasses to incentivise using the dodge, which feels like a move backwards faster button and is just annoying to have to constantly press. The only real time you need to dodge is to avoid the Fleshpounds and their tracking slam attacks and Gorefast stabs, because even if you sidestep before they even start it, they always seem to connect, but whatever - skill issue.

So... yeah. Wait on it for a couple years and come back to an amazing game? Fat chance, I'd wager now this game will be completely abandoned within a year once the team gets axed for it's poor sales. It flopped on launch and I don't see any breath being breathed into it anytime soon and HEY - if only there was community content to keep things alive and fresh. I wonder if that's ever been done before?

Edit: Oh look I forgot to mention, just like the team forgot to push out - that Halloween passed and no themed event in sight, maybe that's another thing we can say got lost in translation.

review:
Never bought and refunded a game so fast. My reasoning is solely from the fact that the visuals and audio feedback in this game is a MASSIVE downgrade from KF2. Anyone that thinks otherwise has to be lying. And yes, this whole review is JUST about that, not even including the gameplay issues that other reviews mention. I wanted to give this game a chance despite the reviews.

When I'm playing a horde shooter, I'd expect the gameplay to actually pack a punch and feel visceral. KF2 nailed that with the animations, gore, sound design, etc. Same can be said about games like L4D2. When you shoot and slice through gore in those games, it has excellent feedback and makes the repetitive nature of killing the same enemies over and over more fun. The zed animations in 2 were all mocapped by an actor, and you can see the fluidity of the movements in game. KF3? All the animations look stiff as a board. None of the zed animations look like they were mocapped. Just look at ANY zed running animation from KF2 and compare it to the zeds in 3. It is a night and day comparison. Also, most of the guns feel like plastic toys. 

So why does this matter of all things? Cause you'd think that the third installment of a series would be an improvement over the last in some way. I would've been able to let everything else about the game slide if they at least kept the FEEL of the game quality similar / better, but it's just too jarring and distracting to keep me engaged.

So unless they manage to do a massive overhaul of the animation system or something, I can't justify buying this game in its current state. It's honestly kinda sad that fans have waited so long for this only for the game to be released like it is. "But KF2 had a terrible launch too!" Why are we justifying KF3's shortcomings just cause the previous title did the same? Don't we want a finished final product on release? The problem is that this game didn't release as an early access title.

review:
I was really looking forward to Killing Floor 3, but honestly… this has been one of the most disappointing launches in recent memory (beside PAYDAY3).

The gunplay and atmosphere should be amazing, the core DNA of the franchise is still here, but none of that matters when the game runs like this. Even on a high-end rig, the performance is a disaster. Constant stuttering, random frame drops, and inexplicable input lag plague every match. I’ve tried every combination of graphics settings, driver updates, and even fresh installs, nothing makes it consistently smooth.

Worse yet, the optimization feels completely unfinished. CPU usage is erratic, VRAM spikes for no reason. Some maps even tank the framerate to the low 40s despite “optimized” presets.

It’s frustrating because beneath all the technical mess, there’s a genuinely good game trying to break through. But right now, it’s buried under poor optimization and half-baked polish.

Tripwire needs to take this seriously and push out performance patches fast. Until then, I can’t recommend Killing Floor 3 on PC. Wait for major updates, or for the inevitable “Enhanced Edition” down the road.

review:
As a Killing Floor fan since the early days of the Unreal Tournament mod, I have watched this series grow from the very beginning.

And while KF has had its shares of ups and downs. It has never reached a level this low. And while I do think that KF3 is a good game and while I do think that Tripware is trying their hardest to fix many glaring issues. It simply isnt ever going to be enough.

It would be a disservice to the Killing Floor community that I love so much to recommend this game. I had waited for the Rearmament update to post this review in case drastic changes from launch were implemented. The main being the operator decoupling. Which was a huge debate going way back to the Alpha stages of KF3. Tripwire didnt need to listen to the feedback, but they were kind of forced to. So I commend them for getting it done and I truly do trust them to keep supporting this game. Which is why I preordered it and continue to play.

That said, to waste time fixing problems they created in the first place, is the absolute definition of this game. It didnt need to be released on a broken UE5 engine, but they went with it. It didnt need a  paid battle pass and cosmetics in 2025 but they went with it. It didnt need customizable weapons(AND I TRULY MEAN THIS ONE) but they went with it. 

Killing Floor was always defined as a horde based shooter with fast action gunplay and slight horror elements. Allowing players to choose from a MASSIVE selection of cheeky characters and customize their perk to meet their playstyle.

While that still exists, it is severely hampered in KF3. The guns are boring lego block abominations that have no identity in sound, design or feeling. The operators were initially locked to your class but represent a very boring cast of generic punk girl, generic spanish girl, generic ninja guy, generic engineer guy and ......Mr. Foster.....but a clone?? I dont even know or care about these characters. Nor did I care about the cast in previous Killing Floor games(probably because you didnt need to) but they still managed to have more charm somehow. The perk system is nicely laid out in KF3 but I didnt feel that progressing through more than half the tree even mattered. With the slight incremental gains but no real noticible perk upgrades compared to KF2

KF3 has a decent story and campaign actually. Which is ruined by its random map design which doesnt play out as good as it sounds. You basically go from Lab 1 to Streets to Lab 2 to Forest to Lab 3 on a roof this time. Like its not bad but its not memorable as something like Nuked or Evacuation Point in KF2.

The Bosses in KF3 are also pretty good compared to previous games and the music slaps as good as always. But performance issues aside(which have improved over time drastically), even if you wanted to play the game stable. The movement and flow are way off. Everything from healing, to using the map traversal shortcuts is so much less fluid. 

So while the game is good. I dont have the same itch to play as much as I did the previous games. It sounds and plays the part slightly. But it has lost too much of it's identity along the way. I really would like to come back to KF3 in like 3 years to see where the progress is at because KF2 didnt have a very good beginning before becoming great. But there is a lot of work, so much so that it would basically require most of the base game to be reworked. And for that I dont see it even with the impressive roadmaps and commitment from Tripwire.

The communication is out there from them and I want to give them full credit for addressing the issues. I hope to give them another shot in the future. But there is a lot to be learning from KF3.

While i avoided the game when it came out because of all the absolute awful decisions they made about the game, my girlfriend gifted it to me after they walked back some of the decisions, here is everything i noticed, if you want to skip the review : I still cannot recommend the game, if you play for 30 minutes you have played for 2 hours, there is a massive lack of anything in the game, but my girlfriend likes it because its alot like cod zombies in some ways and that helps her as she isnt very good at games at the start

Things that dont get points:
Gunplay ( find me one shooter that fucked up gunplay so hard people quit it, i cant give points for it, especially when literally everyone would get the point for it, its a useless metric as a positive, but if someone fucks it up, it would be useful than) 
Graphics ( i don't care what games look like, if its in 4k or if its low-poly, im impressed by both at times and marginally left not caring for the most part )
If its fun with friends ( while i do enjoy games meant for friends to play together, RV there yet, Peak, Lethal Company, Repo, etc, i don't give points for it, because everything is better with your friends )

things that do get points:
Is it fun alone? ( if you can enjoy it solo for an hour or not, and will you lose enjoyment in hour 2 and beyond )
amount of content ( it doesnt need alot of content, but it cant have to little, and if applicable, the grind to get to certain content locked behind something )
lessons learned from previous games ( if applicable )
the rule of cool ( if a game lets you do something not because its realistic but because its cool af, are the weapons following reality or do we get a plasma cannon and vice versa, i don't want a plasma cannon in my ww2 game but i do want it in my zombie game )
the dialog isn't CRINGE ( really hard for people to get this sometimes, we know the types that make it cringe, for the most part we don't want a whiney kid / teenager / somehow adult with blue hair inserting themselves into games, or if your playing as a character in their respective world and the fellow residents treat you like a visitor explaining things that your character should know to " build the world ", how many times do you need to remind someone " big bad event happened ",
that's why we "x, y, z", i prefer it when games treat your character like a part of the world, like clair obscure: Expedition 33, they don't outright tell you about the festival or what its for since your character has been living in the world and thus knows, but you get enough context clues to figure it out on your own. if you couldn't figure it out though, the game down right shows you instead of just telling you, there is a difference between showing and telling )
Politics in games ( i don't want real world politics in any game, not from either side, now its fine for the games to have their own political factions, and portraying both sides in their own way, and to not preach it to you, i like to make decisions based on my faction, i don't like my faction making me reconsider my decision when they try to talk to me about real world politics, and its usually really easy to see because they are blatant about it )

PROS:
Gameplay feels pretty good with some exceptions from the changes they made. ( support still cant repair doors, removed the welding tool and made it the "multi-tool" with 3 uses and you need to pay for those uses, it only does 4 things, turn turret on, make zipline, open door, turn on trap, it takes up a slot for other things, but i prefer walking up to the traps and flipping a lever not aiming at it and holding 4, that way anybody can use them, personally a better system would be to cost DOSH to turn turrets on, spend time fixing the door to open it or something, pay DOSH for the armor restock to open the little crate, pay DOSH to activate zipline, there is a better system out there than what we were given, but its decent)
They walked back some of their bad decisions, the ones that were Anti-Player / Anti-Customization (step in the right direction, PERKS are no longer tied to Specialists (characters), that was a big one for me)

CONS
lack of content / customization ( not just lack of cosmetic customization, each match is only about 6 waves, maybe 7, but you cant increase or decrease it, you are stuck with 6 or 7, and with the cost of the last weapons you only get them for about one round and then the boss, so you dont get to use them for long, the characters, the only one from the line up that i know is Mr. Foster, the rest are cringe, there is almost no customization for them to boot )
the weapon upgrade system ( its cringe, its like the dead space 3 weapon customization system but someone realized they shouldnt add the microtransactions at launch, no weapons have WEIGHT anymore and you can pick what you want, as long as its 2 primaries and 2 pistols, or melees, i dont know to much about melee because i thought ninja was cringe and didnt play the perk, im waiting for berserker, you can upgrade your weapons not in match but in hub, you click customize and you can give it bonuses depending on the weapon, like +90% DMG for the grenade launcher but also has - 3 clip size and you can upgrade it 3 times, each costing more and more resources you get from in game shooting certain objects, it kind of feels like busy work and takes away from what your focus should be, to kill ZEDS, not shoot a camera get some scrap )
IM WILLING TO BET THE CHARACTERS ARE SO CRINGE THEY REMOVED 90% OF THE DIALOG ( in the previous titles the characters had so much banter going on, now it feels like they dont even moan in pain when they are getting stabbed or slammed, if your lucky you might hear a voice line after the start of the game, excludes asking for DOSH)
this is a 50/50 ( DOSH no longer gets sucked up by the player, in the previous games if you threw DOSH at someone they would absorb it, if you throw it in this game, it goes through them and they have to pick it up, but they also added the ability to give them dosh through a menu instead ) 
Jumping has a cooldown ( personally i like to jump like an autistic kid, and i could in the previous games, run and jump around non stop while waiting for things, here you cant, you have to wait for like 2 seconds after you jump to jump again, not a big deal to others but it bugs me )
there are 5 weapons per PERK ( literally it )
The setting is CRINGE ( for those that dont know, they decided to move the setting 70+ years into the future, its like 2090 or something, we no longer work for HORZINE but for the Patriarchs "third kid? i thought he only had 2 but fuck it we ball or something" they took Nightfall from the first game but now it feels like a cringe version of overwatch with less budget tbh, i dont like the setting, its all futuristic cyberpunk distopian, the thing i liked about the old maps is that we were basically exploring our current day or previous however many year world and just walking through a awful whole world went to shit version, now its all boring, i dont care about any of the maps, they have very limited visuals anyways, before you could look around the cities and see beyond the edge of the map, so far there is only 2 maps that let you do this and they did a bad job at it, as in its very limited, i know they said they "wanted to move the setting so far up so they arent restrained by the games established setting", but it really feels like this game is an example of why some people should color between the lines instead )

all in all, it really felt like someone said "thats it, stop working" after they showed the reveal trailer and then they all sat on their asses until release, this was such an easy win because the fans love the original formula and they changed the recipe

i wouldnt recommend this game for a couple of years, definetly not a couple of months, they really need to dial in, lock in and add a ton of content

review:
If you want the tldr of what I think about the game, it is barely a 4/10, just narrowly escaping a 3/10 rating. It is slightly worse than kf1 and noticeably worse than kf2. Do not buy this game.

Okay now for the long answer: The best thing about this game is the moment-to-moment gameplay. It is better than either of the two previous Killing Floor games. That is literally the only thing I can definitively say is better about this game. Everything else about it is either not improved or somehow worse than before.

Killing floor throughout its lifetime has always suffered the curse of having good gameplay with nothing else to tag alongside that gameplay. It's why despite me being a big fan of both the 1st and 2nd game, I can really only rate them a 5 and 6 out of ten, respectively. They have good gameplay, but nothing else, and without any replay value, its gameplay becomes a harder selling point, especially when as you play those games more you become more in tune with all of their flaws and annoying quirks.

Kf3 decides that in order to tackle that replayability issue, that it should have a crafting system for weapon altering mods, that also have RNG based bonuses, that requires you to upgrade to the max with resources that you must ALSO grind for in game in order to access said bonuses. Oh, and you cannot exchange your more common resources for the rarer ones, so have fun grinding your ass off for gray matter and ESPECIALLY biosteel. Seriously, Deep Rock Galactic already has a resource exchange system, and Darktide used to be infamous for having some of the worst RNG grinds/crafting systems ever seen in a video game, so the fact that the devs decided to go this route while also half-assing it is baffling. The only good thing I can say about this crafting system is that recycling mods gives you back most of the resources you spent to craft it, but this wouldn't even be an issue at all if you could just... exchange your more common resources for the rarer ones.

Oh, speaking of grind, have fun playing normal and hard for the first 25 levels of each and every one of your perks, cause you do not have the damage or tankiness required to deal with Hell-on-Earth enemies before that point. And the leveling system takes nearly twice as long as kf2's, Hooray! Honestly I'd rather deal with kf1's leveling system, because at least there leveling up gave you a substantial boost in your abilities, can't say the same here. You not only have to grind for levels to get skills, you have to grind for skillpoints to then upgrade those skills to make them more potent, AS IF WE NEEDED ANY MORE FUCKING GRINDING IN THIS GAME. Oh, and the cherry on top is that you aren't allowed to swap skills between waves whatsoever, something that Kf2 and even kf1 allowed you to do. This is literally a downgrade in every single way.

And even though the gameplay may be fun, most of the weapons sure as hell aren't. The feedback for most of them are terrible, and on Hell-on-Earth, you only get a few options to use: The Vulcan, G33 with enfeeble grenades, the Striek with quad barrel and enfeeble slugs, or the scar. And you must always have your upgrades geared towards damage, bonuses included, because the more damage you deal, the faster you kill, which means the less time something has to attack you. And because bonuses are entirely RNG based, that means you could potentially grind for a ton of resources to get parts with specific bonuses, AND THEN JUST NOT GET THEM ANYWAY.

And don't even get me started on the performance issues. Yep, it's built on Unreal 5, and you know what that means: Lots of lag, Lots of PC resource hogging, and crashes. Lots and lots of crashes. I would have more to say about what is wrong with the game, but to be honest with you, the game crashes so much for me that I cannot point out other issues about the game outside of the immediately obvious ones. Mind you, my PC can run Helldivers 2 buttery smooth, 90+ FPS, and that game is INFAMOUS for having godawful performance. Something about Unreal engine 5 just makes games using it perform terribly, and the bad performance alone is why I wouldn't recommend this game.

This game had every opportunity to succeed, and Tripwire fumbled the bag so badly that I honestly do not see any future for this game, and I'm scratching my head over the people who claim otherwise. "Just wait like a year or two bro, it'll be better then!" Have you guys seen the player counts? They are fucking abysmal. As of right now, this game has around 300 concurrent players and a peak of a little over 600. It is BARELY beating out Kf1 right now, a game made almost 14 years ago. So yeah, do not buy this game, and do not listen to anyone who says otherwise, they are either currently high on copium or lying to you.

Honestly? I like it, conceptually. I get the idea; they wanted to do some sort of Killing Floor Vermintide, blending ideas from both series. I can see the vision at least, and it's a nice concept for a spin-off title. It's obvious as much in the hub and VA work as it is in class design and mission layout.

However, it's not a spin-off, and that's going to kill it. It should've stuck with its original name of Nightfall... even the .exe is still called that. This being "Killing Floor 3" is devastating both to what you should expect from it, and to what the developers seemingly intended for it; I'd go so far as to say it's nearly false advertising to call this KF3, and I can't recommend it on that alone.

IMO, in the context of what seems to be the game's intended design, most faults are down to lack of content and a need for tuning. Both of these problems could be easily solved with time and sales, because what's there is interesting...

...But you know what would've given you both, Tripwire? Not calling this a sequel. Let spin-offs be spin-offs. Not every game needs to be a mainline entry, especially with drastic fundamental changes like what this one offers.

review:
Sequel that I tried to love but just couldn’t.

Killing Floor III was the long-awaited sequel in the series and when I learned of its development, I pre-ordered it immediately. I was excited, hopeful and could not wait for it to come out. The experience I got at release was a wild ride of disappointment and sadness. 

Killing Floor III is, in the core, the same game and principle as the previous installments. You choose a map, fight waves of enemies (Zeds) and in the end, fight a boss. You can choose a class, earn experience and level up, after which you can unlock abilities and skills for your characters and upgrade them. 

Killing Floor III looks amazing. Graphics, animations and enemy design are all very good and the PhysX effects and ragdoll are spot on. The only problem here, is that all the maps are very, very dark and too “realistic”. The blood and gore effects are great and the carnage when playing a match (and not crashing) is intense.

The sound effects are also spot on, and the metal soundtracks are back from the previous games, although not as many and not the greatest tracks in my opinion.

Gameplay wise, Killing Floor III plays similar to the other games, with some small tweaks. Every character now has special items with them like a shock trap, multi tools or ammo bags, which can be selected in the load outs. Every class now also has a special attack that recharges overtime. 

Another new feature is the mods and add-ons for your weapons. You collect parts salvaged from camera’s, digital billboards and antennas to create and upgrade these mods, which can be installed in your weapons. 

The first problem with this game was its horrible, horrible launch. Never have I seen a game so broken, unstable and f@cked as this game was when it came out. There were constant “Unreal Engine GPU Crash Dumps”, stuttering, performance issues and matchmaking issues. I never crashed so much as with this game, and I was not alone. The developers were doing nothing at first and were just fixing some waiting issues in the matchmaking, better matchmaking and server performance and all kinds of other, useless fixes, instead of focusing all their attention on fixing the game breaking crashes. 

Then you got hundreds of glitches, which let you just delete a complete mod add-on because you press the wrong button, or the skills that you assigned did not assign but the points were gone. 

Although my main issue was by far the horrible performance of this game, later on, when everything finally was playable (and I was somehow still playing), the gameplay loop and lack of content got boring really quick. You cannot select the number of waves per level, so variation is a no go. There are three bosses and 10 maps and that’s it. 

You can upgrade your weapons with mods, as mentioned earlier, but this results in some Frankenstein creations in which your character becomes invincible, and all challenges are gone that the game has to offer. There are also certain spots in levels that makes all the enemies come at you in a straight line, so picking them of is very easy.

And for me, the final nail in the coffin is the fact that, even when this game becomes stable, playable and gets more content in terms of levels, bosses, selectable waves, new enemies etc. I just don’t have the same feel with it as the other games, especially Killing Floor 2. 

I thought by myself that it was just a matter of nostalgia, but many times, after I was done with Killing Floor III and started a round of Killing Floor 2 with some friends, the immense action, optimized game, graphics, soundtracks, beautiful maps, content and experience hit me in the face with an overwhelming force.

It was this moment that I realized that Killing Floor III is, and never will be, the true successor for Killing Floor 2 and is just a poor or “okayish” game. 

I would not recommend it.

The gameplay is functional and I don't mind them doing things differently from KF2, but there are a few observable technical issues with this game. For one, it crashes quite often, roughly every 1-2 matches on average. It may crash on the first game after starting it up, and it may do this repeatedly after having previously crashed. It also occasionally puts me into very high-ping matches even if I'm the only player in the lobby, and the lag prediction seems to like to break, causing my movement to become stuttery. I don't have a VPN or anything to warrant these issues.

I would like to enjoy this game as it is, but it is very annoying to constantly crash this frequently and repeatedly and having to start the game again and again and make the walk to the VTOL again and again.

Other mildly annoying things:
Holding your secondary action (ADS/block/etc.) during a weapon swap does not queue it. You have to walk over to the VTOL and wait an additional 10 second timer afterwards to begin queuing.

Rest of it includes specialists and perks being decoupled (which should have been done before launch), performance updates and bug fixes (which could have been pushed in minor updates anyways), and some UI updates (which... I don't even know what to say about that).

This game has strong foundation but it'll take at least a year before it gains some traction, and as of writing this review it has around 300 concurrent players on Steam. It might end up being a game that no one cares about by the time it has healthy amount of content in it.

You're better off sticking with KF2.
The average player peak of ca. 350 (before the recent update; see https://steamdb.info/app/1430190/charts/ ) basically tells you everything you need to know.

***
Gave it another try in Dec. 2025, after the DJ Scully/Stalker update and it's worse than before.
Vastly lower average FPS and annoying hitches while traversing the map.
And they f*cked up the controls again, with some staying "hardcoded" to keys that are not displayed in the controls settings.

I think I'm done with this dumpster fire of a paid pre-alpha version.
Due to the small 20GB install size I'll probably check back in after a while but I expect nothing.
***

I gotta admit, the KF3 movement is more dynamic and you can use the attachment system to make weapons effective with different classes. The gore looks good.

[h1]The rest of the game, though:[/h1]

• They keep re-introducing bugs like a rookie developer (actually worse). They just f*cked up the controls, again, so you have to delete certain files and re-assign everything, or wait for a fix.

I won't be surprised if this keeps happening with every update.[/h3]

review:
Even after months of hotfixes and one bigger patch, this is still a buggy, unfinished mess. The gunplay does feel better now, but there's just not enough there there. As has been said before, this is an early access game in every way but name. A substantial delay from the initial release wasn't enough to bring this up to the same standard as even KF2's early access launch.

There are some good ideas in here, but for every neat new thing there are several baffling design decisions that don't add to the experience in a meaningful way. Missing features are punctuated by the ever present MT/battlepass, which oddly feels even worse than the loot box hell that KF2 became.

This doesn't even feel like a game for KF fans. It's more like a bridge toward more popular established game trends. Killing Floor is better when it's its own thing, and not just another co-op shooter. 

This is going to need a lot of attention to win back 99% of the playerbase (not an exaggeration, it went from ~20K peak to >200 players in 3 months). At this point, I would even say that if TWI wants anyone to play this, they'll have to go F2P within the first year and just rely on MTs to keep it running. Because as of right now, they have managed to piss off their entire fanbase and have no hope of saving this beyond lowering the barrier of entry to nothing as a hail mary.

review:
I'm a huge fan of the Killing Floor series, but I bought the 3rd game and I'm a bit in shock. How can a game made in 2025 be worse than the 2nd one, which was simply a masterpiece? The color palette here is just awful; everything merges into one blob, and I don't even want to be in the game. There's no real interaction with the monsters at all; it feels like they just react to stimuli and an animation plays. The weapons don't look good, they're not unique—just identical pieces of metal. The textures are terrible, like something from 2017, and the optimization is awful. Grenade explosions look like they're from a cheap game, very unrealistic. There are very few characters to choose from. It's hard to understand how to buy and select weapons; in the second game, everything was clear, but here it's unpleasant and not intuitive.

My friend and I were playing, and it took us three tries just to play together because the game crashed for me, then for him. And when we finally got a game started, it crashed for me again at the end of the match. This is just a disgrace.

There are some positives, of course—new features like the spiders climbing walls, the weapon recoil feels nice, and the shooting has generally gotten better.

I am begging you—please rework everything. Killing Floor is one of the few cool games that I loved so much and still love. I was so hopeful that this game would be great. But at this stage, I don't want to play it. I'll have to keep playing the second game until this one becomes something adequate. I really hope you will rework everything drastically. Please don't abandon this unique project that is loved by so many people. You're just risking new players not coming to the game if something isn't done drastically right now.

review:
Killing Floor 3 ain’t a sequel, it’s a bleedin’ liberty, innit? They’ve taken a cult classic, ripped out its innards, and tarted it up like a Croydon scrubber on a two-quid hen do. The old games had grit, gunpowder, and proper graft. This one’s got more polish than a copper’s helmet and half the soul of a bag of pork scratchings.

It’s flashy, hollow, and about as British as a vegan pie in Greggs. The whole thing’s a right dog’s dinner. All the glitz of Piccadilly, none of the heart of Peckham. It struts in wearin’ designer clobber, but the moment it opens its gob you realise it’s thick as two short planks and twice as wooden.

All hat, no kecks, absolute pile of pony. Avoid this like a kebab shop salad. Ain’t worth the dosh or the heartache.

If KF1 was a pint of proper stout and KF2 was a cheeky double at last orders, this one’s a warm shandy nicked from the rub-a-dub floor. Stick a fork in it, mate. It’s done, and not in the good way.

review:
This piece of Early Access trash game is an absolute disgrace. It’s got only 8 maps, no custom maps, no workshop, but hey, to make you even happier they added battle passes. So if you want your skins, you’ll have to pay for everything and buy in-game currency with real money, on top of the game’s price, which is sold for the same as a AAA. Basically a live service. If you’ve never played KF2, go play it before saying “I lIkE tHiS gAmE bEcAuSe I pAiD fOr iT wItH mY MOmMy’S WeEkLY AlLoWaNcE”, you’ll see how big the difference is.

I received this game as a gift and since I had it I thought, okay I will try this trash. There are still too many things that are unbalanced, from bosses that one shot you to weapons that deal very little damage. The next major update will bring new weapons and some balancing changes, but right now this game feels rough and unpleasant to play, lacking even a text chat to coordinate with your team, and if you are in a squad and using voice chat with people who do not even know english, that is useless too, not to mention that not everyone uses a mic, but i use it. 
This kind of game requires cooperation, and the lack of a simple text chat which was present in KF2 makes everything a mess. This game is still in early access in every way, even though that label was removed from the store. There are very few weapons available, and you always end up using the same strongest one, the Vulkan, which becomes boring. The perks are interesting but need improvement. My advice, disable crossplay or you will end up playing with idiots from consoles. The downside is that if you disable crossplay, the servers will be empty on PC. The enemy design is well done, but most of the game does not have the same feeling as KF2, it does not convey the same sensations. Several classes are missing, for example there is no Berserker which is one of my favorite classes in KF2 because it is a tank with melee attacks after activating rage, but it is not here. I understand that it is still in development, but the worst part is the lack of a damn text chat that should have been there at launch. It is not acceptable that everyone in the team just plays however they want, and you are forced to face tough bosses alone, because of this lack of cooperation several matches were lost. I am trying the Firebug, but there are really many weapons missing.

Only the ninja has melee weapons, all the others have only the basic knife and ranged weapons. This means that if you are surrounded by enemies and need to make your way through with melee attacks like in KF2, you are literally fu*ked, especially if you have big enemies in front of you.

For the few weapons available, there are three variants for each model with different stats, but no completely different weapon models. Weapons can have attachments like sights, stocks, and more, and these components can also be upgraded by farming materials during matches. This is an interesting feature because you can add these upgraded weapons to your preferred loadout and buy them later with the dosh you have earned. 
In just a few hours of playtime I got disconnected from the servers multiple times, and a few other times the game crashed while trying to join matches, leaving me stuck on a frozen screen right after the lobby loading.

Right now it’s only being played online by console users, I’ve seen very few pc players because this game is completely unbalanced and unfinished.
At the moment I do not recommend buying this game as it is now. It will probably improve, but there are still far too many things missing, because who decided to create this game in this state and sell it at a price that is completely unreasonable is not only a scammer, but should also be fired from Tripwire.

review:
PERSONAL FEELINGS:
I played the first Killing Floor game as a kid, and it really scared me. The monsters' appearances, sounds, and atmosphere were perfect for the time period. The second game was a bit more modern, but still felt like a sequel to Killing Floor. This third game, however, was a mix of Doom + Gears of War + Dead Space. I played it like the Killing Floor skin mod had been added to another game.

OVERALL REVIEW:
In previous games, you felt confident as your character progressed, but in this game, the weapon impact and body damage are very weak, and instead of providing a challenging gameplay experience, it becomes tedious. The dash system doesn't work to prevent damage because you're definitely taking damage. The gun's appearance is definitely sloppy and space-themed. The inability to pick up limited syringes and ammo boxes is a complete disappointment. The game tried to combine the survival mechanics of Resident Evil with the mind-numbing, just-shoot-and-hunt-the-monsters mechanics of Doom, but it's completely incompatible. If you run out of syringes, you have no alternative, and likewise, if you run out of money, you have no alternative to pick up ammo. (The AMMO BAG is useful for multiplayer.)

CREATURE REVIEW
Siren, Fleshpound, Husk, and Screamer are well-designed, but Clot and Crawler are smooth, air-filled jelly, like Demi Eligos's cutest creatures from Evil Dead the Game. Furthermore, even if Screamer and Fleshpound lose their slow, intimidating gait and don't take damage, they still chase you furiously, and your damage-dealing time is very limited. Husk has received a major mobility boost. Also, why does Bloat run, and his acid-spraying behavior is hilarious. Executions feel like stabbing through the air, not like hitting something solid, so they're unsatisfying. MOST IMPORTANTLY, WHY ARE THERE NO STALKERS IN THIS GAME?

FINAL WORDS:
The game throws random creatures at you, and you try to kill them with useless dashes and damaging weapons like bead guns.

I'm going to play this game because I love the genre and because it has a system for XP, character, skill, and weapon upgrades. If it weren't for these, I'd refund the game.

I hope the old developer returns and the next game is a KILLING FLOOR (2009) REMASTERED OR REMAKE (THE GAME KF FANS ACTUALLY WANT)

55/100

review:
[h1]This game is hopeless, this game will never get better, you should never give this game a chance.[/h1]
tl;dr
－KF1 and KF2 is better game, this game is made to please the shareholder, not you the player.
－KF3 now has 10% player count of KF2 (300 vs 3000)
－it took them very long time to release a update that makes the game worse
－Gameplay has no depth, unpolished, bug appears all the time, a lot of meaningless design.
－I got all the Hell on Earth achievement on solo before lv20, skill issue is an invalidate argument if someone want to use that against this review.

So why do I have this game? because apparently gifting KF3 to your friend who is a big fan of previous Killing Floor game is such a fun thing to do, and I play it solely because 100% achievement in this game is so easy you can literally do it in 25 hours.

[h2]Biggest issue of the game - Identity[/h2]
This game has no its own identity, this game has so many features in it and none of them coordinate with each other. You have this weird syringe limitation that seems to try to make healing a precious resource and then you could got infinite healing dart from other player, or skill you can spam and got half of you health back again. Which gives solo a very strange reason to be more difficult than coop.

There are a lot of feature feels like lazy fix for the issue this game has. You can call turret with multi-tool to clear zed and save your ammo, you can zipline and easily get rid of the zeds (which is pretty op and I guess that's the reason they make so many zed has range attack, and the cooldown on zipline also makes no sense)
And that ended up making developers don't have to think about fixing the zeds because of these fast solutions they offered, while also makes the game worse because developer has to come up with a solution to counter these tools they gave to the players.

[h2]Zed Design is a mess[/h2]
This game has a weird lighting that if you don't use flashlight then all the zed looks really dark. Not to mention they are also pretty grey at the same time. You won't be able to figure out where the Scrake and Fleshpound is in the group of zed in a glimpse, and that being an issue in a fast paced game is very problematic.
And like I mentioned before, if you want to make health a rare resource, that's ok, but [b]every Zed can literally do everything to hurt you.[/b]
Almost every enemy does range attack :
－Cyst can shoot you
－Crawler can shoot you from the wall
－Bloat can charge and shoot bile bomb onto you
－Siren shoots fast traveling sonic wave to hurt you
－Scrake has a grapple hook with very unnoticeable visual cue but completely silence despite it can literally end your game.
－Fleshpound has mid range attack and also chases you extremely fast.
[b]－Husk can mortar you from 50m away on roof or wherever you won't notice, shoot you from the sky, does the super annoying jump flying flamethrower animation which makes him hurting you a lot but also super hard to hit.[/b] and the ground fire he create sneaky hurts you when you can barely notice it.

I get that the more tool you give to player, the more threat enemies should offer. The ironically thing is in a game where the aggressive abomination tries to chase you down, most of your damage is caused by ranged attack, you might as well give all of them a gun and make this game Payday.
And in such vulnerable environment for player, the syringe is limited? Dark Soul can get away with it because most enemy has predictable attack pattern and they usually don't have 10+ enemies at the same time for the information dumping. Not to mention a lot of attack in KF3 just felt really unfair and random. Dodge doesn't do anything most of the time because zed tracks you really well (unless you side dodge, but most of the situation does not allow you to do that)

Do you know why there's only guide telling you how to kill Scrake and Fleshpound efficiently instead of telling you how they work so you have a strategy to kill them with minimal risk? Because no one knows how they work. If they decided to run to you, they just do that, what the zed does is completely out of player's control. All you have to think about is how to dump damage as fast as possible before it kills you, or make a status effect build that can somehow make them unable to move at all. Either way it's just math game, no skill involved, this game functions more like a loot shooter in this aspect.

This game on the one hand encourages you to be precise and calculating, while also asks you to be reactive and agile. If this game really want to fix itself, it either has to get rid of all the complex zed movement and make them more threatening by doing what they are supposed to do (Which makes me think Gorefast is the most well designed zed in this game), or make the movement system works better and every attack the zed does is reactable in a chaotic situation (like Left 4 Dead 2 where spitter glows, smoker has particle, or hunter being very loud)

In the end, they threw a lot challlenges to the players and forgot these challenges are also what developers have to solve.

[h2]Terrible Communication Experience[/h2]
This game has no text chat. If you don't have microphone, terrible in game voice menu is all you got.
the UI in this game is so painful to navigate, for some reason they made voice detect chat enabled by default so you'll hear random speaking with his family without realizing it (which is like the only entertainment I can have in this game but I felt bad for people who aren't aware of it)

This game does have character voice menu but it requires you to hold for a second to call it out, it even has second page so if you are into saying sorry or thanks frequently, you have to hold the voice menu button for one second, middle mouse to switch page and then select the voice. this redundant process has made me never ever want to open the voice menu again. you can argue KF1 voice menu does the same, but there's no delay for KF1 voice menu. I can literally press V23 in 0.1 second and my character will say thank you. If the button doesn't do anything when I just press it, why do I have to hold it for so long to call it out?

It also has ping function, I like to use ping function a lot in PvE game to make my teammate aware of the threat, but in this game when you ping enemy, there's no enemy outline, no sound effect, character doesn't speak anything. If you didn't happen to face the direction your teammate pinged, you'll never notice it right away.

This is a coop game where it feels like everyone is doing their own thing. They see each other being low health from time to time, they shoot the healing dart and go back to do their own thing. Even the different perk doesn't have a role. Everyone can kill small zeds efficiently, you don't have to help ninja to kill husk and siren because he had a lot range weapon to do that. You don't have to help Firebug to kill the big zed because Vulcan does everything in this game.

[h2]Conclusion[/h2]
For some reason this game has a lot of frantic defender. If you had fun in this game, I'm happy for you, But I think your precious time deserved to be spend on better passionate games. There are a lot of more superior choice in the PvE market that are more enjoyable. go buy Killing Floor 1 or 2,  Left 4 Dead 2, Deep Rock Galactic, even Warhammer 40,000 Dark Tide which was terrible at launch but redeemed itself with so much update.

This game can't save itself, unless it stops to try to contain everything and finding its own identity, this game will most likely be a completely wasteland before 2026 ends.

And if you unfortunately received this game in some way and has addiction to full achievement games, I made a guide for power leveling. Mute the game, turn on some valuable podcast and start your mindless grind.

review:
First and foremost, let me say that Killing Floor is one of my favorite franchises. I started all the way back with KF1, and when KF2 launched, I instantly bought it and have never really stopped playing it. I might not have the most hours in the game, but played it on and off throughout the years.

I was quite hyped for KF3, and initially on launch I had a 50/50 feeling. I liked some parts, disliked other parts. Nonetheless, I still had fun for the first 10–20 hours, partly because it felt refreshing, but also partly because I played with friends.

More and more however, I started to see through this initial hype. Let me start with the good parts.

Killing Floor 3 has much better movement mechanics which suit the game well. The graphics also got a nice boost and the game looks really good and the gore is also better than it ever was.

Sadly, there’s much more downsides. Starting off with the low map pool. KF3 only has 8 maps, and with the lack of the workshop support this is just not enough. Especially not because the maps are designed quite badly. In KF1 & 2 the maps were designed in such a way that running through them and kiting the ZED’s was the go-to move. In KF3 you just.. Camp in a hallway with the full team and that's it.

I also don't like the revamped weapon system. Making your own classes and weapon combinations seems fun at first, but it takes away from the game. The moment you need to google for best builds and need to grind loot to buy upgrades, you really take the core focus of just killing ZED’s with good music away.

But that’s not all. The most important of everything… Is the stability. The game runs like shit, performance is low and there are lots of crashes. The game isn’t receiving a lot of updates either. Each patch that comes out breaks more than it fixes, and content is nowhere to be seen.

KF3 also launched with a lot less perks than KF2 or KF1. Which is not bad on itself, but considering everything I said above, this is just another downer.

Considering everything together, I just can’t recommend KF3 right now. The game has potential, but sadly it just doesn’t feel like a real Killing Floor game. This together with all the bad points I listed above, and the player count going downhill quickly, I would hold off and see where this game is in a couple of years. Just for the record, I did really try to like this game. I’m a massive fan and really wanted to like this one.

I regret buying this game.
Some things just need removing — like the crafting and grinding for salvage. It’s tedious. Just make it so we can buy different attachments in the shop.

Get rid of the fortress or hub area. It doesn’t look bad, but I’d rather not have to load into the main menu only to spawn in the hub, then run to the console just to look for a match, and only then run to the chopper — who is annoying to listen to.

Get rid of the ultimate abilities and just turn them into weapons. I’m not playing a hero shooter.

Bring back the old way of healing with syringes.

People saying this is like how Payday 3 went down — I disagree with that. Payday 3 was botched at launch. This just had some minor performance issues. Not great, but not unplayable in my case. This went down more like Dawn of War 3, if people remember what happened with that game — just out-of-touch devs and management chasing trends. Ultimately, fans don’t like it but can’t do anything about it because we know they’re still going to force skins and operators, resell old operators and weapons all in a bundle, while also pushing season passes and battle passes — all because of trend chasing.

They’ll fix the bare minimum after this update. They make these roadmaps just to shut people up — like the decoupling of perks and ops. What a waste of time. That’s genuinely how I feel about this game: a waste of time and money.

There’s more I could talk about. It’s not a bad game — it’s just a very big meh. Painfully average. I probably won’t play this game again for a while. I’ll keep checking for updates to see if it’s improved or been abandoned. Only time will tell — and if the devs or management even care.

I'm very easily entertained by simulator games, even if most of them are the same. I can find enjoyment in them even if they aren't perfect or have some issues but this simulator has some MAJOR issues. Just glancing at the discussion board will tell you that. 

Game is extremely slow, especially at the start. Milestones are easy to reach and feel rewarding but a lot of the interface is confusing and unclear. You're charged sales taxes every day but can never know ahead of time how much the deduction is. There is a significant game breaking issue around level 20-25 with the unlock of the 5 tier pharmacy shelf where you cannot move product between shelves even if the product is the same. This made restocking a pretty major hassle for me. Many other players are reporting this same issue. 

Amount in stock also reflects products still in boxes but not on the shelf which makes restocking confusing. In order to hire an employee your counter has to be closed and reset for the next day - things that aren't mentioned. The amount of product you can buy vs the size of the shelves is also strange. Why 10 items per box but 20 spaces per shelf? 

Will edit review if bugs are fixed. Might be worth the reduced price but certainly not more.

review:
Can't recommend in current state. I really want to like this one, but I think there's still a long way to go.

Enjoyed the tutorial for the most part, but after the initial quests it gets *really* repetitive, and leveling takes a really long time. It would take serving over a hundred customers to get to Level 10 to take the first exam to get new meds. There doesn't seem to be an overt way to make more XP by doing well, so having streamlined stock management, good decor etc isn't going to make a difference. I wanted to make it to the first exam and I just got so bored very quickly.

The game is very unpolished too - dialogue translations into English are not very good, and the UI for the different stores is really simplistic and isn't fantastic design-wise. I think there's a LOT of room to improve here by adding more dialogue and bringing in someone who can design the storefronts to be a bit more high-end and professional looking.

There's so much potential here, so hopefully throughout the game's early access period there will be further improvements. At this point I don't feel like I got my money's worth quite yet.

review:
This game is very unpolished, lacks depth, and seems like a money grab. Labels are clumped together and look cheap, translations are incorrect all over the place, and some UI elements don't even show up correctly on the medicine. It gets repetitive within 20 minutes, I highly recommend you DO NOT buy this game. Not now and probably not even in a year. When asking customers what they want, you're given the same options EVERY single time, either: "don't have it" or "sure". 

The graphics are good but that's the only thing I can compliment in the hour I played it. You put a shelf up, order some medicine, put the medicine on the shelf, and proceed to serve a line of 4 customers the entire 40 minute long day - doing the same thing over and over again. When I first unlocked the scale I got excited, only to learn that the customers will use it, get in line, and that's literally it. The progression system is based on every other one - which is - licenses. There's plenty of things to sell, but the game lacks any difficulty, purpose, satisfaction, and everything else a game needs to be successful. 

Not to mention some of the unlocks saying "Available Outside of Demo", what a terrible game. 

This game needs an immense amount of gameplay, polishing, and an entire re-haul before it's worth even a dollar.

review:
Played this game for a long time and went all the way through every map. 

The positives first: 
1) Fish hook pretty quickly. 2) Maps are diverse and so are fish. 3) Error 404 additional reasons not found.

On to the bad stuff: 

1) Fish are VERY difficult to catch. Not the small stuff, those are fun and challenging. I fought a shark for an hour. 1 hour of my life before he swam all the way to the end of my line and I got fed up, turned my trim to 100% and broke him off. 
2) The game isn't finished. End of story. The last map has a huge area of water surrounding an island. Around the island there are a lot of fish but away from it there's nothing. My friend and I boated for 10 minutes to the edge of the map and there were no fish after the 1 minute mark. 
3) There are fish in the encyclopedia you cant catch. A blue marlin is listed in the encyclopedia but isn't located on any of the maps. The maps say what fish they have and multiple do not exist in the game. 
4) Your house has a massive aquarium you can't use. Fish can only go in the aquarium if they're under 30 lbs or so, which is very few, and there's a HUGE aquarium taking up the center of your house that you can't put anything in. 

TLDR: I don't regret getting the game, I'm glad I only paid $7. If it's ever actually finished I'll amend this review. I did have fun, only because I played with a friend.

review:
Man..spending almost 45 minutes trying to catch a catfish that was literally close enough for me to pick it up when it took the bait is infuriating.
I was using a level 10 Rod, level 12 reel, level 10 line and a spinning lure in Kiel Canal and the fish never seem to get tired.
The fish shot to 2000 ft out, gave me 200 ft, then shot up to 3000, gave me another 200, then shot up to 5000 ft out and was going from 5000 to 4700 and would never seem to get tired. I fought with this thing for 45 minutes and it never got tired...ever. There's no way that a 70-80 pound catfish has a 2nd and 3rd wind like that. That's just insane. I found myself nodding off in the middle of trying to reel it in because of how long it was taking. I got tired before the fish did. I ended up having to just give up and go to bed.

 I can't recommend this game until the developers or "developer." figure out a better system for tiring fish out. It should not be 100% reliant on the equipment, if you fight a fish for 45 minutes, at no point after the 30 minute mark should the fish have enough energy to keep pulling your line to the other end of the map with no return. I understand that the "fight" is exciting, but most of the time it's just the fish winning and the players giving up because it's too much of a hassle.

Positives -I like the environments and levels and choices for equipment and the graphics are really quite good, just need a better system for fighting fish.

The ground feeder system is completely broken — I can’t even describe what’s going on with the rods when using more than one. Topwater lures go straight down into the water instead of floating. Fish jump out of the water like they’ve been shot from a catapult.

On the new Alaska map, you can’t even use rod stands. There's also a weird input delay when casting — sometimes it takes several seconds before the cast actually happens.

Lures still lack proper animations. Honestly, even the old Rapala fishing games had better lure animations — at least they had them.

Despite all that, I’m still going to play this game... for now. But yeah — it’s a mess. Maybe the devs should focus on fixing what's broken instead of adding more content — especially since the new content tends to be buggy too.

I want to enjoy this game so much, and I really want it to succeed. I am a veteran player of UFS1 and purchased the sequel as soon as I heard of its existence. Unfortunately, aside from the graphics, UFS2 is a direct downgrade of its predecessor. Here's a list of missing or unclear features:
