review:
[h2]For the price, and what it offers. I don't think its worth it, multiplayer is also pretty dead. 
Most i connect to have an icon showing they're cross-platform and not on steam.[/h2]

I enjoy the setting of the world, the tasks and everything is more interesting than what i've seen in similar games. 
With that said, the game is also VERY confusing if you get into it for the first time. I will admit i was fiddling with settings because i accidentally screwed something up and had to restart the game, and when i did i didn't get the tutorial popping up for me again and couldn't re-play it.
So the tutorial might go through some of the basics, i am aware of this going into the review which is why i focus more on the [i]"logic"[/i] of things in the game. 

[h2]-Fire[/h2]
This is the most baffling thing to me, because the game has a thing where enemies on fire [b]hurt you more[/b] it does damage the enemies but if you have a fire damaging effect you better be killing them quick after you gave them that fire damage or they'll be returning the favour two-fold. Yet, the special attack of the Splash kit is to make the water gun spray fire instead, igniting enemies, friendlies and you alike. And since its your watergun doing it, you can't soak people if you actually set them ablaze, so i just never use that ult. There's also fire damage modifiers for weapons and a fire grenade and just... Why? 
Fire is kind of treated like "Fire, bad. Water, good!" in this game so why the hell do you then give players some fire damage weapons?! Just have them swear off fire entirely, don't touch it, if you see it remove it. Or at the least do something like how Vermintide 2 has the Skaven shoot green warp fire, while the hero Sienna shoots regular fire. So you can tell good fire from bad fire. That way the player can deal a special fire to the enemies [i](Maybe a graphite mixed fire since graphite seems to be the bane of the Hiss' existence?)[/i] that only damage them and not buff them. 

[h2]-Water[/h2]
In this game, water is healing, but for some reason only at certain times. Like in shower stations, from faucets and from a watercooler. But when shot from the Splash kits gun it just soaks you and give you the wet effect. I understand its for balacing reasons, the water gun with its fire rate being able to heal would be quite OP. But its just BS that it does nothing. Like, can't it at least do pitiful low but still some healing? Why is water different from water? 

[h2]-Highlighting items[/h2]
You will have tasks in this game which involve you grabbing or destroying items. These are worthlessly highlighted though, getting only a square marker once you are close to them. 
The maps in this are quite large and you are often assaulted by endless waves of enemies until the task is done. It doesn't give you breathing room. So running around, leaving cover only to aimlessly look for a task among so many other things, is a confusing mess. What they instead should have done is Left 4 Dead's old highlighting system.
Where it gives glowing contrours of the item and you can see it through walls. This means that if you get to a area where you need to grab 10 different things, you can see them and the challenge only becomes getting to them through all the enemies.
Especially things like the corrupted items. 
For context: 
Corrupt items are a game modifier where a item spawn in the area that boosts enemies, debuff you or breaks things  constantly that you'll need to fix. You need to find this item and destroy it for the modifier to disappear.
Now these items vary but the worst one of them is f*cking stapler that zooms around like a rabid mouse.
And these things can only be killed with a special item, a Graphite Grinder, that you also need to run around and look for. And once you have it, its ammo is limited so you can't miss the item too much.
And these corrupted items are NOT HIGHLIGHTED! So someone has to run around and find the graphite grinder and then run around more to find the corrupted item and destroy it. 
While carrying the grinder you can't fire your weapons too, and while the thing does damage enemies keep in mind what i said. Limited ammo.It grinds down the graphite in like 4-5 seconds of uninterupted firing, and you get about 3 graphite blocks. So make it count.

[h2]-Movement and interactions[/h2]
More than once i've had issues in this game related to the movement and interactions of it. The specials of all kits all involve something that the player needs to deploy. But the frankly idiotic thing about this is you need to stand still and let this animation play out of your character dropping the item, which takes like 2-3 seconds.
These items can be the difference between life and death. I don't mind the animation playing out, but if me and the team is running away from a group of enemies, i want to be able to activate the item and keep walking away from them, then i can stop and activate it. I don't want to stop, place the item, activate it and then run. 
If you try to place an item as you are moving, they will play the animation but not place the actual item, but they'll still automatically swap your weapon out for your class tool that's used to activate it. 

I think the game shows potential but it has a lot of things that just makes combat awkward and not fluent, the readability of it is just... Off. 
Its a weird world, that's the intention and i like that. But in return that means that objectives, elements and all that need to be grounded somewhat and not be [i]"Some water heal, some water don't"[/i] and [i]"Fire make enemies stronger, here use thing to set enemies on fire"[/i]
They should also lower the price down to about €20. 
For three classes, nine weapons and about 5-6 missions for €40? Nah man.
And its not fun playing alone so it needs multiplayer to survive. Currently i struggle to connect to a server where it doesn't lose connection or glitch out and connects me to someone's lobby but i can't ready up 
(The button isn't there for me to click)

The game apparently had a rough start and by a look of the numbers, its pretty dead in the water.
I do hope they work on it but the things i feel it needs to improve it are probably harder to implement than just a quick patch. I do hope they do though because at its current clunky state and its price, i don't see those player numbers rising anytime soon.
I got the game as a gift from a friend who wanted to play it. And him and our 3rd friend have pretty much dropped it. Its only me left, and i wasn't even the one who paid for it.

review:
This game can be really good. It looks good, an awesome setting, sounds nice, and the gunplay is pretty decent. There is a really good game here, and I absolutely love Remedy games, but in its current state I can't recommend it at all. I don't think the other negative reviews on this game do a very good job other than to say this game doesn't have content. So I wanted to record here all of the glaring problems my friends and I had with the game in our short time with it to help others make a more informed purchase:

There is very little content in the game. There are only 6 levels, and while they are very good, they are not very replayable because there is one scenario per level, there aren't different objectives for each level. When you run it once, you've seen everything it has to offer.

The level modifiers are neat, but there's only a handful of them and they really aren't that meaningful. They also all are dealt with in the same way, through the blackrock gun you find at any ammo station. I thought the supernatural items were gonna have a much much larger influence on this game, that was part of the draw for me buying the game! More on this later.

There are only 3 kits. They are varying levels of bad. I played the water kit mostly, and it was awful. You have a healing tank that gets destroyed instantly and is extremely onerous to even put down. And why would you put it down outside of combat, because most people just run back to the shower and ammo stand! And that's it. You get a water gun and water tank. You don't ever unlock anything else.

The buildcrafting is pretty much nonexistent. No upgrades you get are meaningful. Even good upgrades don't really buff you enough to feel like it matters. Leveling up just doesn't do anything, and any interesting perks are locked to really high levels. 

The equipment items are so weird. Why does the water gun have the left click ability at all? It's takes forever to charge and shoots a meaningless water bubble and overheats your equipment super fast. The right click and hold ability is the only usable one, and I've heard the other kits feel very similar.

My absolute biggest gripe with this game is the fact that the supernatural class items are so meaningless. Each kit gets ONE. Thats it. I thought we were going to deal with supernatural items in the levels and maybe capture them, so we could use them ourselves. Instead everyone gets one item and some are better than others. This is my biggest issue with the game. This is the coolest part of Control and it is just a sidenote in this game.

Weapon progression is bad. The only good weapons are the pump action shotgun and the smg. Every other weapon, especially the single shot weapons like the revolver and hunting rifle are just awful. There are way too many enemies and they have way too much health for these guns to be any good. Maybe if you could have two weapons at once? Every weapon feels like it should do a bit more damage to be honest.

The glacial pace you crawl when you are down is really dumb. Let you crawl faster or just remove it!

Environment effects are extremely annoying. It feels like the constant fires in the levels only exist so that the water kit can not feel useless. It is really obnoxious that the turret kit causes fires. Status effects are either useless or annoying, like when you accidentally electrocute yourself or your friends with the electric augment. Or the radiation augment, because yeah I want to irradiate enemies so that they run up to me and irradiate me and my friends with no way to get rid of it without going back to a shower!

Movement feels kinda bad. You are unreasonably slow with certain weapons. And why even have a crouch slide when it serves no purpose? Mantling isn't very consistent.

The encounter design/director is awful. Sometimes you get levels where the enemies will spawn forever. They spawn in front of you, behind you, and don't give you time to rest. Being stuck in a safe room forever is so stupid. This completely breaks the flow of a horde-like game, as you never have the point where you can relax and retool. Not to mention, you'll face infinite enemies while running around, but when you'd expect to be fighting the hordes during defense objectives, the enemies are nowhere to be found and you're left just sitting there. And this is very common we found.

The difficulty levels are also odd, as it feels like it just ups the amount of enemies substantially and that's it? Normal mode is hilariously easy, whereas hard mode is insanely swingy between easy levels vs enemies spawn infinitely levels.

Progression is annoying. The same currency used for actually improving your kit is ALSO used for buying cosmetics! So basically I never got any cosmetics during my playtime. The voice packs that the game director was super passionate about are non-existent? The characters don't really interact and when they do it's for some terrible joke like asking your boss for a raise. I thought they were going to expand the lore of the FBC??? The characters don't interact basically at all in-game, which is wild. The cosmetics also look kinda lame.

There is literally only one boss in the entire game. Sticky Ricky. And he wasn't that engaging to fight. Every other boss is just a buffed up normal guy. THEY ALSO NEVER DID THE "STICKY RICKYYYYYY" YELL IN THE LEVEL!

There should also be a lobby like in Deadlock where you can actually move around and there could be world-building elements in it.

review:
TL;DR: Amazing world and vibe, creative enemies, but the gameplay is slow, repetitive, and unbalanced. Wait for updates before buying.


FBC FIREBREAK has a lot of potential, but in its current state, it’s hard to recommend.

The Good:

The strongest aspect of this game is its setting. The bureau feels like CONTROL, but further along the timeline, with clever details and fun touches. The environment alone makes exploration enjoyable.

Enemy designs are also solid. Many are familiar from CONTROL, but the new ones (like tall enemies made of post-it notes or giant foes wielding massive water pipes) are creative and visually striking.

The new weapons look interesting too, though I haven’t had a chance to fully try them yet, as they are locked deep in the progression system.

The missions themselves were engaging, especially on first playthroughs. Discovering objectives and figuring out mechanics felt rewarding initially.


The Bad:

Progression is painfully slow. I hit level 13 in ~6 hours and didn't unlock any of the new weapons or any weapon upgrades.
Most of these upgrades aren't even very noteworthy, as there is at best two types of useable gun damage type perks out of the 6 that are useful.
And the grenades don't seem to do anything in any difficulty higher than normal.
The tool placement is also off, there have been more than 30 times where I had my turret cancel out for no reason and failed to deploy it in time because of it.

Replayability is poor. Despite a recent update promising more variety (like a “response team”), most missions remain the same aside from minor resupply placements.
The ability to modify how many altered items spawn during a run has been removed. In my dozens of runs, only three missions had altered items, and even then, I only saw about four unique items which is far fewer than advertised (no traffic light item from the trailer, for example which is pretty disappointing).

Difficulty is inconsistent. Normal mode is fine, but hard mode sometimes spawns enemies faster than you can kill them, making some missions nearly impossible. 
This inconsistency feels like either a bug or a glaring balance issue since it seems to have appeared after the latest update by looking at the forums.

Multiplayer is basically dead; I couldn’t find a 3rd player with a friend, which makes harder missions frustrating. Also good to note that the game doesn't scale encounters based on the number of players, so you're always at a disadvantage if you're less than 3.

I feel like the staff working in the game are either understaffed or overworked (or both), as the new weapons don't even have a video showcasing them and what they do, so for now I just gotta go on looks alone because you can't even try them until you unlock them.


Verdict:
FBC FIREBREAK is fun when initially discovering missions and exploring the world, but everything beyond that feels underdeveloped. The game has clear potential (especially given its CONTROL-inspired setting) but much of it is wasted in the current state.

I’m hopeful for the upcoming November update, which is supposed to add a roguelike mode (and hopefully make missions more random, increase rewards and improve enemy wave balancing). 
Until then, I recommend waiting for news or updates before purchasing.

Edit:
The endless mode isn't tied to anything else in the game, meaning you can't progress your account, level, etc... while playing this new mode.
They changed the way perks work so you can have up to 9 perks (even upgraded) instead of just a few.
But because of this change, everything is tied to your account level, meaning that if you want the fun gun perks you need to be at least level 27 to get the first perk and 47 for the final one.
I shouldn't have to explain how bad this is as the rate at which you get XP is extremely slow ESPECIALLY FOR A DEAD GAME WITH LIKE 50 CONCURRENT USERS THAT WONT GET ANY NEW UPDATES AND IS LEFT ON ITS DEATH BED

Anyway yeah don't buy it.
The final update bought a few good QoL changes but not enough to make it worthwhile, even at a permanent 50% discount.
No new maps have been added and the endless mode is not that interesting. They did try to add different objectives to the current missions but the fact that there's so little already and none have been added makes it just disappointing.

name: FBC: Firebreak

review:
I like the idea of the game, playing with friends is fun (usually) and FBC: Firebreak is able to provide a quick "jump in, play a bit and jump out" while using Control's universe to provide an unique FPS experience, but the game has various problems which sometimes makes playing the game very frustrating.

[i](I originally played the game first time through Game Pass during July 2025 and later in October bought the game on sale. This review takes both states of the game into account).[/i]
Also need to point out, my review comes from the perspective of a Solo player, but I do enjoy the team play too. The game was not designed around solo play and the developers have stated it.

TL;DR: Game has some good bits and if you are a fan of Remedy's Control, you might enjoy the game's setting. Otherwise the game is just not quite there, there's bugs and game gets repetitive after some time. Solo play is not very good, but it's possible. I don't recommend the game at full price and I don't think it's worth 40€.

[h3]Positives:[/h3]
As mentioned above, FBC: Firebreak is very unique where it mechanically relies on status conditions (wet, on fire, frozen, etc...) to bring a very clever way to playing the game and being "wet" is actually a good thing. Enemies (and players) on fire slowly take damage, frozen condition slows them down (and freezes enemies), electricity is actually quite good way to stun enemies (where it doesn't affect the players as much as you think) and few more. Water is treated as the "universal good element" where drinking from fountains/showering in showers heal you and sprinklers and water [Weapons] "soak" the player, giving them resistance to other elements.

The setting of Control's universe adds a bit of that "SCP" spice into the mix, where you aren't dealing with any supernatural forces, but sticky notes that are quite lethal in large amounts, ever spreading goo that blocks everything, sentient skill lifts with extreme cold temperatures and living furnace? (which is not a good thing if it gets out of control). So as a loyal "office" employee of the Bureau, it's your job to scrap in the water cannon, grab a weapon and go deal with the anomalies. Also, the elevator arrives faster if you spam the button, hint hint. Also, you are not going to be using the top of the line or the most traditional weaponry, so get used to it :)

Each player is equipped with a dedicated crisis kit with unique tool and a role in the team, though don't worry if you accidentally stack the same kit as every problem can be dealt by anyone, specific kits just do it a lot faster. The game also features a "special meter", which is your crisis kit's special weapon that can wreck havoc were it in the form of a gnome that creates thunderstorms, teapot that turns your water cannon into a fire cannon or piggy bank that causes vortexes.

One highlight I do have to point is the "resonant perk system" where players are able to select a "3rd tier" of a perk (1st tier provides "weak" version of the perk, "2nd provides strong"), which shares the perk with team-mates as long as they are close-ish to each other, which can be a very handy in coordinated teams (maybe you want to play as a support person and other other players pick lots of perks while you provide few important ones). 

I also like how easily the player is able to restock ammo from the ammo desks.
And while the tasks require to do a mini-game to complete (tap Q or E in certain order shown on the screen), I kinda like it and the environmental hazards can be put out by doing the mini-game (where failing will hurt, but that's why you need to be precise and not spam the keys).

[h3]Neutrals:[/h3]
Game can get repetitive as there aren't that much variety and any variety the game has is very quickly experienced. When playing with other players, there aren't (at the moment) good ways to communicate with the other players as the game lacks a voice chat (pings and quick voice lines can help and when have played with friends, we usually are in a voice call via discord or equivalent services), but having something in the game would be handy. I am not sure about the game progression as most of the perks and equipment

Another aspect that goes into neutral is the "resonant" and "shield system" where closer you are with your team-mates, stronger your shield is, which encourages staying together. Though in some cases I am not sure if this is a good feature as in some cases it can be very dangerous to be together if the enemies manage to surprise the players, or rush with large amounts of enemies... or throw explosives which force players to move, which can lead into tough spots. 

Solo play is... decent. Where playing solo the game feels a bit more responsive, you really miss the team-mates tools to do certain tasks faster. But the solo experience dives down very quickly when the enemies start ramping up and more waves keep appearing while you're trying to do tasks. Hard solo difficulty is manageable, but it really depends what you are supposed to do. If you have to fix things, you are screwed.

[h3]Negatives:[/h3]
Personally, the biggest problem the game has is consistency and many bugs that frustrate. Healing in the game isn't instant and takes a moment before it kicks on, which can be a very serious problem as I have very consistently experienced cases where I'm close to dying and about to heal with a shower or with a water grenade, but I die because the healing didn't being immediately.
Another problem is enemies are very difficult to hit as they tend to flail around a lot and flying enemies are pain to shoot down (even with precision weapons). And also, let's give one of the flying enemies the ability to throw grenades that are hard to notice as the UI element warning about the grenade blends very easily on the screen and deals a lot of damage. Also, those enemies have near perfect aim, where they will (especially in solo) tear your shield and health apart. And on top of that, they stagger you.

Another problem with the game with enemies are... there are so many of them. Every so often you encounter enemy spawns that keep overwhelming the players and they just keep coming and especially on final objective they just keep coming.
And what is even more annoying than millions of enemies appearing to ruin your day? Those enemies breaking the things you are supposed to FIX in order to progress. I have no idea who thought it was wise to let the enemies break the things you are supposed to fix in order to complete the mission!?!  (I had a mission which lasted over an hour because enemies kept breaking the valves I was supposed to fix and even when I ran out of reinforcements, the reinforcement cool-down was so short enough I was able to push through it until I eventually failed because I ran out of reliable healing).

More problems to add to the list are weird menu UI behaviour, some crashes, unable to pick objects if they slightly go inside the world terrain (I have lost so many resources because I couldn't pick them up even though they seemed like I could) and game balance relying too much on "Here's a wave of enemies that feels like 2-3 waves worth of enemies. Have fun"

[hr][/hr]
I really want to enjoy the game and I have enjoyed the game so far, but there are just some days when things don't work or it drives me so mad that I don't want to play the game anymore. It has potential, but execution is not great nor consistent. I hope the developers manage to fix the problems.

For the price, I don't think the game is worth 40€, probably 30€ max after the majority of the problems have been fixed. I'm not sure if I would recommend it on sale either. If you get the game, I highly recommend playing it with friends as solo is not as well balanced. If you can try the game on Game Pass, maybe give it a try... maybe.

review:
I love Remedy and 503 but this just struck out with me. Simply? It didn't feel Control universe. It's just all wrong. Too cartoony, and some questionable design decisions (or lack thereof).

First off? You got drill sarge guy ordering you through the objectives. I never met this personality in Control. I imagine him as having a cigar stub hanging out of the corner of his mouth, and a green 1950s army helmet that's too small for his head... We're not a bunch of privates at boot camp... And the music? Sounds like something from a driving game...not Control/ FBC. When you look at the FBC headquarters it looks like something out of the 1950s/ 60s, so put something inspired from that era as the lobby music. The colors a vibrant and bubbly, instead of drab, cold and kind of spooky. The gear your character wears looks more Tank Girl post apocalyptic comic book than it does FBC. Where are the FBC uniforms? I wanted to role play this as an FBC security force, or ranger or something. 

Smashing/ breaking is considered repairing:? Couldn't they do a Battlefield Bad Company thing and have an engineer class that has a drill or something? I think this game would have done alright as literally another franchise. Like? I don't know...an Area 51 themed game where you're trying to contain and alien threat, as little aliens run around shooting ray guns at you? Because this game comes a cross to me as something between a multiplayer version of Rage 2 and High On Life. One of those games is post apocalyptic with a punk flair, the other is a whacky and spunky alien game. 

Why couldn't they include Control characters in the game off the get-go? Even FBC agent Kiran Estevez from Alan Wake 2, since she's fresh in our heads.  Heck, the person you're working for in this game could have been Simon Arish, instead of weird drill sarge guy. No Jesse Faden either... or whomever the current director is at this time. We could have had Emily Pope, Dr. Darling...any one of these people, right off the intro, in order to hook us into the Oldest House and make it feel related. It really should have just been first person Control. Like, maybe we're reliving the moment before Jesse's arrival but after Trench died, when everyone was first getting HRAs made, before Darling disappeared. in which case? We could have also included Helen Marshall. Literally anything like this. It could even be after AW2, or parallel with the Control story line. 

There could have also been classes, such as the before mentioned rangers, engineers, trauma team, spec ops etc. And it would have felt more tactical/ FBC. Blue/ black uniforms and tactical vests/ customizable HRAs. It was like these developers didn't play Control and so  didn't bother capturing the essence. Also? The Hiss aren't even spooky in this game. They're just a brainless horde that runs into your bullets for you. It makes me feel bad because I love Remedy games but this just didn't feel like one. I think it went too surreal and spunky.
name: FBC: Firebreak

review:
Really solid!

Innovative, interesting, fluid, dynamic co-op design revolving around the 3 tools to repair and apply statuses to enemies/terrain. Your gun is only 1 part of your kit, teamwork is essential for Hard and higher. 
Died on launch due to, mostly it seems, lack of content. While I agree, there should be more than this, what's there is enough to be enjoyably replayable with different kits, guns, builds, all while progressing through the cosmetic/perk trees. Most of the hate is baseless, to be honest. Look for negative reviews over 1 whiny sentence. 
Peer to peer networking, but requires a constant connection to Remedy servers just to launch, which I think is a bad idea when the Solo play is actually kinda solid. Ziplines feel really clunky. It fails half the time I try to ride them. There isn't much RNG to levels, but what's there is good, and more could be disorienting and detracting to the intended pace of the game (don't want to have too much of the game running around looking for the objective when you're clearly intended to stick together under pressure). Gun animations seem to argue too much with other player actions. There's a period in the reload when you've completed the reload (number full) but the animation isn't finished, and it cannot be interrupted. If you want to grab something, throw a grenade, fire, ADS, or repair something, you cannot for some reason. This is minor, and gladly there's no other examples of this kind of anim fighting. 

If I had to reduce it, I'd call it Payday 2 level design (minor RNG, but after a few runs you'll always know what to do) with DRG co-op design, but there's nothing quite like the full buffet of interplaying systems on display. Just make sure to work and stay together! Lone wolves don't get barrier ;3

[h2]Great, real great![/h2]

But I cannot sincerely recommend purchase. The idea is great, the balance is on it's way, thousands of players are already sold on the world, but the crippling dependency on decrepit servers, hallway-like mission design (which completely betrays the nature and selling point of the Oldest House, even worse than how CONTROL failed to fully utilize this aspect outside of literally one event), the 4 months between a major update and a fairly alright gamemode being added, and how few players there are make this game a true struggle to enjoy even for the most optimistic gamer. It literally averages 7 Steam players. That is joke-level bad! That's how much Payday 3 players say they have total! 

It's really such a shame, but in it's current state, this simply is not worth your money, nor do I think it will be for a long time (year [b]at least[/b] given the current rate of development), unless you have a willing friend and the spare cash.

review:
Sadly I don't think Remedy has the experience needed to make an FPS of this style. Here are some problems that made me uninterested in continuing to play. 

Visual issues. Not problems with how the game runs, but the signature wacky and weird effects found in their past successful games. They do NOT work for a first person situation. The Hiss haze makes it hard to see what you are doing when shooting at groups of enemies. It's not fun to rely solely on the hitmarkers to know if you are hitting something. 

Input responsiveness. Most inputs feel sluggish. Nothing much more to say about that other than it doesn't feel good, especially when most games with a similar playstyle to this one have near instant input response which makes the gameplay more engaging. 

Difficulty. I started on normal, playing solo cause no one was there to matchmake. Normal felt far too easy. Second game, while playing solo still, someone joined me. They had some kind of grenade launcher? With them it got boring. So next round I upped the difficulty, and suddenly I did barely any damage to anything. 

The always online thing. To my knowledge, a good handful of the popular horde shooters just use Peer to Peer networking? I may be wrong. But obviously that didn't go over well with players. 

In the end, knowing there are other games I can play that feel better all around, I can't say I recommend this. Try Warhammer Vermintide 2 or Left 4 Dead, or Deep Rock Galactic.

review:
I cannot, in good faith, recommend this game.

It's sad to say, since I admire Remedy and have been a huge fan of their studio for creative powerhouses like Alan Wake, Control and Max Payne. But this, this isn't it. This isn't their forte, and a live service shooter is something they should've stayed away from and shifted their focus and manpower to strictly develop single-player experiences. It's also unfortunate because I was genuinely looking forward to this game, and to expand on the Control universe with a whimsical and whacky entry into it's story, it just falls flat from poor balancing, monotonous and laborious objectives, and flat gameplay.

PROS:
- The universe and implementation of corrupted items is a nice touch. I like that different corrupted items dynamically change the game environment, despite how easy it is to destroy them.
- The cosmetics add a nice touch to the whimsical aspect of the game since you're standard employees that know nothing about anything when it comes to combat armaments and protection. Seeing the jerry-rigged outfits and improvised tools is a funny and intriguing aspect, especially how they work.
- Playing with friends is about the only thing that makes this game somewhat enjoyable.

CONS:
- Enemy behavior and balancing is not good. Enemies can shoot through obstacles you take cover with; they run right past you to a distractor device on the other side of the map and won't be bothered if you shoot them; they sometimes turn invulnerable even after their buff has been destroyed; they are stupid weak and extremely squishy; they are limited in variety; the list goes on. They are simply boring to fight and variety is too small to even consider that they're worth a fight.
- Environmental hazards are poorly implemented and don't function as intended. The pink goo perpetually respawns, as does fire, despite your billion attempts to extinguish or remove it. They cause more damage to you than most of the enemies do, and that says something.
- Your shield is also poorly implemented and works appropriately during solo runs. I get that staying together is a factor in charging them effectively, but even if you get separated (which is 99% of the time since there's no voice chat and everyone ventures off to do their own thing), you're up shit creek without a paddle because it won't charge until you get into proximity of a teammate... if they really wanted it to work, just let the shield charge normally by yourself and exponentially faster surrounded by teammates. It's that simple.
- Progression is a chore with barely any satisfaction, and weak perks do jack shit. To invoke a difference in your play style, you need Strong perks which take up two slots (a balancing effort I still don't understand but whatever), and resonating them is useless given how much more powerful you are as a player after the Overhaul update.
- Missions are monotonous and extremely boring. Go do this, destroy this, and fix this. Rinse and repeat... with limited variation in these objectives, it's more laborious than it is fun to complete these missions. Ramping up the difficulty only adds to that.

I really wanted to enjoy this game, but it just fell short and that's truly disheartening. Again, these are my personal gripes and I don't speak for the game, as others have enjoyed it and I aspire for them to envelope in that joy as much as they please. If they add more content with better variety and enemy composition, then it could be a pretty decent shooter that serves as a time killer and pleasant experience. Other than that, it's just a "safe bet" product that turned out to be a let down.

review:
If this was a random game by a no-name studio, it might have had some merit. Since this is Remedy game, it dares to stand where Control stood, it will be judged as such. This is really, really, really bad. Pure, distilled garbage. 

The concept sounds very intriguing. Play not as the director, but as a regular employees, face the same threats Jessie did, except in a new way, without super powers, with very hastily put together equipment. Almost like horror-survivor. What it ends up being is drugged out, incohesive power trip, a poor man's Darktide. Enemies that were minibosses in Control are now grunts that you kill by the hundreds. It. Just. Does't. Work like that. 

It doesn't even feel like a Remedy game, feels like a poor imitation by someone who saw a few Control screenshots, skimmed over one paragraph of the plot and decided to make a coop game out of it. There are familiar assets and environments but everything looks and feels way worse and cheap. The tone, the atmosphere, the unique elements about the setting - gone. Poor sound design, game crashes to boot.

There is nothing wrong with capitalizing on a successful IP and making a live-service game out of it, been done before: Outlast -> Outlast Trials. This one feels like and insult to the original game.

Poor. Uninspired. Trash.

review:
I actually liked it more on release somehow. I saw promise in the game when it came out but it clearly wasn't finished but the newest update was a genuine disappointment. Everything that was frustrating seems to just have been doubled down upon while the interesting stuff got reduced.

I get they added new guns, cosmetics ect but that wasn't really my issues. My issues before the recent update was a number of things.
Before the update:
1) Enemies just respawn so much that you can't actually get any sense of progression.
2) Enemies designed to effectively instantly destroy you or groups in a single instance with bloated hp values being spammed.
3) Balance around just really unsatisfying mechanics like ammo. You run out of ammo? That's well.. it.. unless you kill a heavy enemy who used to respawn fairly often but still annoying.

I liked the creative mission ideas and the corrupted items. Gunplay is fine but audio needs work badly.

After the update:
1) New enemies added that have extra health and spawn in even bigger numbers and just as fast as before. Seriously who's idea was this? Just replace all normal enemies with more AND armoured ones so instantly half the games weapons are thrown in the trash due to immensely low armour damage. What's the point of the system if 99% of enemies have armour?

2)Perks for guns are immensely disappointing. They seem to have massively nerfed every gun in the game in exchange to adding perks to them but its just insanely disappointing and vague. "When holding the trigger, increases damage by up to 75%" okay but.. for how long? Is it based on mag % or number of shots fired? A lot of perks are like this and picking good perks will still get your weapons nowhere near to a decent performance like before. Especially combined with the fact all new enemies have armour. Many of the perks seem effective requirements like bullet penetration considering how many enemies there are.

3)Removing ammo drops? Whyyyyyyyy? It only makes everything so much worse. I absolutely hate this obsession with dealing with difficulty this way. When you just hit a "Oh you can't play the game now, I guess thats difficulty?" I get people are going to say that there are ammo perks and skills ect but then the entire game is just built around those perks. You go to an ammo room, find out there's no ammo and thats just....it. That's it, game over thanks for playing. It's horridly amplified by the two points mentioned above.

4) More enemies designed to instantly destroy you. Even better now, they got jetpacks, can fly into the room in a corner behind everyone and just throw a grenade and instantly kill you. What's the point of this enemy? He looks like every other enemy in the game, completely blends in with a crowd so even in narrow areas they can easily just jetpack behind you. Then with no warning, you just suddenly explode, hit the ground and can see it behind you in the corner of the room roof clipping through the wall.

I get that there is more content, more enemy variety and more weapons and more perks. On release I felt it just needed more time but right now it really seems like they don't know what to do. They release new content sure but nothing works, the game feels worse to play. Why remove ammo drops and make weapons worse AND buff enemies? Why add new enemies but all of them are just frustrating and not fun? Sure, new content but is it fun and well designed? No.

review:
I’m going to be completely honest: this game can be great—amazing, even—but certain decisions and the lack of important bug fixes made the original release frustrating at times.

The core gameplay had potential. I loved the original five missions: they were fun, thrilling, and exciting. But they got old quickly, especially since the content pool felt thin. On top of that, the bugs made things worse and discouraged long-term play.

I waited until this most recent update to give my thoughts, and unfortunately, what I’ve seen so far is even more disappointing. The new mission cycling system feels like a miss. Sure, it’s a twist, but not one the game really needed. The update also changed the corrupted items—arguably the original mechanic that made the game stand out. Instead of being a consistent part of the experience, they’re now locked to randomized missions. While I understand the intent (to encourage players to try different missions for rewards), the scattered placement makes progression unreliable. Players can’t be sure whether they’ll get the resources they need to level up.

This game still has massive potential, and I don’t want to give up on it yet. But the direction it’s heading is worrying. The lack of content, frequent bugs and crashes, and questionable update decisions make it harder and harder for players to stick with it. If the developers don’t address these issues soon, they risk burying the game before it ever gets the chance to shine.

I genuinely hope they can turn things around, because there is still so much here worth building on.

For now It's not recommended, but I really hope to change this in the future if the devs turn things around.

review:
[h1]I really wish I could recommend this game but at it's current state I just can't.[/h1]
I want to preface this by saying these are just my personal bad experiences and gripes with the game, I hope to come back to this review and edit it down the road and hopefully be able to recommend it! 

[h3]Starting with the negatives[/h3]
Me and my friends were so excited for firebreak we immediately purchased it as it came out. At first the content seemed plenty for a new live service game and we could look passed the bugs as they weren't game breakingly bad and more of a challenge if anything. 
Now 3 months from launch the bugs seem to have gotten a little out of hand and are frustrating us more than giving us joy. One day we can play and have the best of fun and then the next we can't even complete 2 jobs because the game refuses to let us revive, making us restart the game only for then the status effects to not be showing on your screen or healthbar and so you just die out of nowhere. Another one of my gripes has been the lack of content in 3 months, for a live service game this just feels too slow and i really hope to possibly see a build up to new content in the future. In game events would be really cool or even just new cosmetics for the inbetween periods like now, and id really love to see maybe a 'lore' tab with some of the files we collect in the oldest house the loading screens move way too fast to be able to read anything on them.

[h3]Now for the positives[/h3]
I really really love the witty voice lines between characters. Hank and jerry are so interesting to me and its been fun just puzzling their stories together from the few lines we get in the lobby menu. The game play loops are fun and challenging and I really love the different area's we get to revisit from control in a different way. Trying to come up with new perk sets for our individual play styles and strategise with different weapons feels really good. There's a lot of goofy funny things that can happen especially playing with the right group of friends when the game works it can be a lot of fun!

[h3]Conclusion[/h3]
[b]Safe to say that firebreak sadly can't compete with other live service games at it's current state. However, I still won't give up hope and am looking forward to future updates! Please don't give up on this game it still holds so much potential it just needs that polish to make it shine.[/b]

Extremely fun game, given that the circumstances align. This may not be the live service block buster they wanted it to be but it is extremely entertaining.  It works with some hitches/jittering/frame drops on Linux.

I hope Remedy continues to add the critical features the game desperately needs and adds much more missions (community mission creator and community missions added to the pool after vetting maybe?). I also hope that they look to this as something outside of a live service cash grab (seasons, battle passes, flagrant and rainbow vomit customization) and double down on making this experience a universe enrichment initiative, setting up/teasing some Control 2 plot elements and adhering to the original game's tone and visual art style.

review:
I bought FBC: Firebreak with genuine excitement. As someone from Iran, I face constant regional restrictions, but I was thrilled to finally support a game I believed in—especially one from Remedy, a studio I’ve admired for years.

Unfortunately, the game refuses to work. I’ve been hit with endless errors: 22008, 11011, 11006. No matter what I try, it just won’t connect. And I’m not alone—many players in restricted regions are locked out due to the game’s heavy-handed DRM and unreliable peer-to-peer matchmaking.

I’m a huge horde shooter fan. I’ve played Helldivers 2, Left 4 Dead 2, Warhammer: Vermintide, and countless others. Firebreak had the potential to stand proudly among them. But without LAN support or offline options, it’s inaccessible to people like me who genuinely want to play and support it.

If this game simply worked, I know many more players—especially in underserved regions—would buy it. But the current system is broken. Remedy, please reconsider your approach. Firebreak deserves better than to die under the weight of its own DRM.

God.  I had such high hopes for this game.
I liked the original version pre-Breakout.... every mission felt curated.  There wasn't much content, but what was there felt so good to play.  This used to be a positive review.

What the game needed, however, was not limiting the unique game modifier (corruption) to random levels.  It was not more types of currency.  It definitely was not a hoard mode.

Pre-Breakout, I enjoyed making my own hoard mode by just fighting endless Hiss at the end of a level.


What this game needed was level variation.  Not "sometimes the shower is over there instead", *actual* level variation.  It's set in an endlessly shifting building, for crying out loud; it's the perfect setting for a procedurally generating environment.

I had high hopes, and I still do.  This game is so close to being so good.  But don't see the problem as a hole which needs to be deeper, see it as a hole which needs to be filled.

Why does this game insist on making me feel like a wimpy janitor? Also why is the group size 3 and not 4? What the hell were they thinking?

Then there are lots of quick-time or rhythm events where you have to quickly mash Q or E in a sequence and if you press the wrong button too often you get damaged, this can down you very quickly and is super annoying but also a core mechanic of every level. review:
TLDR: Game-breaking bugs, constant disconnects, clueless teammates (public matchmaking) and subpar optimisation (DLSS or FSR are a MUST to achieve comfortable FPS while the visuals are OK at best). I will update the review depending on future fixes, but for now the game is a hard pass.

Growing up with games like Max Payne, Alan Wake and later Control set my expectations of Remedy games pretty high. FBC: Firebreak is... the first Remedy product to disappoint.
Somehow, the game feels rushed: Devs pop out weekly patches trying to fix and balance, but all that should have been done prior to release.
1. Constant disconnects: I am unable to finish the first mission because the connection drops at any stage, with no possibility to rejoin the lobby. If the host gets frustrated and leaves, the mission is practically over, and players DO get frustrated fast, see my next point.
2. The game mechanics are not explained clearly: 90% of players in my lobby had no clue what to do with the Furnace (the very first mission). There is no voice or text chat, that means coordinating the effort is non-existent, so most of the players just run around like headless chickens until the heat incapacitates them. The intro video is a nice touch but a proper tutorial level would have been better.
3. Optimisation: the plague of modern games... DLSS and FSR were supposed to help lower end systems with modern titles, not be an "always-on-otherwise-25-fps" setting. Optimising games is still a must, slapping upscaling on a game and calling it a day is lazy, especially when the visuals are nothing to write home about.

I really hope that the game unfolds in the near future because it has the potential to be a true Remedy game. For now though, your money is better spent elsewhere.

All respect to Remedy as they've got a good team behind the art, but it really seems like nailing gameplay is just completely out of their reach with their current team, it feels as if they haven't made a game with tight gameplay since Max Payne 2.

The best I can say about this game is that it wasn't as bad as I expected it to be.

review:
This game is not worth $40 Yet. This game is Good and many people do not give it a fair shake, it has solid game-play and good balance. Just lacking some variety and stability.

Mission rewards are plentiful, it doesn't feel like playing you are 10 Soul crushing COD zombies matches for minimal progress. Depending on the difficulty you play the XP and Currency gain is at a rate that most who have a real job and most importantly a life can appreciate.

 Most compare this game to Left 4 Dead 2 witch is an genuinely unfair comparison to make for ANY coop horde shooter unless the game itself is trying to compare itself to Left 4 Dead *cough cough* [Back 4 Blood] 
There is no way a company of Remedy's class can come close to the RIDICULOUS amount of polish and detail that Left 4 Dead has, Left 4 Dead rests on a distant star in a far away Galaxy and we may never see anything like it for a long time. (Valve Time)

For a live-service Coop-horde shooter Firebreak is very Unique and does little to waste your time witch remedy should get a FAT F---ING GOLD STAR for not making a content limited game with a fully functioning in game slop shop were every bundle and item costs more than a medium pizza with a 24oz soft drink. A LIVE SERVICE game in 2025 that isn't there to milk your wallet, its crazy to think about.

This game isn't here to rob you, Remedy respects you. However as i am typing this it has Mixed reviews on steam and ill tell you why. 
First and this is a big one. FBC Firebreak lacks content, Currently there are 5 Unique "Jobs" with different challenges. However These "Jobs" are very linear and severely lack Veriety and Dynamic Gameplay. The maps are set in 3 stages. 
The Intro, Same as the intro stage but with added complexity and the "Boss" witch only one job has a boss the rest of the jobs just add a unique problem to solve.
 On top of that these maps are not procedurally generated witch is a HUGE missed opportunity for a setting that is known to shift when not "Stabilized". They are well constructed maps with Zero change in layout and objectives are always in the same places every time you play.
 This game can get stale FAST if you spend a lot of time playing games and try to be as efficient as possible.

Second This game lacks Serious Optimization, when you open up the game for the first time you should see a pop up window telling you where to start. None of the pop up windows work in this game it just shows up as a blur on your screen that you need to close. Games take a very long time to load with good Internet and beefy hardware and normal settings, often you will be looking at a black screen for several minutes at a time and on the very rare occasion you might get stuck in the level entry elevator. (Someone Removed the emergency call button from the elevator)

Lastly there is very little ability to communicate in a COOP shooter, there is a ping system and a Comms wheel with 4 Lines and only one line is useful. Firebreak is missing:  Voice chat, Text chat and worthwhile voicelines.

FBC Firebreak is not worth $40 in this state, it gets old fast and needs some kind of system to change up gameplay maybe add some more chaos by mixing enemy types. if you are not a fan of Remedy but like coop shooters Firebreak isn't ready for you. If you Love Remedy like i do and play maybe a few matches here and there its a well crafted game with a great foundation and is pretty fun and sometimes Just sometimes a little toxic. :)

review:
Oh man, Remedy, you should've let this cook. For a lot more.

So it's a class-based extraction shooter thing ala L4D and DRG. You go do objectives in the Oldest House to get the anomalies under control. Kill hiss and other stuff on the way. Collect random upgrade-related crap on the way. Get out when done.

Not exactly inspired or original to start with, and pretty ugly aesthetics on all the otherwise samey characters. But maybe if the gameplay is solid, it'll be a fun change of pace from DRG especially for the Remedyverse fans? Right?

Well... Let's see some glaring problems I've had with this in my hour of trying:

- When I first started the game, my screen started flashing on and off every 30 seconds or so. It kept doing this even after quitting the game (?!), and I had to reboot the computer to make it stop.
- No communication possible ingame, other than sprays and pings.
- You usually jump into a game that's already going on, and have to run around the samey levels trying to figure out how to get to the rest of your team.
- Nothing is really explained, other than a "press this button now"-forced tutorial when you first play the game. What do the kits do? What are all these status effects? Where is this damage coming from? Why am I randomly starting to burn? No idea; good luck figuring it out.
- People often ragequit in the middle of the game, because of the above confusion.
- If your host in the random pickup games this game throws you into ragequits or otherwise loses connection in the middle of the game, everyone gets kicked out for no reward at all. So you just wasted 10-20 minutes.

Maybe once some of the above is fixed, I might give this another shot, just because I really want Remedy to succeed here, but it's not looking good.

review:
UPDATE: My last three attempts at playing this “game” resulted in the first two culminating in a connection failures and uninstalling/reinstalling the software. The third attempt (tonight) caused me to force shutdown through holding the power button—I couldn’t even open Task Manager. Steam refuses to refund my money.

Keep playing Helldivers, buy Nightreign—even the Gex Trilogy apparently runs better than this freaking piece of content that should have been a free-for-all content boost to Control.

I'm mad. I'm mad that after the last patch, I spent an hour trying to troubleshoot why I couldn't load into a single job.

But that's the surface. I'm mad that this game has so much potential. I'm mad that at this point, despite two thirds of the systems that this game released on having an immediate day one pool of players who got it for free, I can't get a full team for a Level 3 (i.e. COMPLETE LEVEL RUN) mission. I'm mad that so many people will decry "Too little, too late." when Remedy tries to rectify the situation. I'm mad that we're given an infinite sandbox to play in (The Oldest House) and we're stuck doing the same five chores for all eternity. I'm mad that I paid full price for this game, and this game feels like something that came out during the Xbox 360/Playstation 3 era.

review:
I'll be frank. I saw this and thought "L4D in the Control universe? Hell yea!" Control is easily my favorite store-based game in the last decade.

This game... Does not play like L4D, nor Control. It plays a little more like Visceral Cleanup Detail with poor direction. I spent 40 minutes filling barrels and doing furnace maintenance. I spent another 30 with a broom sweeping up post-it notes. And then another 30 trying to get rid of some pests in the basement. Even when I was shooting and being shot at, it felt tedium, until a horde of 40+ enemies spawned and then I felt helpless, until I realized I could cheese it with the water gun.

The interact and fix-it mechanics are cool. I like the ideas for the classes (though the water one seems to be leagues above the others). I just... Can't help but feel that whatever it is they were going for here, they missed the mark. I played for 2 hours and felt like I was doing chores but getting nothing done. I quite two zones into the third mission.

____________________________________________________
EDIT: Alright.... I've put another 6 hours into this game. I've had a few realizations:

First off, it's more fun once you realize what it's asking of you. The new player introduction is harsh, there's goals and objectives given but how you make those happen is sorta missing. Once you've played through a mission once, it's a lot more fun. The first time is the worst. 

This, however, highlights the bigger issue: *There is no content.* I did 2 and a half missions at Clearance 3, thinking that this was the lowest tier. It was not, it was the longest tier. So.... I have now done all 5 missions (total!) avaialbe in-game. I have done them at the longest setting, and done them on the Hard difficulty. I have most all of the equipment unlocked. I am only 8 hours into the game total.

My review still has to say "Do not recommend". The game needs at least 2x the number of separate missions, and then each of these missions has to be like twice as long before I can recommend this.  Again, great concept, great setting... But the execution is still lacking.

ALSO: There's no chat of any type. No text, no voice. I've watched so many people run past the water foundations, their health bar so low it doesn't render, and I can't tell them what to do with the stupid water fountain, the ping doesn't highlight it... The new player experience is made worse by lack of ANY type of communication in game.

Wishing I could give a ''mixed''. I like the game but there's 2 major issues right now.

1.  Poorly optimized and prone to crashes. The game looks as good as Control with none of the destruction physics. You'd think it would make for a more stable experience but no. It crashes very often at the default graphics setting and occasionnaly at the lowest. It's probably because of the amount of particle effects there can be at once. This is very frustrating and kills any entheusisms of playing. The biggest offender is the level Paper Chase, which filled with these post-its that you must destroy and have particles when destroyed.

2. A lack of onboarding and tutorializing. The game is very clear about what you have to do to win, but a lot of important mechanics are not explained or, if they are, in missable popups on the side of the screen. Things like how to neutralize anomalies, the lives system, how to get specific progression materials to spawn and how to utilize your tool to it's full extent. It's good in some ways that the game just lets you have fun right away but these things I mentioned are critical to your survival and overall progression.

Minor issues now: Gun sounds are not as punchy or good as they should be. This is not a game that relies on sound cues so it feels like a downgrade from Control, which had amazing gun sounds from... well, The Gun.

Paper Chase is by far the worst level and I wish they'd rework it. Shooting and meleeing post-its is not the height of fun. it gets better once you hit the 2nd and 3rd part, it's just the first part with it's ridiculous quota at higher levels.

Some positives before the end: It's still Control so still got that great writing and sense of humour. I like the mechanics and the coop works. There's great potential here.

review:
FBC: Firebreak – A Deeply Disappointing Experience

Firebreak is, quite frankly, one of the most boring game I’ve played this year. 
Despite its potential, it ends up being an lifeless CO-OP shooter. 
Here’s a list of some issues I had with it:

- Gunplay is uninspired. In fact, I’d argue that Redfall delivered slightly more engaging combat than this. Weapon variety is virtually non-existent. There are roughly six guns and three grenades. You start with weaker versions and can eventually buy upgraded ones, but none of them feel satisfying to use.

- Poor status effect feedback. I died repeatedly to fire damage without realizing I was even burning—there’s minimal to no visual feedback to indicate you’re affected. Or, at least, I could not notice it

- Classes feel meaningless. Each class only has a unique weapon and two perks tied to it. That’s the only distinction. While some classes might perform certain tasks more efficiently, every role can essentially be filled by any class. To make matters worse, there are only three classes available, which is just not enough for a game like this.

- Class progression is poorly designed. Locking class perks behind game completion is (subjectively) questionable choice, but the implementation makes it worse. Upgrades are divided into four tiers, unlocked by spending enough currency in each. This forces you to buy perks you don’t want just to access the ones you do. A class-specific skill tree based on progression would’ve made far more sense.

- Lack of enemy variety. Most enemies are lifted straight from Control, which I could accept if there were more unique designs tailored for this game. Minibosses are just regular enemies with inflated health pools. Compared to what we have in games like  Vermintide 2, L4D2 - it’s a joke.

- Grind-heavy and badly balanced economy. All major unlocks—bonuses, class skills, and weapons—share the same currency pool, which adds unnecessary grind. Why can't we have separate progression for each stuff. One currency for weapons and skins, one for bonuses and last one for class perks?

- No tutorial whatsoever. While the gameplay isn’t complex, I’d still expect at least a basic onboarding experience for a game of this scope.

- Lazy use of QTEs. Nearly every mechanic—ammo refills, generator repairs, and more—relies on QTEs. There’s no creativity here; different tasks should have had unique interactions.

- Missions are tedious and repetitive. There are only five core missions, each with three levels. But instead of offering new challenges, each level just adds more objectives—often the same ones repeated (like cleaning sticky notes twice). Mission design lacks logic or creativity, and each takes just 10–20 minutes to complete. Worse yet, there’s zero incentive to replay them because the gameplay loop simply isn’t fun.

Unless you’re a die-hard Remedy fan, desperate for a new COOP shooter or game is on sale for 10$, I’d recommend skipping Firebreak. For $40, you can find far better experiences in games like Nightreign, Darktide, Vermintide, L4D2, or Outlast Trials. Firebreak lacks variety, polish, and—most importantly—fun.

fun but needs weapon variety and ur fkin crazy for releasing a co-op pve teamwork class-based game with no TEXT or VOICE chat. add dat shit and its a positive from me.

After playing dis game is awesome, and fun. Its chaotic and is definitely one of the best co-op games I've played in a minute. [strike]The missions and enemy variety are good and the challenge is fun but not too overwhelming (medium and hard I've with no comms with a random). [/strike] The difficulty is nonexistent after playing on terminal; even with the brain dead enemy spawns crowding people on top of us. 

The only thing holding is back right now is the either the servers or hit-reg. I don't know the technical terms but the feedback on enemies is awful; shooting into a crowd hits a single enemies who does an awful delayed stagger; projectiles leave your gun almost 10 seconds after which desyncs with what enemies you've might hit and with what you're visually seeing. It's very akin to back 4 blood and its not only really ruining the intensity and immersion from me but also making it hard to tell whats going on. During the game your flooded with screen effects, literal mobs of enemies, a hud system which can really clutter the screen sometime (it looks cool at least); which results in you not being able to tell who you've shot, if you shot them (which you might've but good luck telling who the hitmarker was on); and if they're dead. In a pve game this is so noticeable because all you're doing is shooting these guys. Though I do wanna acknowledge that the clutter and chaos was definitely intentionally done and I enjoy the chaos of whats going on and it keeps you on your toes and the blood pumping (almost as good as vermintide);  but this excitement is different from the annoyance cause poor hit reg and enemy feedback. If I was on a longer run or a higher difficulty this would become a pretty big frustration. 

The other thing affecting the intensity is that the ai is so lackluster; I mean you'll be standing right behind the strong hiss (juggernaut ish enemies) or the boss hiss and you'll just slam headshots and farm them until they finally notice you. This also splits up the mob of melee hiss and leads to them flowing really oddly and it looks very unnatural and uncoordinated which really makes the game MUCH easier (horde shooter but the enemies don't horde). Even when the ai does work and you have a group of guys running at you; as long as you're sprinting or just moving they can't hit you. The ranged hiss also don't play any cover or position at all they just stand out in the open sometimes just walking straight towards (while missing most of their shots). With the ai being so detrimental to the difficulty of the game you don't even really need to play with your team (which defeats the gimmick of shields being strong when you're grouped; which is a cool feature). It would be cool to see the hiss security guards act like they're using their pre-corruption training while being commanded by the hiss hive mind or whatever; I don't remember the lore too much. Considering they use and wear what they had before they became hiss it wouldn't be to big of a sretch. Gameplay wise it would help immerse me and put more thought into the game if the enemy horde worked in tandem. Maybe using the strong hiss (guy with a literal bomb squad outfit and a minigun) as cover or letting him lead the way; even just pointing out the player when they spot them. This is just at best missed: potential; at worst: a huge oversight. Hopefully they add onto the ai but its a far cry when the game is already released.

While I might being doing a lot of complaining the only actual negatives of this game is the price; $40 for a game that rips enemies and many assets from another game is pretty crazy especially when this game is missing key mechanics (VOICE CHAT IN A NECESSITY IN A CO-OP GAME PERIOD)... Consider that a lot of strong hiss (enemies with boss health bars) are just standard enemies with more health; they use the same exact model which to the top it off every enemy type has only one model JESUS christ. As of now this game is NOT worth your money.

So like... I think it's a polished product for what it has.  It's just that what it has is lacking.  Obviously the devs played darktide and helldivers 2, among other horde shooters, but I don't think they understood what keeps people coming back to them.  I know people are complaining about "5 maps", but that's not really the issue. 

In no particular order, the main issues with the game:

2-No theory crafting on your build, you can pick a weapon and some perks, that's it.
3-The perks are uninspired and aren't going to change the way you play.
4-The unlockables are all very samey at the moment, that's understandable, but also not very exciting.
5-You don't get choices for skills, and some of the skills SUCK.  Like the turret for the fixer is awful.

There is no such thing in this game, and if they could change that, it would be a fantastic big fat first step to making this a much better game.

review:
FBC: Firebreak is a first person team based style co op shooter that focuses on three players that take on the role of containment in the "Control" universe. These teams focus on the weird and strange types of creatures and enemies that are controlled by the extra dimensional enemy Hiss. 

The Good

Much of what this game does well really relies on the co op aspect and how you work with your team mates and or solo. Levels are simple enough, three parts one per each level and as you beat one part it unlocks the next until you've done all three. Character option and customization and simple and straightforward and the list of abilities is decently expansive and overall from what I've unlocked are neat and helpful to my style of game play. Graphically the game is visually quite nice to look at and run pretty smooth on high settings. 

The Bad

Were to start really, this games just lacks so much of what I thought Remedy would do and give us. Everything about this game can be summed up in 2 to 3 hours of game play leaving you wondering if your missing something you should have gotten from the start. Lack of characters, different levels, customization, any real understanding of how this all ties into the Control Universe and the feeling of is this a beta or a whole game. To me this game had all the potential in the world to be like  other titles in the same genre but it misses the mark on so many levels. Bugs and glitches were rampant and on some levels people were just disconnected or never even able to join. I hope that Remedy realizes that even though this is their first attempt at a different style of game that players want to be able to fell like they get their money's worth and sadly this is not it right now.

Overall Thoughts And Score 

Really wanted to enjoy this game and put a ton of hours into it but right now it's not even close to being there and for 40$ I can't say I would recommend this. Down the road with updates, content and a price reduction I feel this game could be worthwhile. Even playing with friends I feel that this game can only keep many contempt for a couple hours and then your just like well what else it there. My hopes of this game being good are still there and I feel like in the long run they will bring it to it's glory. 

Score 5/10

Also, if Fire is meant to be a common thing we put out, add more ways to put it out, I get the game is a team effort but with random players with bad matchmaking, we ended up dying more to the Environment's fire effect than enemies cause the shower was at the opposite side of the map.

There's also only 5 missions, each taking 20 minutes tops. I usually gauge a game to be worth £1 equalling an hour of gameplay. This game is £33, and at the rate the first mission was going, it would only be worth £5 tops due to the bad matchmaking, and that's if I'm counting matchmaking to be gameplay. Even taking into account the Corrupted missions, that's still only £10 at most.

As much as I loved Control, I'd recommend waiting to get this game until a few patch notes and more content. The Matchmaking needs a massive overhaul, and you need to disable the host being the reason the game ends, one match I managed to get into, we got all the way to the end, just for the host to disband the party, which is a massive pain.

review:
As someone who has 800 hours in DRG, 600 in payday 2, 250 in Helldivers, and 122 in L4D2 I have a strong love for the PVE horde shooter genre and was interested in the trailers I saw for FBC FIREBREAK, keep in mind this is coming from the Perspective who never played control or Remedy's projects or heard good things about them.

After 11 hours, while I did enjoy it there have been some major caveats that prevents me from actively recommending this game. I will start off with some positives though

1. Love the idea, having an team of First Respondents that consist of volunteers fighting abnormalities and other extra dimensional shenanigans for the Federal Bureau of Control is just a great idea, and it a great premise for a game

2. The limited weaponry, while this is a contentious point and a lot of people here complain about only 6 weapons, as someone who came from Payday I much rather prefer a small range of weapons that differ from each other quite a bit rather than 300 weapons with 270 weapons being useless or inferior to something else.

3. The Perk System, for it just starting out I will say there is quite a solid system here, with a lot of build customization to tailor to your weapon, build, and mission as well with having up to 9 perk slots, it can make for a lot of personal choice in what you want.

4. The mission concepts and abnormalities are great, having to fix an immensely hot blasting furnace. self reproducing mass of sticky notes, globules sticking to engine to power the facility, the mission concepts or unique. And the abnormalities that in each area will negatively effect the mission is cool and can make for an interesting challenge

Now unfortunately I have to get into quite a bit of the negatives this game has

1. EDIT: They have since changed progression and put all weapons and toolkit upgrades into it's own separate page, making this original point mute. Good change!

2. The early experience it just kinda sucks, cause of that pass system and that you start with just clearance one missions, what your experiences is that missions barely last 8 minutes, the game fails to clearly tell you what to do at times, since the missions you DO have available only have 2 shelters and just 1 threatening enemy you barely get the points needed to upgrade the pass and I can see why it gave the idea that progression in this game is immensely slow. Progression is significantly improves once you reach clearance 3 with corruption 3 as with 6 shelters, and 4 threatening enemy spawns, I was able to gain 70 slips in just one mission of that length.

3. The Missions are unfortunately very short. As mentioned when doing clearance 1 missions they at most last 8 minutes, and if you know what you are doing they are even SHORTER, Hot Fix and Frequency Shift are especially egregious as they can take what feels like only 3 minutes to finish once you know what to do, fast enough that not even 1 threatening enemy spawns. While this is partially fixed by Clearance 3, it still feels like you are going through them way too quickly

4. The abnormalities just don't do anything at times mainly cause when playing decently they get destroyed before having any lasting effect. Due to there being a shelter in every area you can always go there to grab the black rock gun to destroy it, due to the length of running towards the shelter the first Abnormality lasts the longest. However the blackrock gun has more significantly more ammo needed to destroy an abnormality, so you can carry it to the next section and if the next one is just right there you can destroy it before it can even do anything, even if it isn't directly in your path just having the blackrock gun in hand before entering a new area makes the time to take them out significantly shorter, further impacted in that more than 1 blackrock gun can spawn. The only abnormality that avoids this is the Table Saw due to how disruptive having no shields is when facing that first wave of hiss in a new area. Overall abnormalities just don't survive long enough to have an impact in a mission and when they do survive sometimes it isn't all that noticeable for some.

5. Now this is probably the biggest issue this game has, the lack of variety, which is the biggest killer here. There have been a lot of complains in the reviews of lack of content but I think it's really just a lack of variety. I will break this into 2 segments over going the mission variety and enemy variety

5a. This is the smaller issue of lack of variety as enemy variety makes for a more fun game, but as it stands it's still disappointing once you clear a clearance 3 your have essentially figured it all out, it would be nice to have some layout change so that you have some variety in approach instead of just taking the same path or route as you always do, even something as simple as switching around where the junction boxes are for lights would be great cause as it stands from my experience there is always one junction box in each room which will always be in the same spot. Would be nice to have to actually search a few potential spawns instead of just going directly to the box to fix it.

5b. The enemy variety is unfortunately lacking. Mainly for a lot of these while there is some priority it doesn't fell all that impactful. A lot of his just feel like something you can dump bullets and the bigger enemies don't feel that threatening for you to target them. The only 2 threats in this game is the Hiss Charged as their self detonation deals a significant amount of damage and the Hiss Distorted as their invisibility and massive close range aoe damage that you need to kill them, but with any focused fire or just the rifle they can very quickly be killed. In this game we have cannon fodder (melee, ranged, and flying ranged), the trooper, big guys with a weakspot on their back, the hiss distorted, hiss charged, and the paper enemies only on clearance 2 of paper chase. That's only 7 different enemy types. Keep in mind L4D2 amongst the uncommon infected has 8 special infected that are all high priority or at least disrupt your pace, Payday 2 has 6 types of special enemies where multiple are either a high priority for you to kill as fast as possible or if you don't have the tools you have to avoid at the best of your abilities, and DRG has a spawn pool of 16 enemies and this doesn't even include biome specific, random spawn chance enemies, passive mobs, or  ALL THE RIVALS. The lack of enemy variety that change the flow of the mission and how to approach any engagement is easily the biggest flaw of this game and what makes it feel really repetitive.

5b. Edit, as of patch 1.2 they did slightly address this, mainly in increasing enemy health so that enemies don't immediately die, and that the powerful enemies and just larger enemies survive for longer and can cause more nuisance. It's a good chance but would like some units that are more common in other PVE horde shooters like units the immobilize or separate you from your team if not careful like the Smoker from L4D2, Mactera Grabber in DRG, or Trapper in Darktide. Or a an actually serious long range threat like a sniper. Just more unique enemies would greatly improve the combat gameplay

I REALLY want to like this game, and want to have a lot of fun with it with friends, but there's just some massive glaring issues with it that prevent me from recommending this game. That said there will be a fall update with a new mission type and weapons, and what I am hoping is that we get new enemies that actually affect how you approach a combat scenario or just more threats, or more randomization in the missions, something that makes it feel like I already faced all the encounters and scenarios this game has to offer in just 11 hours
