I think they could have put in a sliver of a story line and that alone would have made it feel connected to the expanded universe but it is unable to stand alone as is. 

I hope this doesn't discourage the developers or publisher from implementing multiplayer into their better games but firebreak in all feels like an unfinished DLC or akin to Resident evil's mercenary mode but separate for some reason.

Like guys. What did you expect here, really?

Look. The only reason I'm writing a negative review is simple:
You know how every fucking game company nowadays just puts out a game that has some performance hitches, has a noticable lack of QoL or some other features that really SHOULD have been there when the game released and has you thinking "Surely they should have just delayed this a few months to fix that up?"

People say guns lack feedback. I understand what they mean. There's a lack of "Punch" when you *hit* an enemy. The gun sounds are fine. But there's a lack of audio feedback on connect. 
Some enemies just. Kinda straight up hit you through walls. Constantly. 
The gun guys never stop yelling in pain.
Teammate's guns just. Don't make sounds. At all.
A lot of elemental effects and what they do isn't well communicated.
The big Hiss... thing that wields a big pipe and melees you is entirely made redundant with simple circle strafing. Half of the time it animation cancels out of staggers to hit you.
Seriously. How do teammate's guns not make sounds?
Sometimes you get stuck on terrain and just... slide around and move really slow. And there's no real rhyme or reason to why this happens.
FOr a game about the Oldest House, I don't really feel like I'm exploring a place like the oldest house.
This game lacks the same kind of sauce and presentation CONTROL did, I feel. You still get those big texts on the screen, "FREEZER DUTY", and that's cool. But something about it *feels* sauceless. 

Why does every big name studio at this point feel the NEED to put out "Live Services" too early with too little polish, knowing full well the initial impressions are going to be bad, in an industry where first impressions matter?
Maybe they'll address this. Soon. Maybe they won't. Maybe they'll do the thing where they fix some things and update it and break 8 more things and fix 4 things and break 8 more things and make the game run worse and then "Balance" the game in a way that dumbs it d- oh wait I'm describing helldivers there.
Look. It's a trend. And it doesn't make me hopeful about this game's future.
The part that bothers me the most, it's... it's not even that bad. The gameplay is fine. Bugs aside, it's... perfectly *okay.* Like. "Mid", as they say. "Mid" isn't even... bad. It's just, you know, mid. Mediocre. Alright. Fine.

UPDATE: The review says no *for now.* And it's largely because this game is still missing some very noticable polish. The sound mixing is still terrible, I had to rejoin a match because being revived while Pink Goo'd makes the good stay on you and visibly block your view, making it damn near impossible to play normally. Upon doign this, almost all sounds were muted but the music was pretty clear. From what I could hear of the music, yeah I liked it, but not being able to hear gun or enemy sounds or any feedback is... Not good.
They added melee damage to the wrench. Good!
They made collectable items that give you money to spend more visible, and they now make sounds! Good!
All the kits do feel useful, at least. Though the Swivel Turret is still horrid. It misses like 80% of the time, but if it hits it CAN clear crowds.
All of the parautilities are fun and pretty strong. No other game has let me say something goofy like "I AM READYING THE GNOME." with such serious weight behind it.

review:
I bought this mainly because I'm a big time supporter of Remedy. I even put down an extra 10 on the deluxe edition (which by the way, does not *give* you extra cosmetics. It unlocks them in the store for you to buy by grinding out in game currency)

Honestly, I really wanted to like it, but I don't. It was advertised as a game for casuals that you could drop in for a couple hours at a time and have some fun, butt he truth is it's a hardcore grindfest. All the kits tools you have to buy. The guns are extremely substandard in power until you put hours upon hours grinding currency to upgrade. [strike]The store is designed in a way that you have to buy multiple cosmetic items you won't ever use, like sprays, before you can open the next pages to buy real gear.[/strike] (Patch 1.2 removed forcing buying cosmetics but increased the price of guns so you still have to grind lol). Every kit needs you grind levels to unlock perk slots.

And then on top of that the levels are, 1. short. Clearance levels 1 and 2 (which you have to play to get to 3 where the Corruption modifiers eventually are) are 5-10 minutes long. Clearance level 3 might be 15-20. 2, there are only 5 of them, and you will be playing them over and over and over. There aren't campaigns like Left 4 Dead, you are just grinding out the same five 15-20 minute levels.

And *then* the gameplay itself isn't even that fun. Each level is [collect 10 of these items], or [do a repetitive button mash minigame on these 12 objects], and [destroy 20,000!!! of these sticky notes] and then you open a door to the next area, and it asks you to do even more! It's all so tedious. And like mentioned earlier the guns are crap and do very little until you grind out hours to tier 3. And even after that most of the guns aren't very good unless you are working with your own team who is all kitted out properly. And speaking of which, this is a co-op game with no voice chat! You can't coordinate with your team unless you're all on a discord call or something. The ping is pretty useless! There are no tutorials for anything, even for telling you what all is on your UI! I had to read the Remedy discord just to figure out the two bars on the top middle of your screen are your shield and stamina.

tl;dr I would say this game is worth at most $30, but by the time it goes on sale I'm guessing the playerbase will be 5 diehards and no one else. So just skip it.

I hate to give a bad review but I’m honestly disappointed with Remedy this time around. FBC Firebreak feels like a misstep from a studio that usually delivers great games. 

The gameplay loop is repetitive and quickly becomes tedious. It feels like a chore, lacking variety or any real sense of progression.

There are a few positives. The Control universe is still a fascinating setting, even if it’s turned into a caricature this time. And as expected, the art direction is still very strong.

review:
[h1]< We are Disappointed/Displeased but there is still Potential/Hope/Coping >[/h1]

I wasn't sure what to expect after seeing the game launch into Very Negative as its review score before climbing up to 60%+ Mixed but what I got was... pretty underwhelming. Obviously, everyone and their grandma at this point knows that there's an extreme lack of content despite the foundation they've set for the gameplay loop and setting. I considered that as long as the core gameplay is fun, it wouldn't matter too much (I have 250+ hours on The Outlast Trials) but it's basically just Darktide with [i]really[/i] shitty combat and even more repetitive and boring objective types.

My playtime isn't as high as I would've liked it to be before I made this review but the game can be an EXTREME slog to try and progress in if you don't have a premade. Similar to Elden Ring: Nightreign, for whatever reason Remedy decided to make a co-op focused game without any way of communicating to other players with the exception of rudimentary pinging (although you can ping enemies so +1 over Nightreign at least) or 4 character voice lines which are more to spam this games equivalent to "Rock and Stone!" than to communicate teamplay. I haven't been able to successfully matchmake into anything past clearance 3 hard's so most of my thoughts and experiences will be from there.

[h1]< It was not this difficult for the Director/Writer/Detective >[/h1]

It is kind of insane [i]how bad[/i] the guns feel to use in this compared to any other Remedy release. All 5 of your weapon choices handle like complete ass and you might have to grind a good couple of longer missions out to get through your warbond far enough to upgrade them but when you unlock the pump shotgun every other gun except the machine gun becomes obsolete anyway.

 I get that you're John Expendable in a hazmat suit but shooting enemies just feels [i]off.[/i] Obviously you don't get any cool abilities or gimmicks either, you have a water gun that saves you from the deadliest threat in the entire game (burn DoT) or a wrench that might as well squeak whenever you hit an enemy because you're supposed to use it to speed up like 3 things and the entirety of Hot Fix and that's it. Jump Kit is fine i guess idk your shock gun pairs with the other 2 kits (electrocuting wet enemies or powering up the wrench so it actually does damage) and the movement tech is fun even though it has no real point on most maps.

[h1]< Your Task/Objective at hand >[/h1]

You go in, do a basic task and then get back in the elevator. In and out, 5 minute adventure. Where the game gets any replay value is that completing these short-ass levels lets you do it again but now you get to go deeper and do the exact same objective again but in a different area and [i]then[/i] leave. Then, you can do it a third time where you go even deeper and you get an actual different, climatic objective as the finale before you have to sprint back to the exit. The second part to this is that on higher difficulties, progressing to the next zone will usually spawn a Powerful Enemy (one of the enemy types that isn't a common goon but slightly spongier) and an Altered Item.

If you really like Remedy's worldbuilding and lore and that type of shit then this is the only time you're going to see any of it (even though I love Hank and Jerry, this is not anywhere close to comparable to Control or AW 1+2) and from a gameplay standpoint, they add a "modifier" to the mission for as long as they're "active" and you need to find a special gun to destroy them. There is never a reason to not destroy them as they will NEVER affect the Hiss negatively, only debuffs to the players (tankier enemies, enemies explode on death, you no longer have a shield, etc) and this is (imo) a huge waste of what could've been a cool mechanic.

[h1]< It's time to Wrap Up/Complete this Presentation/Review/Lightning Round >[/h1]

A few things I wanted to note without each one having it's own paragraph;

The game is inconsistent on if it wants to hide info like objective markers, altered item markers, etc. which is fine if that's how they want the game to be designed but you can do things like hide neutralizers from the rest of your team which leads into the next point.

There's weirdly high friendly fire damage across all difficulties that I do not see the point of existing. I can understand Frequency Shift requiring you to be mindful of blowing up your team but you can just freely nuke or shoot teammates down with zero penalty. Only the arbitrarily assigned "host" can kick players and, yes, that means you can kick people at the end. 

If Remedy pushes out some patches sooner than later then the gameplay is at least salvageable but even then it's going to be a struggle to ever say this game is worth $40.

EDIT: v1.2 made a few things better like starting at clearance 3 for Hot Fix and splitting the warbond so that you don't have to burn medals on cosmetics to unlock the later upgrade pages, the wrench actually does damage regardless of upgrade/buffs from a Jump Kit player and samples/medals being easier to see is nice but introduced it's own bugs like the effect staying even when they've been picked up. I'm really happy to see Remedy is working on improvements though. unless like 90% of my review is made obsolete i'm not rewriting it tho cause i'm lazy lol

Additionally, with 19-ish hours on record I've obtained all achievements, all warbond items and hit the level/rank cap of 49. The only thing new I could unlock is perks I would never run or just run CL3 Extreme's for "the fun of it" but Extreme does not seem to be any different from Hard and anything that can kill your run would kill it on Hard (table saw zone 1, host dies, proceeds to rage quit and close the mission) and every single run usually goes the exact same.

review:
I have played co-op games, including co-op shooters for a total of 6,000 hours. Mass Effect 3, DRG, Sanctum 2, Gears 5, Warframe, Payday 2, and so on. My most recently played game, other than Firebreak, is Nightreign.
Over the course of playing such titles, I have naturally built high standards when it comes to co-op experience. 

From my point of view, this game is, without a doubt in my mind, garbage.
For the record, I played Firebreak on Gamepass and got all classes to Level 7 (9 is max). I also cleared all content on max difficulty (Extreme Threat + 3 Corruption). 
It took me 8 hours to do so.

Combat feels dull, uninspiring, and directionless. Enemies are not specialized enough to force certain tactics, and feedback is missing in a lot of area.

Well-made co-op games design monsters in a way that forces players to bring specific gear in a loadout. Multiple players cover each others' weakness via specialized loadouts, and this is where cooperation occurs in a fight.
But in Firebreak, every enemy except the Sticky Note boss can be dealt by spamming your weapon fire. There are 6 weapons available, but ultimately they don't matter whichever one you choose. Enemy types are not designed with certain roles, strengths and vulnerabilities in mind. 

This is why you just end up shooting over and over, without thought and consideration. Teammates are there just to add more firepower.

The element system which governs status effects in this game, despite having a major influence in combat, is not explained well (thus underused).
You may combine class powers or perks to exploit a certain synergy (such as Electric on Wet enemies, or Fire on enemies made out of Paper).
This is the part where I think the developers attempted to add depth to the combat, and I can respect that to a certain degree.

However, as mentioned, the element system is not pronounced well in-game, and attempting to combo with a random teammate is either a hit or miss since they may not know what their class power is capable of. 
And I once tried to combine Electric attack with a teammate's Water attack, and while it was effective at crowd control, I realized that I was also constantly zapping everyone due to the large splashes on the floor, and friendly fire is always on in this game.

The idea is neat, but the execution feels clunky. So what ends up happening is players still mostly rely on guns to deal with threats, and the element system ends up only affecting players instead, acting as an obstacle as a result.

Furthermore, the game lacks tutorials, descriptions, and communication tools.
If a new Splasher player doesn't know that they can remove static effects with their Water gun, or a Jumper player does not understand how their Electro gun works, your team has to suffer from serious inefficiency.
This problem is deterioriated by the lack of text and voice chat (in a 2025 game). You cannot tell your teammates what they should be doing, and can only spam the rudimentary ping in a hope that they will finally understand.

Another issue stemming from the same root, is that there is no explanation for neutralizing Corruption items which can be devastating if left unchecked and stacked. Each item will generate a disadvantage to the player, but I had to look up online to figure out that normal weapon fire is useless (you need to fire a Black Rock shredder, which is a special weapon). 
Requiring a different solution is fine, but if there's only one way of dealing with the problem, then at least the game should be very clear about it.

Half of the objectives in this game are annoying to deal with.
There are radiated pearls that you must transport to the cart, but every second near them builds up Radiation and constantly damages you.
Repaired Fans will trap and kill whoever is inside the tunnel if the fixer cannot leave the area immediately. On top of that, the outer fan will rotate left and right a bit to prevent you from escaping.
Pink Goos have the potential to insta-kill you if you don't remove it in a timely manner.
These objectives feel like they exist to screw the players.

All weapon hits, whether you are dealing damage or taking one, lack feedback. This renders gunplay poor and unresponsive.
I often cannot tell if I'm sprinting or walking due to stamina exhaustion. Even the basic footstep for your character lacks a sound effect. 

The only thing that kept me playing was the Perk Unlock system that borrowed its formula from Call of Duty.
But after getting kicked out because I got killed by getting stuck in a fan tunnel (knowing that I should leave immediately but the outer fan constantly blocked my path), I concluded that this game is a waste of my time. I got riled up to the point where I went out of my way to buy this game on Steam again, and idle for 5 minutes just to leave this review.

I wish I could get my money spent in gamepass, but I know that would not happen.
Do yourselves a favor, and buy some ice cream. That will be money better spent.

tl;dr; Don't buy, game will die fast - and is not worth the price. Go buy DRG, HD2, Darktide, or anything else.

I wanted this game to succeed, but ambition meets reality, their capacity to delivery is really underwhelming. 

Let's address some points:
- No communication: a ping system, unless perfect (which is not) can replace text/voice chat. But there is none of the three. 

- Learning curve: because you can't communicate, you can't make people understand things, like that special weapons destroying the anomaly. and its infuriating to see 3 anomalys with peoples handling the cannon at... hiss while being slowed, w/ no shield and exploding corpse...
The game try to gives you some hint, but they are so fast you can't learn under pressure.

- UI: its pretty basic and every information is hidden somewhere (they have outdone themselves here). Who the F designed the ready button? fire that guy. 

- Matchmaking: it's the first time in my life I've seen something this bad, you can machmake with people that are not ready and won't be before long... you want to quit and restart matchmake? Why not rematch that same person. Unless you quickplay, you won't find someone.
Also they dropped a patch day one to give some proper error naming like "party disbanded" (I am PRETTY sure they masked some connectivity errors behind that - I was with 3 friends and had that error appear...)

- Connectivity issue: the number of disconnection from a game is unforgivable considering all the other point. That should be the only thing on point. 

- Difficulty: The only difficulty is playing with person that don't know the game mechanics... so replayability is pretty low

- Longevity: there is little to none procedural generation (yes spawn change... then what?) you play the same mission, grind few hours then you are maxed out.

- Kicked from a game result in no experience, no currency. And I've been kicked more in this game than any other game... (I wonder if it's not another connectivity issue hidden behind a fake message.)

- Price: HD2 dropped at the same pricing range. And the only problem was getting back on a game that crashed. They even implemented "getting in your own game once you got kicked". 

I wanted this game to shine, but it's below standard. It's sad, and following the roadmap, it was either a cash grab from remedy, or a bad team working on a pretty good concept. 
I buy most game and never call for reimbursment even if it's "meh" - I don't care for money. I would love to reimburse this one - it won't get better than that.

review:
Sadly find this difficult to recommend over most other horde shooters on the market currently, a huge shame considering how great of a studio Remedy are, but something about this spin-off release really misses the mark.

Weapon feel isn't great even for AA standards. The kits (classes) all feel underwhelming. Progression uses the same currency for both weapon and kit ability unlocks as well as perks which means you'll likely completely ignore perks, as the weapon and ability upgrades are far more beneficial. Furthermore, there are some simply baffling gameplay decisions present here that predecessors of the genre such as Darktide had already made and been strongly criticised for long before FBC's release; overshield and buffs being determined by your teammates proximity to you as the biggest problem here, which on paper encourages team-play however in practice inhibits efficiency and creativity.

All this being said I'm still having some fun with this one, but the fact of the matter is that for the asking price of £32.99 you can afford far more content filled and competent horde shooters (both at full price, but especially on sale) such as Deep Rock, L4D2, PD2, Helldivers and Vermintide, leaving it really hard to recommend this one over the aforementioned in its current state unless you're a diehard Remedy fan.

review:
Unfortunately the game has quite a few flaws that while fixable, don't justify buying it for the time being to me.

- The amount of content that seems to be there at the moment is quite limited, it's 6 maps with optional shorter versions of it that don't have the finale segment which is the best part of them. 

-Character upgrade unlocks overall are fairly uninteresting.

-there is a bunch of things requiring you to do a QTE, which is always the same, requiring you to press Q and E in the order it shows you. Except that's a lie, spamming Q and E mindlessly completes it just as well.

-The difficulty... so after like 3 maps I switched to the hardest difficulty and it was only a very minor challenge while doing maps for the first time, without having power increases from the various upgrades. This leads me to believe that it is going to get boring very fast.

-Audiodesign has been inconsistent, one of the weapons sounds like a pea shooter, the grenades are so silent you wouldn't know you threw one if it didn't knock enemies around. (Which btw, if you use the rifle or the pistol who oneshot trash mobs, have fun using a grenade that does like 50% trash mob hp so didn't affect time to kill at all unless you spam multiple)

Now it is possible that there are enough anomalies to fix the difficulty and the low seeming content, but tbh I rather refund the game than gamble the 2h time limit on something that based on what else the game showed me I highly doubt.


I do think the game has potential to be good after a bunch of extra content is added and some fixes, probably give it a few years and get it on discount.

review:
The game play of Left4Dead/Back4Blood with tasks like Deep Rock Galactic, warbond system from Helldivers 2, set in the world of Control/The RCU.

It really reminds me of Back4Blood because of the lack of content, and its insistence that the content is the core gameplay. It could really benefit from a season pass-like unlock structure like B4B/DRG believe it or not. After completing the 3 sub-levels of the 6 locations, you have really seen the entirety of the game. Each sub-level is just the same location opened up more each time. There is currently 1 boss, and its a cool boss, but it feels like there should be one to every location. There really isnt anything groundbreaking to unlock down the line, so interest tapers off quickly if youre not a completionist. After a short while, it feels like quickly running through objectives like im trying to pull off a COD Zombies easter egg, spamming LB and RB frantically between waves.

If you have 2 other friends who really like The RCU, and enjoy seeing the game through a few playthroughs, i could maybe see it worth the asking price, but $40 USD is a lot for what i would consider 6hrs of main content.

Im past the 2hr mark, so i cant refund, but would unfortunately, even as a huge RCU fan. im really holding out hope that there are some updates/DLC later that can make up for at least the lack of actual RCU lore. Maybe a Zombies-like survival mode. But in no way can i recommend buying at the moment

Early weapons are for the most part terrible and feel bad to use, the Resonant level perks are kinda buggy and some feel like they dont work right, Like the extra ammo cap works for people close enough to you but if they start wasting ammo pickups of any kind once you are out of range because the game doesnt recognize being too far for the buff.

There is very limited enemy variety aswell, aside of your regular mooks, melee and with guns there is like 2 special mobs along with 2 elites.

Lastly the game is way too easy, at one point we just picked the highest difficulty and rushed through each mission with ease despite being rather unorganized.

The maps have no random element to it, they are always the same, they could have utlized changing layouts since the FBC building has a thing going for it of its changing layout and mostly non-sensical layouts which has not been utilized here at all.

There is some good however. The Kits you can choose from are pretty neat, the tools you are given are mostly pretty useful espicially the Splash kit. The controls handle well aside of minor gripes in the movement i have.

TL:DR: I was kinda hyped for this but despite the long dev cycle the game has not much to show for with alot of problems needing immediate adressing. It gave me the weird feeling anything coming out on Gamepass on release day might be a red flag.

Barebones, poorly optimized, and missing that extra spark that makes these role-based co-op shooters work. There is fun to be had, but it demands an outrageous amount of your time considering how minimal the content offering is. Modifiers don't make up for the meager 5 missions, and frankly, it needs at least twice that many to avoid feeling repetitive and stale. This feels like the suits took Sam Lake aside after spending 10 years on Alan Wake 2 and told him to make some money by year's end.

review:
Bad game that can eventually be good, and i will change my review if they manage to fix the problems this game has.
I wont repeat what is already here but i will say my 2 cents.

The game wants you to stick together via the shield system which is good, however the game does not want you to team with friends as the party system is convoluted, and the game is designed around having 3 people in the game at once. In fact the game encourages quick play with randoms. This game NEEDS a communication system. You cannot communicate with your team in literally any way other than your characters auto callouts which tell you literally nothing. 
Are you on fire and dying? Character says "Damn!"
Are you being encased in sticky notes or goo? Character says "Damn!"
You cant say "I need water" if you are going to burn out, you just need to trust the random guy to do their job well or you suffer and die slowly. The only way to get someones attention is to friendly fire them, intentionally frustrating design for no reason.
Also the Jumper kit "Ultimate Ability" the gnome, is a buggy mess that sometimes works, and other times just sits on my kit and i can't use it at all until it suddenly comes out while Im shooting a different gun and it kills me. 
The missions themselves are fantastic too, but only at the higher levels of difficulty. There's no reason why the lower level missions only difference is the amount of rooms you get to go. Thats why everyone is saying the game has no content. A level 3 mission takes on average 30 or so minutes, its action packed! 
Remove the requirement to Unlock Levels 2 and 3 and or do away with the system entirely and make every mission max length and the only change is the difficulty. The corruption system is fine the way it is and honestly had me coming back.

review:
well, the new update is out. it seems like a lot of people really like it, which is great for the game, but unfortunately I'm not one of those guys. the complete overhaul of everything with no in-game explanation has been baffling. 

- the crisis board takes away the ability to play whatever mode you want to, and you're stuck playing whatever missions they give you, which includes mostly the exceptionally unfun mold ones. now we also don't get to choose if there'll be corrupted items in the round, nor do we get to retry the missions we wiped on.
- the mold mission(s) make no sense. cold is supposed to stop mold from happening, but there's nothing you can do to stop your firebreaker from eating the mold? even if they have full cold effect on? the game makes it sound like that's a choice you're going to make but it sure is not. the mold shooters cannot be stopped, just temporarily shut down, which sucks; there's mold enemies that will literally powerwalk their way through entire throngs of hiss and take 10000 damage and STILL manage to vomit mold on you, 
- the hiss but especially the mold enemies do so much damage that I've experienced multiple team wipes from opening a safe room, when that used to be a spawn that we could at least handle. 
- the massive jump in difficulty wasn't conveyed either, so my team and I blundered straight into the difficulty we'd played before and got trashed. moving a difficulty down didn't help much either.
- the drops are impossible to find now. bosses that used to drop a good amount of stuff now only drop ammo (which is impossible to see on the floor most of the time), and I've yet to see one of the fancy traces that's supposed to give you the fun cosmetics. 
- none of the guns feel particularly good anymore; before, I had unlocked the pistol purposely at it's highest damage level and with headshots I could reliably put down a fair amount of hiss, now it feels like I'm unloading 18 shots into these guys and they just sponge it all up. 
- somehow the PC loading is *worse*. I don't even get to see the loading screen pages anymore because the textures won't rasterize before the level is loaded. I start every mission seeing into the entire map/skybox/world for 5 seconds. despite my computer being as fast as my friends' xboxes & the only one actually hooked to an ethernet cable, I take like 30 - 60 more seconds to load into anything, making everyone else have to wait for me to play. 
- we're supposed to be able to have random events during missions, but I'm yet to actually see one?
- being forced to play the tutorial was fine, but when you're forced to play the tutorial for a game you already knew how to play that doesn't explain *any* of the new updates and then going into what feels like an entirely new game afterwards, it makes you wonder what the fuck the tutorial was even supposed to explain, especially since it didn't seem to explain the differences between the kits, what half the abilities can even do, and seemed to assume you'd always be fix kit?

idk, I've been in this game's corner since release & it feels like the reason the game was made is being entirely abandoned to cater to a wider audience, which isn't a *bad* thing, but definitely isn't the game I enjoyed & got my friends to play with me. I'm going to give it another round or two but as of right now everything in the new update feels bad, and I'm not inclined to return to it anytime soon if this is the direction they'll be taking for the rest of the updates.

review:
It's cool, but definitely not fully fleshed out and realized. The game could have really benefited from random level generation to increase replayability. The missions are always the same set pieces, which means players will get very familiar with the levels in time. Although I admit at this point I'm not sure how randomized objective locations are within these set pieces. So far they seem very much the same, with maybe some elements being placed differently, but not varied enough. But there are some fun ideas here, just wish the level structure was more varied each time.

Now the enemies in the game. There just isn't enough variety here either. Pretty lacking. I feel like only one mission has a unique enemy in it. But you'll be combating the same handful of enemies every mission, and they also just aren't interesting to fight really.

And unfortunately weapon variety here is yet again, lacking. What's here is alright, but I feel it needs more, and weapon cuztomization. The gadgets you unlock access to as you progress are fun, but again, I feel like there should be more choices here. Each class just has their 3 unique gadgets. Which are useful and fun, but give me some more alternatives for each class. All in all, I want more loadout options with more guns and gadgets/tools.

Also, no text chat or even voice chat. Just a ping system. Kinda hard to communicate with your fellow players. As of right now everyone is new and a lot of people are very clueless as what needs to be done during a mission, as it isn't very obvious in some cases.

There will be two major updates later this year, one in the fall and in winter. Both of which are to include a new mission and new enemies. And also new gameplay systems, not really sure what that means. And of course some new unlockables. Hopefully those are weapons and gadgets.

Still, I am enjoying it and I want to continue unlocking everything and play all the classes and see how it feels when I get even more familiar with the game.

Update -
I have to say, once you start playing harder missions with corruption and have competent team mates, the game becomes quite a bit more fun. Abusing the elemental damage types and combining them together just melts enemies. A splash kit user and a jump kit user working together to just shock hordes of enemies is very satisfying.

Or, on the other hand you get such unstable servers that you and all the enemies are lagging around and it really destroys the momentum the game can get from time to time during enemy spawns.

A proper tutorial- An absolute need!!! This game just sorta throws you in and expects you to learn by playing which I would have been fine with if it had GAME CHAT. Nonetheless, there still needs to be a proper tutorial including how each kit works and how they combo with each other.

More levels- Having what im assuming by the board in game 6 levels is sorta a low amount for 40 bucks. If the game was 25 bucks id be okay with it.

review:
This game is definitely a bit hard to recommend currently. I personally enjoy it, however there's a few design choices that I'm struggling to understand. 

For one, there doesn't seem to be any voice or text chat, which I feel like any good co-op shooter absolutely requires. In a game like this where so much can hinge on your teammates knowing your intentions and when to move, it really makes it difficult to coordinate effectively. Yes, we have tools like Discord to help us talk to our friends, but what about randoms?

Another thing that I found a bit annoying was that you drop important progression items on death. While this in itself is not the worst thing ever, my issue stems from the fact that often, your dropped items will awkwardly fall or spawn in positions that make them unable to be retrieved. Pretty wack.

As a big fan of Alan Wake and Control, I was excited to be able to return to the Oldest House, but it seems like this game needs either more time in the oven, or at least a dedicated team that will fill out this game with more content. I would temper your expectations if you intend on playing. The game can be fun, but it really feels undercooked.
After having played it for a bit longer, the flaws really start to show themselves. Stay away until you wish to be subjected to mediocre gameplay.

review:
Cannot recommend at the pricepoint, had a heap of performance issues, framerates absolutely tank to the point of near unplayability especially when lots of enemies spawn, even on lowest graphics settings, seemed to be a GPU memory leak or something, as it was fine at first, but as I kept playing it got worse and worse. AMD 6700XT GPU.
Level difficulty it seems is not very balanced and some are presently incredibly frustrating even on lower difficulties (frequency resonance), and others are a cakewalk on maximum. Difficulty scaling seems to be purely by increasing monster spawns, and doesn't appear to have any effect on the actual combat or types of enemies spawning. This would be okay if it worked like helldivers where I can stack up 20 odd kills with one well placed grenade or ability, which feels AMAZING (DRG also does this very well), but the grenade you get ingame (without grinding out upgrades) can't even kill a basic enemy without 2-3 grenades thrown. I think the game could be really really fun and there's a lot of stuff I do enjoy about it, but it's just not worth the price at release with all the current problems. Would probably have been better suited to early access at a lower price until the issues are ironed out.
Unfortunately I did decide to refund, but I will look at buying it again once the problems are sorted out, but I just can't morally lend my support towards games that feel so unpolished, on release.

review:
When reviewing this game, I had to think to myself what it is that really makes this one miss the mark. What makes games like Deep Rock Galactic, Earth Defense Force, and Risk of Rain 2 succeed where this one fails.

Let's start at the gunplay. It's bad. Each class can use any of the weapons, but none of them feel good fundamentally to use. They are unbalanced for a horde shooter and lack punch when you use them.

The music is bad. The exit music that happens every time you exit a level is just horrible, and when horde waves come through, there is no audio indicator that this is happening to really amp you up for things getting serious. That being said, the boom box  gadget has a song I found really pleasant to listen to.

The classes and gadgets, while varied, don't do enough to make them that impactful. Your classes do unlock more gadgets to help that, but with the game length being less than 4 hours to complete. Unless you grind previous levels, you may not even play with unlockable gadgets.

The level designs are simple and small and don't change at all between runs. You must do the levels in 3 intervals: the first section - then extract, the first and second - then extract, then all three sections together. That leads to playing the same levels over... and over again. With a singular level having a boss battle out of 5.

All this to say, the game is just boring after the first time you do the game loop. You have seen it all. The same 4 enemy types, the same levels, the same bad gameplay loop. What a miss this was, I was very excited for this one. This is just an unfinished, early access title sold for full price. I'm definitely  looking at Remedy Entertainment a bit differently now.
name: FBC: Firebreak

review:
Having played about 10 hours of Technical Test in total earlier this year, I can say that I totally get the flood of Negative reviews from people.

FBC is definitely a strange game - it took me a bit of time to get used to what the game wanted me to do and how it worked, but once I understood the mechanics and started playing on anything beyond Easy difficulty with clearance 2 and above it definitely got way more fun and engaging. 

However, I do not for the life of me understand why they had to lock away the core mechanics of the 3 kits behind progression that will take multiple missions to unlock. You need to unlock the first gadget of any of the kits that you use, and then multiple more missions to unlock the "ultimate" ability so to speak, not to mention that the alternative fire of the 3 kits are also locked away right out of the gate (but luckily they are the first upgrades you can get after just completing a single mission) so you FEEL completely powerless and the game feels much more simplistic than it is. It betrays itself - because the game revolves around the abilities of the 3 kits and the elements that you can inflict on enemies (and each other) yet you are not shown any of it for multiple missions on end.

Another reason why I don't understand that progression is that it's the 'cool stuff' that we've seen in promotion material and yet when you start playing you don't have any of the 'cool stuff'. Without the alt-fire of kits, the gadget and the 'ultimate' AND having to play on lowest clearance level with no upgrades means you start off on very simplistic, short and boring missions because nothing happens in them beyond you running from point A to point B and then leaving. The onboarding experience is really, really off in my opinion, and it's probably the major factor that contributed to the overwhelming negativity that I see in the reviews section.

FBC: Firebreak is basically one of those "trust me bro it gets super cool a bit later" games. Not to the level of Monster Hunter's 40+ hours, but you do need to be prepared to play with a bit of a barebones loadout for a few missions. That said, if you have a couple of friends to play with and you all play with different kits you might breeze through the unlock process and get good builds quicker than the average quick play player would, because you also level up each kit individually and you HAVE to use different kits to do good in missions (ok maybe not on Easy difficulty clearance 1, lol). I sincerely hope that Remedy will make adjustments to this because I can absolutely see why people would be thrown off from even trying to play beyond first 2-3 missions.

review:
I am deeply saddened.

Was really looking forward to playing the game and even recommending it to some of my friends.
I absolutely love Remedy games and I'm just really sad and disappointed that this was not a home run. 

What is in the game is fun but this is not nearly enough content for the price.
Severely lacking in weapon, enemy and class variety (and various other pain points).

Don't get me wrong, what's here at launch is great but the fact that I've literally experienced everything the game has to offer in less than 6 hours (I've completed all the jobs and done multiple full corruption runs) gives me absolutely zero confidence that I'll continue replaying this.

Once again I'm really disappointed and absolutely cannot recommend that anyone give this game a try. If you're really that interested, rather go watch a YouTube video of someone else playing the game to experience it.


Edit after Breakpoint update:
In summary - More of the same. You can't unbake a cake.
The additions are fine I guess, the grind and progression was never my issue. A few new weapons, okay. A few new enemies that play exactly the same as every other enemy no counter play or any sort of mechanics to them, you just shoot them till they stop moving. The new map looks cool but they're still tiny and sorely lacking in variety of how they play out, the first 2 zones still require you to do the same thing which is just boring and uninteresting and also means that you've experienced basically everything after your first run of the mission.

Still so disappointed that this game had all the incredible world building and story of Control and decided to do nothing interesting with that. 
Something like building shifts could have been implemented to randomise your point of entry or the entire layout of the map but because of how linear the objectives are and how tiny each of the zones are this probably wouldn't work.
Altered items are yet another disappointment. In Control Langston mentions how certain items have rituals or certain ways of dealing with them, some of them altered the environment, some required you to constantly keep an eye on them, etc. So imagine my disappointment when I see an altered item and find out that you just deal with all of them by blasting it with black rock and that they do nothing interesting other than adding modifiers to the mission. Forget finding an item on the map, completing a side objective to complete a certain ritual to subdue the item or even an epic boss fight like with the Anchor, none of that its just "gun go brr". Minor inconvenience solved.
Enemy types in control had a level of counter play thanks to how fun Jesse's kit was and the way she played. Maybe you had to doge certain attacks or have your shield up or use certain abilities against an enemy. Although you were basically doing the same thing it was still fun and interesting and till today I find myself going back to control to play it again. Unfortunately, Firebreaks crisis kits are so bland and one dimensional that they just don't mesh well with the same enemies.
None of this matters though and at this point I can't be asked to type out all my other gripes with the game.  

Say what you want about my play time or that I maybe don't understand certain aspects of the game, whatever. There just isn't many things that are enjoyable or have anything that makes me want to play more of it or do another run. How the Remedy managed to take the incredible world of Control and make something as bland and shallow as Firebreak, I will never understand.
I'm not going to sit here and cope that the next update will add something life changing or fix everything because moral of the story is, you can't unbake a cake.
Still. Disappointed.

name: FBC: Firebreak

review:
Tutorial
The tutorial broke on me and my only way to play the game was to skip tutorial. This makes the onboarding significantly worse for anyone that looks to understand the game. Luckily ive played more than enough games to not need it in order to be fine.

Levels
The game has 5 missions, which you must play through multiple times to unlock the real missions. So, technically 15 missions, that then each have 5 difficulties. The enemies spawn randomly and really dont increase the tension all too much from what i could tell. If you think L4D hoards that run at you at certain checkpoints it really isnt that way.

Mechanics
It has competent gunplay mechanics, that being hitscan. The in level mechanics are infuriating and the game is not built for solo, the option should just not exist as it just makes the game unfun. That being said, the basic premise is to fix whatever is wrong with the level, so essentially run around has handimen and do a little QTE on whatever is pinged. Then the level exit will open and you leave. Enemies spawn randomly throughout the level and are not hard to deal with.
Since i dealt with the fire mission directly, the mechanic is that the level is hot and there is fire on the ground and the vents sometimes vent fire. If you catch fire it is permanent until you reach a shower OR specifically have a teammate with the water gun thing. So if you are solo, ur dead which has no consequence so just keep on the mission until your hp depletes.

COOP
Its a coop game that relies on coop to make the content as far as i can tell. And if the game is purely meant to be coop, voip is necessary in this day and age. If this was meant to get the streamer crowd to do their usual hype of a game that is mid then i think it failed to generate that. The inter player interactions dont seem to be there enough straight off the start as streamers and most players will bail before unlocking that kind of content.

Kit Problem
You get 3 man teams and there are 3 kits. you are not forced to pick all 3 kits but they are each highly recommended to use. Meaning if your team isnt coordinated, you will have a worse match because of it. I think this would have been better if these characters had a story with set personalities like L4D where we have an evolving story from some amazing story tellers at Remedy.

Oldest House
Im not as big a remedy fan as my buddy is, but why is the oldest house a bunch of fixed missions? it makes no sense to not have procedural generation. Being that remedy created this fantastic setting, it feels wasted not to use it properly. SCP is super big on the internet and theres no reason to not capitalize on it. Everyone wants the next big L4D clone, and this isnt it. This game has / had potential but it cannot launch like this.

BattlePass
The "battlepass" system they have mimics helldivers requisition system. Pages are unlocked by spending your points. It gives you a small amount of freedom of what you unlock when. Not my favorite system, but its passable overall.

Other Progression
You dont start with any anomalous items which isnt an issue, but if thats where the fun is then locking it isnt a good idea. You dont start with a grenade in your grenade slot, you must unlock it. You dont start with any perks, instead you are a guy with a gun and a kit class. The perks seemed interesting but why should i care. The melee enemies cant hit me, the base pistol 1 shots them to the head, what do i need?

Reviews
One thing i notice is that over 2 hours reviews skew to 90% positive. If thats the case, then its either cope that they cant refund, or the game suddenly completely changes for no reason after this period and should just be that way from the start to avoid this perception.

SteamDB
Peaked at <2k players on launch day. Thats going to be rough to keep an audience with any amount of retention for a live service. Especially with how negative the reviews are.

Performance
I didnt have an issue in this department, didnt even think to open the menu. Im playing on a g9 in double wide, had no issues with scaling. 7800x3d and 4070ti runs the game fine with not a single issue unlike every other release in recent memory.

File Size
Oh and for those of you looking for file size, the game is 12gigs. Which it sucks to have to not like this game for in game reasons, because it really does respect your harddrive.

VPN
Also this game hates my vpn, its the only game i have that freaks out while on a vpn. Im used to having higher ping, but this game just boots you out every few minutes much like twitch. Since i believe they are using AWS im sure they are on the same service.

Other Games in the Genre
I find that this game simply lacks a unique concept that would give it staying power in a horde shooter game. It doesnt have the story telling campaign of L4D. It doesnt have the procedural generation of DRG nor its more fleshed out class system. It doesnt have the community engagement of Helldivers 2. It doesnt have the economy and round based structure of KF2. It doesnt have the insane mechanics of Warframe (nor the years of constant reinvestment from DE). It doesnt have weapon variety, class variety, enemy variety, level variety. Hell, this is the Oldest House, make it a rouge-lite like every other game on the market, it would atleast give it SOME depth.

TLDR: Gameplay is Shoot Head + SAME QTE and repeat.

review:
I've been really excited about visiting FBC Firebreak so I hope to provide some helpful feedback to others while benefiting the game overall <3 This review is day one with about ninety minutes of play. I do not intend to refund the game right now, and hope to change my recommendation. I've seen reviews say you need to spend more time with it, and I hope that's true, but this is how I feel right now, as a simple excited gamer.

I love a lot of Remedy, especially Control, and was drawn into Firebreak almost exclusively for this reason. This world and the FBC are very intriguing and it's a fun universe to fit this type of game into. The big and bold FBC level intros and their fonts put me right back into The Building, the voice acting has been welcoming more than distracting, the soundtrack fits; I am okay with the premise of this game in the universe and was never wholly torn away from immersion. Big plus!

I love shooting stuff, especially when it feels good. I'm not a competitive FPS player, barely even a casual in the genre. Shooting stuff feels pretty good to me here so far. The starting weapons have a good punch to them, and I think the feel fits in with the aesthetic. Does the feeling compare to picking up and shooting the Director's pistol in Control? No, but it doesn't seem to be going for that exact vibe, and it does have that Remedy charm and production quality.

BUT, for someone looking at Firebreak right now who doesn't have a shared love of Control or friends to play with: I'm not sure there's enough here gameplay wise right now to justify the purchase. 
I don't know really know what's going on from the moment I boot up the game. The tutorial didn't really help me understand the aspects of the game I would want the tutorial to explain to me. 
I have mostly shot stuff, and won. There have been a couple mechanics, like running over a bunch of sticky notes and cleaning them off in the shower (which I though would culminate in the big sticky note boss from the trailer, but I guess that's at a higher level), 
but otherwise I have shot stuff, got on an elevator, and have either moved on to another 10ish minute round with the same party or been forced back to the menu to queue again; positively both of which were quick and seamless options. Adding another plus here, I have had zero connectivity or performance issues in my time with the game.

This is a somewhat unique blend of an established single-player franchise and multiplayer genre, and as long as they can pull off somewhat captivating gameplay, the strength of the franchise and production budget can carry a lot of weight. However, Elden Ring Nightreign just came out, and it's hard not to make some comparisons, especially at the same price point. For a three-player romp through an established franchise in Q2 2025, this game is outclassed.

My main takeaway is that I feel good about casually shooting stuff and getting some easy wins, especially in a universe I'm happy to explore more of, but this feels a tad like an early access release without a hook in a sea of similar games it may drown in.

name: FBC: Firebreak

review:
It's another fun first-person 4-player PvE co-op game. You know the type: L4D2, Vermintide, Darktide, Deep Rock Galactic, etc. 

- FBC's early progression system means you won't have access to much at the very beginning, but your options will open up a lot the more you play. There are a lot of unlockables to work towards, which you can see in your Research menu and Requisition menu. 
- Game objectives are varied like games like Outlast Trials and The Blackout Club, while also having plenty of combat like Left 4 Dead 2, Deep Rock Galactic, and GTFO. 
- Game session length (called Clearance) is customizable just like the mission difficulty at the mission lobby. Missions can be very short or much lengthier, and the short ones are surprisingly short, reminding me of Warframe's mobile defense missions. This will definitely be convenient for people wanting to squeeze a little game time into busier days.

BAD:
- Menu keybinds are weird/bad and too varied in a lot of specific instances. Usually, this is a hallmark that a game was made for controller/gamepad. Also, the Requisition page is nigh identical to the battle pass-esque catalogs in Outlast Trials, and unlike the catalogs, you can't use the mousewheel to scroll through Requisition pages.
- You may often lose connection with the host, sending you back to the main menu. This is the worst part of the experience.

Awful new player experience, the game barely explains anything about the mechanics while also locking away most of your tools behind a terrible battlepass progression system that forces you to buy cosmetics in order to be able to actually unlock your core abilities, or to upgrade your peashooters into actually useable guns. 

Sure maybe that could be excused if the core gameplay and mission design was good but that is not the case either, the objectives are all essentially chores you do; you spend about a minute doing boring objectives, the game spawns in a single wave of 10-20 enemies that you dispatch and then you go back to a minute of just no enemies being present while you do these mindnumbing objectives. The clearance levels are also just a baffling design choice, why would I ever just want to play 1/3rd or 2/3rd of a level instead of the whole level? But you are forced to play clearance 1 and 2 before you are allowed to play clearance 3 which means by the time you have unlocked the full mission you will have already gotten tired of replaying it.

The only redeeming quality would be the setting of Control, but the game is mostly just recycled assets from that game which means it basically has nothing new to present there either.

Personal experience and opinion from playing at launch

The game has quite a nice foundation and I see the vision, I want to like it, but in practice is not fun moment to moment, so will refund for now and wait to see if in a month or a few it gets better

In general my biggest complaint is how sluggish and unresponsive the entire game feels, not in a technical aspect as it runs fine for me, but in that it always feels like you don't get a good feedback of what you're doing, click a button in the UI? have to wait a second before the game notices it, characters feel slow, base weapons feel like toys (and the melee is laughable), it's hard to tell if you're even damaging enemies as it seems their health bars take a second to update after you hit them, animations feel slow, the "press Q and E" QTE is just kinda annoying and repetitive, and so on and so on

It's understandable wanting to make the player feel like they're struggling, but making the game feel like walking trough mud, shooting nerf darts, and hitting with a pillow is not the fun kind of struggling. (And don't come to me with "the game gets better later", a game should feel good from the start! Even if you feel underpowered the game should feel engaging and like your actions are meaningful)

This is more situational probably because it's launch day, but I honestly could barely play online, as I was constantly being disconnected in the middle of the missions, out of the dozen or so I tried playing, could only get trough 2 in their totality, every other I got a connection error or got kicked for seemingly no reason

And what didn't help that is how few missions there are, I got to play "shoot the stickies in the office" quite a few times more than anything... (why is there no way to select which mission you want to play in quick play?)

Not a 'bad' game, but certainly not engaging when you have options that are better in many aspects from the start

[h1][Original Review:][/h1]

It's my first day at the Bureau.

Recruiters were really talking it up and we were all jazzed to descend into the Oldest House after filling out pretty extensive agreement paperwork, which I probably should have read more thoroughly. 

After surprisingly poor and very blurry training that was most likely redacted, I excitedly donned the uniform and jumped out the door of the elevator to do my job among my teammates. They were clearly confused. Many were poorly equipped and clearly bought the deluxe gear to be differently the same. Equipment was failing, so many fires, so much Hiss. Folks were zigging when they should be zagging. My goodness, lots of accidents. So now I am processing a pile of incident reports for Security and Safety.

I expect more HR memos plastered around the watercooler on how awesome the gig is. But darn it, I am still hearing the muffled screams of my teammates and the smell is worse than burnt popcorn and microwaved fish in the breakroom. Lots of folks were saying it is clear we signed on for an empty, hollow existence as a corporate tool hoping to find purpose in grinding tasks and shuffling paperwork for branded swag. That this corporate simulation is terrifyingly real. Some say a clear parody of the industry as a whole. Right down to being a bit overpriced for minimal "Early Access" level content. 

But I don't see it. I deeply appreciate that we can roll up our sleeves and do this extremely essential and meaningful work for the Director. It is amazing. I have yet to meet my supervisor. I believe that is his voice on the intercom. Darned if I can find my Employee Handbook. I may have dropped it outside the elevator and no one will answer my questions. I will spend more time in the company store once I complete orientation and understand what is going on. Well, right after I clean my teammate, Jerry, off my boots.... Anyone know how long orientation is?

I am so looking forward to my second day. Happy to be here. Thank the Board!

review:
[h3] Time to clean house? Eh, tomorrow maybe?  [/h3]

[b] Ahti’s floor mopping seemed more entertaining than this tbh [/b]

Don’t get me wrong - I’ve been loving everything Remedy’s put out lately. I entered the Oldest House as Jesse and dove deep into Alan’s nightmare with full interest and zero regrets. I loved every minute I spent with those games. Firebreak feels different.

What I love about Remedy’s titles (besides being genuinely good games and their ongoing collabs with Poets of the Fall) is how they tell stories. I’m not gonna list all the ways - you probably know what I’m talking about. What Firebreak lacks is soul.

Yeah, the familiar Control setting is here. It seems to take place after the events of Control. But we don’t know much about the characters, the anomalies we’re here to clean, fix, and [spoiler]moisture [/spoiler]. Sure, they’re some version of the Hiss - but that only makes sense if you played Control. What about everyone else? Who’s this for?

A lot of people say this game feels more like a second job than something you’d play for fun. I kinda agree. I get that co-op shooters aren't necessarily about worldbuilding,but still - where Left4dead being pioneers, landed some awesome cinematics. Where Deep Rock Galactic gave us a good looking hub - this game brings nothing of a sort. There is not a single weird side character, no surreal moments, not many mass culture references. Nothing that screams “Remedy” except the font.

In the end, Firebreak isn’t terrible - but for a studio that gave us Alan Wake 2, this feels weirdly lifeless.

review:
Editing my originally positive review for this game. Initially I thought Remedy got off to a bad start with a rocky launch but that they'd get a handle on it and smooth out some of the rough edges to make this a great little horde shooter, but as time goes on and their attempts to balance the game get more and more desperate, it's become clear they have absolutely no clue what they're doing with this game. 

At launch I think Firebreak was actually great. People complained about the economy and progression systems but I didn't actually think it was too grindy or anything. I had some minor gripes (e.g. having to unlock pointless cosmetics before you got the upgrades that actually made your kit work) but they seemed committed to working out those kinks. Admittedly the onboarding experience was rough but they've certainly made strides in the right direction since then. 

However, since the massive player drop-off after launch that they never recovered from, the game is basically unplayable. Fewer players result in almost all jobs being solo-only at this point, and the game does not seem to compensate for number of players in a match in any way. Enemy spawns are way overtuned, enemy health seems like it was shadow buffed, and all the while you're trying to handle multiple objectives by yourself, dealing with hazards that were designed for 3 people to keep under control, constantly dying even on Normal difficulty. This isn't even accounting for a handful of persistent bugs that make the already-overwhelming gameplay even more difficult to navigate.

Firebreak had a lot of potential but Remedy completely squandered it by hitting a deadline to release a minimum viable product. A couple of months in early access/open beta could have saved the game. As a massive Remedy fan and someone who was really hopeful for this game, I can't BS anyone by saying that it's worth your time.

Played all the missions on max length several times over and I gotta say... that's it? 

The progression system is a slog, all early game equipment feels clunky and unwieldy. You have to play the same 5 mission over and over just to unlock one new equipment. They decided that doing the helldivers warbond thing would be best thing for progression on guns and equipment. Yes I love being forced to buy a new pair of pants just to get access to new tier of the battlepass to try a new gun.

Also running the same missions over and over is a slog, its honestly baffling to me that the oldest house is known for constantly shifting its interiors and being a maze yet none of the mission layouts ever change so every run tends to blend together and feel samey.

The game has a lot of potential and personality but I wouldn't recommend buying/playing it in it's current state, not only because of the weird design decisions but also because it lacks content to begin with.

review:
Gameplay loop is so much boring. Run here - press LMB 2 times (if you have the right class), then run here, press Q-E-E-E-Q-Q-E-Q-E-E.... (you got the idea). Then some enemies would spawn and you shoot it with only gun you allow to have. Then you go to the next area, there are a lot more enemies. Repeat multiple times. 

And it would be nice gameplay loop. If killing enemies would've been fun. Remember CONTROL? You had cool abilites, you had one gun but with multiple shooting types. And mixing shooting and those abilities was so much fun! 

Welp. There is only shooting without any additional stuff. (there is also grenades, but not very original and satisfying). Just hold LMB untill all the enemies die. That's it. 

The game has cool music! BUT it's too shy to show it and you will hear it 2 times. In the main menu and during final extraction.

I played for awhile and didn't get any stronger. No cooler guns that I would like, no abilities that would change anything significantly. 

I 100% completed Control 2 times. Even roguelike mode was fun to me. And this... is not fun at all to me. 

I don't really know who and why would like this game. While HD2 you can play literally forever (just by trying new stratagems loadouts), this will ran out of content much sooner.

If you have 40$ - buy Helldivers 2

I guess I'm gonna complete CONTROL 3rd time after playing this nonsense

review:
[b]I love Remedy games with all my heart, but this one is straight up dogshit.

Gameplay feels very boring and repetitive. Movement is very slow and stiff. All weapons feel the same and unresponsive, you just hold one button and shoot crazy zombies. To heal you need to run to the very beginning of location and stand in shower for about 5 seconds. To refill your ammo you need to run to the beginning of the location again, stand infront of some thing and press Q and E, or go look for some bunker. There are like 3 enemy types: zombie, spongy guy and zombie in flying chair. There are about 5 different missions, each takes place in different location, but all missions feel the same. You are sent to a revamped location from Control, you fix some shit by pressing Q and E and kill zombies. There are also some “bosses” that are actually just same zombies with a lot of hp. All missions are finished in 5-10 minutes.

No voice or text chat in coop game that they think worth 40$. That is honestly unbelievable. 

I chose a mission and waited for someone to join my squad, but for some reason no one ever joined me. I was only able to play with other players if I play quick game. New weapons are unlocked through something like battle pass. In general, the progression here is not interesting.

FBC Firebreak looks like a game that was made by an indie team of 10-15 people and released in early access, the only difference is that FBC has "AAA" graphics. It seems that in mid development they did not know what to do with this game but still decided to release it hoping for a miracle.

Do not even think about buying this game even with a discount. If you have Xbox Game Pass and you are thinking of trying this game, trust me this shit is not worth an hour of your time.

I think fate of this game is obvious - in a month it will be at 50% discount, they will release content they promised, and gonna abandon this disgrace.[/b]

review:
Unfortunately, FBC: Firebeak- despite being my most anticipated release of this whole year- Falls completely short of being a good game. 

First, when playing there is barely any guidance on what to do during a mission, just a short dialogue from the radio-guy and you're set off to run around and figure it out yourself.

Second, most of the cool utility mechanics that you see in the trailer are NOT accessible on hour 0 of your playthrough. They must be unlocked with in-game tokens similar to the medals of Helldivers 2. But now imagine locking behind core gameplay features of a kit behind a warbond page, how ridiculous is that? Artificial content-locking I say.

Third, acquiring these ingame tokens are very one dimensional. Aka, just kill an enemy with a screen-wide healthbar and pick up their dead drops. Very engaging, I know.

Fourth, Mission lengths. The point of Co-Ops is to play through a whole mission with your team and complete it as a team, that's what makes it fun. Here? You drop in for 5 minutes running around aimlessly randomly shooting hiss that spawn with no real reason nor choreographed waves until you accidentally complete an objective and press a button to extract in less than a minute. That doesn't feel rewarding or stressful or fun in any way shape or form. By the way, notice how I said an OBJECTIVE, SINGULAR.

You drop in to do ONE THING AND THEN LEAVE. 

In a cramped map that IS ALWAYS THE SAME.

With a kit you MUST SPEND TOKENS TO HAVE FUN WITH.

With guns that BARELY KILL ANYTHING.

Trying to do missions that are BORING.

This is the type of torture people infected by The Hiss go through, this is probably what they have to play in their heads whilst floating in the air, where I get to play as an actual cool character with cool mechanics in Control.

Heed this warning, Remedy. Go back to making Alan Wake 3, lest you figure out this type of game isn't a loop, but a spiral for this studio.

review:
This game is an immeasurable disappointment. When I played this game on day 1 of launch, the gameplay was so fucking good! It had an interesting level system, perks and unique guns and great gameplay mechanics that made the game feel fun and satisfying to play.

Things were not perfect though. The advertisements for this game made it look very different to what people were expecting. And within 3 hours of the game going live, people were review bombing it. Complaining that it wasn't Alan Wake, CONTROL or any other Remedy Game. People were mad and instead of refunding the game they complained that it wasn't the examples I gave above.

And so the small team of 12 devs with this passion project of which they spent 6 years of their life making, decided to change the entire game to accommodate the people who'd never play this game as they had no interest in Coop PVE shooters like: Payday, Helldivers or deep rock galactic. That is when everything started to go down hill for this game...

Then the changes came. They made enemies more spongy, suddenly the currency changed, suddenly the gunplay changed, they added broken weapons, combat became awful and boring, they changed perks and levelling, changed how mechanics worked, changed the maps. Changed literally the entire game, just to accommodate people who had review bombed the game and had no interest in ever playing this game again after believing this game was going to be like Alan Wake 3.

This game had so much potential to be so much better! It had a solid foundation and a small community of players who genuinely loved this game (Me and my friend included). Yes, there was a lack of content. Yes, there was only 4 maps. Yes, connection was an issue. But it was fun. It had really good gameplay! And I know if you hopped on this game on the modern version of it, that is hard to believe but it was actually really fun and satisfying when it first came out! 

There was a solid foundation that could be built upon and expanded. In time this game probably would've grown something bigger with a community around it. But instead we've ended up with this rotting carcass of a game, that has had it's wings hacked off and told to fly.

It hurts me to not recommend this game to people and tell them to stay away but sadly that is what I'd have to recommend. But repeating myself again, this game could've been so much more then what it became. I had a lot of fun playing this game in the beginning and I wish I could still play that older version. I hope that one day this game can find it's trajectory again and can become actually fun to play again.

review: Not your typical Remedy game, but still amazing in its own right. The game plays better than I thought, the missions are really fun, The leveling is pretty good and the systems all work together fantastically. For a FPS made by Remedy, I'd have to say they did a wonderful job. Reminds me of when I first played L4D, as well as some Helldivers and Deep Rock vibes. Edit: For those saying it lacks content, they already said that more jobs and things will be added. It's almost like no one payed attention to their marketing or something..... Also, only thing "wrong" with this game is that occasionally you will get disconnected from a mission with a message saying "lost connection to backend". That has happened to me 3 times in the 7 hours I've played. But some errors are to be expected, Remedy does single player stuff, so this being mp and only that being an issue tells me they did really well. It's unfortunate it didn't launch with voice chat or at the very least text chat, but I do not doubt it will be added soon. Edited to be negative: Idk how they made the feel of the game worse, but they did. The new mission select screen sucks and you can't choose to do any mission you want, its whatever is up in rotation for like 30 minutes, then the team damage seems like they upped it 10 fold, all the damage I was taking was basically from teammates and I was downed like 5 times after just joining a match, the new systems in place are good for the most part, but they need to reevaluate how damage is done in this game now cause I cant even play 5 minutes in a match without dying due to teammates. If you are wanting a to farm a certain currency, gotta wait till that mission is in rotation, or do the random one, and that im not too sure on if you get all currencies or if it is depending on the mission, but either way in that regard I think its a step backwards. The pink goo mission is also broken, completely takes health away even tho not covered in it, and not close to it. Ridiculous they thought this was a good update. There are positives with this new update, but imo, they took 1 step forward and 2 steps back. I hope they can make this game as amazing as it can be, the fundamentals are there, the foundation is there, the follow thru tho on it is a bit of a letdown. I still love Remedy and will continue to support this game as well as anything else they make, but I am disappointed in this update personally. Am glad others are liking it tho. Still cant recommend this. It is pretty much unplayable now if you were a fan of how it was before the terrible update. Edit: Now they are done adding content, which is fine, but they never added the 2nd campaign content they had on the roadmap since release. Give refunds or something cause this is bad. Blackout never happened, only the 1st one released. They focused on the wrong things and this game went to crap because of it. RIP.

The maps themselves are short, their lengths can be increased, sure, but even then if the two I played have its equal in the other three they are still beatable in 25 minutes each. Yes. There is a total of five maps.
Progression tied to a battlepass filled with dog**** such as sprays and I wish it wouldnt get worse.
It does. 
A severely limited weapon roster with a total of, hold unto something, six weapons. 
Weapons start of feeling like noodles and increase in damage through the battlepass. Not even a cosmetic upgrade. The below average quality starter revolver does not change in behaviour (other than a flat damage increase) or looks when it becomes the highest grade version of itself.

review:
So, obviously my playtime is limited, but I know how important early steam reviews are to a game's success so I'm inclined to leave a positive one.

EDIT:

Changed my review to negative, which I'm reluctant to do, but I simply have not had a positive experience. 

Content is a bit sparse. It's very well laid-out, I like the pacing and the fact that each mission is three small missions that you progressively unlock with a big finale at the end. However there are only five and in an hour I beat all of one and started another. So, conservatively 6-8 hours to beat all three phases of all five missions, which are handcrafted and not randomly generated. That time could go by MUCH FASTER with a full party who can efficiently divide tasks.

On top of that, you only have 6 weapons and (critically) BARELY ANY MUSIC. I can't stress enough how the lack of music drags the experience down. Minimal ambient tracks, very few combat tracks (certainly none that I remember after 2.5 hours). Every good co-op experience has superb music to set the tone and organically feed information to players. 

The visuals are cool, the few missions available are fun, and the few guns we have are good. There's just... not enough (which I hate to say because I know how much work it takes to make a game). So I have to leave a negative review in the name of being somewhat objective. I desperately hope the game finds its footing in the near future.

However, the only difference are 3 new missions that are shorter than those on playtest. While I like variety in how tasks look and feel, but they are either "go to first point, then next" or "bring item X to place Y", just with different objects and explanation behind them. There is no difficulty progression in missions (level 1 of first mission and last one take the same time to complete), because difficulty is chosen by party host before starting the mission, there is no incentive to play new levels other than to change scenery, because you were tired of previous one.

Don't get me wrong, game is fun to play sometimes, but I won't force myself to justify paying 40 euros on release for so little content. If they will update the game and add at least comparable to L4D content amount on it's release, then I could re-evaluate my opinion, but not now in this state of the game.
