review:
WARNING! ABANDONED GAME
Bugs, Broken Promises, and Silence from the Developers

Unfortunately, this game delivers little more than frustration and disappointment. While the concept itself is appealing, the execution leaves much to be desired.

Bug-Ridden Game Play:
One of the most glaring issues with Kebab Chef is the sheer number of bugs that infest nearly every part of the gameplay. From glitchy kitchen appliances and disappearing ingredients to inexplicable crashes and save files that corrupt without warning, the game often feels more like a stress test than a relaxing simulator. These bugs are not just minor annoyances; they frequently disrupt any progress one makes in the game.

Updates Are Few and Far Between:
If you’re hoping these problems would be addressed with regular patches and improvements, prepare to be disappointed! Updates for Kebab Chef are remarkably sparse. Months can pass without a single patch, and when updates do finally arrive, they are often small-scale and fail to resolve the game’s deeper issues. Long-standing bugs often remain untouched.

Lack of Developer Communication:
Perhaps most troubling is the near-total silence from the development team. The developers are essentially non-existent within the community. Instead, all communication is filtered through the game’s moderators, who do their best to relay concerns and feedback but lack the authority to enact real change. Questions about bugs, future content, or the direction of the game are met with vague responses or simply ignored.
It is clear that the developers are more concerned with their new game they released.

Broken Promises and Empty Road Maps:
Kebab Chef's history is littered with false promises. Road maps are posted with bold ambitions and then quietly abandoned. Promised updates either never materialize or arrive in diminished form, far removed from what was originally outlined. New features—such as expanded menus, multiplayer modes, or enhanced customization—are dangled in front of the community only to be forgotten when the next wave of disappointment rolls in.

My Final Thoughts:
In its current state, Kebab Chef is a cautionary tale of squandered potential. The core idea is strong, but the absence of reliable support, the overwhelming presence of bugs, and the lack of transparency from the developers make it impossible to recommend. If you’re seeking a cooking simulator that values its community and delivers on its promises, you would be best served looking elsewhere.

Pros: Fun concept, visually appealing at first glance
Cons: Buggy game play, infrequent updates, absent developers, unreliable communication, broken promises

Save your time and money for a game that truly delivers on its promises to their community.

review:
Kebab Chefs! is a fun and chaotic little restaurant sim that really shines at the beginning — especially in co-op. Managing a kebab shop with friends is a unique and entertaining experience that sets it apart from other cooking games.

That said, the game currently lacks depth. You run out of things to do pretty quickly, and the number of recipes is really limited. After a few hours, you’ve basically seen everything it has to offer.

There are also quite a few bugs — some are just annoying, others actually affect gameplay. The frustrating part is that many of them seem like they’d be easy to fix. I know it's still in Early Access, so I’m hopeful things will improve, but right now it feels a bit undercooked :) Keep going! AND BRING NEW GOURMETS PLEASE ITS SO BORING

review:
Played the game last year in June, 2023, and it was great. 3 of us in total, almost zero bugs in 3 person coop all the way until the end of the game (at that point in the update cycle) having a fully upgraded and decorated restaurant and patio. Coming back to the game now on Jan 12 2025, we can't even get past day 4. People unable to join, cutting board noises that never go away until you reload, the ringing phone sound in the tutorial would not go away for everyone, bug after bug after bug. On top of that, Juan comes to our restaurant for a second day in a row, and it completely bricks our save. 

I'm unsure what these devs have been doing since June outside of the update announcements I've seen, but like so many others have suggested I would highly recommend fixing these bugs, from annoying to game breaking, before you release any more major updates. Game has become unplayable, when usually it's the other way around in Early Access games. Game is buggy at release and gets better. This one started great, and apparently go far worse. 

Once at least the game breaking bugs are fix I'll definitely revert my review to Recommended, but until then I would avoid this game.

review:
The game really has potential. But right now I cannot recommend it, sadly. I was planning to play with my significant other, but I tried the game first and sadly it was not up to par.

Good: Many varieties of stuff you can cook; Different cooking utensils and machines that allow you to cook from simple grilled beef, to kebabs, to pizzas, to minced meat and beyond; Food and dishes graphics are good, the dishes you cook look beautiful.

Bad: The game right now feels like an early alpha preview at best; All NPCs seem to share these same few 3D models (everybody looks the same); Characters animations are weird and robotic; The sound effects are really simple. They sound like they come from some online stock; The same 10 seconds music keeps looping and trying to change the music in the radio does nothing (there's only 1 music that plays constantly from the moment you launch the game); Discord community is quiet (very little activity in English channels); The last update completely broke multiplayer, it's simply unplayable right now. I'm sure the dev is working hard on it, though; For those who want to chill and cook peacefully to relax, you can't. You are only allowed to cook one portion of food at a time and this portion has like 3 or 4 servings. These 3 servings will inevitability run out during service. Which means you will have to scramble yourself to cook fast during service. This is more of a personal preference, though; You cannot cook just 1 serving of food for a customer. You need to cook the entire portion of 3 servings. Which means there will be wastage every single day, no way around that; Visual glitches all over the UI; Some parts of the UI have white text over yellow background, poorly designed UI/UX.

I'm sure the developers are working really hard on this game. It's probably just way too early in development. I know it's early access and all, but for me, I didn't like the core mechanics of the game. Namely the cooking fast during service and the impossibility to cook a single item for 1 patron. Also, the fact that an update with a bug was pushed to production and caused a total meltdown of multiplayer, means it could happen again in the future.

Now don't get me wrong. These are my constructive criticism and I hope some of them get fixed so that I can try it again in 2 or 3 years time.

review:
Please focus on bug fixes before adding more features to the game. My girlfriend and I love this game but it's incredibly frustrating to experience so many bugs.

After getting rid of the halloween decorations, there's some massive game breaking bugs that occur in multiplayer:
- Players who join the host cannot put food up on the serving table. They fall on the floor.
- If the host puts a dish on the menu and serves it with the serving tray, other joined players can pick up the same dish off of the floor. The serving table then is serving a dish, without the model of the dish, and the player can re-store the same dish for later use.
- Staff do not continue working (aside from washing dishes) past closing time. Once the final guest has left they no longer continue to collect money and dishes.
- Kebab Wraps unwrap every time after loading the game
- Bins from the Industrial Metal Shelving and Industrial Sink appear after loading the game, even if the items are in the players' inventory.
- Skewers model increase in size when joined players (not the host) pick them up.
- Counter corners do not snap properly, only one side of the counter corner snaps. 
- Selling Knife Blocks will keep the knives in your space.
- Selling Frying Machines will keep the frying baskets in your space.

EDIT: Nov 17
This game is getting worse and worse with every hotfix.
- Multiplayer is completely broken now. Complete de-sync with other players. Players can't move, access menus, literally do anything.
- Everything that was previously placed correctly into drawers or kebabs has been completely jumbled. All of our hard work prepping food has gone to complete waste.
- NPCs no longer do anything.

The halloween update completely broke the game. Just re-instate the previous build you had before Halloween. I wish I could ask for a refund at this point because this game is literally unplayable (I actually can't even access menus to leave the game if I wanted to, I had to alt+f4).

review:
This game is a buggy mess. When collision issues aren't causing you to waste water and soup, you'll see customers completely ignoring table collision to walk through them. Plates sometimes disappear completely when picking them up or putting them down. 

If you bought individual plates and wash them, they won't be placed into the clean dish bin, and you have to grab them from the sink while you're still "washing" it to remove it, else it will go back into the dirty plate bin and become dirty again. Sometimes you can't put individual plates back in the plate shelf, other times you can.

Plates also somehow end up in the clean plate bin while they're still dirty... *after* you just washed it. This causes you to prioritize the "dirty" plate from the clean bin and repeatedly wash it in an infinite loop. The only way to fix it is by putting the "dirty" plate back into the plate shelf. 

These are just a few of the bugs I've experienced while playing the game with my girlfriend. Beyond that, the lackluster English makes it difficult to take the game seriously at times.

When it comes to simulator games, my expectations are typically very low because of the experiences I've had with them in the past. Games like this one only lower that bar further and make it difficult for me to go in with an open mind.

Do yourself a favor and look for something else. The core game here is fine, but the bugs make it a miserable experience that I can't, in good conscience, recommend to anyone.

review:
Fun game and well worth the money on sale (10,49 EUR), at full price I'd be a lot more cranky about all the bugs. It's a fairly simple game both in terms of graphics and gameplay.
It's fun prepping the food and customizing the restaurant.

The audio is kinda funky, certain sounds are very loud and seems stacked on top of each others when for example frying a lot of fries at once which becomes extremely loud despite everything else being low volume.
Some descriptions of objects are not implemented which gives the game a lower quality impression.
The game makes my computer run very hot even though the graphic is very simple.

In multiplayer the game is very buggy but still enjoyable. There is a lot of desync issues which can cause crashes and game breaking issues (such as one player sees an object but the other player doesn't, another example one player can interact with an object and the other cannot.)

[2025-05-04]
DO NOT BUY until a new update comes out, the game should be treated as abandonware until a new update or new information comes out from the devs.
I can no longer recommend anyone buying the game.

review:
Edit: Im glad we have exhausted the content that it had before they added tons more bugs to the game.
Also im not convinced about the direction the development took.
Coop would need far more features to be worthwhile and the base gameplay needed a ton more mechanics, better AI, more options like having two restaurants and so on.
Instead they add stuff like a bad PvP mode.
But bugs are left unfixed.
It still doesnt matter how the food looks, often not even if its hot served or from a day before.
I can still prepare 20 dishes, store them in a fridge and then microwave the entire day to still get max ratings.
The ultimate skill in this game is to manage 10 microwaves.
Theres still a ton of metrics missing, like visual appeal, dish quality and the AI wont have any interaction with your restaurant besides sitting down and eating.
They arent acting realistic in any way, like looking at stuff, making a selection or speaking with each other.

They need to refocus their development very fast.
But i see that 2025 will already have them finish 1.0 and i assume thats because they want to wrap it up and call it a day.
MORE dishes or restaurants wont make this more fun.
It needs more mechanics that make it more complex and deeper in terms of management and customer variance.
What about Service Quality as a factor thats totally missing?

Add more proper mechanics, not just noise.


---------------------------------

Its a really fun game, if they fix some quirks, bugs and design issues it can become stellar.
Add more recipes and options to create food or manage your guests and its possibly the best food simulator out there, especially due to coop.

Bugs is a bit vague so i describe what type of bugs appeared to me:
- I sliced potatoes to "sliced potatoes", basically wedges. Wanted to create Pomme De Frittes. I placed the wedged into the fryer, but nothing would happen, the wedges wouldnt cook/fry/heat up.
I realized i needed to slice the wedges again, picked them out and sliced them, placed them back into the fryer. The fryer now constantly lists that it has 4 sliced potatoes inside, which ofcourse it doesnt.
This stays for the rest of the game.
Its these types of bugs. Clipping things, physic based bugs, stuff that doesnt get removed or stucks in the air.

Problem 1: The game should allow me to place wedges into the fryer and they should heat up.
In general the game doesnt give you a lot of leeway and freedom to create food or "interpret" recipes. Maybe i wanted to fry wedges instead of Pommes and maybe the guests would love that far more.
Which leads to Problem 2.

Problem 2: The guests are one dimensional. 
They can only come in (and you can only open your shop/restaurant once you have cooked something) once you selected a recipe and serve it.
And they come with one of the offered dishes in mind.
That makes sense, since you do the same in a restaurant in real life.
But that also means i can only offer the food, the game allows me to offer.
So i have potatoes and i have chicken and i have pepper bells. But i can only create chicken with fries and (unsliced) peppers.
I cant, for example, make it Chicken Stripes with Wedges and Sliced Pepper with Sour Cream.
I cant serve the Chicken Filet with Salted Cooked Potatoes instead of fries.
I cant combine ingredients with each other to create a result and the people entering my restaurant wont react to what they get.
Even when we messed up recipes by missing an ingredient etc, they were super happy with it.
I think i never had a situation in my first 2 hours, where a customer went out unhappy with what he or she got, even if burnt stuff or cold fries from the day before.

In a great game, if i could wish for something to drastically improve, i could customize the recipes or outright combine ingredients to create my own.
More like Pizza Connection but without being limited to Pizza.
Let me cook potatoes, grill a steak, a tomato and a pepper, place the stuff on a dish with a bit of ketchup and serve it and then have customers come in, each with their individual taste and preferences randomly applied, eat it and rate it or even leave the restaurant again when they see it wont meet their taste (vegetarians etc? to give an example).

More like a mix between the food creation system of Pizza Connection and the customer mechanic from Rollercoaster Tycoon.
Create something, present it with a certain style and then clash that creation with your customers expectations.
 
Problem 3:
You can cheese the game.
Due to the bugs you can break the game too.
For example, if you go outside and stand in the path of an NPC he will stop and the game code will search for a new path.
Doing that you can lead NPCs into your restaurant.
I just stood outside and blocked them infront of our door to lead them in.



In general the game lacks choice and options combined with some depth in areas that are important to be deeper.
I think customers in a game about serving dishes to people are an integral part i expect to be as deep and complex as they can.
They need to have "opinions" about your restaurant, its outside style, its inside style, the food or the prices (ah yes, you cant adjust prices at all), the taste, the service and even the menu (only mains, sidedishes?, deserts? Drinks?).

But they really dont.

Same goes for the cooking. Its flat. You have predefined recipes and thats it.
You cant even.....empty a cooking pot.
I poured too much water into it when creating soup and i was screwed. Cant pour out water to fix my fault. 
Cant even scrap it entirely (empty the entire pot).
Same goes for heat.
You cant tell whether food is hot or not.
I had a soup pot and wanted to keep it warm/reheat by putting it on the stove.
But when serving it the game told me it was only 53% hot enough, reducing the rating.
But i couldnt tell how hot the stuff was before serving it to people.
Also cant take it out again to reheat it more.

Heat is also basically the only dimension food has.
Theres no skill or other influences to my dishes.
I cant experiment with spices (chili on my chicken? No? Why not?), i cant become better at slicing stuff or preparing meat etc.
It all just comes down to timing in the heating process.
Your only dimension of how good your food will be, depends on how well cooked the ingredients are and how fast you serve it (as it cools down).




If they fix these things and expand the game there, its incredible.

As of now, i recommend it becuase its low priced, has coop, is fun (still) and offers some content.
But due to the above issues theres lacking replayability, lacking options, lacking depth and thus lacking experimentation.

I really hope the devs keep going, as the basis it has is great and has potential.

review:
Let it cook, it is "fun" if you like the cooking portion, or repeatedly making the same meal as a sort of relaxing type of game.

As for a restaurant sim, it seems like theres much to be done especially when we talk about progressing through the game. Microwave trivializes your ability to make items to order in a coordinated fashion so heat is an important mechanic. Aspirations apart from more meals you get fairly passively by just playing thegame seem thin, money doesnt seem to be a real issue you have to manage and the biggest item seems to be an upgraded size restaurant. Gourmets are a nice touch but seem to be pretty simple and static across play-thrus which makes it pretty easy to meta should you have to start your game over. 

At the time of playing there were no rewards for making an elegant looking restaurant outside of bragging rights.  

In general, if you like the cooking piece I'd say get it on sale. If you are looking for the simulation part of managing a restaurant from nook in the wall to world-renowned and feeling rewarded for hitting progression markers, I'd recommend holding off to see where the developers take the game.

review:
This game is terrible. Not just because of the bugs.

 It is an idle game and the trailer is completely deceiving. You make a dish and put it out. The NPC take the same dish over and over again until the dish is just a dirty plate. Had it been a buffet game, this would have made sense. Even then you'd need a buffet table with different textures to show the certain items slowly going down. Not sure how the devs thought this was acceptable. Even One Arm Chef is better and it is a F2P game. 

Blackjack table is a joke. I am talking about the camera that it puts you in. The betting slider, when it wouldn't be to hard to add chips to select amount.. Also, the dev doesn't even know the rules of blackjack.

Drinking is just a meter that goes down while holding your drink. You don't even bring it up to your mouth. People tagged this with physics. This game doesn't use physics at all. It is more of a grid. 

Character customisation is god awful. Make certain parts of your body too big and it just clips through the clothes. It even does this with your beard. 

And the final nail in the coffin is how fast the days go by. What a slog of prepping one of each meal to sit there while the game idles for 10 minutes. All you do is collect money off the table. No till. Grab the plate one at a time. Put them in the sink. Do a an animation to wash. Put each plat back one at a time. Go to sleep. Wake up and prep one of each dish. Collect dishes. Clean them. Clean floors. Maybe if I hire employees I won't be doing nothing at all. 

This game is made by corner cutters for people with no standards. Its a cash grab low effort game that will never be good. What a slog..

The problem here is, as always, its limiting gameplay loop, including but not limited to: amount of dishes, variety of clients, kitchen utensils, recipe assortment, and preparation steps. 

It's a fun concept, but like many other "simulators,"  this one severely lacks the diversification of products and services offered to both the customers (npc) and players alike. The fine threat to dangle upon is to make it easy and fast for challenging gameplay, but with a USP, or to make it just complex and diverse enough for authentic gameplay while still being fun. This game tries to be challenging and fast-paced and bring complex recipes to the table, but both do not mix well. It feels so incredibly slow-paced for a cooking arcade game and, on the other side, absolutely barren for an authentic cooking sim.

Hard pass atm.

review:
Reviewing this game is tough. I enjoy the game and find the mundane operations of a motel/store/gas station engaging. I keep playing it for that reason, despite the critiques below, but definitely feel a certain sense of discomfort with it.

CODING/DESIGN
The game is unpolished in a number of ways (example: buttons or signs that I assume were placed to rectify an issue, but that do not blend in at all) and there are UI things that bug me (example: lists of items that are not alphabetised or sorted in any sensical manner). Some of the people have weirdly proportioned bodies.

DEPICTION OF WOMEN
This very much comes across as a game created by white, hetero men in their early 20s. Is that actually the case? Who knows. The number of women scantily dressed is irritating, as is the specific attention it took to animate some women's skirts blowing up with the breeze a la Marilyn Monroe. Some of the women also sport a sashaying strut that is irritating.
I deactivated it immediately, so I don't know how it actually plays out in the game, but my impression is that the dead bodies in the rooms are often/usually prostitutes. I'm not real keen on the dehumanisation of a vulnerable population. 

ESTHETIC
I think that a lot of my critiques can be summed up by saying that the esthetic rubs me the wrong way. I get that the developers were going for a certain vibe and obviously that is a pretty subjective thing, but the presence of dead bodies, only dirty cops, and robberies that can only be solved with a shot gun just aren't things that I find fun or entertaining. Again, I totally get that for some folks those elements are pluses rather than minuses. I am grateful that those elements can be turned off.

I can't recommend it at the moment. It's got way too many bugs. TLDR - It's got a strong start, but it falls apart quickly. I'd suggest watching a few let's plays on Youtube first, then wait till it's heavily discounted.

It starts out fine, you go about running your fledgling motel: decorating, furnishing and cleaning the rooms. Subsidising your income with a gas pump and selling the occasional chocolate bar and soda.

However once you start growing (about 8-10 hours in) and become dependant on staff the game utterly falls apart.

The employees are completely useless with the possible exception of the gas pumper:

The cashier - often bugs out and just freezes resulting in an ever growing queue of increasingly furious customers. 

The cleaner - cleans 1 thing at a time and seemingly takes forever to clean anything specific (i.e. the motel rooms)

Warehouse assistant (stocker) - Carries 1 box at a time (as opposed to the player who carries 5) and then slowwwwly moves things from the warehouse to the store. They also completely ignore the fact that large bottles only fit in the large slots and so you forever have large bottles clogging up the warehouse as the buffoon has filled the large spaces in fridges with tiny cans.

The housekeeper - By far the worst. She takes an eternity to ready the rooms, carrying one object at a time, then running back to the warehouse to get a towel, then running back to the room to pick up the dirty sheets. USE THE CART YOU MORON.

Then on top of that the process of hiring out rooms is buggy as well. Say you have 4 rooms, well after you've hired out the fourth you'd think the giant Vacancies/No Vacancies sign you spent $1000 on would stop further people enquiring every minute if you have a spare room. Nope, you have to manually turn off the motel part of the business. Then manually turn it back on again when you have a spare room. Awesome.

Stock management is a nightmare. Especially once you unlock the bus station upgrade. Pricing is a pain too as you can't shift prices up and down with arrow buttons, you have to type in a numerical value for each of the dozens of items. Periodically manually changing it as needed.

In the end I had to stop as it was just painful.

review:
This game has potential, but it plays like an Early Access game... like a VERY early access game. There are several bugs. 

• Sometimes your workers just stop working, and its a total pain to get them to start again. 

• The "Run" function (holding shift while moving) just stops working, kinda random but it stops working EVERY TIME for me after I use it like 3-4 times.

• At the beginning of the game you get these little quests like "add an additional room", Fuel 20 cars / Sell 20 items / Rent 10 rooms" etc. but these stop very early in the game. Having these incentives continue would make the game better.

review:
Gosh as someone who rarely writes negative reviews, I just wouldn't recommend Sengoku Dynasty to anyone, especially if your coming from Medieval Dynasty. Before I discuss my complaints, I would like to say after reading through other users negative reviews I noticed there are some serious die hard fans who refuse to hear criticism of this game. It gets to the point they just resort to insulting people and making nasty comments which is disappointing to see. The whole point of the steam review feature is to share your thoughts and experience, which yes can be subjective but who are you to judge someones experience. If you dissagree just keep scrolling and grow up, does it really affect you that someone on the otherside of the world doesn't like your comfort game, just childish.

Now when it comes to game design, there needs to be a hook, no game ever should be a "just give it a chance" kind of game. People need that hook that will get them immersed into the game world. Coming from Medieval Dynasty this fell flat. Of the top I noticed the WHOLE DYNASTY SYSTEM ISN'T EVEN THERE, you don't age and there is no heir system from what I know, which kind of kills the whole "building a village for future generations" idea from Medieval Dynasty. That is what made that game so special after all. Some people may get butthurt over that say "Well Beck, their both two different games it's gonna be different" THEY ARE BOTH IN THE DYNASTY GAME SERIES SURELY IT'S NOT UNREASONABLE TO ASSUME THEY'D BE SIMILAR!!!! You can't even drink water, like who make a survival game without a water system?

Visually it looks cheap, and I would usually let that go as graphics are not something I care about too much, however it is terribly optimised so it has terrible performance even with a high end system. I as well as people I play with experience numerous visual artefacts such as buildings not loading in for other players even when standing beside them.

A massive issue I have is the world building, in Medieval Dynasty, the world is full, literally. Walk into a town and tell me how many bit and pieces you can pick up, wether its pots and buckets or even swords and bows. Almost all objects you find you can pick up or open. Even in bandit camps or random places of interest which is completely random, there is still so many items just laying around. The world feels so much more interactable. In Sengoku it feels empty, the first bandit settlement I raided had all these little items all around the place, COULDN'T BLOODY GRAB THEM THOUGH. It feels so dead and lifeless. I hope other people feel the same way.

The combat is an issue I have seen come up in reviews already, it's horrible, even worse in first person, WHICH IS LIKELY WHY EVERY TIME YOU WATCH THE DEVS PLAY LIVE OR RELEASE A TRAILER, IT'S ALL THIRD PERSON. It feels cheap and out of place, like even when hunting it feels like a turn based game with it's goofy lock on system.  The bodies of fallen foes also despawn half a second after their killed, leaving a sack of loot behind. This makes it feel like a mobile game.

I can't comment on every detail this game has to offer, as I never stuck around to try it all. Again that first hour is the most important, I wasn't hooked and it felt like a downgrade so I refunded simple as that. I tried to give it a chance but it fell flat and left me craving more. I hope this review will help you in your decision to purchase.

Things that are different/better are being able to liberate regions across the map andddd that's about it. 

Things that are not that good:
-It is very difficult to balance the needs of your villages. The maintenance of the village is gonna kill your resources.
-The production buildings are huge, but the area in which you can build is small. So you are quickly going to run out of space in your village.
-The NPC are very NPC like, there is no funny interactions and quests. Mostly it's just "arigato" and "sayonara" that's about it.
-There are less options for furniture and decorating.
-The workers don't have skill sets, so if you assign them to work somewhere else you are not gonna remember where you should bring them back afterwards.
-Making their working stations near their houses is not of any help, because houses do not have managing boards that help  you can check who lives there.
-If they work in a field you can't help them work in that field so that they finish faster. Once they are assigned to a field only that NPC can work on it.
-NPCs can't get married or have kids.
-There are no animals or animal product.
-If you want to craft their daily needs and you wanna make 100 food items you are gonna have to wait for all 100 items to be crafted one by one.
-There are no market stalls that you can build to sell your items at ( if you manage to have items to sell considering how difficult it is to stack anything).
-Money wise you are limited to how much NPCs can trade you for which is around 700 gold per season.
-If you can 20 logs in the nature your inventory is full, because they don't stack and each log takes one slot of your inventory, same with tools.

I am disappointed but, you might not be. So take it with a grain of salt and try it anyway :D

It can be pretty, but the game itself is quite shallow. Grindy, in an almost zen-like fashion -- so long as you avoid the combat. The game loop's simple; gather resources, build things, recruit people, rinse and repeat. Which would be fine if not for the flaws in the other half of the game: combat.

The fighting itself is incredibly frustrating. You have enemies that instantly recover from a poise break in melee, making anything other than a katana or a knife quite worthless. At range, the AI is unsatisfying to fight at best; they will route back to their original spot if shot from a far enough distance, regardless of whether or not they can see you after approaching. It honestly makes the Skyrim AI's sneak response look good, and that's saying something.

Melee is problematic as well. Fighting without lock-on would be fine if it adhered to the standard Dark Souls rules. But when you fight against multiple targets, your melee attacks will suddenly lock on to the nearest target instead of where you're facing. Fighting with lock-on will break if the enemy gets into knife-fighting range, making it completely worthless for the one situation it's supposed to be for.

Performance wise, this game is HORRIBLY optimised. In busy areas, rotating the camera around will get noticeable frame skipping and dropping, probably due to loading in assets and entities when they enter the view of the camera. This is particularly frustrating when you're dealing with multiple enemies at once, and the game decides to drop a half-second lag spike in your face.

Verdict: pretty, enjoy it for the scenery and for the zen-like grind. The action and fighting aren't very good.

Updating my review after playing the new updates and I'm sad to say that it's just not what I was hoping for. This game sits in between Bellwright (combat focused) and Medieval Dynasty (farming+building focused), and it feels not good enough on doing either of those aspects.

On base building, it still feels a little weird when half of my NPCs just doze off during the day but the materials would magically appear at end of day. It seems the game would do one final calculation every night. This kills the immersion aspect because the fun part of playing a village sim is watching the villagers doing their assigned tasks and carrying the goods back and forth. I assign a guy to go work on a farm plot, he stands there like an idiot, then the system says everyone finished their job, a stack of parsley goes into my storage, smh. 

-Still no "max amount" button when assigning tasks, you have to hold the plus sign every time, for every task.
-You either deposit one item, or hold E for depositing EVERYTHING into storage. Why no keybind for depositing one stack?

On combat, we still cannot equip our villagers with armor and bring them along to go on journeys. What's the point of giving them a weapon when they get one-shot by the raiding samurais?

The villagers feel more like a burden than helping me in anyway. Recruit a few of them, assign all of them to gather food and cook food. Recruit a few more, water is required, send new recruits to get water. Then heating, then health, then maintenance requirement. No matter how many I recruit, I have to worry about fulfilling their needs instead of helping me nor helping the village. It's always about villager needs.

It's great that the devs are still working on the game, but we keep getting more content such as skins, weapons, enemies, etc. Maybe dial back on new content but instead focus on village QoL improvements.

review:
Sengoku Dynasty, an ambitious blend of survival, building, and open-world exploration, aims to transport players into feudal Japan with community-building mechanics and immersive gameplay. Unfortunately, while the concept is promising, the game currently struggles with significant technical issues that undermine the overall experience.

Performance and Stability Issues:
The most pressing problem is the game’s poor optimization and unstable performance. Frequent lag spikes disrupt gameplay, and the game often becomes unresponsive for several minutes before recovering. In addition, full crashes occur on occasion, forcing progress to be lost. These problems make it difficult to enjoy the game as intended and contribute to a frustrating experience. Because of this, I currently cannot recommend Sengoku Dynasty to most players. Unless you are a true fan of survival games and are willing to commit despite the technical setbacks, it may be wiser to put your money toward a more stable title at this time.

Gameplay Impact:
Much of my time spent in Sengoku Dynasty was devoted to troubleshooting or waiting for the game to respond rather than actively playing. This prevented me from fully experiencing the depth of the survival, crafting, and settlement-building systems the game offers, and it made the gameplay feel frustrating and tedious.

Potential and Promise:
Despite these issues, Sengoku Dynasty does show promise. The setting, concept, and scale of ambition could create a unique experience if performance concerns are properly addressed. With improved stability and optimizations, the game could grow into a strong entry in the survival-building genre.

Conclusion:
At its current state, Sengoku Dynasty is hindered by severe lag, lengthy freezes, and frequent crashes, making it difficult to recommend for most players. Only those who are deeply invested in the survival genre and willing to work around the current problems may find value here. For everyone else, it may be best to wait for significant updates before considering a purchase.

review:
Utterly disappointing after Medieval Dynasty. From the start it greets you with poor performance even though the visual doesn't really differ from MD. It seems bigger but it lacks features that made Medieval Dynasty great.
1. Population management. 
Villagers can't form families and can't have kids, so you just cram people randomly into houses with maximum available number of beds.
2. Job management
Villagers don't have stats, so you just recruit whoever and assign any job. And it will be done at the fixed time of the day regardless of when you assigned the job.
3. Crop management
A single field can grow only one type of crops when operated by villagers and it does it on the same fixed hour. There are no stages through different seasons and there's no actual work on the field done by the villagers — everything just grows on itself when a villager is assigned to the field.

But instead we have:
1. Bandits that respawn at numerous indestructible small camps scattered around the world every season.
2. Clunky combat system that feels like it was designed just for the sake of it.
3. Annoying raids instead of taxes.
4. Progress that's locked by the "occupied regions" that you have to "liberate" or you won't have efficient recipes to sustain your growing villages. But to liberate said regions you have to grow your villages without those recipes.
5. Broken economy (there are numerous merchants in the world but there's no point to bother growing crops to sell it as crops are extremely cheap. Instead you can get insanely rich by just chiseling rocks).
6. AI-art

I tried to love this game, I gave it a lot of chances.
But trying to build a farming village finally broke me. I tried to find a relatively flat plain to build my fields, but even a 5x5 field (which is a maximum for a villager to work on, even though the field itself can be up to 8x8) is a pain in the a** to place because of the "lack of flat surface".
I just can't anymore...

review:
I find it hilarious that the main menu image depicts a pretty cool game with attractive looking characters, and then when you actually get into the game, you have a bunch of grandpa/granny faces with the most limited and basic character customization ever. 

That's what Sengoku Dynasty feels like, an advertisement of a hamburger. It looks all juicy, plump, and rich looking. But when you buy the actual burger, its flat, squashed, sauce all over the place, buns aren't aligned, and they forgot the cheese.

Not only does all the characters look ugly with a ultra simple and limited character customization, you have-

A really bad combat system where enemies can't be read through animations at all. Whether they are stunned, or knocked on their arse, the animation is janky and has no in-between moments. So a guy flat on his ass will shoot back up and start attacking you. Enemies you think are 'stun locked' will just start swinging at you without a moments notice.

Badly dumbed down version of Medieval Dynasty. Only 1 worker can be assigned to a building, you cant upgrade it. All you can do is build another huge work table inside the already-small building to assign more workers. What do you get with a brainded AI npc? They either just teleport or get stuck in/on table walking forever in place. Actually the work doesn't even need the AI's to actually be at the table, so you can just make a building filled to the brim with tables if you don't mind seeing jank AI everywhere.

Villages is really bad. You have to satisfy not only food and water, but maintenance, security, medicine, etc etc. How do you satisfy them? By getting your villagers to work in specific buildings. But they need tools to do work, how do you get them? By putting npcs in buildings to produce them. But you need resources to make tools, what now? Put npcs into buildings to get resources. But the farming seed bags can't be produced until way later in the game, how can we farm? By grinding for it through other means. The village mechanic is not only tedious, but very annoying to manage due to the clunky management UI. When assigning jobs, you can't even see what's listed for the very bottom people because another UI hud is blocking it.

You have jittering tree and log physics... Trees you cut down are so jank, they fall at 15 fps.

Swimming kills you, literally. If you plunge into deep waters it actually just takes a chunk of your health, not stamina.

I could go on but I don't see the point. The only thing this had going for me is the fact that it's set in Feudal Japan. Other than that, Medival Dynasty is by far better designed and polished than this is. Even if you level the playing field, and go back a couple updates on Medieval to match with Sengoku, Medieval takes the win. The only reason I'm bringing up Medieval is because they both have the same publisher. Actually, Toplitz Productions seems to green light a lot of these Base Building games. So do your research, and beware when buying from them. Some are good, some are bad like this one.

review: I wanted to like this game, and there are some things to like. I can't just ignore the two sides of positive and negative. First, the positive. The world is actually very attractive, and into the game when you go through the flight of the world when you reach the tower that is stunning. Many of the views you have when traveling are wonderful to see. Visiting other villages was interesting. Hunting small game, is fun as is growing your village. What is the downsides? Your village is severely hampered, adding villagers is easy, but once you have them the demands greatly outweigh the benefits. Production received from foraging is insignificant, you have to build repetitive numbers of foraging, harvesting, and other types of production to give food, drink, etc to your villagers. There will never be enough. Diversification of building types and jobs is minimal. You will need to just produce everything and hunt to feed your villagers because they're pretty worthless. You will constantly run out of materials, having to run into the woods to collect sticks or logs for a few walls and setting up production will not matter because again the production vs use is so out of balance. An example, foraging, you need to select what is to be foraged, everything is a percentage of time, want a single mushroom? It may take 18%, want some berry? 22%, next thing you know your villagers is collecting 6 or 7 things a day which by themselves aren't useful and they are completely out because the consumption exceeds it. Want to farm? I was pretty excited about the idea I could take over new territory and build camps in each of them, but when I got to my second area I found out you can have a max number of 100 villagers across the entire map. With the number of villagers it takes to run the different buildings and the constant effort to try and get enough of a single resource you find out quickly that 100 is a joke, that when you want to sort of make things work in your main village you have to have 35 or more villagers there, and to setup production elsewhere it doesn't make sense to the number of territories vs the small number of villagers you can have. Hunting is painful, shoot a deer with an arrow and they'll run, then you spend the next several minutes just trying to run after it. They have not masterfully combined any aspect, each aspect of the game feels like they put in the bare minimum thought. This game was very fun for the first hour, but from there it just continues to go downhill.

review:
I played Medieval Dynasty for nearly 90 hours, and really enjoyed it, so I thought I would try this game. I don't know how a game 3 years older than this one beats it in seemingly every metric:

Graphics - even on max settings this looks worse than MD, the characters look like something pulled from an asset pack (weirdly spindly, basically no options for customisation)

Animation: I only played for a very short time, but I saw all I needed to - The attack animations are stiff and jerky, and the run animation looks like my character crapped himself. Much like the art style of the characters, the animations look very much like they were grabbed out of an asset pack and used without much thought.

UI: They tried to go for a more stylised UI than Medieval Dynasty had, with a kind of parchment effect on the map and inventory UI. Leaving aside this is really cliche (like using the papyrus font for your school report on Egypt), it's also a lot less clear than MD's UI, the icons in the inventory are massive, and the map seems blurry. They didn't use this style on the boxes when you are talking to NPCs though, just a basic box, which seems too big yet also manages to have kerning and text alignment issues. Also, it's a small thing, but MD had numbers next to your response options so you could press the number on your keyboard instead of clicking, which this one doesn't have.

New player experience: In Medieval Dynasty you start on a road, with a clear goal and a nice waypoint to show you where to go. In SD you are plopped on a beach and told to find someone, with seemingly no waypoint or method of finding them. I brought the map up to try and get some clue and was bombarded with information about becoming a Daimyo and taking over territory. This was overwhelming for someone with lots of hours in Medieval Dynasty, I can't imagine how bad an experience this would be for someone new to these games. 

In conclusion this game just looks and feels awful to play. If you enjoyed Medieval Dynasty, make sure you check plenty of videos about this game before making a decision because this is really not a sequel or improvement over the previous game in any way.

I...I just can't. Look, I'm going to wind up playing more because it's my "Jank Night with Friends" game night, but can I suggest others spend money on this? No. No I cannot. There is just too much that sucks about it. They put out 78962346 of these games and it's all the same junk with a new coat of paint - emphasis on junk. It ticks survival crafting boxes and that is it.

You start with stone tools, get copper, bronze, iron, steel...I'm on iron now, and nothing feels different. They're no faster, they don't gather more, they don't last longer. But I have them, and some things require I have them. Box checked.

You have a food meter, and you have food. The food meter has a numerical representation, and food items say "X Food". Except...that variable is completely fucking worthless because it never restores as much as it says. I eat a 60 food item with 50 food missing and MY FOOD ISN'T FULL! Box checked though!

You have weapons and armor.
There are enemies to fight.
Hahahahaha holy freaking poop IT SUCKS! Box checked though.

One of the most egregious boxes though? There is gravity. Gravity means fall damage. Except fall damage is...negated by armor...'cause plummeting six stories naked kills you, but that same fall in steel armor? Barely a sprained ankle. Box. Fucking. Checked.

Now, a lot of this could be because I'm not host in a multiplayer game, and that CLEARLY comes with problems. A lot of perks I unlock clearly don't do fudge all unless I reconnect, and even then...only if it feels like it.

This game EXISTS. It is - technically - functional in that you can launch it and play it. Is it GOOD though? No. No it isn't. Don't spend full price, and only play with people to laugh at the jank as your friend scream "BUT WHY THOUGH?!"

review:
By it's core, this is a decent game if you consider it an "Adventure Game".
But if it's "Dynasty" part of ruling the village, they have serious issues to fix.

This is one of those game that, if you managed to create a production-logistic cycle where everyone compliment each other,
then you can just leave them there to stack the number.

Under most normal circumstances, this would be a bad management game.
But it actually helped in this case, because the Management UI has LOTS of Bugs in it.
If you are playing with a Controller, the cursor on the UI could jump anywhere.

Each time you get a new Villager, you have to scroll down to the last person in the list.
If you have a big community, this alone might take nearly a minute to solve.
IN, GAMETIME as well, because the Game doesn't pause when you do this.

If you are a micro-manager Player, then you won't have time to go adventuring,
which is needed in order to unlock higher stuffs.

_________

The combat is actually decent, but in a Soul-like way than other games in the same Genre.

Even though you have Villagers under your rule,
you can't bring them to the fight with you.

And most of the Enemies are stronger than you are.

Unless you are a Veteran Souls Player,
you will have to rely on lure - then hit and run to clear off Enemy Camps.
Which isn't really that fun.
Luckily, the DEV realized this, so you can turn on an Immortality mode in the option.

________________

Suggestions on how to improve.

- Fix the Management UI for Controllers
-- Add more Sort Options, as well as auto-assign Villagers to houses and empty Work Position.

- Allow Villagers to join you in Battle.

- Before placing the Village Bell,
Hilight / explain the Resources in the vicinity of the Bell.
Even if you are in an area with minerals, 
Miners won't go find them unless the building has Mineral in its vicinity.

- Option to destroy the Village Bell, so we can relocate the Village.

- Option to rename Village and travelling posts.

review:
Sengoku Dynasty – When "Dynasty" Means Downgrade

If you ever wondered what Medieval Dynasty would be like if it lost a bet and had to wear its cousin's hand-me-downs, welcome to Sengoku Dynasty! It takes everything its older sibling did… and does it slightly worse. Every. Single. Thing.

Let’s break it down:

Graphics? Imagine Medieval Dynasty but after eating some bad sushi. The textures feel like they took a vow of simplicity, and the lighting makes me wonder if feudal Japan was just permanently overcast.

Mechanics? Think Medieval Dynasty, but with all the screws a little loose. Movement feels off, combat is about as smooth as a rice field in a drought, and every action seems like it needs an extra step—because, why not?

Building? I hope you enjoy watching your character struggle to place structures in the most unintuitive way possible! In Medieval Dynasty, building was a pleasure. Here, it’s more of a meditation exercise in patience.

Combat? If you’ve ever wanted to fight enemies with the intensity of two drunk samurais trying to swat a fly, this is your game. The AI attacks with the coordination of a toddler wielding a broom.

Story? There is one…  But like a missing katana in the mud, it’s hard to find and even harder to care about.

Despite all of this, the game could be fun if you enjoy open-world survival and have a high tolerance for jank. Maybe one day with enough patches, Sengoku Dynasty will be worthy of the “Dynasty” name. But for now, it feels like the "bargain-bin" edition of its predecessor.

Final Verdict: 5/10 – Needs more honor and polish.

review:
I recommend playing this game, BUT NOT NOW, maybe in a year or two.

The game has a wonderful setting, interesting mechanics, beautiful world design. If you don't go through the game to the end, you will even have positive emotions.

Now the minuses, mostly they start from the second half of the game. 
1. If you play with friend, be prepared for the game will lag. Running, and especially fighting with opponents will be almost impossible. And if the host is still more or less can play, but the one who is connected suffers from these problems is much stronger.
2. Terrible production manager, no sorting, no search. And if in the beginning it is not so noticeable, then by the end of the game you get tired of scrolling and looking for the elements you need.
3. Bugs in the combat system. Damage may not register, arrows may be stuck in the air in front of you, enemies are stuck in place, or move with wild speed. Don't expect difficult fights, because the opponents have a terrible AI.
4. There are also bugs in the production of items. You spend resources on production, but the items themselves are not created. And this is not an exceptional problem. Almost 25% of production is useless because of this, because nothing is produced.
5. The game has memory leaks, in 2 hours of play it would consistently crash 1-2 times. Very annoying. And mostly it happens during autosaves.
6. Uncompleted dynasty quest. You can't physically finish it, because they just haven't finished it)))) Cool, huh?
7. And a bunch of small bugs, such as - not correctly counting experience (I think in the last patch corrected, but still not completely), glitches in the use of items, etc. It's like the game is still in early access, it's not ready.


I give this game 2 hara-kiri out of 10.

-------------------------------------------------------

Я рекомендую поиграть в эту игру, НО НЕ СЕЙЧАС, может быть, через год или два.

В игре прекрасный сеттинг, интересная механика, красивый дизайн мира. Если вы не пройдете игру до конца, то у вас даже останутся положительные эмоции.

Теперь о минусах, в основном они начинаются со второй половины игры. 
1. Если вы играете с другом, будьте готовы к тому, что игра будет лагать. Бегать, а тем более драться с противниками будет практически невозможно. Причем если на хосте еще более-менее можно играть, то тот, кто подключен, страдает от этих проблем гораздо сильнее.
2. Ужасный менеджер производства, никакой сортировки, никакого поиска. И если в начале это не так заметно, то к концу игры устаешь прокручивать и искать нужные тебе элементы.
3. Баги в боевой системе. Урон может не регистрироваться, стрелы могут зависнуть в воздухе перед вами, враги застревают на месте или двигаются с дикой скоростью. Не ждите сложных боев, потому что у противников ужасный ИИ.
4. Также есть баги в производстве предметов. Вы тратите ресурсы на производство, но сами предметы не создаются. И это не исключительная проблема. Почти 25% производства из-за этого бесполезно, потому что ничего не производится.
5. В игре есть утечки памяти, за 2 часа игры она постоянно падала 1-2 раза. Очень раздражает. И в основном это происходит во время автосохранений.
6. Незаконченный квест про династию. Вы физически не можете его закончить, потому что его просто не доделали)))). Круто, да?
7. И куча мелких багов, таких как - не корректный подсчет опыта (вроде в последнем патче исправили, но все равно не до конца), глюки при использовании предметов и т.д. Такое ощущение, что игра все еще в раннем доступе, она не готова.

review:
Honestly had good hopes going into the game, everything seemed pretty promising but I feel like the execution is poor.
-The combat takes a bit to get used to and is still a bit wonky, but not completely terrible.
-The cost of upkeep is beyond absurd and despite attempting to look up guides there isn't a clear in game way to help you improve how much your villagers bring in farming (fishing at least seems easy with the net, but the level of detail with tools is stupid).
-Half of the game there is mild indicators where you can find resources but for the most part you will be relying on merchants to get what you need, so good luck getting goods if you don't like clearing bandit camps.
-Technology is locked by region and not resource, and it is a pain in the rear trying to get materials to improve while baby sitting your own people.

name: Sengoku Dynasty

review:
Can’t recommend the game.
There are just too many issues, bugs, and signs that the game isn’t properly polished.

You can clear an entire bandit camp using three basic bows and around 70 starting stone arrows. Enemies often skip animations or don’t play them at all. The most irritating part? When enemies swap weapons — during the weapon-swap animation, they somehow still manage to shoot you instantly, giving you no time to defend. Sometimes they even fire two arrows in under half a second. Arrows track you unnaturally, melee enemies can stun-lock you, and overall combat feels unfair and inconsistent.

Building a village or town isn’t satisfying either. There’s no reason to care about layout or management — you can just throw all your buildings in a straight line and call it a day. Why? Because resources are magically added at the end of each season. Villagers don’t actually go out to gather or perform any tasks; they’re just decorations.

Item values make no sense. You can sell a 20% durability bow for 0.10, but buy the same one for 40.

Exploration feels pointless. There’s nothing meaningful to discover besides a few predetermined locations.

The AI is more “A” than “I.” The village requirements scale absurdly fast, making progression feel forced rather than natural.

Quests are few and far between — and none of them are fun. The story barely scrapes above a 0/10.

To make matters worse, the game even trolls you sometimes. I once saved, quit, came back later — and immediately got killed by two hogs that spawned behind me.

Combat also has major problems with stamina and blocking. Even when I have enough stamina and hold ALT to defend, I still get hit for no clear reason.

Finally, the clutter and looting system are frustrating. There’s no clear indication of what’s lootable — except for a few crates with lanterns — and the world is filled with objects that look identical, some of which can be looted and others can’t. It’s confusing and lazy design.

Overall: The game has potential, but right now it’s broken, unbalanced, and not fun to play. Unless it gets a major overhaul, I can’t recommend it at all.

review:
Updating the review after few hours in full release version.

Well, as I expected, nothing changed. The game still feels like some early beta or day 1 of EA. Let me breakdown what it has and what it hasn't. I wish there was a 'double negative" or something. This game is an example of how it looks when not a single person in team gives a shit about the game.

First, pros:
- the graphics are ok. I've just upgraded my PC so I have smooth 165 FPS on max settings and it looks ok.
- building mechanic from Medieval Dynasty is still there and engaging.
- combat is ok too. A bit clunky, but pretty fun.

Now, to cons, I hope you've got some tea, food and water supplies for a month, because the list is infinite: 

- game has no management challenge, like, at all. Only challenge is lack of basic UI features. 
All you do is build a building, set an NPC to it and get free resources. You need like 5 NPCs in your town and set what they produce once. They will produce immense amount of resources, so you'll never be in need for anything until you reach some new resource requirement.

NPCs are free. You don't spend anything, you don't need to meet any requirements to invite them, they are all literally waiting for you to come say "you are my slave now" and they say "ok" and start working.

NPCs don't have any skills or stats. They are all exactly same, all equally effective at anything, no management needed.

NPCs require amounts of food and water, but not type. Stack 1000 of raw basic vegetables and they will be happy with their food forever. 

NPCs don't require anything in their houses. They need a house and a bed made of grass in it and they are happy forever. No point in decorating or improving their beds.

All resources are being spawned in your storage out of thin air. NPCs don't do anything but playing animations in this game, just like in Medieval Dynasty. You don't have to think where to place your village, coz you don't need to make sure there are trees around or smth. Only the fishing building requires a water to place, but all the resources are just being spawned in your storage by the end of each day in exact amount you set in production buildings. Logistics, town layout to place production and storage conveniently to cut delivery times? Forget it, nothing is being moved or delivered. Everything is just being teleported. 

- there are lots of weird design decisions in production chains. 

To make a fishing net you need a rope, and for rope you need straw.
You can make straw by your hands from grass, but there's no such recipe in any workbench or building. So if you want to sustain your fisherman you need to make 40 straw out of grass by your own hands daily and put it in storage. You can automate ropes and nets, but not the straw. 

To water your plants you need buckets of water. You can collect water from a well, but to put it in a bucket to water your plants you need to craft a bucket, put it in well, wait for water, collect the water BUT NOT A BUCKET from a well, create new bucket and then create a bucket with water on a workbench. The genius who designed this must receive some special reward. 

You need to provide your foresters with an axes to make them collect wood. But you need a separate axe for each work. E.g., if you set 10 coniferous logs and 10 deciduous logs you need 2 axes even though it's the same workstation and same single worker. And that's going for each workstation in the game. You need to provide your hunter with 4 knives if you want them to gather all 4 types of resources at once, and it's a single hunter.

- UI is horrendous. There's no such basic features as sorting lists, income/outcome charts or sheets, lookup etc. All you get in terms of buildings management is a chronological list. So if your first and tenth buildings are woodcutters and you want to manage their production you go to first building in the list, manage it, then to tenth building in the list and manage it to. No copy settings button, are you surprised?

All you get in terms of resource management is a notice that workers had produced all their stuff and consumed all they need, and after that if you want to check how much of what they produced, consumed and how much of what resources remains you have to go to your storage yourself and look how much of what you have in here. No UI to check storage inventory, no charts, nothing. It's v1.0 of the town management sim btw.

The wheel of buildings, yes not a list, a wheel, is a literal torture. Tabs inside tabs inside tabs inside tabs... 

- more weird design decisions.

You want to get rid of bandits in the region? You think killing them all will solve the raids problem? Haha, no, they will just respawn when new season starts. To actually get rid of them you need to go to their camp, kill everyone there, then build a special building, put certain resources inside and make some of your villagers "work" there till the end of the season. After that the camp despawnes and new bandits won't spawn here. Very immersive.

I can go on and on and on, there's literally couple of okay things and a ton of weird, undercooked or just straightforward scamming features, which were introduced just for the sake of being listed in ads and on Steam page. They technically are in the game, but not playable or enjoyable.

This game is a scam, it was never intended to be a product to provide fun to the customer. I bet not a single person on the team cared about anything in it, because nothing in it was made with any interest or understanding why and how it should work. They've just put all necessary features for a marketing, made enough minimum of them so they are technically are in the game and released it. Calling this a game is a big exaggeration really.

review:
This is going to be a great game when its finished and I enjoyed it for a bit despite the issues. However, they have solved very few of the bugs in the last several months and have actually introduced many more in the process - so atm its a Not Recommend from me. Wait until they sort themselves out.

Technically this game should not really be a 1.0 release. They are still in the process of adding important game features, like the whole dynasty element, and still working out some very frustrating bugs and awful performance issues.

[u]Pros:[/u]
- The game creates a great atmosphere surrounding the Sengoku period of Japan, which feels quite pleasant and authentic. All NPCs speak a short line in Japanese when spoken to, which is a nice touch.
- The graphics are beautiful and the animations very good (or they were before the latest update).
- The building system is a nice improvement over early Medieval Dynasty. You can move buildings after they've been built and name them, which makes village planning a lot easier. Buildings can be upgraded to provide more storage, crafting spots, sleeping spaces etc by adding furniture to them rather than needing to build a new tier on top of them.
- The combat is decent and reasonably intricate, although a little unresponsive.
- The map is much larger and much more alive than MD, with multiple villages to build in different regions, and various goals and quests to complete.

[u]Cons:[/u]
- Performance is still a big issue. Stuttering, fps issues, very noticeable freezes when changing areas or moving towards/away from large villages. I can't decide whether the latest update made this better or worse. Performance is not good.
- There is no dynasty element to Sengoku Dynasty. You can marry and have a child but that child never grows up and is currently little more than an accessory. Villagers also do not marry or have children, so your villages do not grow organically, with families.
- Villagers are all essentially identical. They don't have an age or any stats or skills. They are just either male or female - thats it. And most look exactly the same due to a lack of hairstyles, body types and faces.
- Villager animations now seem to be messed up after the latest update. They frequently stutter when performing actions or moving around.
- The villager AI is not good. They rarely turn up to their correct places of work and often either wander around aimlessly, get stuck somewhere, or all inexplicably gather in one random spot for no reason.
- The village UI doesn't provide nearly enough info to organise an efficient society, with simple things missing like sorting for buildings, or info on tool usage. MD handled this much better.
- Crafting buildings cannot handle jobs that require more than 1 tool at a time. So you end up having to build more of them than you might like.

Development seems to be quite slow on this title, but hopefully it will continue at a better pace in the future. I don't think it is worth buying right now, but hopefully at some point in the future it will be if the devs can finally get ontop of all these bugs (and many more new ones!).

review:
I want to love the game but it really was released far too early. Some examples:

- The very worst, but many of the enemy AI are broken. Like legit maybe one/third of an enemy camp will mill around and refuse to retaliate as you cut them down. It is astounding that the game was released in a state where the enemies were broken, on top of all of the other problems below. The enemies that DO work have very little difference between them aside from their hp and the weapon they wield, which is 100% melee weapons and never a bow like you can get very early in the game. Standing on a box or rock and shooting them is a 100% sure way to kill any enemy in the game. While I can keep myself from cheesing enemies, it's nonetheless a gaping flaw.

- Of similar importance, the actual "Dynasty" portion of the game is NOT IMPLEMENTED. It's A CORE FEATURE of the series this game represents and it is not yet implemented in version 1.0. You can talk to a potential spouse, court them instantly by talking to them once and confirming the decision, pay a bunch of money, and you'll be given a child. This child does nothing and does not grow up, it may as well be a backpack for your spouse to carry around. That's the ENTIRE mechanic. It was truly released too early.

- The village management UI is terrible, with no way to organize or sort villagers or jobs, they are listed simply in the order in which they were created. So if you need to hunt down all of your woodcutters to change their production, you'd need to find each wooding cutting job you created since the founding of the village and change each one, one by one. Every task has a ticker for the production amount which you can raise or lower by mashing to click or by holding down the mouse for a long time, something absolutely any other game would have introduced a slider or [select all] button to resolve.

- The villagers themselves are extremely bland, use the same few faces and sets of ragged clothing, and have absolutely nothing else distinguishing them aside from their name. They get stuck on objects and mill around, picking objects seemingly at random to interact with. It isn't unusual to come home to your house and have 5 or 6 random villagers picking through your shelves just because they are valid interaction points.

- The game lags. You can play it alone or play it with friends, but either way, even with a most definitely well enough computer, the game will slow down considerably when it loads alot of content. Even turning down the settings for loaded plants and such to the minimum does little to assuage the problem.

Despite having fun with it early on before I grew disillusioned to all the issues above, I could not in any good conscience recommend anyone pay money to buy this game. It is not ready for sale at all.

review:
[h1]
Let's begin with this:
[/h1]
Disappointment can be described as the difference between expectation and result. Perhaps my expectation is too high or the result is too low, but I will try to justify my opinion regarding various portions of the game as of:
Release Version	1.0.1.1
Build	2024.50.8.18900_prod
And why I have hopes for its future but cannot recommend the game in its current state (even though I have 300+ hrs play time)

(* Note I purchased this as a package with medieval dynasty same publisher different developer)

[h1]
Developer/Publisher Interaction (A-):
[/h1]
Given the thousands of posts both on Steam and Toplitz Productions Discord server that the developers and publisher have posted replies to in response to questions/bugs etc (often across multiple languages) I feel as though the team is providing an earnest effort to address concerns and questions as they are posted by players/consumers.

I do feel both the development team and players would be better served by a standardized bi-weekly/monthly patch with a single thread listing known issues and version notes identifying both fixes that have been completed and work arounds in the interim and anticipated fixes for the next cycle.

Searching through posts (especially in non native language) can be tedious for players and often the same issue/bug is listed in dozens of posts (that the developers frequently provide the known fix/workaround solution).

[h1]
Game performance (C+):
[/h1]
Based on recommended hardware specifications provided long before release and still listed on Steam store page:
RECOMMENDED:
Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
OS: Windows 10 (x64)
Processor: Intel Core i5-12600K or AMD Ryzen 5 7600X
Memory: 16 GB RAM
Graphics: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 TI, 8 GB or AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT, 16 GB
DirectX: Version 12
Storage: 15 GB available space
Additional Notes: Epic 1080p @ 60 FPS

I would suggest the current level of optimization for the game fails to achieve 60 FPS as a solo play mode in several situations let alone a known issue with hosting a co-op game.

While the developers have previously greatly improved performance from early access versions of the game, it is currently an official release and in my opinion should fully meet the standards set forth by the developers. I believe Superkami will continue to improve optimization and performance but at the moment I feel this is a failure to fulfill a commitment from the development team.

[h1]
Game mechanics (B-):
[/h1]

[h2]
Village Management (C-):
[/h2]

The vast majority of the game is about managing villagers, resources, and production across multiple villages.

While you can technically scroll up and down a list of 100+ worksites (late/end game) to attempt to manage workers the lack of filtering and sorting currently available including not knowing which worksite is in which village or which villager/bed is in which village makes late game optimization of workers/resources extremely tedious and time consuming.

(* Many players have posted about this and the developers have stated they will look into this)

[h2]
Resource Management & Production (D+):
[/h2]

As villagers remove items from storage whether for daily consumption needs or production needs there is no clear indication of where an item is being used and can cause issues in production. Are my wooden planks being used for maintenance or for making tools? While you can disable items from being used for maintenance or food needs etc. it can lead to confusion both about where you stand overall gathering resources vs production of end items. Furthermore when beginning crafting of items that have intermediate steps (sake/paper) because production is only evaluated at the end of a day assigning villagers to each step on the 1st day means no intermediate resources are created/available for step 2 or 3 etc. This can lead to a misunderstanding of whether or not anything is being made (as the intermediate resources created day one instantly disappear to be used day 2 in step 2 etc. etc.) until 3 or 4 days have passed and you finally see your end product.

Lack of resource identifiers (D):
While there is a global warning showing that there is a shortage of some resource there is no indication as to which resource is in short supply. Is a cook missing ingredients to fulfil daily production? Is it the blacksmith?

Production Queues (C):
Most people would arguably believe if you intend your blacksmith to make 4 different tools but he/she runs out of materials after the 2nd or 3rd the following day should start where they left off sequentially crafting what they can. Unfortunately everyday crafting begins at the top of the list making the above lack of low resource supply an imperative to figure out before you have 20 hammers and no pick axes.

Production evaluation (End of Day) (D):
Currently all production, consumption, reserving materials for next days use all occur at the instant of the completion of a workday which can lead to a significant lag spike. If you're standing in town this may not be of concern, however if you are currently in the middle of a fight with an enemy boss this can lead to a quick death that you do not even see.

Production special projects (F):
Like daily production special projects are evaluated simply at the instance of transition (from one season to the next). This means instead of having workers assigned to a project for the entirety of a season (or even the entirety of a day) you simply have your villagers abandon all villages the last couple hours of a season and complete 4,5,more projects at once. as long as you pre-staged the materials go wild have all 100 villagers work on projects after they finished that last work day. And bonus as long as you re-assign everyone before the end of the 1st day of the next season you get full production from that day. (yay i threw a farmer in 10 minutes before the end of day and have full crops).

[h2]
Combat AI:
[/h2]

[h3]
Animals (B+):
[/h3]

Overall AI for animals is acceptable nothing special but nothing grossly deficient (perhaps wolves should hunt/attack as pack animals instead of lone animals but that's merely opinion). Animal interactions with the player are largely straight forward either an animal is aggressive and attacks or is passive and runs away. Unfortunately the interaction with NPC's is less than anticipated with boars, wolves, and bears often ignoring NPC's entirely leaving you to fight the animals and bandits at the same time.

[h3]
Opponent Humanoid (C-):
[/h3]

To describe the humanoid AI as weak is likely being a bit polite. Opponents frequently charge straight forward and get caught on some obstacle never attempting to resolve a pathing issue. Opponents have a fixed range they can chase then hit an invisible wall allowing the player to simply stand mere feet away and shoot them in the back as they turn to walk away. Players can climb on structures and pepper opponents with arrows since they never climb up to chase and depending on the weapon they wield do not have an upward arc in their attack. Opponent line of sight is greatly diminished at night easily allowing players to kite one away from a group to fight one on one (though this can be accomplished in daylight settings as well).
