review:
While this game was taken out of early access, it's still very much incomplete at the time of this review.  It needs several more months of continued development before I'd consider it a complete game.  You'll occasionally run into performance issues, missing features, and poor AI on both sides of the fence.  It's very much unfinished!  You'll still get fun out of it, so it's worth getting (on sale), but it's just not done.  Be prepared for a bit of aggravation here and there.

That said, it's quite the beautiful game with a lot of potential.  It has more than a few quality of life features that I feel other sandbox games could benefit from!  For example, you can pick up and move a building.  As someone with OCPD, I find that absolutely wonderful!

While a bit simplistic, and only sometimes punishing (not quite in the good way), I do like their approach to combat.  It's not a bad system, but it needs a lot of polishing.  For example, enemies will just reset their positions out of nowhere - often before they even take the three steps to get to you.

As lovely as it is to move buildings, it's an area of the game that needs a lot more love.  There's no real progression in architecture and its minimally cultural, the interiors have the bare minimum (the storehouse, for example, is a spacious building with a single item in the back of it), and there's not much decor to flesh out these places.

Passive NPCs (villagers) have no authenticity to them.  They will either stand around like lumps on a log, wander around aimlessly, or get themselves stuck somewhere - be it in the ground, in a building, or on the fishing dock.  Even with a tailor and clothes in storage, none of them ever change out of the rags they show up with, either.  Or wear shoes.

It needs more animations, better and varied sounds (all animals sound the same, for example), greater variety in furniture and placeables, more customization options for player and NPCs (all look identical to each other), a refined economy, more versatile and informative village management options, and less micro-management.

As it stands, I can't recommend this game in good conscience.  I've grown disinterested in early access games of late, and the fact Sengoku Dynasty was released in such a state feels like a betrayal.  For now, I've put it on the shelf, but I do look forward to getting the complete game!  I think it'll be something special.

The building system in this game isn't what I expected. There is very little customization outside of a few material variants. You can't change the shape of the building at all, you can only change a wall into a window or an entrance.

I was really disappointed by the interiors and the lack of interior walls. Every building is just one big walled room with a roof. This might make sense for the smallest houses but even the new mansion building is like this. There is no way to subdivide a building to have multiple rooms or interior corridors. 

Some of the assets like tools and weapons aren't historical or are out of period, and the flora choices around the map are strange. I don't think they put much effort into realism.
The UI is buggy and ugly with lots of typos, and performance is pretty bad. This game doesn't look good if you're not using 4K upscaling, and this still runs poorly. 

If you're looking to simulate Japanese architecture I can't recommend this game.
This is just another open world survival crafting game but with a minimally Japanese skin.

review:
At first this seems like a fun little crafting/empire building game but after a while it becomes apparent that it relies on an insane amount of grind to fill its content. 

Want to build a single house for some people to live in? Better build 3 or 4 hammers because those will keep breaking as you go. Need more logs to build those hammers (and also the house)? Better build 3 or 4 axes for that. 

This coupled with an annoying progression system that is locked based on what regions you have yet to take over means that upgrading is slow, requires a lot of resources that are tedious to gather, and the rate at which you villagers do it is not enough to offset this. 

Added to the grind is a clunky combat system. This game should have stayed in Early Access a while longer so it may be a good game to waste a few hours in if you can get it at a decent discount.

review:
I wish Steam allowed neutral reviews, because while this is an excellent little contained experience, it also still plays like an early access game despite being marketed as full release. I like what it tries to do, but lacks many quality of life standards which should come by default these days. Gamepad controls are flimsy and you can't change it. Customisation is also greatly lacking and optimisation needs some work, stuttering is common.

It has great potential, and it's a good example that you don't need ambition to make a decent game. I just wish it had a bit more polish, its current state feels like it was released prematurely.

I don't want to give it a negative review, because I genuinely love the concept. But until there's been some substantial patches, I can't recommend it either. I'll change my review to positive in the future, when--and if--the game approaches the more release-ready state it should have been in.

review:
Its like Medieval Dynasty and Ghost of Tsushima had a retarded child.

We had 80 hours in Medieval Dynasty, loved it in spite of it being somewhat rough. So we waited patiently in excitement for Sengoku to release as 1.0.
Boy oh boy, was it a surprise jumping into it.

The game feels like playing alpha build straight in the engine, everything is clipping, popping, disappearing, flashing. We have different information on resources needed when playing coop, unexplained errors when building, literally so many issues and bugs thats its actually impressive there could be SO MANY DIFFERENT ONES.
Game performance is insanely bad, game is jumping between 20 to 80 fps every couple seconds, loading textures ALL the time. Another player teleporting is freezing both game instances, ridiculous and borderline playable. Setting everything to Low does 0-5% fps gain from Epic.

The good:
- Visually building your village - THE ONLY good part of this game

The bad:
- Balance and challenge - sucks, teleporting is basically free, no tax, lack of purpose, no child/dynasty system
- Combat - its boring, basic, unexplained, stuttering unfair, clunky af
- Locations and POI - expanses of nothing, sparse animals, caves are so empty its like 1995
- Audio and Music - bare minimum, 0 satisfaction, some sounds out of place
- UI design - its so bad, 0 filters, 0 customization, absolutele nightmare to manage any village above 20 ppl
- Story and NPC - I see the intention but it feels like the budget for it was cut right away, slapped some cutscenes that feel too long and relevant to the gameplay struggles
- Probably more but lets just stop


As a fellow game dev I can probably guess that the team was heavily underfunded and was cutting corners/features like crazy in spite of highly ambitious initial plans but its so sad the game HAS to be released when clearly no sane person on the team would call it ready to leave early access.

It feels like alpha v0.6 - it has a great premise and so much potential but its failing at EVERY fundamental aspect.
Please at least fix this insanely bad performance so we can finish our village asap without going mental from watching single digit fps drops every couple seconds. I would love to revisit this game someday, enjoy it as much as Medieval Dynasty and change my review to Positive, wishing best to the devs.

review:
The building selection UI is horrible and still black&white while the rest of the game looks great. There were a lot of times I was really confused in which section what building or whatever structure is. It needs a rework into something either standard or more intuitive.

The game does not provide guidance on progression. It is true that the game is survival type, yet survival is the easiest thing to do - in fact, after 1h of gameplay you will forget this fact. The game is all about unlocking building and items, then managing your villages and population. So I thought, why not just kick everyone out and just keep building stuff to upgrade myself and just razing the map. Well on normal and  difficulty(probably also higher) you also have to build special project that require villagers which tend to leave you if they are not happy. Bummer. The big problem is that in order to balance something you will be recruiting people and assign them jobs, but the more you recruit the more stuff you unlock and with that more problems/villager needs. It was really hard to make every box green. In fact I only managed to do it while on 50 population and still the spiritual/luxury needs were in red(last unlockable needs) - never really enjoyed the gameplay because of it. It was a constant struggle to figure out what to do with the village.

You can build only 4 villages(and probably 100 villagers) in total but you can not demolish the previous. The map has regions and regions have resources, your villagers can harvest. The problem is that once you unlock iron, you won't need bronze, so if i made a mistake by settling in starter area like everyone else who did not read forums/wiki, then you are f-ed because you will need such things like ice and later more resources. This shows that you will not be able to automate everything by using villagers. So why struggle with base management to begin with?

The resource management UI is also bad. It does not allow to pick the amount i would like to store for Winter or, as another example, "get and keep 20 bronze in storage, after that amount continue on consuming it on whatever".

Why can't I assign the same person to work on different things during different season without manual intervention?(or to do the same with building resources) This made every production like even more annoying to manage. For example, during winter almost nothing grows, so you either stock up(which you should) or choose different things to grow like wasabi or enoki mushrooms or hunt for meat, get more fish.

The game does not guide you towards the usefulness of the items much. This is either because of the UI or lack of guidance. Want better heat? Get charcoal kiln. How? F you. Want to know which food gives you more village needs right from the menu? Lol, go to the traders and look for that food. I would really appreciate an in game "help" section where i can look for every recipe or mechanic instead of checking said wiki and forums.

The whole game is pretty much like this. Go build special projects and kill boss in the region if it has one. There is really nothing else to do. There are quests, but those are really silly and irrelevant except the one that gives you the bell to establish another village.

The combat approach is weird but it works. Essentially you are a 1 man army against the map. Can't use villagers for anything related to combat.

Probably the biggest goal of the game is to get as rich as possible and as fast as possible. Without money you can't unlock anything and have only other choice of scavenging - not for the game progression, but for base management - it doesn't make sense.

I strongly believe this game is made to play on the creative mode an not on any other difficulty otherwise it's just not worth the time. It has good graphics, theme, music but most mechanics are simply bad and not enjoyable by the balancing the game gives you. I do understand that it could be more efficient to play as 4 people multiplayer, but at that point, the game is not worth its price. I'd recommend just skipping this game as it does not deliver equal or more worth than something standard like DayZ or Subnautica.

review:
I am writing the negative review for this game with a heavy heart, because I absolutely loved playing the early access version. The village building is fun, managing your villages's needs can be difficult but generally manageable, and the visuals and sound are beautiful and immersive. The basic gameplay loop feels pretty good and seeing your village grow from nothing to a bustling town is satisfying.
That being said, this game should not be released yet. It was fantastic for an early access game. There were many issues, but I though to myself, these will surely be fixed with the full release. 
I was wrong.
The game as it is now simply feels unfinished. I have to wonder if the developers even bothered to have dedicated playtests done. The issues I'm seeing here aren't even major things, since the essential gameplay works, but small quality of life issues that cause the game to die of a thousand paper cuts. For example, your hunger bar is in the bottom left corner, where you rarely look if you are just building your town, but there is no audio queue to tell you that you are hungry, so I have starved to half my health before even realizing that I need to eat. You can set the exact amount of an item your villagers should craft or gather, in some cases on a range of 1-250, but you have to do it via clicking on the increase/decrease arrow repeatedly. You can upgrade previously built beds, but that registers them as new bed and the previous bed as destroyed, so your assigned villager not only loses their home, but their job, and you have to reassign everything for them again (and click on decrease 100 times again). There is no way to filter the UI for a certain job, so if you want to know how many villagers are gathering wood for example, you have to scroll and look and hope that you aren't missing any woodworkers you have assigned.
I am honestly severely disappointed. This game is feature complete, but feels like not a second was spent on making sure that the existing features don't just work, but work well. I can only hope that these issues are solved in future updates, but until then, i cannot in good faith recommend such a rushed release.

review:
[h3](BEFORE READING) It's my personnal and only experience about this game ! Everything I say is purely related to me, maybe you'll experience the game, completly differently than I did.

+I have been playing only in CO-OP, which means that in solo, there's a lot of bugs, you wouldn't have !
[/h3]
[u]
Well well well : 
[/u]

I've been trying to get the 100% on this game, and OH BOY, let me tell you it is horrible. Not because of the core gameplay itself, which has a long lifetime playing, but because of everything else.

[b]Here are the positive points about the game :[/b]

-Good lifetime, I mean, in solo, I think you can reach the end game in 80h-100h, whereas in CO-OP, with two players, you can reach it in about 30h to 40h, and you still have a dozen things to do.

-The building system is pretty decent, nothing to say about it, a good variety of objects and structures. It's really satisfying to build your own village in this game !

-A good management system, it's pretty easy to understand, how to assign villagers to an house, to a job, what tool the villager's missing, or even what he farms for you and the other villagers. So yeah, it's good.

-A lot of differents enemies, and 11 places to discover and explore, it's well sized. Don't need more or less :D

-The game price is really OK ! I mean 27€ for a game of this size, is reaaaaally cheap (but you should wait a bit of updates !)

[b]Now are the negatives points :[/b]

-At the end of the day, when villagers are done working, there's a freeze for almost 10-15 seconds. We don't know (I say we because I play with my friend) where it comes from. It happens every single day, which is kinda frustrating ngl.

-A lot of enemies / animals are clipping into the ground, or sometimes into objects, which is sometimes funny, but sometimes it breaks the game (ex : enemies who are clipped in objects and can't move, so you can 1vs5 them, or a bear which has his head out of his wood cage, so you can kill him while shooting arrows on his head etc..)

-The enemies stamina, are you guys ok ? I mean, sometimes they can just combo you (especially if you have a bow) like 10 times in a row, and you [b]CAN'T[/b] dodge, like litteraly.

-The multiplayer is laggy, but like really laggy. And it's not about my specs or my friend specs, or even our connections (I'm hosting and around 932,1Mb/s in download and 502.7Mb/s in upload, and my friend has a good network too, so we don't get it), but it's really really horrible to play in those conditions. He (my friend) would have enemies who teleports, as well as animals, which makes fighting extremely difficult. Same for cutting trees, mining etc.. sometimes it rollsback or teleport, we don't know why, and that's a major issue.

-The enemies difficulty feels... almost random ? Sometimes you'll fight 3 ashigarus with no problem, but sometimes, some randoms pirates will kick your ass in 1vs1, and put you mid life, while having less stuff and being less stronger, so, I don't get it at all ?

-The stamina is random as well. Before 1.0 or 1.1, I remember losing a lot of stamina while mining, or cutting trees etc.. which was ok, I mean, in game design, that's working and a part of progression. But now, we're not losing (or almost not) stamina while doing this, but we're losing a lot by dodging ? So I don't know, how the stamina system works inside, but it feels weird anyway !

-To a certain point, map is completly unreadable, you'll have to zoom in everything to find the villager, or quest you must give, because every information is displayed and we can't choose which info we want to see or not. (I can assure you, when you've discovered almost all the hunt places, it's HORRIBLE).

-When you want to loot some dead enemies, you can't, because firstly you're kinda forced to take their weapon, which is on the exact same place, and take the priority on the loot. This is 80% of the time an issue, and it's frustrating.

-As I said previously, we can kill animals in their wood cages, I mean, the update of that is cool, but at least, don't let people abuse of that ? Like the first bear we've encountered was in one of that cage, and we just spammed him with arrows, and he died ? It lowers the difficulty, that's kinda sad :(

-The "bosses" are .. weak. Like really weak. We can easily 1vs1 them, and the funniest thing of all ...

-We can loot bosses chests by just running past them, they'll maybe hit you once, or not even, you can just run away while having the best armor of the game, at the begining of it ? I mean, I didn't do it, but it's possible, and that's sad, ruining the game is easy by doing this.

-The stuff in this game feels, almost broken to a certain point. When you unlock iron, you can do "almost" every enemy camps. So basically, every kind of copper or bronze (armors / tools / weapons) will be useless. (unless you give everything to villagers).

-Ok hear me out for this one. [b]WE CAN'T BREATH UNDER WATER[/b], I mean, WHY ?! Just, WHY ?! That's so stupid, at least a small status bar (like the one you guys added, for being burned, freezing etc..) but with oxygen ? This was really too hard to put ? It just makes no sense.
Oh and btw, I take more damage for not breathing for 1 second under water, than being bullied by ashigarus, so what's the point of that ?

-When the season change, you're getting teleported to your village. I mean yes, but no. Was it to hard to make the player refresh his map ? Even if he's far away from his village ? (I can understand it in CO-OP, but in solo ? Eh ?)

-You guys need to nerf bows. They are to powerful. Like enemies using bows, is too powerful. They can spam you, and when you're hurt you can't move, even from really far away, even while jumping or whatever. I understand it's supposed to make a lot of damages etc.. but sometimes it's just too much don't you think ?

-We can't destroy a village and replace it. Of course we can move the bell of the town, then travel around all the map to replace it, but it's way too long. A functionality to broke the bell and then get it back in our inventory will be refreshing ngl.

-Slopes are weird, you can't really fight in them, if the enemy is above you, he can hit you, and if you spam your dodging bind, you'll lose all your stamina in 2 seconds. But if you're above him, you can't hit him ? It's weird.

[h1]FINAL NOTE : 10/20[/h1]

I mean ... The game has potential and is really, reaaaally good so far ! But bugs and lags ruins it all. It really feels like playing a beta game which is not even fully released, but hey, we're in 1.1.0.7 ! 

I will update my review with time, because I will not stop playing, but playing in these conditions make the experience pretty disappointing and dull... 

So far so good, keep it up devs ! You guys are still doing an amazing job ! :D <3

review:
Noticed that this wasn't on early access anymore, so I got it. What did I get? - A jank game with a jank village management system and an empty world. The open world bit just feels empty, there wasn't much left to do after you went out and discovered the few other villages that were there and cleared out some bandit camps or roamed around to acquire the few resources I required. The bandit camps do not seem to respawn, so those are only a one time thing. I didn't read any guides when I started out, reading guides usually ruins the game for me, I like to figure things out on my own. So, managing the village upkeep doesn't leave you much room to screw up and it's never really fully automated, you always need to craft or gather something. You'll be pulling your hair out trying to manage the village with its awful lists and misinformed abstract production numbers and no way to easily calculate the total expenditure of your resources. First of all, every building needs to be linked up to the correct storage facilities. At first, the general storage will do, but eventually you need to build several other types of storage buildings, each requiring a building of their own and you need to make sure that each production building is properly set up. I had a ton of trouble managing the village maintenance, because four carpenters in a village of less than thirty people were barely able to keep up with the maintenance quota, my rickety shacks were suddenly falling apart left and right, the only way I managed produce any lumber again was to get a large stockpile of clay, mine it manually and then burn through it in hopes of getting more villagers. But if you think that getting more villagers might help - you're dead wrong! The more people your "dynasty" has, the more stuff they need. Pass a certain threshold and suddenly everyone needs a ton of cough medicine, which means reworking your entire production chain all over again. Why do I need to manually change each forager individually to pick different a different type of mushroom during the summer and winter? - Why can't you just tell them to go pick up any edible mushroom they come across that happens to be available in each season - there are many such similar annoying cases of micromanagement with this game. You cannot set up a proper production of items separately for each season, you need to always fiddle and tinker around with the people's workplace or micromanage the menus and it gets really bothersome to do with the janky lists and the scarce amount of information. So, after cough medicine, comes security, which means more work for the blacksmith to craft weapons, in addition to the hammers, axes, adzes, knives, bells and whistles that they're already crafting! That also means you need to designate some of your villagers as 'warriors' at guard towers to guard them from enemies that never seem to invade your village. After that, your villagers start requiring spiritual items, so you need to start crafting straw hats, God forbid you craft any other spiritual item than straw hats because you cannot keep up with the demand. Let's say that you'll try to satisfy your villager's needs for spiritual items with expensive and hard to produce deity stones, used for building shrines - That's a big no, because your villagers smoke large deity stones like crack. After spiritual items, it's time for luxury items and that means, you guessed it, more different type of straw hats! Ok, that's no big deal, those are made of straw but make sure not to run out of straw or your entire straw production halts - you always need to have items needed for production and upkeep stockpiled if you wish for the villagers to produce. At some point, you might reach a point where everything balances correctly and you can finally stop worrying about the village's numbers staying green and only need to craft seed bags or some other item only once every few seasons. Then you finally go out to the empty world and get mauled by a bear and pick up from a save and you realize that the game's been saving every five minutes through the entire time that you've played it and each save file is sized at around 14~mb, WHY? Thanks for hogging up the space on my SSD! Why is there no limit on how many autosaves the game creates, do you really need tens... hundreds of autosaves? 
The final straw was the God-forsaken Ore Processing Plant, I built it, made a town, eventually set a worker there to mine iron ore, using a steel pickaxe. The worker's production tab tells me that the building is producing a good amount of iron ore, ok. I go to bed, do a time skip, and the plant does not produce a single nugget. Why does the game have to flat out lie about it? Then I realized - it's a special jank building that you cannot add items inside of it, so you probably cannot link it to a storage building at all, but the game just decides to flat out lie about the amount of iron it produces. Then, finally, I try to look up information on the ore plant and there is none, besides a few random discussions - there are no guides, no tips, no hints and no tricks on how to work it. Probably because there have ever only been a handful of individuals who've persisted as far as to have first, building the thing, and then tried connecting it to a town and then use it - Only found a few discussions from 2023 saying that it's bugged and doesn't work. And now, here I am, writing an over 5,000 letter rant. Do not buy - it's still early access carp, it's nowhere near complete. Save yourself from frustration that is... Sengoku Dynasty.

The Good:

- Some improvements over Village Management in Medival Dynasty.
  - Luxury, Spiritual and Safety needs are interesting
  - Filling needs with *jobs* and services, vs. items is good addition
- Interesting combat system.
  - Very different animations across weapons
  - Enemy camp "dungeons" with bosses to take down
- Region Control mechanic.  Requires "building" key control points to gain access to advanced resources.

The Bad

- Pacing. They added quests in EA and for this release they just changed them all with Region Control so that the quest and story just doesn't make sense anymore.  E.g. there's a quest to learn ironworking that requires you to advance much past where the quest is to acheive the quest.  Additionally the quest is still worded as if it unlocked ironworking (like in EA), when in fact it does nothing of the sort.  Lots of instances where mid-game "better recipes" is locked behind quests, but you can rush towards later game recipes instead with better outcomes.
- Clunky. There's a LOT of missing quality of life features.  E.g. a notice that workers are doing something not valid in the current season, a notice that workers don't have enough source material for the % you have them allocated to a task.  Or even just the ability to *sort* in any menu, ever.
- Economy. The one BIG missing feature from Medieval Dynasty is having sales people sell your stuff.  I usually have my villagers make massive amounts of one item and I craft/derive the needs from there.  However, at some point I wound up with a ridiculous number of logs and it was VERY hard to craft all of them or even sell them, due to how the interfaces work.  This is after I had moved to oil for heat, but had forgotten to tone down the deforestation.


The Ugly

- Base/Town Building.  They have TONS of great decoration, but simple things like getting walls to line up or controlling the roof-style of *some* buildings is buggy or not working.  There's no great way to control the terrain around your base, and some buildings you expect to line up (like mansions/monastery) just may never line up if you didn't pick flat enough ground.
- Depth. Crafting is fun. Combat is fun. Managing the Village is fun.  But you can easily get to a point where you're either doing something you've already done a thousand times.  Additionally, leveling "monk"/"spiritual" just never made sense to me and I could barely get anything out of it.  I wish there was more quests or content around this aspect of the game.  Or that having a family actually DID something, not just "hey great, we sent your kid somewhere else to live".


Don't get me wrong, I do like the game, I just think once you get past the early game it just leaves you hanging with what looks like deep, rich content, but isn't.

review:
I can see the vision, but this game needs A LOT of work. The concept of building a bustling town by hand is very appealing, but this game just feels dead. None of the NPCs really matter. All your villagers just exist to produce and consume resources. They do not feel like your faithful townspeople, they are robots. There is no one to latch onto. They say nothing of substance. Not to mention that they are butt ugly and visually identical to each other. In playing from the actual perspective of the town's leader, I would imagine there's at least a surface-level connection to my people, but I feel nothing for them. They barely even benefit me. Everything they do is in service of meeting the consumption/production quota. Why wouldn't I just play a traditional city builder? What's the point of me having boots on the ground?

That's my main criticism, but there are other things that irk me, too. 

There's little point in having a season system. All the food sources you're likely using still function year round. There's no temperature system or anything so winter is just a visual change. You don't need to wear warm clothes, nor do your townspeople. Same idea with summer.

There's a clothing slot for gloves but in 14 hours I have seen no glove items. They might not exist. I've read that the slot is a holdover from early access that wasn't removed in 1.0 [EDIT: this has apparently been fixed in a post 1.0 update]. That's already pretty annoying to me, but wait until you hear about the "Dynasty" part of "Sengoku Dynasty".

Here is a quote from the store page:
"DYNASTY MANAGEMENT: Create a prosperous dynasty for generations to come. Oversee the growth and development of your villages. Get married and ensure your legacy continues through your successor."

As you can see, one of the main selling points of this game is starting a family of your own, thereby "ensuring your legacy continues". But when you approach someone who you aim to start a family with, you're explicitly told in a pop-up message that your kid won't actually get to grow up and do adult things until an update that comes later. They'll be eternally stuck as children in the meantime. This game is seriously called Sengoku Dynasty when there is no such dynasty to be found in 1.0. Here's the Merriam-Webster definition of "dynasty": 

1
: a succession of rulers of the same line of descent 
a dynasty that ruled China for nearly 300 years
2
: a powerful group or family that maintains its position for a considerable time
born into a powerful political dynasty
a baseball dynasty

SENGOKU DYNASTY? MORE LIKE... SENGOKU... THE-DYNASTY-ENDS-WITH-ME! The first definition definitely does not fit here, since you will be the ONLY ruler with no such role being passed to your children because they will be babies forever. Ironically, the second definition actually does fit because you will be ruling for an ETERNITY! You could sleep tens of years away in this game and the only thing different would be the ever increasing size of your stockpile. Seasons will change, years will pass, but no one will age, no NPC towns will grow, and resources will stay plentiful. It's like the whole world is inside a time bubble. Your town will steadily grow each year... and the first villager you recruited in year 1 will still be alive to witness you welcoming villager 274 in year 102. Your kid will still be a baby, too. This really adds to my whole robot comparison.

Did I mention that villagers can't have their own babies? If you want new villagers, you have to manually scour the world for people that magically appear every season. They're all robots, I tell you.

Besides the "Dynasty" part being incomplete, another missing feature slated for LATER is enemy raids. Despite this, my people will still desire "security", aka another number for the robots to consume. Why should I, as a player, care about the security of my automatons when I KNOW there is no real threat? That feature is coming later guys, you don't need protection!

Combat is also disappointing. Enemies can only see a few meters, but hey, at least they have 360 degree vision. Enemies don't aggro as a group either, just inch into an enemy's vision circle (not cone) so you can pick them off one by one. Spears also make this game super easy; just take one step back, press attack, and the enemy will walk right into the hitbox because enemies can only walk straight at you (which also gets them stuck on obstacles). I saw other reviewers dare to liken this combat to Dark Souls, which, frankly, I find offensive.

What I've written about is just annoyances that I could come up with off the top of my head. There is more I could write about if I opened the game again and dug a bit deeper, but I'd rather not see this game again for another year or two or three. The most fun I had with this game was thinking about my android peasants being stuck in time for an eternity, aka writing this review. 

Basically, this game has no personality and shouldn't be in 1.0. It's objectively unfinished and they can't even bother to act like it's done. It's amateurish slop.

review:
For a 1.0 release, it's pretty buggy. I'm into the mid/late game and the cracks are really showing. I dealt with the very clunky combat up to the iron stage and it really feels bad the further you go. Enemies with knives are starting to bug out and spam attacks endlessly and are unaffected by parries entirely. The combat has boiled down to trading hits with knife enemies since their poise is seemingly infinite. 

Parry timing is hit or miss on most enemies. Sometimes it works and sometimes you just get a block or just take damage even though you timed the parry perfectly. I had to really tune down the damage enemies could deal since the game likes to throw 3 enemies at a time at you, but the mechanics aren't built for it. Katana enemies will 2 shot you even though you are wearing heavy armor. The game is horribly balanced. 

Since production doesn't finish until the end of the day, the game does a horrendous synchronous update that causes the game to freeze for 10 seconds when the day ends. This is pretty trivial, but then the game drops frames into the sub 30's while the game is trying to catch back up. I'm only at Dynasty level 15 with 58 villagers and it's chugging this bad already. No amount of DLSS 3.5 can keep the frames up. My PC is no slouch either. 

Villagers are starting to unreliably complete their tasks each day now too. My smithy is only producing iron hammers in spite of having pickaxes, knives, Axes, etc. selected. I have checked and rechecked all materials are available and made sure all proper storage is available in the smithy, yet it won't produce anything else but hammers. 

This game is probably going to need some more time in the oven before it's ready. $30 is a little steep given the state this game is in. Honestly, given this team was willing to slap a 1.0 on this game in this state, I wouldn't expect the above complaints to improve much.

review:
Decent game with alright amount of content. 
The major drawback for me is the repetitive nature of recruiting new members for your villages. You literally need to pray for RNG to spawn refugees near you. If you aren't lucky, the only alternative is running around the map for 20+ minutes to be able to find some or sleeping to progress to the next season for zone refreshes.
The resource management is a pain in the butt and the UI was completely bastardized to allow for console gameplay. It's very obvious that they changed the UI to let this game be played on console, without regard to how much this impairs a PC players ability to look at what your village is generating and consuming. The needs are balanced decently, but the bad resource management makes it difficult to understand what you need to build next or change production to.
The production system is basically a matter of selecting different recipes for your assigned worker to craft for you, which is great in theory but fails to be good in reality. The process of choosing a recipe is a mess because you can't see what your village is actively producing and consuming on other crafting jobs. 
The processing is done all in a single batch at the end of the day, so you don't get incremental resource dropped into storage throughout the day. This means you'll end up having production of 100+ logs but no logs to build with for the day because the workers haven't deposited yet. This is another hurdle for managing the economy because there's a lot of guesswork needed to plan what resources you need vs what you already have.
There are massive performance issues related to changing seasons and work processing at the end of the day. There are framerate issues within a city with a lot of player buildigns and npcs. This game does not scale up very well, but that may be my own hardware limitation. I don't have a top of the line PC but that's no excuse for framerate drops and freezing with all low settings.

Overall, I give this game a headache / 10.

review:
Sengoku Dynasty - Promising, But Not Ready Yet

I’ve put in about 25 hours into Sengoku Dynasty, and while the game starts off with some promise, I can’t recommend it in its current state. It’s technically out of Early Access, but honestly, it feels like it’s still in development — especially when it comes to multiplayer.

Multiplayer is Rough:
The multiplayer experience is extremely laggy, and that’s being generous. I’m running a high-end PC (RTX 4090, Ryzen 3900X, 128GB RAM), and the performance is still awful. The game constantly struggles to keep up, and enemies often just wander around aimlessly without attacking. You can hit them like they’re ragdolls, and it feels more like you’re testing a broken demo than playing an actual game.

FPS Issues:
Once you start raiding the Ronin camps, the FPS drops to unplayable levels (2-8 FPS). It’s hard to focus on combat when the game is struggling to even render the action. Enemies are nearly impossible to hit, and the lag makes it all frustrating rather than fun.

City Building is the Highlight:
The city-building mechanics are decent and the most polished part of the game. You can create and manage a village, and it’s enjoyable as long as you can look past the other issues. But unfortunately, that’s where the positives end.

Final Thoughts:
Sengoku Dynasty has a lot of potential, but it feels unfinished and unpolished right now. If you’re hoping for a stable multiplayer experience or smooth gameplay, you’ll be disappointed. SINGLE PLAYER IS FINE THOUGH! The city-building is solid, but the game needs a lot of work to make it enjoyable overall. I’d recommend waiting at least 2-3 years for updates, assuming the devs continue to improve it. Hopefully by then, it’ll be worth playing.

If an enemy is killed, all arrows hit a wall of air where he was last standing... they also don't stay on an enemy, except for the last one. Have fun searching... The AI bugs out at times as well and their bodies sometimes bug out and are barely visible. Also a grid for placing structures would be great (though they have one for the inner spaces, which is nice). Also don't expect a lot of armor/clothing combinations. basically only some head, foot and main gears.

But let's get to the good points:
I like the liberation system
Many skills make it a little more of an RPG
Parrying actually works OK
Fast travelling to some villages

Overall? 
Buy if it is on sale. Maybe 15 Euros for this game in its current state. I will continue playing but also rage at times.

review:
Huge disappointment.

Compared to Medieval Dynasty, the game offers more enjoyable village automation, but you are continuously frustrated by the stupid game progression design. It turns out that access to advanced resources requires having numerous villages. The main quest caps the number of villages, and it advances very slowly. If you could hire new villagers whenever you want, the main quest could go more quickly, but of course, that is not possible. You must look for them in the wilderness in random locations throughout the seasons, unlike the Medieval Dynasty, when you could hire them in any village. To obtain two to three villagers per season, you must traverse the entire map. Which is the speed of the sail. Because of this, my population cap is constantly higher than the actual population count. It's just artificial bull crap limitation.  

Other than village count cap and constant lack of villagers, you have to unlock regions. And boi its mess on whole other level. You need to build notable buildings to unlock regions. You need to assign villagers to build notable buildings. The severe shortage of villagers forced me to reassign villagers from food production. This doesn't count as village automation in my mind if I have to change jobs every season.

And if you do unlock a region with higher quality resources, pay attention because a building that can process these resources is unlocked in a different region at the other end of the map.

There are too many mechanics that limit your advancement and none that reward you for trying to actually play the game.

review:
I give this a "soft" thumbs down. Interesting concept of a game: a kingdom simulator, but first person. Sadly though, the sim mechanics are pretty shallow. I wasn't expecting "X4: Foundations" levels of depth, but even then this is pretty shallow. The villagers just magically make resources appear by standing around in their buildings. And you, and only you, can build the village buildings. The villagers do very little, they're more like set pieces, and the world doesn't feel very real or deep. For me, it makes the game feel kind of rudderless; after a few hours of play, you've seen the gist. Part of the joy of sim games is discovering deep mechanics, and emergent behavior that comes with it.

The combat is decent, probably one of the more polished parts of the game. Everything else though feels "jank" and unfinished. I had to double check if this was an early-access game or not! Even little things are wrong: sometimes you just _cant_ swing a tool (yes, you read that right) in situations where you should be able to. If you are in a menu and an in-game notification fires, the entire menu stack gets messed up, replacing letters and graphics, forcing you to close and reopen (hope you weren't busy with something). Inventory just disappears when put in the "village storage" (hours of grind wasted). 

The game is grind-y too; long distance fetch quests, low resource yield for lots of time spent, tools breaking with little use, village buildings locked behind a _slow_ XP accumulation gate.

To wrap up: I probably would have returned this if I wasn't 6 hours in. Assuming the devs don't abandon it, I'll give it a try in the future. As is now though, this is not a complete game.

review:
Dont bother.
This is a total piece of rubbish.
Every single system is badly programmed, unfinished, and likely to be a 'worst in class'.
The inventory is terrible. The ability to switch items in your hotbar is terrible.
The combat is buggy. You will get stuck on the interface and the game will refuse to fire your arrows.
The deep water is instant death. You drown quicker than a hollywood movie.

Basically, they have a great setting, some very nice graphics - and then they punish you every moment you play.

I played it for a bit, but I ended up frustrated every few minutes with something that the designers should either have fixed, never started with, done the same way as every other quality game, or just spent three seconds thinking about before they created a crappy solution to an already solved problem.

Absolutely the worst implementation I have ever had the misfortune to play.

[EDIT]
Played again after they fixed a few things. So I knew what I was getting into the second time.
I hear that the devs call this a 'village simulator' rather than an RPG. I'm not thrilled by that idea, but let's take it on board and examine.
Is it a village simulator? No. You build things, sure. But your villagers are not simulated. They are just a set of numbers for production and consumption. And if that is the case, then surely there are systems to help you manage production and consumption. Again, sadly, no. Everything is hidden behind some 'interesting' design and interface choices. Or to be more honest, some worst-in-class screens and layouts. Nothing here is simple, nothing is made clear to you, and there are no consolidated stats as you might expect. And even if there were, it would just be a spreadsheet focused on the least interesting part of the game IMO.

The best part of the game is the world, and expanding your knowledge of places and what you can build and grow. This will occupy your actual brain time. Not the village, or at least only in steps as you add a new refugee, tell them what to do, and then forget them forever.
If that is the case, the devs have indeed created an RPG. And it is actually quite good at this. But without quests and personalities, you are stuck with gated adventuring and combat situations that lead towards new areas.

Combat though, just sucks. Absolutely sucks. I'm not overstating that it is without doubt the most bug ridden useless piece of junk ever released. In theory, the one to one combat has nuance and flair. But the ranged attacks are god awful, the enemy pathing is abysmal, and I'm running out of bad words to use. Truly terrible. Never should have been released, and I would be ashamed as a dev to say that it is in a 'release 1.0 state' at all.

So where does it go from here? I could imagine new expansion lands, new items to build, new crops to grow (and god help us because seasons for your crops is an exercise in self-abuse for the player). This would all be pointless because it wouldn't address the real challenges.

Can they fix combat? Sure. Everybody else has. Lets assume they can too.
Can they make the village management better? The screen redesign would be in theory very simple and helpful and add some overall statistics. 
But. 
Yes, that's a standalone statement. I'm just feeling that the devs are in love with their own interface and had it developed by separate sub-teams who just didn't talk or share with each other. So I'm betting the answer here is actually a hard 'no'.
Can they introduce personalities and quests? What would be the point in this and how would it work with the other things so sadly lacking. Not clear how this would make it better, or fit thematically.

And now for the good bit(s). The game is absolutely beautiful. The visuals are at least an eight out of ten. Building your buildings is fun for a while and rewarding in a repeated-clicking manner. But after a time, its just make-work. If you have a whole bunch of cool stuff available, make it have an impact. Make your village impossible to build without paying attention to detail. But then illuminate those details to the player. That would be extremely cool, and in keeping with the style. To make this a great village simulator, with complex systems, they need to be intelligible without a spreadsheet. Help us envision that. Force us to make beautiful and functional homes, and to husband those scarce resources to best effect. Give me easy ways to create repeat buildings, and let me focus on the new stuff and making everything individualised (with game impact driven by it).

And for god sake, take away the stamina bar. Sure, in combat would be fine. But everywhere else, just ditch it. Hosing your own game is never smart.

Would I buy it again? On special, yes, absolutely. But it is a one-and-done game. And there was a lot of swearing, and an awfully large amount of 'why the hell did they do it that way' discussion. Not in a positive light, to be clear. The pretty graphics made it liveable, but I would not recommend it with the flaws. They are too deep, and too obvious. If they were going to be fixed, they would already be fixed. So this one is on a pathway downwards unless there is a change at the helm.

Spamming the shoot button doesn't shoot the arrow either when this happens.  Animal you were hunting escapes or attacking bandit kills you.  Very infuriating. Few games allow gamepad and mouse functionality and this game is one of them, which is awesome, but when I activate gyro to mouse, a mouse cursor shows up on the screen while aiming.  Doesn't happen when using only mouse and keyboard though, so I couldn't begin to guess why it would in this specific scenario, but it's very distracting. review:
Shows promise – but clearly still has a long way to go. 
The landscape, day – night cycle, weather and changing seasons are visually impressive and immersive. 
Sadly, the same cannot be told for the people. There is no player customization, not even gender wise. The look changes somewhat depending on the clothes being worn, but these can’t be customized or dyed and there is a clear progression, that makes lower tier clothing obsolete. NPC villagers all look the same, although there are males and females. While you can produce clothing, you can’t make your villagers wear it. Or if you can, I didn’t find out how. 
Finding out how to do things is what I spent a lot of time doing. There was very little guidance inside the game. As can be expected, the game is also pretty grindy. I don’t mind resource gathering, but after having cut down enough trees to build the Spanish Armada, chasing logs tumbling downhill becomes repetitive. I feel on normal difficulty it would be reasonable to expect villagers to be able to provide for themselves, but there is always something missing, forcing you to stop doing whatever it is you were doing and running back to the village to stuff their mouths or wipe their …
Progression felt weird. There are a lot of different resources. Sadly, not all can be found around your starting village. Eventually, as you discover more of the area, you will come across other resources, but some of them are in constant demand, so you need to do resource runs. And there is always something missing. Not only quantity wise (your axe will soon be your best friend), but also quality wise. And then it is a matter of the hen and the egg. At one point, I was asked to produce steel tools. Naturally, the NPCs would not allow me to use their forge, so I had to go home and build one. But to build one, you need to be a certain “dynasty” level, which is mostly done by recruiting (otherwise mostly useless) villagers. And then you need other resources, and tools, which require new resources and buildings to make… the list is endless. Which would not be problematic, if there was some sort of natural progression. 
Combat felt like a transplant, something pushed into the game to make it less dull. After having bum-rushed by wolves for the third time, the charm wore off quickly though. For some reason, boars, wolves and especially bears are much harder than the NPC bandits. And unlike bandits, they don’t have a visible health bar, for some reason. I can understand the immersion factor in not knowing their health, but on the other hand, humans have a health bar, and so do your tools.
There is some sort of quest system in place, but it is very basic and honestly not much fun. It also decidedly needs more information on how to accomplish certain goals. 
Talking about basic: there is no voice over at all after the intro. Granted the conversations with the NPCs aren’t especially exciting anyway. 
For how basic the game is, it is surprisingly hardware-demanding. I had to tune down some of the recommended settings because my computer started to make worrying levels of noise. There really is no reason why such a quaint game should be more resource demanding than say Cyberpunk 2077. Clearly, optimization is possible (and badly needed).

Verdict: Would not buy again.
Recommendation: Wait a year and then buy for 20 $ or less.

review:
I love survival crafting games like this, and I don't mind playing them in early access.  I only hope the developers will take my feedback and make the game even better.

First off, lets just get the #1 issue out of the way.  There is currently no combat system for this game.  For a game where I strive to become a Samurai or a Lord, there should be a robust combat system where I can challenge people to fight, and then actually fight things.  I'm chalking this one up to what we have now being placeholder, but Superkami, you have got to invest time and money into a good combat system or it will kill your game.

Secondly, tools break far too easily.  I can only chop down and cut into logs about 4-5 trees before a stone axe is broken beyond repair.  Either my durability is draining too fast, or they need more.  Please look into this for a future balancing patch.

I cannot believe in this year of our lord 2024, we are still holding a button to gather.  Please add an accessibility option to gather by clicking.  It's tedious and can actually cause pain in your players' hands.  Also, when you gather, you should gather all of that resource in a small area around you.

Not being able to move the city Bell needs to be changed.  I set up my city initially and then as I started laying things out I wanted to change its location.  Let me do so.

The UI where you assign your townspeople to jobs or housing is a bit buggy in that you have to click in specific spots or nothing happens.  Consider some adjustments to clickable areas on this screen to make it a bit more friendly.

All that said, the game is beautiful and so far pretty fun.  It has good bones, but just needs more time to bake before it's really ready.

If you are a fan of the survival crafting and village building genre, I'd suggest holding off on this one for now.   Pop it in your wishlist and watch those updates.  Wait for a combat system to be added.

review:
[h2]Summary[/h2]
13 hours sounds not much, what did this guy even do?
Well I have 300 hours in the PREQUEL, Medival Dynasty, and have some gripes to share.

[h2]Straight up downgrades[/h2]
Right of the bat, nothing in this game feels scarce. The Water Meter is gone, so we're back to being the Übermensch for our village who can work 4-5 times as hard as any villager, 4 days straight requiring zero sleep with no debuffs. So instead of carefully managing production chains, you end up pocket- or station crafting to make huge stockpiles once in a while.
Nothing is dangerous - in Medieval, you wouldn't duel a bear without planning, a good crossbow and maybe a friend. In Medieval, hope you have enough Stamina to outrun the wolves. Or even better, a mount.
Here? 1:1 a sixpack of wolves with the basic spear, no problem. Most of the time you don't even react to damage, have fun randomly dying. A boar did this to me randomly while chopping wood, didn't hear it over the loud music, I died, the boar spawnkilled me for the next 10 minutes because the game bugged into the complete UI not reacting. Fun times, had to kill the program and reload.

[h2]The WHY?!s[/h2]
There is SOME few and rare upgrades to systems, i.e. the ore/stone deposit stuff.
WHY is there recipes requiring just iron ore now, that... just doesn't make sense.
WHY does a lake have 4 ice "deposits" - the whole lake is frozen over and I have to look for 4 magic spots, 3 of them just not where they're shown on the map, which don't trigger my pickaxe to actually do stuff.
WHY do we now have to assign villagers with tools for stuff when the definition for the job says "any type is fine" and I provide them with tools.
WHY is it not easy to track which villagers actually work and if not, why? I provided everything for my Charcoal-Maker to make charcoal, yet he sweeps the floor with 340 units of Firewood in storage.

WHY is there, in 2024, Quests with greyed out text?! THIS WORKED IN MEDIEVAL JUST GO COPY THE CODE?!
I double and triplechecked, the quest for turning in 5 iron axes and 5 steel pickaxes, which I had in my inventory, just doesn't let me turn them in.
The quest to get rid of mask woman told me to first go to Kengyou to find out what to do. I found mask woman first, tried talking, couldn't figure it out, now the "!" for Kengyou was gone. Yeah I'm not looking for that guy, there's wood to be chopped.

WHY is all crafting time 1s? The point of making it tedious is so perks are an incentive and outsourcing stuff to your villagers feels worth it. Now I'll just craft 300 soups.

WHY have tons of clothes to pick from, only to never shiver in the winter anyways? I was out there in tabi and half-naked taking zero damage.
WHY is debarking vs. firewood a thing oh god I need BOTH for leather/steel and charcoal/steel which leads to AXE - ADZE - AXE and kills all the benefits of the multi-use

WHY is spirituality so ill-explained? Why not have the tutorial stuff saved in the menu to look up later?
WHY is there 3 perks per tree, I played for 2 hours and already had everything unlocked there is to unlock.


[h2]The Ugly[/h2]
Playing this for more than an hour with firefox open makes the game slower. How?
How have you figured this out in Medieval?
Why the fuck does the inventory have a slot system now and 100 grass weigh as much as a singular log, either simplyfy it or make it harder but I can't explore as much as in medieval and that's unfun. Also, have yet to see a backpack upgrade. Is there even?
Mounts?! MOUNTS?!

[h2]Conclusion[/h2]
I trusted Toplitz with this one because Medieval was a hard learning curve, but all the stuff at least made sense.
This one doesn't make much sense right now and seriously would be FINE IN EARLY ACCESS
IF IT WASN'T CALLED A "DYNASTY" GAME, LOOKS AND PLAYS LIKE ONE BUT ALREADY IS SO MUCH WORSE THAN THE PREQUEL?!
Thanks for the discount when I have Medieval tho :)

review:
I'm really trying to enjoy this game, as I love the time period and location. However, there still a lot of shortcomings in game in my opinion.

Pros:
- graphics are great
- background music is fitting to the theme and very relaxing
- crafting from dynasty inventory (has been introduced with the latest update awesome!)
- combat (has been improved in the latest update, but still requires work, especially where movement is concerned)
- skill system (has been revamped in the recent update)

Needs improvements:
- crafting and building mechanics are solid foundation, but could use some improvements (too much clicking through radial menus, clearly designed to work well on consoles, I'm a PC gamer, I don't care about consoles at all)
- villager and NPC AI (their pathing needs a lot of improvement; they constantly get stuck on or even in things, it has gotten a little better with the recent update!)
- story (I know this EA, but God is the story and dialogue that is in the game cheesy and cliché AF)
- character movement (Please stop using the same buttons for two things! If I press A or D I just want my character to strafe left or right and not turn around in random directions. This would also improve the combat. This is again another implementation designed to ease play on consoles, quite frankly IDGAF about consoles)

Missing:
- character customization (I don't know if this a planned thing or not, but this is completely lacking in the game, including the option to play as a female character)

TLDR:
The recent update has improved a lot of things, but to call this a complete or great game yet would be to early. The biggest gripe I have at this point is the controls. It's clearly designed to work with a controller and I hate that! I'm a PC gamer and play with mouse and keyboard! Considering that this game is only available on PC, this is really poor design choice, but I would hazard a guess that a console release is planned in the future.

I wish there were other options then just Yes and No to chose from, but the short-comings of the game I can't fully recommend the game yet! If you want to support the developer and love this genre like me, than by all means give it a go!

Like most EA titles coming out, this one has plenty of issues that need ironed out before it's worth playing/buying.  

Graphics are quite nice and the overall atmosphere of the game is definitely there.... unfortunately though, that ends the good points of the game atm.

Between an endless list of chores to perform just to maintain a minor village and the needs system making you scratch your head on what is what, you'll end up frustrated and confused.  Even playing on creative mode and building everything needed for the village, the micromanagement of having manually swap crops for each season instead of being able to assign a crop rotation is extremely annoying.  Add in super slow progression and feeling like you're a piece of wet tissue paper in combat to make for an abysmal gaming experience.

Compound that further with the mind numbing and rather asinine decision to make the player rediscover motherload resources daily to keep your workers functioning and you'll regret not refunding the game.

I'd give it a good 6 months or a year to see if things have improved but I wouldn't waste my money at this point.

review:
This is just sad. I liked Medieval Dynasty, even tho it isnt a perfect game by any means either.. but this? I dont even know what to call it. Everything is clunky, buggy, and plain worse than in Medieval Dynasty. It feels like a [b]bad[/b] tech demo for Medieval Dynasty, not the other way around.

Game design wise, it feels like you dont get to do the things you want at all. What do you need early on? Food! Hunters are locked behind dynasty level 7. We didnt even get that far before quitting for other reasons. Animals constantly attack you, so weapons would be great too. Dynasty level 11.. oh and it's not like they stop spawning just because you put your village there, nah. Character progression? Pretty much a placeholder. Forget about skill trees, you are lucky if the 2-3 perks even work.

Performance gets really bad, but maybe part of it was because i was hosting. Medieval Dynasty didnt run well either, but this is just a joke. I run a 3060 TI on a 7700k, and entering the first village i already dropped to 21 FPS. This game simply is not that demanding. I earn my living with software too. It just is not.

It feels like an empty husk of a game. When you skin animals there is no feedback whatsoever. No hit sound, no blood.. you stab your dagger next to a corpse into the ground with no visual or audio effect whatsoever, then the corpse disappears. We found trees that had no hitbox. Water only exists as a visual effect. Forget about swimming, you can just run through it as if it didnt exist at all. Truth be told, it will be a smoother ride than on actual ground since there wont be plants in your way. Villagers didnt figure out how to sleep yet. Drinking doesnt exist as a mechanic. I dont think you can get poisoned either. There is no weight restrictions anymore.. you can just walk around with 40 logs or so. Plenty of animations and interactions feel clunky as hell. Clients had tons of problems even swapping weapons in time to fend of animals sometimes. I think they tried to improve the UI, but it just somehow feels even less intuitive where things are. Menus feel too "artsy" imho, but maybe that's just me. The building mechanic is very similar, but the items needed for that part dont show up in the middle of the screen anymore. Paths? I guess they forgot to implement them here. 

[b]TL;DR:[/b] Seriously? Sorry devs, but this feels like a proof of concept tech alpha that nobody should have to pay more than 5 bucks for. Certainly not worth the "full price" (measured in comparison with Medieval Dynasty) you are charging. It [b]absolutely is not a full game yet, not even close[/b]. There might be potential with it, but as of right now, we feel scammed. If we still could, we would probably refund the game. In Medieval Dynasty you wanted to progress, here you just want to get it over with.

review:
The game is pretty bare bones in terms of progression (character perks etc) and overall gear stats. I don't see any genuine armor with useful stats - just cosmetic impact. 
The village management system is convoluted and generally user unfriendly. For example, there is a rations toggle for each villager need that can be switched between enough to make them happy and some sort of half rations that just make them miserable (why is that even there?) and it resets to the one that makes them unhappy at each new season and sometimes during the season. No clue why it does that - totally infuriating. 

The screen that lets you manage the jobs in the village - another atrocity: no sorting, so way to see what the particular building is producing without clicking on details. The bigger the village the more this unmitigated disaster grows. 

And last but not least, the horrendous coop: the host will lag like hell and for the client there will be unresponsive inputs and rubber banding galore. As a client, you press a hot key to switch to a weapon or tool from the bar and an sheathing animation plays but you still have the original tool or weapon equipped. Works just as bad from the wheel. 
Also as a client, once the village is nice and big, it will barely load - like 4-5 minutes after spawning into the game the buildings are still not loaded in. If you plan to have anything bigger than two tents and shit-house in the village in coop, prepare yourself for 'fun times'.

Do not recommend at this stag of development - it's not even at an honest beta. Check back once it's properly of early access unless you have high frustration tolerance, particularly in coop, For SP it works better, but it's boring as hell.

review:
I've played for nine hours and really want to be able to recommend this game but it is absolute garbage in its current state. Toplitz is making bank off of the 'Dynasty' title when Medieval Dynasty is the only good game in the franchise. 

The performance is awful and you can read the horror stories in other reviews but honestly there really isn't anything promising about the game at all aside from the general concept of a Sengoku period 'Dynasty' title ON PAPER. The dialogue is so amateurish that it's immersion breaking at times reading text that almost sounds like modern day teenagers talking. There are a handful of good musical tracks but the animations are the worst and the "water-color" style just come off as cheap. The music is also inconsistent and doesn't align with the weird cut-scenes. The model work and textures seem fine but there's nothing that really makes the game stand out at the moment. The character animations are terrible and sluggish most of the time and the amount of heads disappearing from characters randomly is comical. 

You have the option to play in either Third-Person or FPS but they haven't seemed to figure out how to make that work with the movement, building and combat. In FPS your character will frequently engage in a strange climbing animation that will cause your head to detach from your body and spin around so that you watch your torso and limbs "climb" up rocks and obstacles behind you though it makes zero sense because you can't "climb" over anything more than maybe 2 ft tall. In Third Person mode you have the issue of not being able to target properly. For some reason switching between modes seems to affect hitboxes for items and enemies. It's a strange problem that I don't even know how to better describe. It's most noticeable when it comes to building placement which is one of the biggest problems I have with the game.

The building placement is absolutely the worst aspect of the game after performance. The restrictions on where you can build and what can and can't obstruct placement is arbitrary at best. You can have a giant completely vacant lot with no foliage or objects in sight but for some reason you can only place a tiny building at a specific angle. This is SOMEHOW affected by your camera view as well! Sometimes you can't even place a building unless you switch to Third Person and vice versa. To top all that off sometimes when you initially place the building it will rotate it 90 degrees and now you have a door facing the wall of another building and the only way to fix it is to start over again which can take a LOT of time when trying to line things up in this HORRENDOUS system. There is no reason why there can't be some sort of means by which to align buildings in this game. Either that or they need to be FAR more forgiving with clipping. This especially rings true considering how difficult it is to even place an item. Half the time the 'placeholder' that you set down when you decide to build something doesn't even visually match what it turns into when you construct it leading to stairs and doors being in unwanted places. Did I mention you don't get your resources back once you've placed the flooring down which has to be completed BEFORE the game reveals to you that your building has been rotated? It also wastes hammer durability building and re-building. It wouldn't be that big of an issue if you could freely move doors and windows which you sometimes can and sometimes can't!

With all that out of the way I think the biggest problem with the game to me personally is that it doesn't feel Japanese at all. The icon for the game is just fake Kanji and it really symbolizes the crux of the issues with the aesthetics: this is a game that is trying to LOOK like it takes place in Sengoku era Japan. What the game is desperately missing and I suspect won't ever be fixed is that the game doesn't FEEL like it takes place in Japan at all. It feels like a cheap asset pack using the Medieval Dynasty engine with some lite nods to Japanese culture thrown in to pander to a western audience. It's so off-putting at times that I can't help but wonder who exactly involved in the development of this game is the one in charge of adapting Japanese culture because I find it hard to believe it's anyone with anything more than a superficial knowledge of Japan and access to Wikipedia.

It will take a LOT of work to fix the problems with this game. I know Toplitz games are notorious for poor optimization because I was barely able to run Medieval Dynasty when it launched but I'm fairly sure the gameplay mechanics can be fixed at least when it comes to building placement since it's a pivotal part of the game. The one thing that I will remain skeptical of until I see otherwise is the general vibe and aesthetic of the game. 

The most recent Kintsugi Update released with a trailer that is almost comically unaware of itself. Kintsugi is the art of repairing broken pottery with golden lacquer yet you have to carry 5 axes on you at all times because they're constantly breaking and you have to build new ones rather than repair the one you have. An update based on the theme of repairing broken items in a game that won't let you repair broken items. They also state that they chose the Sengoku setting because it was a time in Japanese history when anyone could become a daimyo. This is an absolutely ridiculous justification for placing a game in this era and is clearly just using the words Sengoku and daimyo because of their popularity in Japanese media and subsequent export to other countries. They make it sound like it was a period of upward mobility and social advancement when in reality it was a consolidation of power between multiple warring factions that bathed the land in blood. This game could take place at any point in feudal Japan with the premise of just being a refugee of war starting a village in the middle of nowhere yet they went with a false pretense. The decision-making at Toplitz is baffling.

Because its boring struggling for breath and taking hours to walk anywhere...and having nothing to do because you can't hunt, or explore if everything kills you.

And I can never guess the right one, so I can't use those decorations...at all.  Why don't you ghost these decorations like the buildings.  So I can build it the same way?

Everything gets gated behind the 'smithy'....so I get stuck at a point where I can't progress and I'm waiting on construction of a particular watchtower to unlock the tool I need to gather it.
You unlock it, then you need to make a BRONZE tool, but you can't SMELT bronze without the Smith.  So how DO you get the Smithy?

I have CLAY right across the river from my city, but I need a 'regional source' to gather it.  But I've conquered regions where its present.  Same with Bamboo.  My dynasty OWNS the region it can be gathered in.  Why would I want to MAKE ANOTHER village somewhere else?  I can send workers for special projects in places I do NOT have regional ownership of.  Why can't I send workers to places I do own to gather MY resources?

The menus appear to have delays updating 'village resource requirements'  so I'll be at a point where I'm good on food...then change one thing, suddenly it says I'm massively failing.  I only took away FIVE fish.  Where did my food production all go?  

There's still some minor visual glitches with the winter snow layer....and weird lags....but otherwise it appears to be playable.  Just...frustrating and impossible without God Mode.  I guess I'm just a GOD HERO now.

I got a 'Fatal Error' game crash TWICE.  Both during season changes while they were finish a construction project.  After (Spring-> Summer year 2, claiming Enjiro Rebels) which it just keeps crashing and I can't continue playing. review:
Why do devs keep thinking it's a good Idea to make systems for survival games that just hinder player at every turn.  Yes it's survival, does not mean make the game menial & time consuming for literally no benefit.

I really want to love this game but I cannot. 

The good:
 - Visual(landscapes, buildings etc *not the animations or characters themselves)
 - Building presets(I do not think this is the best way but the presets are really nice & it does simplify much of the game)
 - Audio

The issues I personally have:
 - No customization
 - Poor tutorial & misleading(The tell you to build your belltower to start a base & that you can explore/run around the world to build anywhere so I jet off running and find a nice spot to build but then you have to keep returning to the tutorial guy in town)
 - Animations
 - Stamina: First of all devs need to stop making stamina that hinders the player for no real reason.  This game has a small stamina bar & everything requires stamina,  trying to place objects/build/gather resources prepare to have to stop and wait constantly.
 - Resource Gathering: Let's look at wood/cutting trees.   there are 3 different variants of wood you can & must gather all from the same trees(1 resource node). As a baseline 1/3 for node->material is bad.   You cut down a tree(which with stone axe at start of the game requires your full stamina bar, then you wait for stamina and use your axe again twice to split into logs(1/3).  You switch to your Adze & debark the logs getting Debarked logs(2/3) & finally you use the Adze again to get Planks(3/3).   You require to gather numerous of each of these resources so be prepared to woodcut for the first while, although logs among a few other resources don't stack which clogs your inventory and you better know where to find bamboo & run all over the place to gather various resources to build storage as well.      Nodes are often far & wide & you will be running->gathering by yourself *always*(see the above notes about stamina because you also cannot do this quick as your stamina drains in about 3-4s of sprinting).
 - Inventory: The inventory itself is alright. no weight limit just space limit however the lack of hotkeys I believe is just lazy.  You must right click & select options of items in your inventory. When your inventory is full & you harvest/gather something it just disappears :(

Hope they make QoL changes going forward.   I look forward to revisiting this game when it gets more updates.

The concept is a good one and the opening artwork is fantastic but the execution is lacking.

The game doesn't look particularly good, even if it is possible to get pretty screenshots - the game in motion has issues with lighting and textures and just isn't as good looking as it seems on the store page.

The interface needs a lot of work and can be frustrating, the map design is a mixed bag and the gameplay cycle is at time of writing shallow and incomplete and even fairly basic tasks feel awkward and slow.

What seems like a game that offers some catharsis, light management mechanics and a long term 'slow burn' kinda game required only 1.6 hours for me to genuinely feel I was wasting my life. Technically, all games are a waste of time, but any that make you deeply aware of that fact have a problem.

I suspect this problem may be more pronounced as I'm an older gamer and so my game time is reduced and feels far more valuable and, perhaps this is you too.

If you want a game that makes you acutely aware of the sands of time leaking through your clenched fist as your weekend evaporates, or a game that subconsciously prods you to mow the lawn just so you can look at yourself in the mirror later, this is the game for you.
