review:
So this is a odd review. The game itself is perfect. More Sniper Elite gameplay. Nice amount of weapons, maps and modes. So why the bad rating? My game crashed every few minutes and I find out why. Denvuo. Once I reinstalled the game without it installed, the crashing went away. I contacted Rebellion and they tried blaming my M.2 drive it was installed on. I mean, I do get maybe thats an issue, even if I don't understand how. But the fact anti-cheat software crashes a game at all is a big issue for me. Now if I want to play online, I can't. Because the game crashes. 

Only good news is I got the deluxe version for $40 at another site. So I'm not to mad, I'm getting my moneys worth at least single player. Which honestly is the biggest part for me.

-update-
After 156 hours now I can say the game kinda is boring now that I did everything. The online is a mixed bag though. Most of the modes have no one playing. The team mode where two teams face off on a small map seems to work. Sometimes you ever get a full lobby. So kinda fun. Though there are common people that most seems to hate for various reasons. Cheap tactics, quitting/joining the other side...etc. 

The funnest and yet most annoying mode is Axis Invasion where you join someone elses games as a nazi. In theory the mode can be fun when the other player does it right. But I'd say 75% of the games you join are people who cleared the map and set hundreds of traps everywhere while they tend to hide in a very hard to get to spot. Which not only makes it boring having to defuse endless traps (or be blown up), but having to try to get to them and dying dozens of times because they won't move. And its even worse when they have coop going as they can camp even harder.

Now, I'm for camping. It's a sniper game after all. But invaders have limited options to actually win. Limited ammo, you can't pick the ammo you want or the items you get. And past that the other player(s) have the special vision that lets them see you through walls. While you do not. Giving them even more edge. So camping back is harder. And the only real way to combat a trap map camper is to sit for an hour and wait for them to quit or get mad and come find you instead. Often making it easier to kill them because their emotions are high since you didn't get baited by them. 

I still enjoy playing the invasion mode and just learn to quit any game as soon as I see the map is fully clear. It's a sign its a trap map. It would really help if the camping timer was shorter and the range of it was bigger. Often you don't have to leave your spot but like 50 feet to make the timer reset. Or better yet maybe remove traps from invasion mode. Or limit them. Or maybe have a feature that if devs see someone is doing traps maps endlessly, maybe they get a strike on their account. 

And by that I mean maybe you now get spotted as soon as someone joins your game and it doesn't stop showing where you are. This way it at least gives the invader a better chance. I don't know, if they can fix the mode, the game would be funner. 

Outside of MP and invasion though, not much else to do. Except wait for the next game. And at this point with the game being a year old, the devs gave up on it.

-update 2-
Been mostly playing MP now. Only two modes in it every really have players, Team Mode (on a small map fighting each other). Or No Cross in which you each have part of a map and the other side can't cross over. While MP is fun for these two modes, people are apparently still able to use cheats despite Denvuo, all the more reason NOT to bother with denvuo. Past that people also love glitching. There are ways to fall under the map, glitched walls to shoot from, and other such things that let you kill people without them being able to do much.

ANd of course they still give you the silly ability to see through walls. Its very limited mind you. But still silly in MP. A good portion of players camp and use this vision to kill people.

review:
This is a real hard one to give a down vote on.

I'm not going to make the argument that this game is just SE5 DLC. That's not the game's biggest problem.

For context, my friend and I play this on either Sniper Elite difficulty or Authentic. Despite that, something about the game felt easier than previous entries. It wasn't until I saw it mentioned in another review that I realized it.

Enemy spawn placement is sparse. In previous games, enemy patrols and general awareness was high enough that we always had to plan out our attack angles and cover our backs. In this one, each grouping of enemies felt more like a separated silo. If you caused chaos at one location, it would stay there and there was little threat of an enemy patrol from the outside coming in the spoil your fun.

Despite being on Sniper Elite mode, we were able to basically stomp around like rambo and throw caution to the wind. If we stuck to just sniping, there were a few maps where we were able to literally clear out the entire zone of hostiles from right next to the default starting location. Because enemy groups were so sparse, there was rarely a situation where we felt like we could get overwhelmed.

The game plays like a SE game without question. In terms of mechanics and general gameplay, it's fine. Outside of what I said above, it feels like its worse sin is not doing anything that hasn't been done in previous games. I honestly think that's the reason so many have said that this just feels like a SE5 DLC game. Frankly, if that was its biggest issue, I'd be recommending it.

However, the sparse enemy grouping is just inescapable. And, to be frank, I'm not sure if that is the specific thing we were encountering. Maybe the enemy AI is just not responsive enough or maybe the maps weren't designed with enough consideration towards how far the player can snipe. Whatever the case, SOMETHING about engaging with the enemy has just ended up feeling lackluster.

This is something that could be patched in some way, but that seems unlikely at this stage.

Campaign

The campaign missions are significantly worse. Most of the new maps are significantly smaller than SE5, and every single map has a massive underground bunker. Massive Underground bunker is a fun trope for 1 mission or something, but every single one is just too much. Especially considering this game is supposed to be about sniping, there is just way too much close quarters. Close quarters and stealth wouldn't be a big issue, but I personally find the combat controls to be very clunky. Kind of a personal gripe, but i feel like if the devs want the speed of intensity of a first person shooter, they can't have that in a third person shooter. This was also true to some degree for SE5, but not nearly as noticeable. 


Survival

Coop Survival was why i bought this game, as my friends and I loved that in SE5. Nobody wanted to buy this game because it seemed like a lot for the same game we were already playing. I decided to be the guinea pig and buy the game on sale with all the dlcs. All the dlcs except the k98 and the 1911 because i'm not going to debase myself that far to buy those. The new guns and maps for survival were why i was interested in this game, far more than anything else it offered. The new survival maps are bad. Very bad. Of the three new maps, two of them (I can't be bothered to remember their stupid names) have absolutely no elevation, which just feels odd for a sniping game. The map with the windmill is nice, but feels like a massive missed opportunity. It's very small, and every operation plays out the same way. I don't know why the tunnels are blocked off, they would have been nice. I don't know why the map is so small, they could have easily expanded the map across the river like the dlc mission it was based on. The map could have been much more diverse than either sit in windmill or sit in barn. The new town map makes my soul very angry, because it seems to have been made out of spite more than anything else. A town map, with 0 enterable buildins. A town map with spires and steeples, that are completely sealed off. Most of the outposts are out in the open, and will be lost if you don't mine the whole map to obilivion. Forgive my uncouth expectations, but i would prefer sniping in my sniping game instead of mine laying. And this map also suffers from being very small, inexplicably. The last new map is a massive flat open area with a sligtly raised path in the middle. Can you fight in the massive hotel like in the campaign? No that's out of bounds silly.  Can you get up in the massive railway tower thing and snipe from up high? No that's all sealed off you silly willy. The devs want you to sit in a concrete parking lot, and that is all you will do. Thankfully the devs have added 3 survival maps from se5, and these three maps are all much better than any of the new ones. Please just add the rest of the se5 survival maps, and we can collectively ignore the new ones. 

Guns

I'm a massive history swine so cool old guns will get me to buy any game or dlc eventually. Hearing about the new guns in this game got me really excited. Some of the new guns are nice, some of them are missed opportunities and some are just bad. I think all three of these ideas kind of are true in equal parts, so i don't feel any of them should be a tagline for the whole topic. The Ruby, model 1935 and the berthier are nice, good job on those. The nagant revolver, and the svt 40 are nice, but not my personal cup of tea so often forget they are even there. The lebel is a swing and a miss. Its close to good, but why does it do less damage than the berthier despite firing the same cartridge from a longer barrel? I could overlook that, but they did not add any french scopes. There absolutely were scoped lebel rifles, but you can't have an accurate one in the game. As a strange aside, most scoped weapons can use a japanese scope, despite japanese weapons being nowhere in the game. They were in se5 but their scoped somhow carried over to resistance. The lebel is close to good, just use iron sights and wonder why it magically does less damage than the berthier. The mas has one of the most iconic, weird looking bolt handles of any ww2 rifle. This was completely ignored and just has a straight bold handle in the game for some reason. None of the french rifles have access to their iconic spike bayonets either. the M1 garand is nice to have, and i like using it. Im just confused that there is a flash hider upgrade in the game, but its not available for the m1. Scoped m1s are possibly the only guns in the game that had flash hiders on their real world counterparts, but almost every gun in the game except the m1 can use a flash hider. Just seems like a strange oversight. The Udm 42 was a nice addition, it would have been cool to have the real stacked mags, even if they weren't functional. Still nice either way. The BAR was a nice addition, especially that it is the ww1 version, its very unique just for that. Its annoying that it does so little damage, despite firing a full size rifle cartridge but thats a common annoyance i have with many games so whatever at this point. The bad guns are very bad. The Mas submachinegun is impossible to configure like its real world counterpart, there is no way to take the goofy foregrip off, and most upgrades give it an aircooled shroud from an m1919 for some reason. Looks stupid, for no reason. The browning hi power is one of my all time favourite guns so i was excited to see it in the game. It actually had a stock option in real life that is not available in the game, but you can get some random stock options from other guns instead. And the magazine round count is off for some reason, it holds 10 when it should hold 13. A lot of guns have wrong round counts, but this one is irritating because it was one of the hallmarks of the hi power. In ww2 when most sidearms held 7 to 8 rounds, the hi power having 13 was a massive distinction. The johnson rifle is also one of my favourite guns of all time. The real life version has a big goofy stupid looking front sight, that is one of the most recognizeable and distinctive parts of the gun. This is inexplicably removed in the game, and it makes me very sad. The fg42 can be used used as a found weapon, so I don't place as much gravitas on its issues as its not a regularly usable gun but still. For some reason the devs turned it into a weird rare submachinegun. The mag holds 30 instead of 20, and it does an absolutely pitiful amount of damage. Same as the BAR, why does a gun firing a full size rifle cartridge do so little damage. But this leads into one of the strangest changes for resistance from SE5, you can't use any german guns. you can pick them up as found weapons, but you can't use them in your loadouts. I don't know why this change was made, but it makes me sad. The guns are already in the game, you just can't use them. 


TLDR
Campaign Sucks
Survival Sucks
New guns Kinda Suck, Kinda good

Devs TLDR
Please add the rest of the survival maps from SE5
Please add the rest of the guns that were available in SE5
Just have resistance be the defacto complete version of the game for Coop survival

review:
[h1]Sniper Elite Resistance: A Step Backward for the Series[/h1]

I’ve been a dedicated fan of the [i]Sniper Elite[/i] series since the very beginning, and to me, the franchise peaked with the third and fourth installments. While the fifth game was acceptable, it was clear that developer Rebellion's practices to monetize their games were in full swing. Because of this, even when a new game in the series is decent, I find it difficult to give it a good rating. It seems the developers don't understand that these scummy monetization practices will eventually drive away the most loyal fans, leaving them with no one.

[h2]Gameplay and Mechanics[/h2]

Frankly, very little has changed in [b]Sniper Elite Resistance[/b] from the fifth game, and what has changed often feels like a step backward. The large, open-world maps that have defined the series since [b]Sniper Elite 4[/b] make a return, which is a good thing in theory. However, the maps feel far too large and empty for the number of enemies present. It seems like enemy patrols roam without any cohesion, making them feel like a scattered, disorganized mess rather than a tactical military unit. This lack of enemy density means you spend more time running between mundane objectives than you do engaging in tactical combat. The days of setting intricate traps and outmaneuvering patrols are gone because there simply aren't enough enemies to make it worthwhile. You can also easily aggro the entire map and pick off enemies as they poorly attempt to find you. They'll just keep coming until only the enemies who are rooted in place are left. It should feel like a shooting gallery, but it even fails to hit that mark because it's just watching enemies run around the map and take cover in the same five spots.

I've played on Authentic difficulty since [b]Sniper Elite 3[/b] and spent countless hours mastering the language of muzzle velocity, windage, and gravity. Unfortunately, it feels like the series has put less and less emphasis on this mode with each new installment. [b]Sniper Elite Resistance[/b] takes this a step further; I've been able to complete entire maps using just a Welrod and a Thompson. For the most part, the maps are completely devoid of wind, even on Authentic, making it feel more like a basic hitscan shooter than a true sniper simulation.

Another major issue is the sheer abundance of ammo and tools scattered across the map. You can find enough ammunition to take on a small army, let alone the hundred or so enemies on a given map. Generators, which used to be a rare and valuable way to mask your shots, are now plentiful. On the third map alone, I found six generators all within close proximity. This laziness in item placement shows a lack of thoughtful design. Ammo carts appear in nonsensical locations, like by a lone shrub hundreds of feet from any enemy patrol. The entire experience feels empty, lacking challenge, and poorly designed.

[h2]Story and Setting[/h2]

Like other [b]Sniper Elite[/b] games, the story is largely a backdrop for the action, but I found myself so annoyed with the main character, Harry, that I turned off all in-game voices and relied solely on subtitles. While I tried switching to Karl, I was disappointed to find he still spouts his same tired, overly-obvious lines, like "Tall grass, good for hiding" and "SMG, in case things get hectic." These lines feel like they were written for infants and serve as nothing but an annoying distraction. Harry, however, is on another level, sounding like a bargain-bin Jason Statham. With his punchable face and horrible voice, I ended up skipping every cutscene and ignoring the story entirely.

[h2]Graphics and Sound[/h2]

Visually, [b]Sniper Elite Resistance[/b] looks like a game from 2010. There are times when it looks worse than games like [i]Halo: Reach[/i], especially the jagged, low-detail mountains in the background. It's clear that Rebellion is still using the same engine it's been beating to death since [i]Aliens vs. Predator[/i]. Anti-aliasing still doesn't work, and like the previous games, I had to install a third-party tool like ReShade to get any modern visual effects. The game has severe screen tearing even with G-Sync enabled on high-end hardware. Many of the assets, including guns, enemy models, and animations, appear to be copy-pasted directly from [b]Sniper Elite 4[/b] and [b]5[/b]. The sound is acceptable, but I can't speak to the music, as I turned that off along with the voice acting.

[h2]Pros and Cons[/h2]

[b]Pros:[/b]

    The fundamental sniping and stealth mechanics are still present, though watered down

    It still feels like a [b]Sniper Elite[/b] game

[b]Cons:[/b]

    Game is far too easy, even on the hardest difficulty

    Mind-numbing story and terrible voice acting

    Outdated graphics and technical issues

    Repetitive and uninspired mission design

    Maps feel empty due to low enemy count

    The inclusion of Denuvo anti-tamper, which causes occasional performance hitches

    Scummy monetization practices for legacy content

[h2]Conclusion[/h2]

[b]Sniper Elite Resistance[/b] is a disappointing entry in a series that I once loved. It feels like a tired and uninspired sequel, relying on the same old formula without adding anything new or interesting. The game's core mechanics, which have been a highlight of the series, are undermined by lazy design choices and a lack of polish. This is all compounded by Rebellion's business practices. It’s hard to justify their approach when they are charging $4-5 for two guns—the Mosin and the 1911—that have been staples in every previous [b]Sniper Elite[/b] game. These aren’t even included in the season pass, forcing players to pay extra on top of their full-priced game and season pass purchase. This makes the company feel more like an asset flip operation than a true developer. I would only recommend this to the most die-hard fans of the series, and even then, I'd suggest waiting for a significant sale.

review:
I wouldn't by any means say this is a horrible game, but its just a disappointment. Sniper Elite Resistance reused assets from Sniper Elite 5, which in itself isn't a deal breaker, but when i can recognize certain rooms from SE5 in SER, that's where we begin having problems. The Kill Challenges are also the exact same as Sniper Elite 5, with maybe a few that are different. I mostly bought this game knowing that I was getting that, and only because i wanted to get all the achievements in this game, like I did in SE5. I'll list off some pros and cons:

Pros:
-It's definitely a fun experience if you can get past it being the exact same game as SE5 (that's why i say it isn't horrible)

-A new range of weapons in all three categories with a lot of the guns that were in SE5 and previous games

-The new propaganda missions add more challenges to the already existing campaign levels. I'm dreading going for completing them on authentic, but that's all good.

-If your computer can run SE5, it can run this as it's the exact same engine.

Cons:
-Harry Hawker isn't really all that different from Fairburne aside from the few quips that he uses when you kill an enemy in a creative manner. The fact that they marketed the whole game on Hawker is a little annoying and odd.

-Blatant asset reuse, there's a room specifically on the final DLC of this game that they used in the second DLC map on SE5. I'm sure there's more, but that's the most blatant one that I can name.

-The Propaganda Missions are a bit lazy in terms of what you're paying for. I do like that you can unlock them as you go through the campaign, but it just feels like another reason to beef up pricing.

-The AI with the enemies feels somewhat more reactive than in SE5, they definitely get alerted faster in this game. It's definitely not as much of a con as these others, but it takes a bit to get used to.

-The price tag... This game should be maybe $19.99, with the DLC being $5 a map. I've seen other people say this entire game is just a DLC for SE5, which I can agree with to an extent. But after playing this, I scratched my head after spending nearly $80 to buy both the game and the Season Pass.

Overall, I think this game can be fun if you're like me who gets excited at any announcement of a new Sniper Elite title. But if you're a casual fan and a little more frugal with what games you buy at full price, I'd say if you're going to buy this, wait until it's on sale. It's not worth the money it is at retail price.

review:
Short but not sweet rehash of SE5. Very much overpriced. Pros: Solid SE5 gameplay (the game engine is obviously very mature by now), familiar gameplay and existing muscle memory from SE5 carry over.  Cons: Where to begin? SER is basically a download-pack for SE5 but sold as a full game. For the asking price thats more than just "cheeky". SE Resistance is way too short, one campaign mission location is even reused with only slightly different objectives, assets and enemy voice lines are ca. 90% identical.

The remaining 10% are performed by the new protagonist, and that one does not come even close to the stoic Karl Fairburne who is rightfully beloved by the Sniper Elite player community. The "new guy" annoys me because of, in my opinion, badly written and overly chatty dialogue. The British accent is fine in my book, but an accent alone does not infuse personality or likability into a one-dimensional, scraggly-bearded guy that I find not much reason to care about. Also, he talks so much that I wish being able to mute his voice altogether.

I waited a long time for a Steam sale to purchase the standard edition of Sniper Elite Resistance, and yet I still feel ripped off by Rebellion. Frankly, if I was not an avid fan of the SE franchise from the very beginning and enjoyed how installments of the series kept improving more and more, I would be even more annoyed. I close my eyes and try to think happy thoughts, but SER is too brief and too expensive to warrant my recommendation.

review:
A deliberately bad review for a mediocre, but quite playable game. I'd like to avoid the cliche's of quantifying my opinion with being a "long time fan since the very beginning" but it does matter here, because the experience of playing Sniper Elite Resistance to a brand new player will be very different than for OGs like myself. As the king of verbosity, I'm gonna do my best to make this a tolerable read.

-A brief mention of Sniper Elite 4 and 5

Most of us Sniper Elite old heads all revere SE4 as the pinnacle of the franchise's greatness. You will have a few argue for 5, but not as many as there are for it's predecessor. Sniper Elite 4 is everything it promised it would be. In particular, the level design, AI, ambiance, it feels intense when you're immersed. Many of us were insane with joy when 5 came out because we figured as the very worst case scenario, we would just get more Sniper Elite 4, and that was ok. Well, it didn't work out that way.

Unfortunately SE5 fell short in a few important areas. I don't know exactly what happened. The team members changed, or the development lead, I don't know, but someone with real talent clearly left. One of the most outstanding qualities of SE4 was the depth, layout, and excellence of it's level design. "Someone", "Some folks?" had a whole hell of a lot of talent and did tremendous work when they helped develop the levels in the game. It wasn't just that they were fun to play, but they were well thought-out, sensible, functioned beautifully as a real, in-motion, alive, enemy environment. The game was truly a landmark achievement in the series and it just got everything right. 

One of the reasons for this (in my humble opinion), is that weapon unlocks weren't reduced to the "fetch-stupidity" of finding benches, instead you had to use the actual weapon, kill so many enemies, achieve so many head-shots, or ricochets, or environmental kills etc. It gave you a reason to force yourself to use each weapon and start to really intuitively understand the strengths and weaknesses, as well as explore the different functions and limitations, and it made you damn good at it. As you progressed, you open the upgrades for each weapon. It was perfect.

-Some core considerations that come down to opinion and preference.

I completely understand that some of you might prefer the simplicity of finding a bench in order get unlocks, but consider this... Each level in Sniper Elite 5, and Resistance are now bound to basing their design AROUND these benches. It means that instead of an organic piece of WW2 hostile territory designed to function as a real place for you to tactically approach, the maps are now just glorified target ranges that are really hollow, lack function, and especially lack challenge. Don't be afraid of enemy snipers in 5, or resistance. You will see each one long before they see you, and even on authentic they will barely bother with you until you disturb the peace. The replay-ability for an OG is abysmal, because all we had to do was find these stupid benches and we never have to revisit a level ever again. For new players it will be better, but certainly not great, because you'll be moving on once the shock and awe of brutal xrays, and the unlock process is complete. 

Some of you might play on authentic like you're supposed to, but you won't really have a reason to keep going once your fetch quests are done. I realize it may seem like I'm trying to sell you a grind, and in some ways I am, but the superior environments of 4 made it hardly feel like a grind. How many of you even know that you can shoot an enemy in the grenade to cause it to explode and watch your target's body rag-doll into oblivion in slow-mo? Oh you had no idea? Yeah that's because the opportunities have been greatly decreased after Sniper Elite 5 and onward. 

-Resistance

To put it simply, Sniper Elite 4 was the peak of Sniper Elite as a whole, it declined sharply with Sniper Elite 5. and now we enter RESISTANCE, which is similar to 5, except even MORE degraded. There are countless bugs, bad pathing, the AI is officially at an all time low, and I was angry with it in 5, but now it's atrocious. Sniper Elite Resistance is a nothing but a linear exploration of a shooting range. It's not a living, breathing, chess-board for you to try to out-think. If you are ok with this, and you just need to pop heads, i'd say go for it if it wasn't basically a 20 dollar expansion for 5, priced at 50 bucks. I once had so much praise for this series, I loved it, but you can see what happens to any IP once it reaches it's pinnacle. The developers come like the grim reaper to throw medicore weapon packs, and more "levels" of flipped assets. 

-No Karl, not terribly important.

I'll mention that Karl isn't a playable character, but a skin you can unlock later, but I'm not really using this as a basis for my low rating. Even though Harry is AWFUL in every conceivable way. Pudgy, uninspired, annoying and infuriating to look at, but again, this is a matter of opinion. I would understand a new character if they took us to World War 1, or Vietnam, or to a new era, but if we are forever trapped in WW2, at least give us the man.

-Mild Quality of life changes from 5 but the bugs make them not relevant.

The typical stuff, graphics, fov options, and modes but otherwise remains an asset flip. I could live with an asset flip, and even a profoundly unlikable protagonist if only the game wasn't a mess. It's shoddy, your character gets locked up on things, you go to throw distraction salutes and literally it never works. They may shoot at you through the wall with their xray vision, or they may shoot in some random direction, or they will ignore it entirely. This game is broken, and most of the people giving it positive reviews are either new players, or surface level players pretending to be long-time players.

I guess that's all I got. If it were 20 bucks, Id say grab it for the lols. At 50 bucks, no FKnG way. Very disappointed in Rebellion as this series has gone the way of Far Cry, and if you think Far Cry 6 was good.... well, you probably wont like this review.

The levels feel cramped and uninspired, more like bite-sized missions than full-fledged battlegrounds. Honestly, this should have been released as a DLC expansion for Sniper Elite 5, not marketed as a separate game.

Don’t get me wrong — it’s not a bad game. The mechanics are solid, and the signature Sniper Elite feel is there. But everything about it feels scaled down, simplified, as if it’s merely a shadow of what it could have been. It lacks the depth and scope one expects from a full release.

What’s more frustrating is the feeling that this was done deliberately, with additional content carved out to be sold later as DLC. This kind of money-grabbing approach, where players are expected to pay extra for what should have been part of the base game, leaves a sour taste. It’s a disappointing trend in modern game publishing, and one that undermines the value of an otherwise enjoyable title.

Less than half-height walls I could not climb over.  I was blocked from going down the same flight of steps I had just climbed.  Clipping through the floor at the top of a ladder.  Wildly misleading distance to objective cues.

Strictly Amateur Hour. This has all the earmarks of a product rushed out the door with inadequate testing - hot to cash in.  Too many bugs for a full release of the 6th game in the series.  This is what Rebellion gets for contracting it out.

If you're new to Sniper Elite, you may like it and the devs may (eventually) come around to actually testing their game, but wait for a drop in price.  Current asking is too much for what's essentially a DLC of SE5, and a buggy one at that.

review:
It's ok, but the premium price for game quality is unacceptable. This game should be about $20-$30 dollars max.  I regret buying it significantly. Battlefield 1 and even the ancient game Saboteur are far better games. As others have said, it feels like DLC and blatant rehashing of the same assets and mechanics (I played Sniper Elite 3 but not 4 or 5). The story is generic and superficially executed. The characters are flat and empty as is the voice acting. The phony French and German accents are especially irritating. 

The map and level design is mediocre.  The physicality of collisions with character controller movement is terrible; sometimes you can vault over sandbags, sometimes you can't; sometimes you can drop off a ledge or over a railing, sometimes you can't. None of the maps feel like real sites, but instead game-world levels. The lighting and illumination feels like it's from the mid 2000's, and is especially poor compared to something like Battlefield 1, the Last of Us or most high-priced modern games. The navigable areas feel highly restrictive (most likely to ensure that AI can move and access the areas) but are still confusingly janky and poorly designed. You will encounter many invisible walls in areas that look walkable (even in the middle of the map) or wide gaps that look like you can walk between something like a truck and a wall but no, you can't walk there. I had one of my grenades stick to an invisible wall 3 feet in front of me.  Harry Hawker might be posing on a roof ready to snipe in the cover image, but you will never be on a roof like that.  This game feels like it should be a sandbox of creativity for getting kills and accomplishing missions, but it always feels the same.  None of your decisions will actually mean anything or do anything to change any outcome.  

If the game designers want to take Sniper Elite to the next level, they might need to look to other stories and media for inspiration. Imagine if they took inspiration from Inglorious Basterds, The Pianist, a Soldier of Orange, Operation Valkyrie or Saving Private Ryan. There are no stakes in this game, there are no people, just cartoons. There's no reason to care and thus no meaning. Once you've done 10 headshots and grenade or mine kills, you've done them all.

review:
Sniper Elite Resistance - A quick cash-grab with reused assets.

This game was unnecessary. I understand that this is a whole new campaign following somebody who isn't Karl (my beloved <3). But this game could've gotten its own subsection in the Campaign Menu of Sniper Elite 5.

This game charges you 50€ (+ one Season Pass of writing this review, who knows if they'll add a second one like in 5). And this asking price is extortionate in my opinion.
Why? Well because Sniper Elite 5's base game costs the exact same amount, but was developed with freshly new assets and huge changes to the  Engine (for better and for worse), while Resistance is essentially just a reskin of 5 which was developed at merely a fraction of the cost that developing a game from scratch would cost.

The asking price is extortionate for what is, at best, Standalone DLC.

And even when you do buy the game, The game still has the same positives and issues that I outlined in my review of SE5, since, once again, it is the same game at its core, but with the caveat that the Level design has almost been downgraded across the board.
It is baffling to me how you can go from Level design that was consistently average-to-good to just average-to-subpar, it feels like the Levels, or this entire game, was outsourced and developed by another company and not Rebellion similarly to how Games in the late 90s and early 2000s would outsource Expansions to other devs (Examples being Half Life Opposing Force, Quake Mission Packs, etc.)

The game has 8 base game levels, 1 of which is a short 5-minute epilogue and 2 of which are the same (One being a short tutorial, the second one being the same tutorial level but with an expanded area added to it, and you start it from the other side this time...Wow!)

So you have essentially 5 levels in this game for the same price of SE5...

The only level in the game that I feel actually lives up to the Design of 5 is Mission 8 - End Of The Line. Because it starts you off in what I consider to be one of the most fun Sniper Nests in the entire series, which is then followed up by a good mixture of urban designs, trenches, and open fields.

There is also just a huge lack of polish across the board. I had instances where I couldn't walk up several of the stairs in this game and I'd just get stuck running in place at the bottom step, or the one time in Mission 3 where upon stepping onto the first step of a stairway, it teleported me several feet up into the air and caused me to go down from fall damage.
I also had several instances of guards during their alert phase just running in place or into a wall, allowing me to even just walk up right beside them and breathe in their face while they shouted at me.

This game released at the end of January 2025, right after christmas season where it would've made sense to rush it out the door. But you already missed that period, so why the rush to get it out the door?

Also, none of my criticisms of 5 have been fixed here either, the levels are still large but not populated with enough enemies, there still isn't a return of SE4's enemy types, no combat between Nazis and Resistance fighters going on, movement is still less precise than 4 and lacks the crouch-run, Surpressed Weapons are too easy to get & Subsonic Ammo is still too common and plentiful.

The only outright improvement that I welcome here is that Sniper Nests are finally worthy of being called SNIPER Nests. You can finally spend more than 2 minutes tagging people with your binoculars and actually take your time sniping several enemies from a good vantage point instead of only being able to shoot 1-2 enemies while the rest of yoursightline(s) are blocked by trees

It is clear that the Sniper Elite series has now entered its "stagnation era", which every gaming franchise tends to get after a while. Rebellion has been working on these games again since 2012 and it shows: The WWII era has been stretched to its limits and I do not believe SE6 being set in WWII would be a good thing, perhaps a shift in time, maybe Vietnam, could help shake things up because honestly? I am getting WWII fatigue from these games now.
Don't get me wrong, I love shooting Nazis in the face and if it was a full time job I would make a career of it in a heartbeat, but you can only do the same thing so many times before it becomes stale, a routine that you just go through, and I believe Sniper Elite has become routine to me, even if its still a fun routine.

But. This game isn't worth your money, unless you REALLY, DESPERATELY crave some more Sniper Elite gameplay after enjoying your time with 5 like me. If you do, then PLEASE do yourself a favor and wait for a sale, this is not a "MUST-BUY-NOW!" title that you should throw your money away for, this is just a quick buck for Rebellion to keep the lights on while they worked/are working on Atomfall and/or SE6...Maybe even a Zombie Army 5? Who knows.

review:
I think it's okay, but if I'm to be honest with you; you're better off just getting Sniper Elite 5 if you haven't already, in my personal opinion the maps are better in 5, it's cheaper and usually goes on sale for much less than this game considering this game is "new" (I use the term "new" lightly because this game really feels like Sniper Elite 5 but with a worse-to-same roster of guns and a different protagonist, who mind you, was a side character from 5, and different maps, which I personally don't feel are much better than 5's and also re-use a lot of assets from 5, not to mention how when it comes to invasions; some scenarios are heavily stacked against you due to map design, as if the odds weren't already stacked against you while invading a host with focus mode and whatnot) 

Haven't played much of the multiplayer or survival since I was never a big fan of either in Sniper Elite 5 so I didn't think I would be here either, tried both, still not my cup of tea, not to mention they seemingly still have hackers and cheaters despite the new anti-cheat, so expect more of the same in that regard, but from a mostly campaign / invasion stand-point, this game just feels like Sniper Elite 5.2 with not enough new additions to warrant the higher price-tag, not to mention locking some of the guns they copy & pasted from Sniper Elite 5 into this game behind a pay-wall like the Kar98k and M1911 which are pretty iconic and some of my favourite guns ever which feels really bad to have to buy as DLC if you actually want them like me. If I had any recommendation for a way to play if you really want to play this game specifically and not just Sniper Elite 5 for some reason; I'd say give it a go on game-pass and see how you feel considering it would be cheaper on your wallet, just personally don't think this game is worth the price unless it's on a deeper sale (I only got this on a 25% off sale, hardly justifiable to me, but I'm a fool so I did it anyway, I'd urge you to not do the same)

TLDR; Just play Sniper Elite 5 instead, it'll be less buggy and probably a more enjoyable experience to you, if you already have, well, you're really not missing out on much, this isn't Sniper Elite 6.

[h1]UPDATE:[/h1]

[h2]It is amazing![/h2]
After 13 months, this game was released, there are still spots on which you can fall out the map.
In the 4th additional map, Striking Range, right hand side of the park bank, in front of the pharmacy's terrace, you just drop into infinity.

Developer and publisher rebellion obviously does not see any need to put their hands on the product anymore to fix errors like this.

Therefore, the numbers below seem reasonable.
The people have lost interest in Sniper Elite as well.

Steamdb:
1,043 players right now
1,061 24-hour peak
7,652 all-time peak, 12 months ago

[h3]Release Date[/h3]
 	30 January 2025 – 14:09:22 UTC (13 months ago)
[h3]Last Record Update[/h3]
 	18 February 2026 – 12:06:31 UTC (2 days ago)

End of update




[h1]Positive:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Very beautiful maps 
[*] Maps with enormous elevation differences
[*] Hidden locations where you can hide
[/list]

[h1]Negative:[/h1]
[list]
[*] The game is too easy – it is clearly aimed more at children/teenagers 
[*] The maps are too small – although larger than in, for example, SE4, the walkable areas are limited
[*] There are too few AI enemies – although on average 50% larger than in, for example, SE4, the number of AI enemies is roughly the same as in SE4 
[*] Too few objectives – with only 19 collectibles per map, the tasks are too limited
[*] Many locations on the maps are empty – empty buildings, nothing interesting to find
[/list]

All maps are very well designed. I like the graphics. Rebellion has once again shown: graphic design is something they do very well. Especially the latest DLC map from Season Pass 1, Angriffsreichweite, is in my opinion not only the most beautiful in this game but also the most beautiful map in the entire franchise. Clearly, they have really gone all out here: there are many elevation changes to overcome, numerous entry points into the central building complex, and just as many ways to get lost. Overall, this third DLC map is the best that Rebellion has delivered so far in the SE universe.

[h2]What Rebellion does very well:[/h2]
Graphic design. But that’s about all the positives.

[h2]What Rebellion cannot do: Game mechanics[/h2]
Because what Rebellion apparently does not master or repeatedly fails to deliver is good game mechanics. These are – repeatedly – as terrible as in SE5!

[list]
[*] In most maps, an invasion (my preferred game mode) can only take place after certain objectives are completed, areas reached, or enough attention has been generated. This often results in players clearing a map of AI soldiers—making it almost or completely empty—especially when playing co-op missions. As a result, the intruder (invader) operates alone against two players and is at a significant disadvantage. Many of my fellow players believe there’s no reason for this setup; invasion should be possible from the start to give the intruder a fair chance to defend themselves or act under cover of AI soldiers.

[*] Generally speaking, all maps have far too few AI enemies. Considering that the game’s theme revolves around fighting against the Wehrmacht—the armies that plunged the world into a devastating war—and that many maps focus on destroying facilities containing deadly weapon systems, factories, and logistical infrastructure, it’s almost laughable to have only about 130 AI enemies per map.

[*] When it comes to killing Hitler—the probably most dangerous man of his time—I wonder why his location is secured by only a maximum of 120 soldiers. Even an alarm trigger only summons a handful of soldiers, which isn’t much of a challenge for a player with some practice. This was already a flaw in SE5; it’s being repeated here. Also, that this man always hides in exactly the same building—a wooden hut with an open window—looks like developers decided early on that this should remain unchanged.

[*] Why isn’t it possible to increase difficulty by raising the expected number of soldiers?

[*] What’s stopping us from making the game genuinely harder for those who want it?

In my co-op games, I’ve often discussed this aspect. All players agree: It would make the game not only more interesting but also more valuable if there were options to play with higher difficulty levels and significantly more AI soldiers.

[/list]

[h2]Additional criticisms:[/h2]

[list]
[*] The AI stands bored around and doesn’t become active even when individual soldiers encounter bodies lying on the ground during patrols.

[*] Alarms are either not triggered or only very late and summon only a small number of soldiers who come out predictably from the same rooms and can often be taken out with just a few precise shots.

[*] Overall, it’s far too easy to memorize AI behavior and their locations—so you’re quickly prepared for what’s coming.

[*] At many points on new maps, it’s either possible or impossible to climb walls—whether through “grapevines” or simply jumping up—sometimes failing because climbing isn’t successful.

[*] On many parts of new maps, it’s impossible to shoot through wall parapets. We’ve long gotten used to not being able to shoot through glass or leaves—that was true in SE5 and remains so in SE:R—but not being able to shoot targets between parapets is ridiculous. It looks like programmers and graphic artists aren’t working together but rather against each other at these points—same goes for fences and railings.

[*] There are many spots where your character gets stuck because something blocks movement—you often don’t even see what it is until you back up and go around it. In attack or defense situations, this is more than just bad—it’s unacceptable.

[*] There seems to be no consistent rule about how high your character can jump from—sometimes jumping from several meters height isn’t an issue; other times falling onto concrete breaks bones as if falling from a much lower height. This was also criticized back in SE5.

[*] Regarding “old bugs”: A few weeks after SE5 was released, Rebellion claimed they fixed infinite reloading weapons bug—but now this problem seems extended from rifles to submachine guns and handguns as well. This flaw can be especially problematic during invasions.
[/list]

[h2]Conclusion:[/h2]
A game that can be completed quickly. Even at highest difficulty level for experienced players, unfortunately no real challenge.

review:
Look, it's fine and fun enough, pick it up on sale, I'm having a fun time with it.
But it feels like it's about five years out of date.
There's a bunch of weird, minor bugs. The animations do that awkward reset when you do a melee kill. You can't seamlessly get to wherever you want, ledges that you can/can't climb over are fairly arbitrary, most doors don't open (except the surprise ones that do), enemies just do the same single path/animation set loop for eternity, the slow-motion kills and x-ray camera hasn't changed in three games, the plot is incredibly ...normal and forgettable. The voice acting is ...fine. The triggers for voice lines trip from both sides, so you can be exiting an area that you snuck into from the back, and your bland protagonist will say "front's heavily guarded, better find a different way in" even though you've already gutted the place and assassinated the front door guards from the rear. The UI is clumsy, and compared to Helldivers 2, the feel of gunfights is just ...way behind the times.
Game's fine. I have fun partly just because it does feel like a game from a simpler time. But it's not a modern game. Pick it up dirt cheap on sale, or buy one of the older games in the series, they're gonna be the exact same thing but cheaper.

review:
Buy it if you absolutely must but never full price. 

The same bugs from SE5 are still here. The same NPCs, the same difficulty. For example, when you invade two players, kill one, and the other leaves but then rejoins the same game, the invasion doesn’t end with your victory. Instead, the countdown goes into negative numbers indefinitely—until you kill again or die. This exact bug was already present in SE5.

Many buildings are reused from SE5. Also, there are no scopes on SMGs anymore, which took away a lot of the fun from multiplayer and invasions.

The story feels like a waste of time—there’s nothing engaging or memorable about it. Some of the maps are decent, but I can’t think of a single one I’d actually want to replay over and over again.

SE5: 588 hours played.
SER: 25 hours (as of writing), and I really tried to prolong the experience and enjoy it. But there’s just nothing to enjoy. It feels more like a DLC for SE5 than a proper new game—clearly made with money in mind rather than gameplay.

If you're a fan of the series, start with SE V2 instead. The graphics are poor, but the plot used to be much better. The developers used to care about creating a good experience... until profits took over.

Kraken

35 hours later update:
The game is fun for invasions only as not so many players from SE5, or they don't know the bugs, exploits etc. Campaign, multiplayer - boring if you play as intended.

review:
oh boy!! Where do I even begin with this trainwreck? Sniper Elite Resistance is less of a full priced game and more of a halfbaked DLC slapped with a $40 tag. Rebellion clearly put in the bare minimum effort, recycling the same tired mechanics while somehow making the experience worse than before.
The most infuriating part? The complete lack of a functioning anticheat. It’s laughable how Rebellion has ignored blatant cheating since Sniper Elite V2, and now here we are, years later, watching players sniping across the map with SMGs like it’s point blank range. How is this still a problem? It’s beyond obvious that Rebellion doesn’t care either they’re too lazy to fix it or they’re just hoping players won’t notice. Spoiler alert: We notice.

This game doesn’t even try to be a proper standalone experience. It feels like a rejected DLC for Sniper Elite 5 that they slapped a price tag on. The missions are embarrassingly short, the maps are empty and uninspired, and the whole thing reeks of minimum effort. Did Rebellion even playtest this? Or did they just copy paste assets and call it a day?
The  so called new content is just recycled garbage. Same mechanics, same AI (which still acts like braindead mannequins), and the same boring, repetitive objectives. There’s zero innovation, no fresh ideas just the same tired formula stretched thinner than Rebellion’s patience for fixing their broken games.
If you’re foolish enough to buy this, you’re rewarding Rebellion for their laziness, incompetence, and outright disrespect for their player base. So if you enjoy cheaters ruining matches, recycled content, and paying premium prices for scraps, then by all means, waste your money. Otherwise, steer clear Rebellion has once again proven they’d rather cut corners than deliver a polished, enjoyable experience. Shameful.

Having played SE3, SE4 and SE5 and seeing the trailer, I was excited for the prospect of a Sniper Elite game with a new protagonist.

However, the game is a disappointment.
Sure, I enjoy playing it, but that's because it's effectively just a rehash of the previous games, but worse.

- There are bugs in the game that should have been patched out by now (can't crouch while you're trying to cross the top of a staircase lmao).
- There are no new game mechanics.
- The matchmaking for co-op hasn't been improved.
- I'm pretty sure they just recorded a few German dialogue lines, but then re-used all of the German voice lines and effects from the previous game.
- They've done nothing to improve the clunky movement hauled over from the previous game.


This game should've been a DLC.

review:
READ BEFORE BUYING!

Did you enjoy Sniper Elite 5? Are you looking for a game that is just like Sniper Elite 5, but with terrible maps, nonsensical placement of enemies, recycled graphics, poor game mechanics, unlimited ammo, and starting locations where you can easily snipe 80% of the enemies in the level with zero effort and earn long-shot medals from? Then have I got the game for you! Sniper Elite Resistance is the perfect blend of Sniper Elite 5, amateur storytelling, and sloppy world building. 

With Sniper Elite Resistance you get a game where the enemy offers no resistance regardless of the difficulty setting.

No more strategizing  how to conserve your special ammo; there is ammo everywhere, it's virtually unlimited.

No more strategizing how to work your way past enemy positions, everyone can be dispatched with ease with the all new "Fish-in-a-Barrel"® troop placement and "Zero-IQ"® AI.

No more hunting for Satchel Charges; there are about 10-15 per level; even if you need just one.

No more wishing you had an explosive or rocket, the maps are literally littered with them.

The best part. . . the pièce de résistance (if you'll forgive my pun). . . is the magic of the standard starting location of every level. This cannot be overemphasized; no longer will you have to look for good sniper positions, no longer will you have to move with stealth to get there, no longer will you have to concern yourself with the sound of your rifle going off. The all new "Fool-Proof"® starting locations have you covered; with adequate cover, ample sound masking, and a line-of-sight on almost every enemy on the map. Once you take them out with zero effort, you can stroll through the ghost town of your own making and complete the mission only occasionally bumping into an enemy; but don't worry, the AI will have them gawk at you for at least 10 seconds, plenty of time to decide which weapon you want to select, reload it, and take up a more cinematic stance before you dispatch them with zero effort.

SNIPER ELITE RESISTANCE: zero effort, zero resistance, and a virtually empty "Underground Bunker" as part of every level's plot.

You can get this amateur-hour Sniper Elite 5 DLC packaged like its a new game for the price of a new game. What a deal!

review:
Being a true fan of this series, I can't really recommend this one to anyone. The problem with Sniper Elite games in general is that Rebellion is trying to make a lot of $ out of it by bombarding games with their games released every 2 years. It is starting to be reminiscent of Ubisoft's Assassin's Creed series. 

I guess every con of this game can be more descriptive if you look at the facts and numbers. After finishing the campaign, I was wondering if the multiplayer (which I used to disregard with respects to Sniper Elite series) was any good. I have been unable to find any match... Checked in-game players on Steam and it turns out there were 500 concurrent players (a substantial portion of them are probably playing campaign). I do realize that the multiplayer supports the cross-platform, but it does not seem to help to find a match, since there are no players. 

I was stupid to buy Resistance for a sticker price. I'd say it is worth buying, but only it is no sale at 75% off the sticker. Otherwise, should definitely be avoided.

It's hard to justify paying about the same as for SE5 and suffering through Denovu's crap anti-tamper software just to play as a propa Bri'ish fella.

The campaign is alright, but fairly short, as has become expected with the series. The levels also don't always feel as open or large as SE5's, and the first and last mission are essentially on rails prologue and epilogue missions.

The maps overall are fine, The invasion mode has returned pretty much unchanged, which is fine.
I've not really been one for mujltiplayer so can't speak to that experience.

The propaganda missions appeared to be broken for me when I first tried them.
Initially the game overheated my system and crashed my game pretty frequently. Still hammers the cooling but the crashes have gone.

The first DLC mission is a returning trope of the series, in a different setting. It's a fairly dull layout, but one you'll get encouraged to go through a lot if you're achievement hunting.

The game overall is a good time, but can't really recommend at the price. Get it on a sale

review:
Bugs are one thing. The ridiculous amount of bugs may be fixed over time.

But the whole design of this instalment is an all-time low in the Sniper Elite Series. That just will not be fixed in a patch, "coming soon™".

Sniper Elite 5 was a mixed bag, probably making more steps backwards compared to SE4 than forwards, but it was ultimately saved with the innovative idea of Axis Invasion. It had its flaws as well, but was all in all, tons of fun to play.
And now they made sure that even Axis Invasion is no longer fun. They took away all the options to tech for damage as the invader (no trench gun, KAR98K is a DLC...), tipping the balance ultimately towards the allied player with their legal wallha... sorry, focus ability. 
Having enough options for firepower in SE5 allowed for some nonetheless fairly balanced matches that were fun to play. 
None of this fun is present in Resistance. It's not fun as an invader, and not fun as an allied player.   

If you enjoyed Sniper Elite 5... then keep playing Sniper Elite 5, and skip this disgraceful cash-grab.

review:
3 years of dev time and all we get is Sniper Elite 5 with new maps? Full-price for the same damn game?!
And then you also have the gall to lock the M1911 & the Kar98k as DLC????
These weapons were already in the game, ripped directly from SE5. WHY IS THIS DLC

As soon as I saw the reveal trailer I knew that this would be the bare minimum. Same engine, same weapons, same mechanics, same EVERYTHING as SE5. What a shame to see a franchise I like being turned into nothing more than a cash grab. Milking fans for all they're worth.

So in terms of how the game is? It's SE5, which was already a mediocre game at best, so don't expect anything better here. Actually it's worse, as there are a ton of bugs on release. How can there be bugs that weren't in SE5?? For some reason this game insults the player's intelligence. With the same 'comment on weapon pickup' like SE5. Handholding for all those gun-ho CoD players that infest this game now. For specifics see [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/MMNL/recommended/1029690/]my SE5 review[/url]. It all applies, because this is the SAME GAME sold to you AGAIN at FULL PRICE. How the fanboys eat this up is beyond me. Even CoD has more innovation. This game has NOTHING new. Seriously, there's NOT A SINGLE new mechanic added here.

Oh sorry, we have a whole 1 new thing. Propaganda challenges, which you'll play maybe twice or until you get gold and never again. Timed, bite-sized missions in small areas of the campaign where you need to take out all enemies before time runs out. Nothing new or interesting has been added with these. Definitely justifies that 3 year dev time.

Get Sniper Elite 4 Deluxe on sale for 9 bucks. You'll get far more out of that purchase. Stay FAR away from this turd. Hell, if you're new to this franchise you can get SE5 for SIGNIFICANTLY cheaper. It's the same experience anyways.

FYI I have refunded this game.

[h1]Sniper Elite: Resistance – A Buggy But Familiar Experience[/h1]

If you're a fan of the Sniper Elite series like me, you might want to hold off on this one until it's on sale—or at the very least, patched into a more polished state. Having sunk nearly 600 hours into SE5, completing every achievement, unlocking everything, and racking up over 1,200 kills in Invasion mode, I had high hopes.

[h3]Bugs Galore[/h3]
I've lost count of how many times the AI has glitched out—walking into each other and getting stuck in an endless loop of walking animations, spinning on the spot, or even spotting me through solid walls. Some ammo packs you cannot pick up, grenades stick to invisible walls, and AI can sometimes open locked doors that I still can't walk through unless I manually pick or break the lock. There are so many window openings that should be climbable but aren't, and hip-high walls that you can't vault over—something SE5 handled far better. Pathways that seem accessible, are not and if you do manage to step onto them, you risk getting soft-locked and needing to reload a save.

[h3]Game play[/h3]
The core game play remains similar to SE5, which is a plus. Despite the bugs, the maps still offer a decent challenge, whether you're trying to complete them undetected or take out every enemy methodically.

[h3]What Doesn't Work[/h3]
Harry Hawker – [i]Incredibly[/i] irritating voice and talks way too much as you play. If you're in Invasion mode, this actually works in your favour, since you can overhear him talking to himself. If you can't stand the forced gritty South London accent, swap characters to anyone but Harry.

While some bugs have been patched, there are still way too many for a game that should have spent more time in QA before release.

Weapon mods locked behind DLC – The Lights, Camera, Achtung DLC unlocks some rifle mods. Wouldn’t it have made more sense to add entirely new weapons as well?

[h3]What Works[/h3]
Bullet time is still satisfying – The signature slow-mo kill cam remains as fun as ever.
Controls stay familiar – No need to relearn everything if you've played SE5.
New challenge mode – A nice addition, even if it's a bit short. Invasion mode also makes a return.

[h3]Final Verdict[/h3]
Would I recommend this? If you're a hardcore Sniper Elite fan, maybe—but expect a rough ride. If you're on the fence, I'd suggest waiting for a sale or via Game Pass. Right now, it's just too unpolished to justify the full price. Here’s hoping the devs sort out the bugs soon.

review:
Sniper Elite: Resistance - A Frustrating Step Backward for the Series

IMO Sniper Elite: Resistance represents a significant misstep for a franchise that once prided itself on tactical precision and immersive gameplay. What should have been a thrilling wartime stealth experience instead delivers a buggy, unpolished mess that frequently breaks player immersion and tests patience.

Technical Issues Plague Every Aspect
The game's most glaring problems stem from its technical shortcomings. NPCs regularly clip through walls and merge with environmental structures, creating unintentionally comedic moments that shatter any sense of tension. More seriously, players frequently encounter game-breaking bugs, including instances of falling through floor textures and getting stuck in invisible barriers that prevent movement. These aren't rare occurrences – they're persistent issues that plague nearly every mission.

Artificial Unintelligence
The enemy AI represents another major disappointment. NPCs display barely any tactical awareness or self-preservation instincts, often running predetermined paths regardless of nearby threats. Guard behaviors feel mechanical and predictable, lacking the dynamic responses that made previous entries challenging and engaging. The result is less a tactical shooter and more an exercise in exploiting obviously scripted behavior patterns.

Harry: The Character Nobody Asked For
Perhaps the most grating element is the new character Harry, voiced by Jason Statham in what might be his most phoned-in performance to date. While Statham's gruff delivery could have worked with better direction and writing, Harry instead becomes an irritating presence due to endlessly recycled dialogue lines. The same handful of quips and observations repeat ad nauseam, making players wish for a "mute companion" option that sadly doesn't exist without muting all other companions.

Missed Opportunities
What's particularly frustrating is glimpsing the game that could have been beneath all these issues. The core sniping mechanics remain solid when they work, and some mission environments show creative potential in their layout. However, these fleeting bright spots only serve to highlight how thoroughly the technical problems and poor execution undermine the experience.

Sound Design: A Mixed Bag
While the game's audio design generally maintains series standards for weapon effects and ambient sound, Harry's repetitive dialogue and some inconsistent mixing detract from the overall atmosphere. Footstep audio occasionally desyncs from character animations, adding to the general sense of poor polish.

Conclusion
Sniper Elite: Resistance feels like a rushed product that needed several more months of development and quality assurance testing. The fundamental gameplay loop that made the series popular still exists somewhere in this package, but it's buried under layers of technical issues, weak AI, and frustrating design choices. Series veterans and newcomers alike would be better served revisiting previous entries or waiting for a substantial patch to address the game's numerous problems.

Score: 3/10

Pros:
- Core sniping mechanics remain functional when not impacted by bugs
- Some well-designed mission environments
- Decent weapon sound effects

Cons:
- Frequent and severe technical issues
- Weak enemy AI that breaks immersion
- Repetitive and poorly delivered companion dialogue
- Numerous collision and clipping problems
- General lack of polish throughout
- Inconsistent performance even on capable hardware

review:
Unfortunately, Rebellion is getting very lazy and greedy with Sniper Elite franchise. I don't think I will pay them more money for this franchise, unless they bring up  some real value for the money we give them.  Their current idea of creativity is releasing a game that resembles their previous game with some minor differences and milking money from their customers. This is unacceptable for me!  

1. Sniper Elite: Resistance is pretty much a polished version of Sniper Elite 5 (SE5) with very few differences.
2. After Easy Anti-cheat's disasterous experince and crashes, they still don't seem to find a better anti-cheat. I saw players who are getting out of map and killing people from there, running lightining fast, teleporting behind enemies and stab them, using unlimited ammo (flare, grenades, mines, etc to wipe out the entire map), using aim assists in multiplayer which makes no sense at all! 
3. There are very few weapons from Sniper Elite 5 in this game, although the story of the game is a sequel to SE5.  You can be German sniper on multiplayer, but you cannot use German weapons of SE5 like Gewehr. You can use Kar-98, but Rebellion thought about milking money from their customers for it. We could use it in SE5 freely, now you have to pay money for that. Being a German sniper with French weapon is stupid to say the least. 
4. I am very disappointed with Season Pass 1 as well. DLC's give no value for the money. They brought back Fairborne and SE5 multiplayer maps with a DLC? Terrible idea! I didn't pay Rebellion to give me the same content with the previous game. It is why I won't buy any more Season Passes or DLCs unless they change their vision!
5. They broke a multiplayer map in one of their updates that was all about advertising their DLC. You can no longer climb some of the ladders, but you can get down from them which is utterly nonsense. I reported it to them, they haven't fixed it for months now, which is alone unacceptable. How can you have a ladder that no one can climb on? Also, there are more bugs I've seen like invisible walls while hiding behind sand boxes, boxes. I frequently saw another annoying bug that makes you unable to perform any action after defusing or planting mines. It's seen like you are defusing a mine, but you cannot do anything. Also you can freeze in game. Sometimes some rifles or smgs cannot shoot even if you push the shoot button, they freeze too.
6. The community of the game is too much toxic. Everyone is fighting with each other. You can report people who are hostile against you, but Rebellion does absolutely nothing for them, just they don't do anything for real cheaters in game. Whenever you kill someone or a couple of players on multiplayer games, they either call you a cheater or they want to kick you, which is unacceptable too.  2-3 people can kick someone without a reason and they laugh at you. Most people abuse kick votes which is unacceptable. Rebellion should find a way for preventing this abuse. This has been a problem for ages.
7. Higher prestige levels mean only one thing: More votes for kicks. Whenever lower people see you joining a multiplayer game, they start voting for you. There is absolutely no reason to level prestige if you don't want to be kicked many times. Perks? Meh...they are useless. 

In conclusion, I'm too much disappointed with Sniper Elite:Resistance. I certainly do not recommend this game to anyone. In fact, I fail to see that this game has any more value over Sniper Elite 5, except for what? Propaganda missions? I can go back and play Sniper Elite 5 instead.

Rebellion should really get their heads back together or they are gonna get a really negative response from their customers on their next releases!

review:
It is fun, but also rather disappointing. I'm not a great gamer but I completed in on the hard setting without really trying. There are bugs like a staircase you can go down, but not up, and a lookout tower you can climb, but when you get to the top of the ladder you can see kit to collect, but cant get off the ladder to actually collect it. There are trenches you can jump into, but not out of, low walls you cant jump over and, on the penultimate level, a spot to place a transmitter but no key option on screen to do so. The other locations to place it all worked for me, but under the viaduct..nope.

Enemies are few and far between, and setting off alarms doesn't usually seem to make any difference to how many there are. 

In total I played for 20 hours to explore everything on each map and finish the missions. So, it you want just a bit of fun, and don't mind the buggy action and the remarkable similarity to the last release, Id say its OK. But don't be surprised if you start wondering "where are the enemies- is it a bank holiday- have they all gone to the beach for the day?"

The last level is as silly as the end of SE 5- It's about 20 seconds long and one shot at an escaping German officer, then it's over.

Overall it feels very much as like SE5 and I'm sure they just re-skinned some bits from that and dumped them into this new version.

Soft-locking in invisible walls, kills with Bren being credited as "MG42 kill", crude models and textures on certain weapons, and more mandatory parkour which gets worse with every game!

At least there are new weapons, but they do not compare against each other as they would in real life. (The BAR has less sight wobble than the Winchester 1907 in game? The Berthier has a higher velocity than the Lebel despite having a shorter barrel, and the same calibre?!) 

As again, the ballistics are unrealistically steep. I know my ballistics well. Most of the sniper rifles in-game have the ballistics of a real-life .22lr. Hard to complain though, since that's been so for every game so far.

The Maps are big, and feature excellent sniping opportunities, but as I said, more Assassins Creed climbing! I hated that last game! The movement gets worse with every game, and I did suffer a few crashes and soft-locks. Good potential, needs work.

Never mind the fact this is so expensive for more of the same, FINISH YOUR GAME BEFORE RELEASING IT!

review:
I was ready to give this game a thumbs up and say it's good. However, the AI has really worn me down over time. It's not fun to play around the AI (half the time). They can see you without Scopes (or anything that works the same) from across the map. The way the AI can mark your (to the dot) location, even if they don't see where the bullet came from, and only turned towards the sound, and how, if one enters combat, everyone within the area is fully aggro and zeros in on your location, sometimes entering into a pathing loop due to not being able to understand how to get to your location. Then there is the clear as day bodyshot aimbotting by the AI. 

I will note, this is all from Sharpshooter. This isn't max hardness or anything. This is middle of the road, done the line, challenge. I shouldn't be punished because an AI decided they can see me through the side of their head or know where I am when they're on the other side of the map because they hear the sound of my bullet hitting someone.

Quick fire of ups and downs
Ups:
- Looks pleasing on the eyes.
- Great lighting.
- Good map design.
- Lots of options.
- Many ways to take on the challenge.

Downs:
- The AI is heavily over-tuned.
- Map glitches make it so you can get stuck on random things or fall through the floor.
- Bullets sometimes don't hit where they should for no reason (point blank bodyshot hurting the target's arm anyone?)
- AI having 280* vision.
- The way map aggro works (why is someone on the other side of the map reacting to combat out of sight and earshot?)
- The AI's pathing.
- Glitches breaking some game options.
- The way the AI marks you (no, you didn't see the bullet or where it came from. You were facing the other way, sir. You shouldn't be able to mark my pin point location...)


Is the game fun? Yes. However, due to the problems I have listed, I cannot, in good faith, say for someone to get the game at full price. I would wait until it is 20 to 35% off on sale and for an update or two.

review:
This game should have been a DLC for Sniper Elite 5, that way at least I would not have to endure Harry's bored voice...

Apart from that the game somehow manages to be worse than Sniper Elite 5 in almost every regard, which is quite an achievement.

Less weapon options, which might increase the historical accuracy factor a bit, as you can only have allied weapons, although that is already thrown out the window with the silenced machine guns in this WW2 game.

Gameplay is more or less the same as in Sniper Elite 5, although with more bugs, which I doubt will ever be fixed. One thing I hate is that the movement of enemies is unrealistically jerky, they twitch all over the place while walking on the stairs, or getting into cover.

The maps look nice, but overall feel unpolished gameplay-wise, as it is never evident which fence you can hop over or not, which rocks you can drop down or encounter an invisible wall. Also I don't understand why every other map has to be dark and rainy. The rain effect looks like shit and visibility is zero. I guess narratively it makes sense to operate in the dark, but I just want to see... An improvement form Sniper Elite 5, is that the maps give you more options to actually snipe in a sniper game (unheard of right?).

Although this does not really matter, as THE MAPS ARE EMPTY. We have these beautiful maps with barely any enemies on them. There is no point playing this game sneakily, trying to get to an advantageous position, as there are at most two enemies every hundred meters. This boils this game down to a run'n'gun experience, which is not what I want to get from a Sniper Elite game. But this problem was there for me in Sniper Elite 5 too.

The AI is braindead.

Generally the game is pretty easy, the only times I got into trouble was when I just ran on the map because there are no enemies, and I ran into a lone soul accidentally.

Story does not even deserve a mention.

Axis invasion is somewhat fun, although the smaller weapon roster effects that as well.

Propaganda missions are a stupid idea. Time limit in a sneaking/sniping mission is just not fun, and is a very weird decision to include it in the game.

The music on the maps is brought over from Sniper Elite 5, they did not even bother to make new tracks...

These maps should have been just added to Sniper Elite 5, a more stable game with the exact same mechanics. This game does not warrant its price, maybe grab it at a sale if you cannot wait until Sniper Elite 6. Although coming from this game, I now have no expectations for that title either...
