review:
[Introduction]

Sniper Elite: Resistance is the latest installment in the long-running Sniper Elite franchise. While many fans were excited about the game’s release, it quickly became apparent that this iteration offers little to no innovation over its predecessor, Sniper Elite 5. In this review, I’ll break down the various aspects of the game, from its campaign to multiplayer experience, and discuss whether it’s worth the price tag.

[Campaign – More of the Same, but Worse]

The campaign in Sniper Elite: Resistance feels like a reskin of Sniper Elite 5, with minimal changes in gameplay, mission design, or mechanics. While the core sniping mechanics remain solid, two of the available campaigns are outright disappointing, offering nothing but uninspired level designs and reused assets. For a full-priced title, the expectation was for fresh content, new mechanics, and engaging narratives. Instead, the game feels like a repackaged version of SE5, which should have been released as a DLC rather than a standalone title.

[Denuvo – A Non-Issue with Bigger Problems]

Despite the presence of Denuvo anti-cheat software, it appears to be ineffective in curbing cheaters. Multiplayer lobbies are already plagued with unfair play, making competitive modes frustrating for legitimate players. This raises serious concerns about the developer’s commitment to maintaining fair gameplay.

[Axis Invasion – A Copy-Paste Experience]

One of the defining features of Sniper Elite 5, Axis Invasion, makes a return here, but in an almost identical form. No new mechanics, no improved balancing, and no additional depth have been added. If you’ve played Axis Invasion in SE5, you’ve already experienced everything Resistance has to offer in this mode.

[Multiplayer Maps – Severely Lacking Content]

The multiplayer experience in Sniper Elite: Resistance is incredibly limited due to a severe lack of maps:

•	Team Deathmatch – Only three maps are available, drastically reducing variety and replayability.
•	No Cross – Limited to a single map, which quickly becomes stale for returning players.

For a game that demands a premium price, this level of content restriction is unacceptable. Multiplayer should have been expanded with fresh maps, innovative modes, and improved balancing, but instead, it feels like an afterthought.

[Early Access Gimmick – A Cash Grab]

The early access model used for this game was nothing more than a clever marketing strategy at best and an outright scam at worst. Rather than investing in proper game testers, the developers essentially charged players to test the game for them. While early access can sometimes be a beneficial model, in this case, it only served to exploit paying customers.

[Bugs – A Lack of Quality Control]

As a software developer, I generally overlook minor bugs, understanding that no game is perfect at launch. However, Sniper Elite: Resistance suffers from numerous glaring issues that should have been caught in even the most basic testing phases. The sheer volume of bugs makes it evident that the game was rushed out without adequate QA, further diminishing its already limited appeal.

[Final Verdict – Buy or Wait?]

If you’re considering picking up Sniper Elite: Resistance, ask yourself this: Is it worth spending $60–$80 for what is essentially a rebranded version of SE5 with minimal additions? If you can find the game for under $30, it might be worth a try, especially if you’re a hardcore fan of the series. Otherwise, wait for a sale or skip it altogether.

[Final Score: 2/10] – A disappointing, recycled experience that fails to justify its price.

[Disclaimer on Playtime]

100+ hours ≠ quality. 

A note on playtime, since it often comes up: a significant portion of my hours comes from playing with friends, not from my personal recommendation of the game. Social play does not reflect my assessment of content quality, innovation, or value for money. When playing solo, I still return to Sniper Elite 4, which I consider the strongest entry in the franchise. 

I paid for it, so I played it. Doesn't mean it's good. Just means I wanted to get my money’s worth. Friends are playing, so I join in. Gaming is social, but that doesn’t fix the game’s flaws.Some of that was me trying to enjoy it, dealing with bugs, or just waiting for something new. 

Developers don’t ‘crumble’ from criticism; they crumble when they stop innovating. Reusing SE5’s mechanics without real improvements makes this feel like overpriced DLC, not a new game. If you’re okay with that, cool. But don’t dismiss valid critiques just because ‘I played it a lot.’

TLDR: If I had a choice, I would uninstall it.

review:
I'm a huge Sniper Elite fan. Charging anything above 30 bucks for Resistance is a crime. There are reused assets not only from previous games here but from level to level again. One level is a retread of the first mission entirely, with some changes to available paths. The story is weak, cutscenes are lazy voiceovers, Harry's voice is grating to the ears. The series is due for a massive leap forward in every way and this game isn't it. I bought it to support the devs, play an extended cut of SE5, and that's basically all it is.

Things I'm wishing for in a new Sniper Elite:

Take me out of WWII. I've killed hitler in at least 6 different scenarios at this point. A cold-war approach would be interesting, running secret missions that would explain why I'm the only one doing anything. A new era would allow for new weapons, slightly improved weapons technology would make things interesting. Remote bomb with a radio please!
Give me a character to care about without relying on tropes.
Make me love my guns. Show me how pieces swap in and out. Make me clean the rifle and perform maintenance at times to improve performance.
The enemies are borderline morons even on the highest difficulty. There's elements of cheating too, both for and against the AI. I want an AI to be so smart that they cause a distraction and I get jumped from behind. NOT a scripted event.
Time to take stealth up a notch - for example, let me steal a uniform.
Don't lose the "tackle the level how you want" approach, but my god it's time for some creativity. Every objective aside from killing a stationary target is "run to this spot, hit E".
On the highest difficulty, please add a wind direction and speed indicator if we get no other guides.
Everything in the world is so static, I'd like to see a new physics engine brought in that allows for destructible environments.

[h3]Where am I supposed to go?[/h3]

Let me offer a perspective about the game's design that I'm not seeing a lot of reviews about- the lack of mega structures or "super weapons". In previous Sniper Elite titles, a player starting a map for the first time will be able to look out in the distance and observe a clearly defined point of interest. Things like giant radio towers, large bunkers, massive artillery cannons on bridges. This game suffers from only having 1 or 2 memorable, large-scale POI's to investigate. 

The game's plot revolves around (Spoiler:) [spoiler]a superweapon so secret, that only a select portion of [strike]Nazi[/strike] intelligence are aware of it. Not even the dictator himself. Turns out this "superweapon" is just a chemical nerve agent, and can easily be hidden underground.[/spoiler] And oh boy, do the game devs like hiding everything underground. Instead of feeling like a sniper game, this game leans heavily into the close quarters stealth aspect. Sniping isn't as intuitive, and is too loud when you're constantly inside of buildings, meticulously picking off enemies just a few meters away from you. The few maps that do offer some decent long-range sniping, the enemies you instinctively want to shoot, are very often in the line of sight of another enemy you can't see. Instead, all you can do is take out enemy snipers that can die unseen in their lookout positions, which gives you more freedom to try and [i]sneak[/i] through open fields, just so you can get within stabbing distance of your next enemy. 

Bring back the skyline dominating mega structures. Stop putting everything underground. Give me something to Snipe, not something to stab.

I regret giving this game too much of a chance.  Not because I can't get my money back (although that would be nice) but because I spent the better part of a week pushing through and hoping it would get better.

It's Sniper Elite - gotta be good right?  When a good studio asks us to put out top dollar for a game, it's not unfair or unreasonable for us to expect a good game in return.  This is why I have bought every single Sniper Elite as far back as I can recall.

Clipping sprites, soldiers being launched through the ceiling from a bullet impact, terrain that won't let you traverse for no good reason.  Poor level design with shots longer than a few meters being made very few and far between.  A kill mission that sets a condition to have a VIP die in a fall that places the map edge at the drop so you actually can't throw him off.  All things that should have been weeded out during testing.

What all of this adds up to is another beloved title that spent too much time and money on the newest, brightest physics engine and not enough doing what we actually pay for.  Making a game that's fun to play.

 Instead, we get a title with too many mistakes, poor design decisions and straight up corners cut.  In a word - inexcusable.

review:
Dear developers!
Congratulations on the release of the new part. But allow me to throw some fly in the ointment on this holiday.

From part to part, this game tried new approaches. And all for the sake of releasing the new part as an add-on to the previous one. Why did you stop releasing DLC ​​for the previous part and release them in one package as a new game?
Overall, I am happy with the game, I pre-ordered it. But there is some disappointment.

1) The maps are raw. You haven't even tested them properly. There are invisible walls (the balcony near the central entrance to the territory of the second map complex, if you count from the first starting position). I threw a grenade, and it hung in front of my face. Sometimes the avatar runs into an invisible step and cannot jump over it at the junction of two textures.

2) Special targets are terribly stupid (in the sixth mission, the scientist point-blank ignores the coal torpedo).
3) Bots don't know where they can go: in the underground factory, they just run into machines and run into them until they die.
4) Huge maps. Really commendable. For example, the eighth mission is a whole industrial complex. But some maps are not filled with life at all. This was not the case in the previous game.
5) The most outrageous. You use a very controversial anti-cheat, but on the very first evening I ran into a guy under the nickname rune8520 and I killed him twice with a rifle (with repeats of the kill), riddled him with holes with a machine gun and glued a grenade. And only after that he lazily killed me point-blank. I met cheaters here for the first time. And I don't know what's worse - if it's a cheater, or a game bug.

I don't consider it a bug, but I'm outraged by the system when an enemy in a network game suddenly gets my favor. I understand when it's a punishment for camping. I understand when he physically saw me. But sometimes it just happens inexplicably. But judging by the notice, that's how it was intended. Sniping is about nerves, iron will. But if you have to constantly go somewhere, it's already some kind of battle royale. I think that the allowed time is extremely short. It shouldn't be removed at all (except in a separate mode), but reducing it to the fact that it's safer to run with a machine gun is also not the case. However, it's a matter of taste.

I don't think many new people are watching this game. That's why old fans will buy it anyway. But this version needs to be treated. And please think about it before releasing the next part. We don't want a conveyor belt. We fell in love with your creations because they are made with soul.

review:
The Sniper Elite franchise jumped the shark with the release of SE5 and this is basically SE5.1. The lack of wind or making it "realistic" has ruined the fun challenging nuance of gameplay, now the game is for console kiddies and noobs.  You rarely have to look at where to aim if your shot is < 200 meters. You just line up the center of the crosshairs and fire, just like almost every other FPS out there.

Giving the ability to heal yourself in coop survival has ruined the fun camaraderie and dynamics of team play and now encourages a lone wolf mentality.

To those that I have read saying they want realism and the lack of wind makes it better, do you then hate that enemy bullets are basically jumbo jet contrails that comes from enemy gunfire showing exactly where the enemy is at in AUTHENTIC? Do you hate that enemy sniper scopes look like maglights pointed at you in AUTHENTIC? When you're playing survival and white outlines show up around the last 5 enemies in AUTHENTIC? Should red exclamation points appear above an enemy when they get startled on AUTHENTIC?

The challenge and satisfaction of sniping is gone. Now, just like SE5, not only is there no wind, they give you indicators in the scope even on authentic of where it aim. It's not quite the red diamond of shame, but it's pretty darn close. So disappointed in where this franchise has gone, and there's a reason why better players are still heavily playing SE4, even 7 years after it was released.

I'm looking more forward to anything that the Sniper Ghost Warrior franchise puts out at this point than anything that the Sniper Elite franchise will put out. It's pretty clear who this franchise is catering to at this point, the casual gamer (mostly console maybe?) that will buy the game, play it for < 50 hours and move on. Well I guess Rebeillion got their money, well played. 

This is coming from someone who put in > 2000 hours in Sniper Elite releases prior to SE5.

UPDATE - HITLER DLC - Finished it on the 1st run through in 16 minutes, seriously. It looked like so much fun. So beautiful , but so predictable. From the 1st tower I carefully removed every single german I could. Then I went to the bridge because the voice said "this person has something I need"  When I got there I went down the stairs and headed back to where there was a "inspect prompt. No one around.....READ MY REVIEW....walked around until I saw Mercedes...yea, Hitler standing there. Over....and literally ran to the nearest exit. Game over 16 minutes. THAT folks, is the best summary I can give you of my detailed review below. 


People, I like many of you really love the Sniper Elite series. I have logged literally hundreds of hours. I really want to understand why my experience from the onset of resistance was so poor. Here is what I found, written out for the developers because this game needs help or it will ruin the franchise. Chapter 1 is so boring that it smacks your oldest players right in the face....SO....BORING!

1. GHOST TOWN - Way too few Germans everywhere! You should immediately double the number Germans in every chapter. We are skilled players and there is little challenge to be found anywhere in Resistance. It is as if you forgot all that you learned about NUMBERS MATTER.

2. TANKS, ARMOR CARS, STATIC TURRETS, MACHINE GUN NESTS- Simply put a huge FAIL. If this is an important operation where are the typical SE defenses? Truck arriving with Germans. NEVER, in fact the state truck filled with Germans waiting for a grenade is...is...idiotic! Drop these things in throughout the next release. ONE TANK      

3. FALSE ADVERTISING POSTER CHILD? The one we all see of the brit standing on a sloped roof. Not ONCE, not EVER was there the ability to do what you needed to show to generate excitement and then failed to provide....the means to get on roofs, cross all the medium barriers, this game paths like a train. Why? Who designed this game? Did they play any of the others?

4. MAIN LEAD vs BRITISH BOREDOM - From dialog to weapons, boring boring boring. All the snap was gone. I barely upgraded my weapons as every table I stopped at gave me ONE goofy thing! Dialog was child like. Why? Why did you do this? Certainly not for the story line....Certainly not for the devices. Why? God knows.

5. LARGE MAPS EMPTY EXCITEMENT - Yes some of them are gorgeous! Not one of them has the density of engagement with the enemy that makes for a game. 

6. VILLAINS? - Nope not in this game. Nothing personal to talk about and certainly no German worth dialog lines. Seriously, Chinese developers? 

7. GERMAN SNIPERS NEED NOT APPLY - All those windows in all those buildings in all the chapters and there were no more than 3 snipers to be found and THEY WERE SO OBVIOUS is was ridiculous.

Never once felt concerned that I needed to rig a pathway in or out of anywhere
Never had to sneak around anything
Never care about the weapons
Never cared about upgrading past the 12x scope went though the whole game with a 5 round rifle clip.

So....I am concerned that you folks just put the franchise at risk. You need to do the following:

1 - Double the Germans
2.- Triple the vehicles
3. Quadruple the German Snipers
4.  Figure out something challenging! Dogs, Planes. whatever.

And finally dump the non-lethal, non American, no story nonsense that somehow found its way into this one.

review:
Sniper Elite:Resistance, was not super hyped for it but was interested as I really enjoyed the previous games. I am no professional reviewer so I will keep it simple.

For starters I have completed the main campaign and got all the collectables for those missions, however personally for me I did not find the campaign very compelling or intriguing and it did not grip my attention, the only thing that kept me going was the sniping and stealth gameplay.

Also personally for £70 for the deluxe was not worth the price even £45 for the base game, if you are interested wait until it is on sale or you get it for a decent price because the Cons just out way the Pros, the bugs can be fixed but I very much doubt they will go out of their way to actually fix the terrain and it just really ruins your experience seeing mass floating objects and AI stuck on bits of rubble or stairs.

While I enjoyed sniping and being a stealthy Soldier, it unfortunately has a few downsides.

Pros:

- Same Sniping glory from the other games
- Stealth is exactly the same so not a hard transition

Cons:

- Bugs, had to restart a few times on a certain mission due to a missing prompt (not saying what due to spoilers), there has also been some really bad FPS drop which I have fixed by turning of keyboard lights in accessibility.
- Graphics seem to have degraded since the last game
- AI is buggy and gets stuck in loops or just take a while to figure out what to do
- Terrain especially in the later levels is rushed and appalling the amount of floating objects I witnessed its like they just pushed it out without checking or play testing, another thing with terrain your player and the AI like to get stuck on areas especially stairs or wooden bridges or bits of rubble.


I hope this helps anyone who was interested in this game.

Overall Rating - 2.5/5

review:
TL:DR - WAIT FOR FIXES AND BUY AT A DISCOUNT

First things first, Sniper Elite: Resistance (SER) is NOT Sniper Elite 6; it's a mere Sniper Elite 5.1, a.k.a. a huge DLC. On a number of points, it's "more of the same":

- the menu structure & UI are the same
- graphics are the same
- weapon customization is the same
- Invasion mode, Campaign, Multiplayer have the same structure

On the other hand, the novelties are quite limited. The main one is a Resistance Challenge mode (more on that later) which you unlock via posters found on the walls in missions. The other one is the return of a multiplayer mode from Sniper Elite 3 (!) where teams face each other on maps divided by an impassable obstacle.

Straight from the start, the "more of the same" leaves place to a "less of the same" feeling. The base game features 9 missions on paper, like SE5. However, of those 9 missions the first one is a Prologue featuring a tiny map extracted from Mission 4 where you get to play the full map, and the 9th mission is an Epilogue a la SE5, a straightforward assassination. As a result, we get to play 7 and a half missions (i.e. less than SE5) for the price of a fully-fledged game. That hurts.

There's a new selection of weapons in all three categories. Most are unprecedented (YAY!) but the roster is small (7 rifles + the KAR 98 if you buy the Deluxe edition, a disgusting move from Rebellion), 8 secondary SMGs and 6 sidearms (+ the 1911 again in the Deluxe edition). That's pitiful and a tad scammy, considering two of the most iconic weapons of WW2 have been gated behind a paywall, and the weapon roster will be expanded later via paid DLCs.

Ingame, we find the same flaws that already hindered SE5, but on a greater scale. In terms of graphics, zoomed-in textures are pixellated and there's a lot of aliasing (especially on buildings over distance). There's ray-tracing but its impact on rendering is minimal. In terms of gameplay, maps feel overall bigger than those from SE5, but are equally severely underpopulated. SE5 missions had a final kill count averaging 100-120 enemies; those from SER painfully get to 60-80, which fosters the impression of roaming empty maps. Enemy AI somehow manages to be even worse than SE5's, with enemies prone to kiting away, camping in place or being stuck behind walls instead of rushing and putting pressure on the player. There's also pathfinding issues with soldiers running against objects, spinning around in place or unable to climb ladders. A number of bugs also affect the player, with occasional invisible "holes" where you fall through bridges and platforms (sometimes through the map itself) or get stuck inside furniture and objects.

In terms of background action, there's a lot to be desired as well. There are LOTS of assets and props reused from previous SE titles, some of which include whole buildings and layouts. Other levels are heavily inspired by previous ones, such as Mission 7 which is an almost perfect crossover between SE5's Occupied Residence and Target Hitler. Credit where credit's due, some of them are cool and awesome-looking but the overall emptiness and number of reused stuff makes the result feel lazy and uninspired. 

As mentioned earlier, the only real "novelty" is the Resistance Challenges. This controversial mode features a handful of TIME-LIMITED missions, one per map on which you unlocked it, centered around a specific theme - stealth, sniping, combat - where you're given a predetermined loadout you don't get to choose and have to complete the mission as fast as possible by killing a set number of targets to earn points based on a combo system awarding you a medal at the end. This gameplay mechanic feels awkwardly out-of-place in a game that's fundamentally supposed to be centered around patience and cautious gameplay. The sniping missions are still somewhat fun but the overall series isn't that much of a challenge once you understood the combo system and has no replayability value whatsoever since there's no point to keep playing it once you achieved Gold in all missions unless you're maniacal enough to try & top your personal best score, especially considering there not even a leaderboard to compare your performance to your friends or random people.

Another missed opportunity is the storyline and setting. Sniper Elite's storytelling (as a series) has never been it's selling point, but this episode is probably the weakest of them all, with poor narration and zero sense of threat. Characters are abysmally caricatural, insignificant & transparent; they are never developped, never even really shown in cutscenes. You never bond to them, never care about them, never even get to know where they come from and what they are doing here... The Resistance itself, which gives its name to the game and is supposed to be glorified throughout the campaign, doesn't exist INSIDE the game AT ALL: unlike Italian partisans in SE4, you never see them, they never perform any ingame actions, sabotages, never attack outposts, never appear as intel providers... They just don't exist. A huge missed opportunity. Same goes for the enemies: Elite german troops (Jaegers) almost completely disappeared from missions in favor of Gestapo members which are nothing more than reskinned Officers: they carry a pistol, can blow the wistle and spot you from farther away but don't have any additional perks, weapons or tools to make your life miserable. Utterly disappointing. Harry Hawker - your character - himself is bland, not particularly sympathetic and ultimately not a hero you end up caring about too much. True, he's quite new to the franchise as a playable character and doesn't have Karl's track record, but still ends up being sadly forgettable. 

Overall, this game leaves a bit of a sour taste, with a last insult: Denuvo Anti-cheat. Once again, Rebellion implemented this overly intrusive system in its game, operating at Kernel levels within your PC. The problem is that, philosophical considerations aside, it also crushes the game's performance. On an RTX 2070 Super/Core i5-13900/32Gb DDR4 RAM/2To SSD (not the latest rig but most modern games still run at stable 60 fps on Ultra graphics), SER runs at 60-70 fps without Denuvo and 25-30 with. You are NOT required to install this bloatware if you intend to play solo, but if you're want to play INVASIONS, you WILL HAVE TO, which is a huge issue for players that have a rig comparable to mine, and I've seen reports from people experiencing difficulties on better rigs as well as memory leaks. There's still a lot of work to do to optimize the game, a song we're all too familiar with in 2025's gaming industry. 

In a nutshell, if you were expecting Sniper Elite 6, you will be disappointed; Sniper Elite: Resistance is a mere DLC to SE5, with less content than SE5 at launch but the same flaws and the same price, leaving an annoying "more of the same - less of the same" feeling. Technical issues are certainly bound to be fixed within the next few months; game design issues, map design flaws, tiny weapon roster and predatory pricing are due to stay however. It looks like Rebellion tried to do with SER what Gearbox did with The Pre-Sequel back in the day, releasing the game as a filler to make us wait until Sniper Elite 6 while charging the whole price of an AAA in the process. In its current state, my advice is two-fold: 
- wait for it to become more polished;
- NEVER BUY IT AT THE FULL STEAM PRICE. It's simply not worth the asking price. Legal sellers like Instant Gaming for instance offer a 30% discount on the Deluxe Edition, which brings it closer to its actual worth; a few months down the line, the game will become even cheaper, and that will probably be the best time to grab it. In the meantime, we'll be keeping a thorough eye on Rebellion which, for the 2nd time in a couple of years, seems to persist in predatory pricing and low-key effort put into game design, content and optimization. It will have to stop.

review:
1. **Poor Objective Design & Uninspired Gameplay**  
   - The mission objectives are vague and frustratingly difficult to follow. Unlike modern game design, which provides clear guidance, this game simply marks a broad area, forcing players to waste time searching for objectives manually.  
   - The level design heavily relies on cramped indoor environments, making movement and combat frustrating. The inability to adjust the camera further adds to the discomfort.  
   - Many aspects feel like a direct copy of *Sniper Elite 5*, but with less polish and minimal innovation.  

2. **Severe Bugs & Technical Issues**  
   - The game is riddled with long-standing bugs that have persisted across multiple installments.  
   - Character collisions are poorly implemented, leading to enemies getting stuck in walls and becoming invincible.  
   - Enemy death animations are glitchy, often resulting in unnatural and distorted positions.  
   - A critical bug involving placing explosives on a safe—if the player defuses it by unlocking the safe manually, the explosive is sometimes refunded, but may still explode randomly. Worse, if this happens before an auto-save, reloading the save leads to instant death upon spawn.  

3. **Performance & Gameplay Flow Issues**  
   - The game performs poorly, with stuttering and optimization problems that make it run terribly on decent hardware.  
   - Maps are smaller than expected, reducing the variety and strategic sniping opportunities.  
   - The game lacks innovation, offering minimal new weapons and features. Some special takedown challenges in later missions are outright broken due to bugs, making them impossible to complete.  

4. **Unbalanced Gameplay & Lack of Sniping Focus**  
   - Despite being a "sniper" game, the level design often forces close-quarters combat, making pistols or melee combat a more viable option than actual sniping.  
   - Enemies are often hard to spot due to poor lighting design, making the difficulty feel artificial rather than skill-based.  
   - Key mechanics, such as finding enemies with keys, are inconsistent. Sometimes enemies automatically get marked, while other times, they do not, forcing tedious trial and error by reloading saves.  

Overall, this game does not meet my expectations for a full-priced title. It feels rushed, unpolished, and not worth the cost.

review:
Sniper Elite Resistance is the same core game and engine as Sniper Elite 5 with 9 (arguably 8) new missions. The price is honestly outrageous for what it is. Both the season 1 pass, the kill hitler mission, and the game should have been included in one 39.99 DLC expansion for Sniper Elite 5. 

The maps are spacious, and decently designed... however, they lack the verticality and replay-ability that I was hoping would return from SE4. They are large, open, and look just as beautiful as SE5. That said, the missions have a "rough draft" feel to them, with one even re-using the map from the first tutorial mission, and there are far too many repeating assets being used to fill out the levels. I've played the first 4 missions and they all seem smothered in that magic tall grass, so much so that it almost becomes too easy (on hard difficulty at least). This is a shame, because I would pay $99.99 for a thoroughly developed and designed 9 missions that combine the best aspects of SE4 and SE5.

Performance-wise, my computer runs the game fine for an hour, then suddenly the frame rate drops into single digits, and the game becomes unplayable until you restart the computer. Thats a problem because the levels take 1hr+ to complete if you're a stealth player like me and hate having your immersion broken. 

All in all, the game has decent, large levels and axis invasion is still a brilliant idea that works well for the series. I would recommend--only if your willing to overspend for what seems like a quick cash grab that leaves a bad taste in your mouth, rather than a great Sniper Elite 5 expansion.

review:
First and foremost, I'm a fan of the series. I've spent hundreds of hours on Sniper Elite 3, 4 and 5, and probably will spend quite some time on this one as well. And yet, I must call it out: this isn't a new game, nor even a finished one. People have said it's more like a DLC for Sniper Elite 5. I would say that's wrong, for two reasons.

On the one hand, it has more content than a typical DLC, in terms of maps at least. That's the good news. On the other, it's less good than Sniper Elite 5. 

Story-wise, the game is called "resistance", but you easily forget about that after the first couple of missions, because there are hardly any cutscenes that feature any resistance members. Speaking of cutscenes, I agree with what others have pointed out: if you place a radio beacon for a fortress to be bombed, you want to see that fortress getting bombed at the end, not hear a voice say it has been bombed.

Then there's the inconsistencies. For instance, more than in any other game in the series, there's absolutely no consistency in what objects you can mantle/jump over. You easily vault over a waist-high crate, but a little chain hanging nearly on the floor outside a café is an insurmountable barrier. There are walls about eye height that you can mantle, and then there are walls about chest height that you cannot.

Or look at glass windows. You can't tag anybody through them, for some reason. Fortunately, you can shoot enemies through them, and they miraculously don't break. Let alone that breaking glass could do something interesting like alert enemies.

Then there's the vocal lines getting triggered at the dumbest moments You walk towards an area that you've just meticulously cleaned of any enemy presence whatsoever? Somehow, that's the moment Harry will tell you the area is crawling with enemy soldiers. Which it isn't, objectively, visibly. They're all dead, Harry. What are you talking about?

For some reason, this game also introduces the brand new concept of indestructible cars and trucks. They look exactly the same as their destructible counterparts, but they're just for looking at, nothing more.

Then there are AIs getting stuck in one place and position for no discernible reason, tanks pushing paralysed AIs around while honking their car horns, the list goes on and on.

Add to this the fact that the most popular weapons from Sniper Elite 5 are now exclusively for people who pre-ordered, and I can't help but feel a bit scammed for buying this at a full new game price. It's just not good enough. Again, I understand that releasing this amount of content as just a DLC is financially just not a great idea, but I don't understand why they didn't finish it before releasing it, if only to counter all the scepticism that existed even before release. I'm disappointed. I don't recommend buying this until there's a big, big discount.

review:
I like this game, but I do NOT recommend buying it. Seriously, what the heck? This game should have been a lower-priced DLC for Sniper Elite 5, because that's what this feels like. Not a full-priced one because it legit feels like a copy and pasted variant of SE5 just with a few details changed, notably the story and characters, but even *then* it feels like they barely did anything. Less story cutscenes/dialogue, no infiltration/exfiltration exposition or animations, apparently fewer survival maps at this point in time, dumber NPC behavior and stealth just doesn't feel fun anymore. Seriously, I keep finishing missions being marked as "assault + lethal" because I keep unintentionally getting diverted into going guns blazing.

I get *what* the Devs were trying to do, give us a semi-new game using SE5's engine with a new story and new missions, but it's just not done well nor as polished as it should be. In fact, it feels shorter than SE5 somehow, even with the new "challenges". The story just isn't there, most of it is given from casual commentary that Harry (the protagonist) makes in game, and the slideshows you get inbetween levels. It doesn't invest you in the plot at all. There's another "wonderweapon" you have to take down which is fine because that's the usual Sniper Elite narrative, but it's not interesting or as exciting. They really don't do much with the weapon's concept, it's just there in the backdrop. The Resistance challenges are pitifully easy if you get the rhythm right, I already have gold medals in all of them and I was just doing them casually. I mean, I'm happy I did well but they're not that fun for as hyped up as they are.

The reused assets are fine and I'm glad they at least gave us some new/unique weapons, but it just doesn't feel like its own game like it could have been, especially when I'm hearing the same songs as Sniper Elite 5 and going into maps that have the same feel, yet are *smaller*.

If I had my say, the devs would overhaul the game by adding new story missions, more cutscenes, more plot and more challenges for you to do. And you know, do more with what the superweapon is this time? This game just isn't that replayable. I'll come back when they add the three--and I mean just *three* new campaign missions for the other DLC I got which will probably have similar small maps that don't add much. It's an okay spinoff game using the same engine and assets with a new story, but the gameplay is barely changed at all for what it should be as a spinoff with a new character, and there's not much new to justify it. This kind of thing has been done before, but much better.

Don't buy it until the devs improve it.

Same old, seen it a million times in a million games that play just like this.


Except, here you also get to deal with hyperaware enemies tuned to spot you at distances you'll almost never get to engage them at, janky AI and player movement. AI will get stuck on stairs. AI will spot you trying to sneak up stairs.

AI won't spot you walking straight past you when you hide by a doorway. AI won't spot your head visibly peaking out over a wall.
An enemy kill target will happily take over truck duty from someone else and drive straight off the map. An enemy group will happily investigate your position because a mine detonated halfway across the map.


If you want to make a game about sniping, make a game about sniping. Not a standard ubisoft stealth game that's somehow even more jank than those titles.

review:
This doesn’t feel like a new entry, unlike Sniper Elite 5, this feels like a cash grab. It’s not a complete disaster, but for fans of the franchise, it’s a disappointing departure from the standards set by its predecessors.
What’s most disappointing is the overall lack of polish. The AI is frustratingly inconsistent. The AI can at times seem like completely brainless bots while at other times, they can spot you through walls with uncanny precision. The graphics are, for the most part, satisfactory but do not seem to mark a significant step forward and at times they are outright worse than Sniper Elite 4 which is odd for a later release. Frankly, Resistance offers little more than what feels like a DLC to Sniper Elite 5 instead of a new game. The mechanics, artwork, and even the user interface looks pretty much the same so it is difficult to consider this a separate game and not merely an expansion pack.
The Multiplayer and co-op modes, which were at the forefront of other games, seem to have been neglected here. These modes have lacked innovation, and even compared to other entries, they feel boring. And let’s not forget the elephant in the room; the developers track record on cheaters. For example, in Sniper Elite 5, the multiplayer experience was littered with players exploiting glitches, cheating, and using aimbots with no penalties, allowing them to run rampant. It is disheartening to see that while there are these types of issues, Resistance shows no sign of addressing them. And, if history is any, cheats will rise again. So, it seems the developers will not stop them.

If you’re still curious, I’d recommend waiting for a  discount before picking it up. It’s not worth the full price!!

review:
Sniper elite is that kind of game, that's a fun 7/10 game where you know what you're getting for a lower price.
The problem is... from SE3 to Resistance, it feels the same, almost looks the same and never goes beyond that. 

The Xrays... it was a fun gimmick in SE2, but every future game they say "it's the best its ever been" but after 10 kills, you seen it all. There's no nuance, no custom camera or replay speed you can control. The Xray camera focusses on the organ you hit so you don't really have an idea of the damage the bullet did during from entry to exit with detail. "See bullets ricochet off bones" Never seen it. I barely even seen soldiers with grenades on their belts. In SE2, when you did a multi kill, you had a camera for each enemy you hit, it followed the bullet from enemy to enemy. That's gone! I honestly removed Xrays after the 2nd mission.

Now for the biggest biittching i have to do, the missions. SE1 and SE2 had cool tailored missions, with scripted events that kept the campaign rolling. Ever since Africa, it's just boring open ended maps after boring open ended maps.
This wouldn't be a problem, if there was some actual good sniping to do. You know, Sniper maps.
If there was more snipers to hunt, more hidden/staged enemies or shooting angles made for long ranges, it would make the game way better, but instead, you get villages and towns, with enemies all within hearing range. And worst of all, a lot of them have you fighting underground or inside... There was one good map, during the night, with rain, it was nice and moody, but the rest is just boring. There's barely any sound mask events that are native to the map and unique. You get one in the first mission (The dam) and first thing you do, is have to break the pipes and cut the sound. There's one in mission 7... but the rest is trucks and generators you have to break. I'd prefer if the game was a shooting gallery type game made like Hitman Sniper Mission, where they could focus on improving the sniping/gunplay, making the xray stuff fancier, and making tailored scenes, instead of getting a wannabe Saboteur (Pandemic Games) game with some sniping where people just walk in patrols like idiots and forget about the sniper threat after 2 minutes.

In the end, i am done with the franchise. Until they announce a rework of the franchise/engine, with a change in era like Vietnam/Cold War, never buying it again. Especially not for 100$ CAD for a 2 day access. If i paid 40$, i'd be pleased.

It's a shame, i want Rebellion to keep making games, they're one of the last good ones that make games like they want instead of doing live crap like most publishers do... but sadly other games evolve with time, and Sniper Elite, did not.

review:
For the first 7-ish hours this game was tons of fun, I liked exploring, gathering resources, learning upgrades, and updating an island of my own. Also the music/sound is very immersive and I thought really added to the overall game play experience. However, I have hit a wall where I can no longer progress, and I am tired of scouring the internet to see what I need to be doing differently. In particular, there are two things that have made me decide to put this game down for now.
1. I have explored two different clusters of islands and have not found a knowledge stone (which means I cannot learn new crafting), I just need one knowledge stone to be able to transport animals to my island, but I do not think that is going to happen. I just want cute little animals to take care of! And no, I have not found any landing pads out in the wild to sketch. 
2. I was finally able to research a second thing in the research lab, a coating station which I was psyched about. Went to build it and I need and upgraded station frame. Okay, no problem, how long until I learn the upgrade station frame? SO. LONG. like at least 6 knowledge stones away which combined with my lack of knowledge stones made this a deal breaker. 

I do see myself coming back to this game, I even showed a family member it yesterday because I was so psyched. At this time I think the reason I am not recommending it comes down to the ease of exploration versus the (for me) frustrations of slow knowledge/progression. Also the glider flying is finicky, having to fly around all the islands looking for little hidden caves and then trying to land in them was a nauseating experience.

review:
As many others have expressed, it's fun for the first few hours.  TLDR; if you like floating islands and cozy base building, and unrewarding grind for the sake of grind, this is the perfect game for you. If you are looking for a fun survival crafting adventure, probably stay away. There are a lot of positives to the game that I really liked, but the negatives are a bit too much for a positive review.

Positives 
- Animations/Graphics
- Movement
- Building
- Map/World
- Concept design
- Building skills done by exploring and sketching the things you see, is pretty cool
- Cozy vibes?
- optimization and stability 

Negatives (and these are game killing for me)

To say the gameplay loop is repetitive, would be an understatement. You do the same thing over and over and over again. The idea of having to fix the local ecosystem of an island is novel, and fun. But then you realize, you're going to have to do one to three things on every island, and it's the same thing in each of the tiers of islands, just with different plants/trees/animals/insects. Including one time, where I HAD TO WAIT FOR A TREE TO GROW, just sat and waited on an island, for a tree to grow for 25 minutes. If you move off the island, they stop growing, so you can't go and do other things and come back, riveting gameplay.

The progression and upgrade system is also pretty lackluster, which makes the tedium of the grind even less rewarding.

There is only a couple of enemy types, and they are all way to easy.

There is no tech tree, you have to find anchors to unlock tech, which is randomly generated, so you have to search basically every island or miss upgrades, models, etc. And even then, it is random, so you might get something cool, or something useless

review:
Updated Review After Latest Patch – Still a Hard Pass
Unfortunately, the recent update does nothing to improve the experience. In fact, it wipes previous progress, forcing players to start over—without offering any meaningful enhancements. The storyline remains vague and underdeveloped, and core gameplay mechanics haven’t evolved.
Skill progression is still painfully slow, requiring excessive grinding for minimal payoff. The developers claimed to have streamlined the corruption removal process, but it’s just as tedious as before—still demanding you repeat 3–4 tasks up to 10 times each. It’s more of a chore than a challenge.
There are no exciting new skills, no added value, and no reason to invest further time or money. Save yourself the frustration—this update doesn’t deliver.




Original Review -  Aloft presents a visually stunning world of floating islands and skybound exploration, but beneath its serene exterior lies a gameplay loop that quickly devolves into tedium. The core mechanic of restoring each island’s ecosystem to unlock chests or recipes is not just repetitive — it’s downright exhausting.
Every new island demands a checklist of tasks: crafting a Field Guide, identifying and planting specific flora, clearing corruption, and managing decomposers. While this might sound like standard fare for a survival game, Aloft takes it to an extreme. The grind is relentless, and the payoff rarely feels worth the effort. Instead of fostering a sense of discovery or accomplishment, the game often feels like a spreadsheet simulator disguised as a nature walk.
What’s most disappointing is how this system overshadows the game’s more enjoyable aspects — like exploration, building, and flight. The constant need to micromanage ecosystems turns what could be a relaxing or adventurous experience into a chore. Even seasoned survival players may find themselves asking: “Why am I doing this again?”
Aloft has potential, but it desperately needs rebalancing. Streamlining the ecosystem restoration process, offering alternative progression paths, or simply reducing the grind would go a long way in making the game more enjoyable. Until then, it’s hard to recommend unless you enjoy your survival games with a heavy dose of ecological busywork.

review:
This is a 4 man coop review: There are several sections of this game (basically at least 2-3 distinct biomes). There is a very very minor plot, but it is pretty disconnected and loose. It serves as just a pathway for the exploration. There are survival lite elements and base building. There is combat, and there is movement (flying your island and yourself). The combat is an afterthought and doesn't feel fleshed out. The movement is great. 

So the draws are exploration basically and base building. 

The base building is good, there is a lot of depth in placing items and not many limitations. This is great, and also finding new pieces for houses is fun, but the drip feed is very slow for that.

The problem is the first biome is really pretty and makes up the majority of the beginning of the game.  Then the second biome type is a less pretty section, which is just sort of boring looking. The exploration includes animals and plants and things. But these get really samey after a while. The exploration gets too slow and painful. 

When you come from a game like Grounded to this, it is just not fleshed out. Oh well, its in early access, it may be better later on.

Review from some friends:
*The adventure is fun but I want more direction and different environments per zone, and I like the animals. Also I hate cooking, takes way too long. And the items don't have a label and that makes remembering what items are what super annoying.
*It would be very cool if the game had cannons. The base building was functional and indepth. 
*The frogs are cute.

review:
The pros :

The updates are adding more gameplay, more structure, more exploring. That's a very important piece of gameplay. 

They have included more challenges, more glider types, more character customization. 

I like the upgraded tools, and the ship building mechanics. 

The recent updates to how restoring an ecosystems works is very peaceful, and satisfying.

The cons : 
There's no instruction on the fact that you have to go to every island. I assumed the game worked how previous iterations worked, where you could skip some islands and still be fine, you just wouldn't have all of the building options available to you since they'd be locked. You'd be down on some rare resources. This was not the case, and I got locked out of advancement for skipping one island chain near the start of the game, and had to spend 40 minutes backtracking. 

The base-building options are ugly. You don't have the amount of freedom I wish you did, so even if 90% of the block you're placing is out of the ground it won't let you place it. This creates a jagged edge, and overall just limits style choices. The blocks themselves are also unpleasing to the eye, an example being that you can't fit all the stairs together in a neat fashion. Why are the endgame hardwood stairs not stackable? The final stair in a set is longer, and it creates an awkward plateau. The trellises also don't fit inside all of the window/frame options, and the window options themselves have rendering issues, meaning any building you attempt to add a window to looks weird. 

In order to plant seeds, you need to place down a dirt mound, and then place a single seed. That would be all great and good and all, but why does it only spawn a single, tiny plant after you do that? The game used to have lush forests available, and now it doesn't. The trees also seem to drop less saplings than before. 

Possibly the worst part is that the wildlife doesn't feel real anymore. The birds/bugs/frogs don't wander about the island repopulating as they used to. They stay where I dropped them from my inventory for 2+ hours and just look strange. 

I hate to see updates in an early access game push the game backwards. Unfortunately, that is how this game seems to be leaning.

review:
-----------------------
Disclaimer:

I believe in a game being GOOD or NOT GOOD.

Not "It's good for the money" or "buy it if it's on sale" or "It has the POTENTIAL to be a good game" or "It's EA so it might be good eventually"

No.

IS IT A GOOD GAME at the time that you invested your time and energy into it, was it GOOD compared to OTHER good games?

That's what I go by.

If a developer posts shovelware, but it's only $.50... it's still shovelware.
--------------------------
What they do good, they do great.

The ambience, visuals and graphics are amazing.

Beyond that, it all kind of falls flat.

It has a pointless building mechanic that apparently doesn't matter even slightly since you can build workbenches outside, sleep outside (even in the rain), put your storages outside, etc.

The whole "Look, Wendy I can fly!" thing is fun for about 5 minutes, then it becomes realistically the ONLY way to get around since all the islands are tiny and spread apart (the 5 or 6 that exist so far anyway)

The whole ONE monster you can fight is only on specific islands that are "corrupted" and you have to kill a tree with two roots so you can basically ad-nauseum loot the island.  Just like you did on the last 5 islands.

The only real difference in the islands appears to be the rare nodes where you can "learn" something you can craft that really has no impact whatsoever.  You can literally fly from start to finish across ALL islands at the very start.  Collect all the learning nodes and ignore everything else. That's.... pretty much it.  Then you go back to YOUR island and "build" things that have relatively no impact beyond being just something to build.

That's it.

That's the game.  it's basically a cozy builder with an opt-in fight if you happen to need/want to go to an island that's corrupted. 

Beyond that, there isn't much to do.  Will it get better?  maybe, but as it stands NOW is it a good game?  It's a building simulator and a lukewarm one at that.  Not the "survival" game it's billed out to be.  Not eating does nothing, not drinking does nothing, falling does nothing, if you die... you get a message saying "I should go home" and get respawned a few yards away with half health.  It's anything but a survival game.

So if you like cozy games, this one is for you.

review:
I've played a LOT of early access games and this is THE ONE that makes me consider no longer buying early access games.... Because it FEELS early access.

Combat:
The combat is horribly clunky. The attempt at "combos" is poor and bland. They decided that in order to use any weapon or tool efficiently, you have to sit there and wait until the meter gets to the yellow spot at the very end and it's the same spot every time. 

Additionally, they decided to put 900 objects all over islands with enemies (corrupted areas) so you're stuck running into things (the excessive amount of large fungi that's basically like being surrounded by trees and stumps) and getting blocked by every single object while trying to perform any combat. This is especially bad because the game is so buggy, you end up getting stuck between the objects entirely and have to spam jump until you can finally get out. 

The dodge is FRUSTRATINGLY inconsistent because there's no designated dodge, it just happens when you're in combat and press space... but sometimes space decides it's bored and it wants to go back to being your jump key instead!!!!! So you just jump around getting hit by things while trying to dodge. 

You clip through islands constantly, sometimes after you clear corruption, the entire island will just change into a new island and you fall through it completely because it is now half the size it was. 

It's bad. It's not fun. 

Progression:
On top of these combat negativities, they set the biome types by ring progression within the map so you're stuck with the same biome nonstop in every section of the third ring, until you finally progress enough to reach the second ring, and so on. This becomes so stale because the progression feels awful. You can only learn new recipes by finding knowledge stones scattered across the islands but instead of giving you what you need to progress, you have to find 50 useless sail types before you can find any type of recipe for the crafting stations you need for better gear or armor or even farming then you get equally sick of that biome being stuck in it for ages. The biomes should've been more scattered, like a surprise, which island biome will this be? 

--------

I genuinely cannot play this game until it's polished, and it's rare I find an early access game that just feels early access like this, but it is just not fun. I got a migraine playing this game. 
It's buggy, clunky, frustrating, bland, and overall not executed well.

review:
Eh... where do I begin....

I guess, first what I'll say is that I realize it is in Early Access. 

Then I'll state the positives. The concept is very unique and neat and the base building aspect is enjoyable - though a bit wonky sometimes). The visuals of the sky are pretty as well for what it is.

But, after playing for quite some time, I realize that the game is a skeleton of one. An empty adventure.

It seems that the devs were so set on making a large map, that they completely overlooked the core of what the player enjoying an adventure game gets excited about - and its simply this - finding cool loot.

You spend hours searching countless islands, find caves, get excited, search cave, empty. Repeat this 50+ times and its really frustrating. This also applies to buildings that are massive, chests you loot that contain wood and stone, and various other things. The work you put into the game exploring, gives you NOTHING.

The devs might argue that you'll find these knowledge stones that teach you various things - but some of these stones require you to 'restore the islands ecosystem' by adding bugs, planting trees, repairing birdhouses - its a hassle. The last 2 islands I just did, it took me a while, and my reward? A trellis recipe on one island, and the same trellis recipe (but a different shape) for the other. Thats like slapping me in the face through the screen for searching for something worthwhile loot wise that gets me excited to continue.

The combat is very childish and not challenging (even though the enemies do quite a bit of damage) - it just feels like a childrens game.

I'm just mainly bummed that I love adventure games with base building - but the entire idea of finding cool loot that get you excited in exchange for the time you took exploring/fighting/ect is missing entirely.

Oh yeah, I forgot to mention that it is optimized poorly. My PC runs it fine,but my GPU gets really hot when my island is parked. When I'm 'driving' around - temps go down. I see much lower temps on demanding games.

I don't like to downvote things as a matter of general principle.  I respect the effort it takes to make a game.  It pains me a bit to hit "no".  But I did refund this game, because both my wife and I experienced really poor performance on our respective computers.

It might be an AMD hardware thing, it might be a LAN thing, I didn't troubleshoot it much.  That said, both computers ran Cyberpunk 2077 decently, so our hardware should be more than adequate.  But, considering how stuttery the opening area was, both in caves and outdoors, for how comparatively few polygons it was pushing, we elected to quit while we were ahead and throw this figurative fish back into the figurative pond.

Oh wow, what an absolute masterpiece! A vast, barren world where you can really feel the emptiness—because there’s literally nothing to do! Brilliant design choice, truly. You wander around, staring at the same copy-pasted landscapes like it’s some sort of budget simulation for existential dread. And the crafting? Oh, it’s so deep… if by 'deep' you mean bare minimum effort slapped together to pretend there’s content.

Progression? Oh, don’t even get me started—watching paint dry feels like a high-speed chase compared to this. The devs really said, 'Hey, what if we made a game where time itself slows down, but instead of being fun, it just sucks the soul out of you?' But hey, at least they were creative about one thing: finding new ways to milk your wallet while delivering absolutely nothing in return.

Honestly, 10/10 experience if your idea of fun is running in circles, questioning your life choices, and wondering if the devs even like video games. Bravo, devs. Bravo

review:
I can't really recommend this game in its current form.  

Pros:
-Good chill vibe most of the time.  Raft-esque stylized graphics.  Base building is decent, though limited in aesthetic options for me currently.  Music helps the vibe

-Unique.  You make a floating island into an airship and slowly move around the map exploring the islands.  Flying around on a glider between them as well but you make a mobile base with the airship/island. 

Cons:
-The gameplay loop gets stale REALLY fast.  

-You have no direction and unlocking things is RNG and some of those things you NEED to progress.  I've been looking for a loom for 80% of my playtime and have yet to find it and I can't progress without it.  I'm kinda done at this point.  Devs have apparently said you can start a new world and use that world to try and get the early knowledge stones that you need to unlock important things but like...im not doing that.  If I'm supposed to play on multiple worlds to REASONABLY unlock something, that's a dumb choice.  

-Combat isn't enjoyable.  Corrupted islands have a sort of node you have to do combat with.  a couple tendrils you break to expose the center and break that.  Then, you do it again.  It could have spiked roots that attack you as well.  3 mobs so far to deal with.  A melee type.  A ranged type that runs the fuck away (often just off the island) and a flying balloon that yells and debuffs you, plus grabs you so you cant move.  I have no ranged weapon to deal with the ranged  OR the balloons in a reasonable way and the terrain is often a hindrance to the point its significantly more annoying than engaging and interesting.  The specials you unlock are kinda fun at least but i find them a bit of a chore to use but i will admit that is a personal preference.  

-General gameplay loop gets old really fast.  Move to group of island.  cleanse via combat and\or improve ecosystem via bringing trees, plants, small animals and such to other islands.  if you don't have any with you, you go back to another island to grab ones that hopefully aren't already there.  Once you have it finished you're allowed to get the goodies on the island which is USUALLY pretty underwhelming.  

I do think with sufficient time this could be a solid game but as of now (early 2025) it's really not.   Once it is, if it ever does, I'll potentially change this review.

review:
This is something I currently feel somewhat bad about giving a 'not recommend', but I want to establish ahead of time that this is another quite literal use of the words. I am 'not recommending' this game as of current, and not saying that it is bad or broken or anything of the sort. It has an enormous amount of potential down the line, and should it be realised, I will happily change it to recommended.

However, I am no newbie to the Indie Early Access scene, so while I know there are plenty of games that have grown from small beginnings, I also know there are many that never fix major issues, and others that outright get abandoned down the line, so I feel inclined to 'not recommend' purely on how it is right now and my feelings about it going in the future.

See, Aloft is one of those games that's in the vein of games like Raft. The idea that you're travelling through a relatively empty space and gathering resources you pass to build up your home and build and so on, occasionally broken up by minor story beats. But, honestly, Aloft kinda misses the mark in a few ways that even Voidtrain managed to nail better (which is saying something, because I felt Voidtrain was very weak overall) which is a lot of the basic concepts.

A large part of the appeal of these types of games is watching your home/base grow as the game goes on. Basically, having your home be as much of a symbol of your progress as your character or quest log. I LOVE these types of games. In pretty much all forms. Games like Factorio are right up my alley because of this reason. But because Aloft uses a 'claim island' system for their base building, and a system where you can only build structures once you've found the recipe or sketched it in a book, it heavily incentivises using a sizeable island early on so that you can actually engage in the building without the thing looking ugly as all hell. But, then you end up just doing normal survival building on a floating rock. There's little to none of that 'base evolves as the game progresses' feeling anymore. But if you pick a small island, then you're forced to jam wooden base pieces all over it and so on, and you won't even be able to place most of the cosmetic supporting beams since you can only construct from standing and in that situation there's nothing to stand on, so it ends up looking ugly in that way, too. 

To refine all that word splurge into one sentence, I would have to say that it feels like this game had one single idea so far, and that's about it. And the devs are trying to build around that one idea, but not really having a good time of it. Because, in all respect to the devs, there are some seriously basic Quality of Life amateur level mistakes being made here. 

Like, why are we still using a 1-0 hot bar and then being given tools that fill that ENTIRE hotbar? Give us a radial wheel. Dynamic item switching (that doesn't require the tool to be in the hotbar) or something like that.

I get it, I get it, 'Early Access' and all that, but that excuse only goes so far due to the reasons listed at the start. There is a point where I am left wondering WHY making certain things work better wasn't the one thing optimised before the game furthered in development.

Like, why go to the trouble of adding the combat when it's just so bad? Clunky, awful hitboxes. Often being hindered by the environment more than the enemies. Boring with little to no reward but forced to engage with for the main progression. Just add it as optional areas for the moment while you work out the kinks and smooth the experience. Don't force it on us.

Why add the ecosystem system when its just so pointless besides adding another hurdle before you can access the same boring resources you've been doing for hours? Hold off on it entirely until you have more to do with it to actually make it a game mechanic!

This just screams 'We have to release stuff to justify people spending money on it' more than 'Early Access quirkiness' and I just don't really like that.

So, with that in mind. I do not suggest buying this game at the moment. Even just to support the devs. There is little in the game right now that really shines or makes it unique, and I have as much expectation that it will never get better as I do that it will.

While the foundation is there, the game is missing critical elements:

Examples:

- Islands all feel the same—the layouts may differ, but the core experience remains unchanged.

- Remove the mushroom menace corruption from the islands by hitting the giant tendrils with 3 nodules on them and removing it from the island. Cleansing it completely.

review:
THE GOOD:
The exploration and expansion of resources is fun, along with the three different biomes. The building part of the game works well and there are a fair number of building pieces to choose from, allowing for creativity and enjoyable builds.

THE BAD:
The pace of the game is absolutely terrible.
Early game is okay. You will spend forever flying from one patch of islands to another, then going from one island in the group to another, picking up sometimes just one of a resource from an island, sometimes a few, never more. Chests' rewards for finding them is always "Meh". By mid-game you're going to be mostly looking for more recipes to build parts of buildings. This is when it starts to slow as you start to rush from one group of islands to another, check them all one by one for recipes, before moving the the next group. The mini game to revitalize the "sick" islands starts to feel like a nuisance that's just in your way. At some point you will have recipes to make things that you CAN'T make because you're missing other recipes to make the equipment to process the right resources. Best example is the sawmill. I had a recipe from early in the game that I could NOT use without boards, but I couldn't make boards without the sawmill. I searched forever for the thing, found broken ones everywhere, even from the start. The game became a real slog at that point and I was feeling frustrated. But since I had been having fun earlier in the game I stuck with it until I found the sawmill recipe on the other end of the map (which took FOREVER to fly my island to).

But it didn't end with the sawmill. Once I had it, I went back to building a bit, and exploring for more building recipes. The game became repeatitive at that point, and I started seeing lots of the same exact islands - copy/paste style. But then I found ALL the recipes and figured I'd make my way to the center of the map. Nope winds are too strong despite the highest tier sails. So... what to do? I've spent hours now flying back and forth across the map, just WAITING for the travel to happen, thinking I'm missing some final recipe needed to unlock the center. Thinking maybe I have to go in from a specific spot, maybe I have to reveal all the available tiles first, maybe I have to visit all the islands marked by an atlas stone. Nope none of those things. The game does not help guide in this.

I have finally decided to throw in the towel and move on from this game, leaving unfulfilled, never to return. In the end I wish I had stuck with other building games that have more content, better visuals, frequent updates, and a SUSPICIOUSLY similar glider system for movement...

review:
If you want a sandboxy, creative, flying island builder: this is a great game. If you're looking for more than that, you're going to want to wait for a bit more polish

I cannot reccomend it because of what it promises through it's tags (and it's description) as some are objectively false. This is not a survival game, you do not need to survive. Food water and sleep are not critical to staying alive, there is nothing, aside from combat that threatens your survival and even if you die in the slog that passes for combat, there is no punishment to dying, you just respawn. That's it, there's no stakes or tension.

The devs describe the game as a "feel-good, cozy survival" game but the feel-good part is being held back by a lack of focus. 
-Combat isn't engaging, the only thing that spices it up are the special attacks wich require stamina that takes too long to refresh. Because there's no death penalty, enemies are a hurdle rather than a threat
-The inventory management is tedious, and if you're hitting up an island with a bad ecosystem you'll be bringing a stupid amount of resources to account for every single thing that can be wrong
-you're constantly rifling through the 4 different inventory menus to move things on the hotbar because you have too many different tools that do different things clogging it up (remove dorkip and put its functionality into the pickaxe, same for the sickle and sword)
-the island-to-island resource gathering suffers from the late-game raft issue where very quickly you'll start going through the motions rather than exploring a new island.

If there is ever an update that updates the combat and adds more settings to world generation (survival mode, resource density, death penalties) hit me up and I'll adjust this comment and sing aloft's praises, but for now I cannot say it delivers what it promises.

review:
There are plenty of reviews that explain that this isn't the greatest co-op game because each player "needs" to have their own island; you can not build an island together with friends. Or rather, you can, but it only saves it for the person who claims the island. You could have a friend always host and you join/use their island.

If you choose to play with friends and each have your own islands, you can (which is what I did) but with the current state of the game you're going to run into issues with having enough materials for however many people you're playing with. Most of the islands are very limited on resources. And lots of them are really small so it doesn't really make it worth flying around to every single one because there is no point. Or fixing them only to get not much in return.

30 hours in and we just now go to the biome which has clay and a bunch of other new materials. But, upon finding those new islands we were challenged with not having enough charcoal to sketch all of the new things we found. Why is charcoal so limited? Why can't you just make it from burning wood (which is very easy to obtain)? It doesn't make sense to me. I have 20+ pieces of paper and zero charcoal. At least it appears that these new island in the "hot" area have more charcoal now. Hard stone is another super rare material that you need a lot of. Why?

Tentacles enemies on the corrupted islands need nerfed. They are zero fun to fight. They deal a ton of damage. You can't block their attacks. You will 100% get knocked off of the islands from them. Sometimes the circles you need to kill are hanging off the edge of the islands; have fun with that.

Building your island is obviously the most fun part of this game and why we continued to play it. It's a shame that they limit you on the amount of control you have on placing items. You'll see really creative islands where parts are rotated in a unique way to create fun buildings and stuff. You can't really do that yourself. Also there's no ability to move built objects, you have to always destroy them and rebuild them which can get annoying.

Lots of other little annoying things, but it's in early access so it has potential to be good one day.

review:
When I initially posted my [positive/forgiving] review many hours of play time ago, the game had just released and I had run into a game breaking bug that prevented me from progressing. Whenever I checked, this bug was still present until the recent bloom & blight update-- and that's like 3-4 "big updates" to the game.

Unfortunately, most of those updates were purely or mostly aesthetic (like the critters updates) and didn't do anything meaningful to improve the game so I let it sit for a long time.

Then the devs released the puzzles update to redesign the puzzles for no apparently good reason, and the wiki lists multiple puzzles that were left in a known broken state. (And appear to still be broken in my most recently playthrough.)

I finally decided to give the game another try when they released the bloom & blight update, which reset all progress (the save file was redesigned and old saves were incompatible.) This was disheartening as nothing new and exciting has been added but I still have to slog through all the previous content to reach my previous progress point.

Bloom & Blight adds central islands in each cluster that have to be cleansed in order to progress through the sector and unlock tech advancements. And each time you cleanse the central island you get an extended recovery mini-game that serves no purpose. Then you have to cleanse the central island in each cluster to cleanse the sector island. It adds wind lanes to make things move faster but when the update initially released these wind lanes didn't work (they did fix this but still.)

As I go exploring I'm finding broken or puzzles with no clear way to solve them (and no one in discord or the wiki has ever figured out how the puzzles work either. It seems like a lot of people skip them or brute force them.) In addition to the broken puzzles there are vines or barriers designed to block your accessing certain things but with the new bloom & blight mechanic there are multiple new types of barriers and they each require a specific cure/fungicide applied to your tools/weapons-- and multiple barriers either cannot be interacted with or won't tell you which you require to clear them-- and they each require a specific one. The strongest cure doesn't work on everything, which means lots of barriers in the alter game become impassable. 

The entire game feels disjointed. Like there is no central authority for game design. Furthermore, the game has lost the element of fun. It's just tedious and bug filled for me at this point. I continue to slog through a few hours at a time but given the long periods between updates, the low content value of each update and the poor quality assurance in each update, I might not even finish the game.

I no longer recommend the game because I cannot separate the forced repetition of the game (due to save file redesign) and the list of severe bugs from the sense of excitement I felt at initially exploring this new world.
