review:
Overall, this game delivers on its promises: you can farm and drive licensed tractors. So far, so good.

But oh boy, the rest of it is just a disgrace of low-effort incompetence and neglect you’d expect in a license-filled slop game. This wouldn’t be so bad if this weren’t the fourth—or maybe third—installment in this series.

The menus are a hacky compromise to avoid making their own PC/console UI, meaning that on PC, navigating them—for example, looking at mods—is a pain-inducing experience. The constant reminder of what each button does is also heavily oriented toward consoles. In-game, this continues, but I give it a pass since there’s a lot of stuff to control.

In-game, the next big thing you will encounter is performance. It’s called “(20)25” but has so little modern optimization, and it runs only on one core. So even if you have a monster, beefy machine to run this, you will have bad performance, lags, and spikes. It’s horrendous how badly this thing runs on modern hardware.

The overall gameplay is also plagued with console controls. The map is a mystery that I think is basically not properly finished, and controlling AI workers is a pain. But as far as I’ve read, they are already far better than in previous installments.

The driving physics are passable but sometimes feel really shit due to performance hitches, and they often do not behave either like a simulator or a casual driving experience. Wheels won’t return to neutral positions, for example—but sometimes they do. Oversteering with keyboard and mouse is a constant struggle.

Multiplayer works, but also rather badly—and even consumer-hostile. If you want to host your own private dedicated server, you need to buy an additional license, as the game prevents you from running the game twice or downloading the server separately like 99% of other games allow. This is the biggest and unforgivable flaw. This is something I have not encountered yet in any game I’ve played and hosted myself! Oh, and of course there is no Linux server either; it all must be run under Windows, which eats performance. Really shitty product.

One thing that really stands out, however, is the enormous amount of mods this game has and is able to run. We did a test run with over 2,500 mods for additional vehicles and stuff, and it ran no worse than with 450 mods—or none. This is really cool!

All in all, the overall pain we had before even starting to play, and the constant reminders and bad experiences while playing, clearly make me not recommend this “product.”

TL;DR: Ein Spiel gemacht von BAUERN für BAUERN.

review:
Played FS22 since it came out & I waited quite some time before picking this one up since I had other games to play. I'm a bit disappointed though.

Issues:
- Game tends to soft crash during saves fairly regularly. I have verified that I have no mod conflicts per my game logs, but there are a fair amount of seemingly outdated mods since textures or paint jobs aren't loading once the equipment is purchased.
- It's already been a week since the last update & I've only seen one 3rd party mod updated, it seems like the mod authors aren't active.
- I found a mod by Giants that has caused my game to crash multiple times, each time I had purchased a MF large tractor. Which is dumb since the Dev added it to the library as free content. It shouldn't break the game.
- Mods seem to not load into existing saves. So in my experience, I had to wipe my save & start over to see the new mods loaded in.
- There was an issue that I had regarding the Shader compiling. Somehow the "shader_<insert random characters here>" file got corrupted after the first few launches of the game after it had soft crashed multiple times in a row. For example, if I remember correctly, the game crashed 5 times in 30min of attempting to play, but it would crash during the load screen. Deleting this shader file & wiping all save games from the C:\Users\<username>\Documents\My Games\FarmingSimulator2025 did resolve that particular issue, but that's ridiculous that I had to even go that far to resolve a game loading issue after verifying game files didn't work.
- There's literally a 3rd party mod in the mod library that supposedly attempts to resolve the game save crashing by making autosave more frequent. However, in my experience, it doesn't work.

Biggest takeaway:
- I really like FS22 & was hoping that FS25 would be a bit more polished. However, I see that, even though I waited just over a year to buy this game, it still isn't in a solid spot based on my experience & frustrations in troubleshooting. At this time, I would NOT recommend spending money on this game. If Giants fixes this game save crashing issue, like a responsible & in-tune developer would, then I'd be willing to change my mind & edit my review to reflect this change.

I bought this game because I figured that it was a passion project and it looked really cool. 

Over 100 hours in now and I'm convinced that this is not a passion project, just a lazy, low effort game to keep that money coming in from the niche market of fanboy sickophants that will literally tolerate anything. 

How many games in are we now of farming simulator and it still has easily fixable exploits and physics issues.

1: The economy is completely broken but all of the exploits could be easily fixed by adding a few lines of code and formula to change land prices etc depending on land states which the game already recognises. The only reason I can think of that this has not been fixed is that the devs simply don't care about making the game good. As long as the fanboy boomer sickophants who always buy the franchise keep buying the buggy unfinished games, then why would they care. 

2: Game breaking bugs and physics issues: Watch out for that low curb with your giant tractor or you could just flip that tractor on its side... 

3: Low effort: Many of the assets in the game look like they are just unreal engine assets. The pedestrians walking around seem more like zombies and dont serve any real purpose. If you run into the pedestrians with your tractor then nothing happens. It would be nice to even see them react when a massive tractor mounts the pavement, however that would require some actual coding and they aint about to do that. 

4:  Mods make the game tolerable: This is yet another lazy game that completely depends on the active modding community to finish it, because why bother finishing a game when you can just wait for unpaid modders to do it for you. 

My main gripe with this game is that it could be brilliant, however instead its just... meh.... its alright but it should and could easily be a lot better. IG this game was the developers first rodeo with a farming sim game then I'd be applauding them for making it sort of work... however we are multiple iterations in now and this is simply not good enough. 

If your going to buy this game wait until there are massive discounts on it

review:
It’s 2025 and FS25 still runs on a very old engine.
That’s honestly the biggest problem.

The game has potential, but the graphics feel stuck somewhere between FS15 and FS17. Almost nothing in the world reacts to light properly, the trees don’t move, the foliage is dead, and the whole map feels static and flat. It’s not “stylized,” it’s just outdated.

The worst part?
Most of the Steam screenshots look way better than the actual game. They’re heavily edited, downsampled, captured in a debug mode or simply not representative of normal gameplay. Once you play it yourself, everything looks overexposed, washed out, and with zero atmosphere.

Even with ReShade you can’t fix the core issues, because the engine doesn’t support any modern features. No raytracing, no GI, no proper sky lighting, no volumetric shadows, nothing. Other simulators moved forward (UE4, UE5, HDRP, etc.), but FS25 still uses DX11 and old screen-space tricks that break with FOV or camera movement.

The trees are a perfect example:
No proper animation, no believable lighting, no depth, no softness, no scattering. They look almost the same as in FS15. And when the environment looks dead, the whole game feels dead.

FS25 plays fine, but visually it’s extremely outdated.
If you expect modern graphics in 2025, you will be disappointed.

Don't forget the wood, it's unplayable. WOOD WOOD WOOD WOOD

review:
Still more “arcade farm” than simulator

I’ve played Farming Simulator for years and honestly thought 25 would finally push things closer to a real sim.

Gameplay & physics
The game still feels very arcadey. Vehicles don’t feel heavy, physics are pretty much nonexistent. For something calling itself a simulator, it really doesn’t behave like one.

Missing depth
We’re in 2025 and there are still no proper pesticides, plant diseases, or any real depth to crop management. Fields feel way too clean and simple. No risk, no pressure, nothing to really think about besides the same old loop we’ve already done in previous games.

Bugs
And of course, there are a lot of bugs. AI issues, little glitches, stuff that adds up over time and gets annoying. It doesn’t feel as polished as a new full price release should.

Graphics
Graphics are slightly better, but better visuals alone are not enough reason to buy what basically feels like the same game again.

Overall

review:
It’s 2025 and FS25 still runs on a very old engine.
That’s honestly the biggest problem.

The game has potential, but the graphics feel stuck somewhere between FS15 and FS17. Almost nothing in the world reacts to light properly, the trees don’t move, the foliage is dead, and the whole map feels static and flat. It’s not “stylized,” it’s just outdated.

The worst part?
Most of the Steam screenshots look way better than the actual game. They’re heavily edited, downsampled, captured in a debug mode or simply not representative of normal gameplay. Once you play it yourself, everything looks overexposed, washed out, and with zero atmosphere.

Even with ReShade you can’t fix the core issues, because the engine doesn’t support any modern features. No raytracing, no GI, no proper sky lighting, no volumetric shadows, nothing. Other simulators moved forward (UE4, UE5, HDRP, etc.), but FS25 still uses DX11 and old screen-space tricks that break with FOV or camera movement.

The trees are a perfect example:
No proper animation, no believable lighting, no depth, no softness, no scattering. They look almost the same as in FS15. And when the environment looks dead, the whole game feels dead.

FS25 plays fine, but visually it’s extremely outdated.
If you expect modern graphics in 2025, you will be disappointed.

Don't forget the wood, it's unplayable.

Pros:
- Baby animals, yay
- Dynamic animal pens
- Colliders (soil/deposited materials react to weight, if i used that term correctly)
- Cleaner HUD
- Steering Assist (great for one's OCD straight-line urges)

- NPCs (IMO, creepy as heck. I much rather liked the 2d portraits from FS22 in the contracts panel)
- UI is obviously different from FS22 that may need getting used to, but there was nothing bad with the previous UI style for the store & placing down buildings.
- No 3rd POV interaction with vehicles and trailers, it is still automatic touch-of-a-button, not a big issue but doesn't score realism points.
- Re-used models, especially for animals (you'd think being a new game, you'd get new models for stuff)

Conclusion:
IMO if the pros from FS25 had been added to FS22, it would've been a near perfect game. I wouldn't pay full price for FS25, especially since modders have gone to lengths to make FS22 more complete with the additions that FS25 included. Seems like a money grab, but whatever floats your boat.

Long story short, FS25 is FS22 with a couple upgrades. I hope this made sense because verbal diarrhoea.

review:
IT'S ALWAYS THE SAME... Hear me out.

I mean, yeah, it is a farming simulator as we know it. However, I don't really see much difference between fs25 and fs22. Two main differencies are ground deformation (we will get to that shortly) and improved graphics.

-- Famous breathtaking ground deformation --
So, the long loooong waited feature that should've been in farming simulator like many yeras ago... Spintires did it perfectly in 2014, why couldn't the Giants even in 2025? It is a farming simulator or atleast it's supposed to be. This game is so arcade-ish that calling it a "simulator" is like spiting in a face of other great simulators out there. I mean, if it is called a simulator, why we cannot interract with stuff, like we could pull the levers in tractors or push the buttons in vehicles.. that's what is missing from this game (I aint calling it a simulator no more). "Ground deformation" is what Giants are calling it. I only see a slight bend of a flat surface and that's what you call a ground deformation?! This is not what players expect in 2025!

-- Ultra hyper photo realistic improved graphics --
NO! Adding cloud shadows with fog that'll eat up 15% of your CPU power is not what an enhanced graphics are supposed to be. Fix your g☺dd♥mn physics and gameplay first, then work on graphics. I mean, yeah.. the graphics are SOMEWHAT better compared to fs22. But sweet god in heavens. The physics are still awful. The've been awful in fs22, 19, 17, 15 and I could go on and on.

-- Awful physics --
Now let's talk about the physics mentioned above. Why do I think they are awful? Vehicles have little to no kinetic energy. Every vehicle feel so cumbersome. They've had theese weird physics in.. every.. other.. farming.. "simulator"... Another thing, stacking many bales on one another sometimes makes them behave strangely. They tend to start wiggle and then blast in every direction (rip 30+ mins of manual bale stacking). This bug (or maybe a feature) was also present in every other fs.

-- Great vehicle "damage" (proposed in fs19 and still awful today) --
You slam into a tree at 90 km/h, suddenly you stand still and there is no damage to the vehicle you're driving or to a tree. Try that in real life if you get the same results. ;)
They've seriously just put a blue marker and expect us to believe that it is a vehicle damage marker. LOL, no! It is supposed to be called a vehicle maintanance marker, not damage. There is no such thing as damage in this game.

-- Very realistic character controls --
They somehow screwed up even a feature that was working just fine in fs22. WOW! I understand that they were trying to "improve" jumping and moving physics. However, they've made a step back with this one. The character controls now feel more like controlling a sluggish man with crippled legs. And jumping? Oh my god in heavens... Don't even try to! If you sprint and jump, you'll lose like 70% of kinetic energy mid-air. They've also added a cooldown for jumping. WHY?!?! LIKE WHYYYY? It's sooo annoying. Character controls were just far better in previous games.

-- Unbelievably exciting gameplay --
Don't take me wrong. I seriously enjoyed playing fs17, 19 and 22 (I have like 250+ hours on each one). Don't tell me that this game is not for me. Why it is so that the best means of money making are also the most boring ones? Smallest tools possible and hours of driving on the same field. Nope, not doing that for a 100th time.

-- Amazing new features --
Doing rice is boring af. So is doing the spinach, peas and all new crops and even not talking about the fact that almost all new vehicles are an end-game stuff. And oh, I almost forgot. New animals, you say? Buffalos? Really? An endgame stuff.. again.

-- Conclusion --
Giants had such a great opportunity to bring us something new and unique. And they've bring us only slightly better graphics and slight bending of plain surface which they called a ground deformation. In my eyes, farming simulator had become an economic-grinding simulator. Like it is not about farming anymore. It is about just grinding for money. Every farming game from Giants feels the same for last 6 years. I don't want it like this anymore. I'm tired of this.

So, after having played this game for just about 90 hours, I am finally feeling educated enough to do a review. Personally, I am mostly playing the game for the horses, but I have also tested out a lot of other thing in the game. I have a thing or two to say about this game. 

1. Do not buy it. If you love supporting developers that don't care about anything other than the income, sure - go ahead. But if you actually are looking for a good game? Pick another. I will never recommend Farming Simulator 25 to anyone - not in the state it is. Its whacky, laggy, glitchy - and in its essentials just a reskin from the Farming Simulator 22. 

2. It's just not reaching its potential. Unfortunately, this can happen to games in the lead, especially without competitors - such as Farming Simulator 25, or any other FS game for that matter. They live on hype and loyalty, and they don't really care about improving their game, create longlost features everyone have wanted or fix super-identifiable bugs. They just simply don't care enough about their own game. As long as they earn enough, they're good.

3. If you buy it for the horses...Believe me, you will be greatly disappointed. The horses...Are simply not horses. They are literally just full of nothingness, and bugs. You can't properly care for them or ride them. Horses suddenly just vanishes. At this point they are unplayable without mods. And having mods to be able to just be able to play with horses is both hilarious and humiliating. And if you are like me, you might look at all the details and effort put into the horses. Well, all I can promise you is get ready for horrible and unrealistic animations. I promise you, you will be taken out of the immersion immediatly. 

4. If you buy it for animals. Just expect them to be boring as hell, living like soul-less machines just... being there. No thought have been put into them, they are just another step in the production chain. Although, yes, Farming Simulator 25 (and prior games) is more about the farming, they have in fact added both animals and forestry - and it is the latter they have put the juice into. The amount of no effort put into the animals is not exactly shocking, the developers are known to be lazy. Like why on earth do you add baby animals to each animal type except horses?!? Laziness or just out of your scope? If the latter, you best turn around and implement your animals promptly. And why, why is there no genders on the animals? Like, you could put in a snippet of code and the game would just feel a tad more on earth - but no no, it is not important enough.

I could write more, but as I am mostly into the animals aspect, I'm going to stop here. Just TLDR: I regret supporting these developers. Their game is literally just a overpriced piece of garbage. Thank you for reading my review and rant from a horse gamer and animal enthusiast.

review:
The Farming Simulator series, once seen as a refreshing niche experience for fans of agriculture and simulation, has increasingly become a glaring example of a franchise coasting on brand loyalty while offering little genuine innovation. The latest installment, released on November 24, continues this unfortunate trend, recycling the same core engine and mechanics with only minor, often cosmetic, tweaks - changes that could easily have been delivered through a patch or DLC for previous versions.

What makes the situation worse is that these marginal updates are marketed as full-priced new entries, effectively turning the series into a cashgrab. Players are paying top dollar for what is, in essence, a lightly modified version of the same game they've already purchased one or more times before. The developers, GIANTS Software, seem to rely on the loyal modding community to fill the gaps in creativity and depth, while delivering the bare minimum in terms of technical or gameplay evolution themselves.

At its core, Farming Simulator fails to live up to its genre’s potential. Despite its name, the game lacks the intricate depth that one would expect from a true simulation. Crop management, soil chemistry, equipment wear and tear, dynamic weather systems - elements that should add meaningful layers of realism - are either simplified to the point of irrelevance or entirely absent. Farming in the real world is a complex, constantly evolving process, but Farming Simulator presents it as a rinse-and-repeat grind with little nuance or challenge.

Even worse, many longstanding bugs persist despite years of feedback. Issues with AI workers getting stuck, poor pathfinding, clipping problems, janky vehicle physics, and multiplayer desyncs remain unresolved, making the experience feel unpolished and frustrating—especially given how long the series has been around. These aren't minor quirks; they're quality-of-life issues that have been present since multiple earlier titles and simply should not still exist.

In a gaming landscape where simulation titles are pushing boundaries—look at what titles like SnowRunner or DCS World are doing - Farming Simulator feels stuck in neutral. It's content to play it safe, releasing just enough to justify a new number on the box but not enough to warrant the purchase.

Until GIANTS Software starts addressing these core problems and rethinks their business model, Farming Simulator will remain a series with untapped potential, diluted by complacency and commercial opportunism.

The fans deserve better.

review:
The Farming Simulator series, once seen as a refreshing niche experience for fans of agriculture and simulation, has increasingly become a glaring example of a franchise coasting on brand loyalty while offering little genuine innovation. The latest installment, released on November 24, continues this unfortunate trend, recycling the same core engine and mechanics with only minor, often cosmetic, tweaks - changes that could easily have been delivered through a patch or DLC for previous versions.

What makes the situation worse is that these marginal updates are marketed as full-priced new entries, effectively turning the series into a cashgrab. Players are paying top dollar for what is, in essence, a lightly modified version of the same game they've already purchased one or more times before. The developers, GIANTS Software, seem to rely on the loyal modding community to fill the gaps in creativity and depth, while delivering the bare minimum in terms of technical or gameplay evolution themselves.

At its core, Farming Simulator fails to live up to its genre’s potential. Despite its name, the game lacks the intricate depth that one would expect from a true simulation. Crop management, soil chemistry, equipment wear and tear, dynamic weather systems - elements that should add meaningful layers of realism - are either simplified to the point of irrelevance or entirely absent. Farming in the real world is a complex, constantly evolving process, but Farming Simulator presents it as a rinse-and-repeat grind with little nuance or challenge.
Even worse, many longstanding bugs persist despite years of feedback. Issues with AI workers getting stuck, poor pathfinding, clipping problems, janky vehicle physics, and multiplayer desyncs remain unresolved, making the experience feel unpolished and frustrating—especially given how long the series has been around. These aren't minor quirks; they're quality-of-life issues that have been present since multiple earlier titles and simply should not still exist.

In a gaming landscape where simulation titles are pushing boundaries—look at what titles like SnowRunner or DCS World are doing - Farming Simulator feels stuck in neutral. It's content to play it safe, releasing just enough to justify a new number on the box but not enough to warrant the purchase.

Until GIANTS Software starts addressing these core problems and rethinks their business model, Farming Simulator will remain a series with untapped potential, diluted by complacency and commercial opportunism.

The fans deserve better

review:
Lots of okay improvements compared to FS2022. However:
Certain contracts, especially weeding, do not progress in percentage due to a bug, making YOU spend money in herbicide that is being wasted on a task that doesn't go ahead. Even worse, tasking an AI to do the task will spend money in herbicide that gets perpetually wasted into zero progress. This bug was reported 8 months ago, checking discussions. 
Aborting the bugged contract makes you at fault of not completing the task so you lose further money, which is just cherry on top. But it's okay. I can just do the contracts I see working.

The last straw was seeing game randomly crashing on the dumbest of things, like turning on a harvesting machine. Literally "press B to crast to desktop". Without mods. Since the savegame is still based on FS22 logic, it saves the moment you pause the game after certain intervals. As it happened to me, you can lose easily 30-60 minutes of progress because you decided to never open the map and have the game saved, completely wasting all your efforts. Have fun grinding back what you were doing.

Overall, I know this is a game about patience, but nothing irks me more than wasting my time because of game bugs and instabilities.

Overall, it also feels like mostly a reskin of previous game, with slighly improved graphics, and new functions based on what modders were doing in FS2022. But more buggy and crash happy.

review:
I've been a regular purchaser of Farming Simulator since it came out in 2008.  The one thing I've noticed about GIANTS is the fact that with each version the actual improvements over the last version keep decreasing while the price tag keeps increasing.  DLC has also always been a thing with GIANTS products for as long as I can remember, with more and more of what should have been included in the base game being moved over to DLC purchases with every new version.  It wouldn't be much of a struggle to say that there are only 2 reasons why the Farming Simulator series still exists.  First, they have 100% of the market share because it's the only "open world" farming simulator out there.  Second, the modding community has always made up for what GIANTS lacks.

Coming from Farming Simulator 2022, I can clearly state that it might not have been that much of an improvement over Farming Simulator 2019, but it offered a lot more improvements than Farming Simulator 2025.  I mean, let's get into the nitty gritty.  In Farming Simulator 2025 we've been given half-assed rice fields with only 2 vehicles for them.  There still isn't any animal husbandry.  We have a couple new animals that are nothing more than the old animals, remodelled and supplying different items.  A lot of the weather effects actually look WORSE than the previous version and we still don't have rain on windshields?!  Don't get me started on the fog they've been so proudly showing off, which seems to happen at such unrealistic times that I'd wager it's just randomly generated rather than following actual weather patterns.  We also now have ground deformation!  (which we had in 2022, but only for landscaping)  Trust me, this isn't anything special and can actually make a mess out of your farm.  I turned off as much of the deformations as I could, pretty much right away.

Farming Simulator 2022 required anywhere from 25-50 mods to actually be enjoyable.  Farming Simulator 2025 actually tried to incorporate the ideas of some of those mods, failed REALLY BADLY at it, and still requires a huge modding community to make up for what GIANTS lacks.  I mean, what's the actual point to this version?  It's pretty much the same game experience as 2022.  Worse, actually, in some ways.  The new menus are absolutely horrible, leaving players struggling.  

Bugs?  Oh my god... While Farming Simulator 2022 had it's share of bugs, they weren't as completely game-breaking as the ones in Farming Simulator 2025.  I've experienced everything from increased loading times, to video stuttering, to needing to restart the full game just to change my screen resolution, to the game crashing while loading the map, to the game losing audio for no apparent reason while playing...  In short, this edition of the Farming Simulator series is absolute garbage.  Knowing GIANTS, they might fix a lot of these bugs but you'll probably have to buy a DLC bundle to get the fix.

Oh, and don't even get me started on the fact that you STILL need to buy a SECOND COPY of their game if you want to run a dedicated server.  GIANTS has been doing this since way back around Farming Simulator 2015 and is the ONLY game developer I know that does.  They also launched this game with DAY ONE DLC and tried to exclude the "Year One" bundle customers.  They faced so much backlash that they had no option but to reverse that decision.  

Put plainly, GIANTS is so money-hungry that I have no clue why people still support them, other than the fact that they have no direct competition.  If another company were to pop up and offer a decent Farming Simulator game, with free dedicated servers and open modding, you would see GIANTS lose their Farming Simulator customers overnight.  I mean, you're gonna see Dovetail (another money-hungry company) experience this with the Train Simulator series once games like "Infinite Rails", "Century of Steam", and "Railroader" get going.... It's just a matter of time, GIANTS.

If you already have Farming Simulator 2022, DO NOT get this version.  You aren't missing anything.  If you don't own Farming Simulator 2022, and are thinking of getting into Farming Simulator, then save yourself some money and buy Farming Simulator 2022.  Trust me, it's a better experience than you'll have with 2025, has a massive modding library, and you'll enjoy it a lot better.  I'm actually trying to refund 2025 as I write this.

Update:  My refund was unsuccessful due to having played over 2 hours (a lot of that time spent trying to fix bugs and going through mods)



-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-


TLDR:  I give this a very strong DO NOT BUY.

HOLY Hell the optimization on this one.

First the good parts i have seen:
there are more contract types, nice to have some more variety.
Graphics can look nice if youre willing to turn your PC into a turbine.
The advanced Helper options are nice and probably useful when you get around to understanding them for multi helper work on a field.
The Saleprice and finance report got a nice overhaul, combining stuff that was seperated in FS22 (where it was seperated in comparison to FS19, sooo yeah still good they went back)

now to the bad:
This Game EATS Ressources for seemingly no reason.
Even on high settings you have repeated Pop in of the final 2 Stages of 3D model (Flat paint far -flat 3D far - rough 3D - detailed 3D) 
tested by doing a straw baleing contract,
to the Point that my Tractor was often above it as it poped into rough 3D.

Even when i set it down to medium i got repeated stutters of the Framerate (while turning the camera), 
without Vsync i got a reliable tear on my screen.
With default settings you have a sort of permanent "fog" like a very sligth gray filter, barely noticeable but especially compared to FS 22 easily noticeable.

And Finally to the UGLY:
The UI symbols have a Faded ligth green Tone... 
when most of the Time the background behind those symbols is 
EITHER
a faded ligth blue background (sky)
OR 
a faded green background (grass ,fields, trees,...),
THATS base GUI design knowledge about contrast, yes there are mods to change that BUT WHY is that necessary?!

Next thing you tell me theres a community Patch out there, 
increasing performance by ~90% 
(with the deliverd result and the taken ressources, 
compared to my PCs experience with Cyberpunk i WOULDN'T be suprised)


The Menu options/categories got the modern Windows GUI treatment, 
no Titles, no Labels and partly random category, just keep switching till you find what you need.

Want to find a certain Trailer, but no its not in trailers because its in the bailer category etc.

Like Construction categories have no title or label (want to get quickly to sculpting or generators? either you know or you wander till you find it)

The Water mechanics, yeah nice to look at but the wave is either underwhelming (if you drive a vehicle in) or way overexagerated (Farmer swiming).


In Total, DO NOT BUY till they have at LEAST fixed the Performance.
WHICH knowig Giants Software, will not happen.

review: While I do like playing this version of the game, there are still so many issues it can become very frustrating to play. Things like hit boxes. When you have a trailer or tool and you want to put it in a specific spot for which you can plainly see it will indeed fit with enough room all around it, but when you actually go to put it in the spot it won't go. In the previous version it was easy to get an AI worker to drive your tractor or truck or whatever from one location to another so you didn't have to drive every piece of equipment from one field to another yourself. Made it much easier to get several pieces of equipment to a field for a contract quickly. I still haven't figured out how, or even if, you can do that in this version. One thing I really hate in all versions of this game is the AI traffic. While you can turn it off, I like having the traffic on the road, the part that erks me so much is that 1) AI traffic doesn't obey any traffic laws, always run stop signs and cut you off, and 2) if you hit a car (even if it's the car's fault) it's like running into a rock cliff face in that you can't move the car with you tractor or other driving item. It's like running into a wall that is indistructable and unmovable. If they would make it like an actual simulator so when you ran into a car it would actually move the car in some direction (like you can in other simulator's like ATS) instead of not being able to move it at all in any direction. I like the traffic, I hate the issue of stupid lawless AI cars that can't be moved though. Also, you can change the passage of time in the game in that you can set the speed from realtime to 5X realtime, you can set it so each day equals a month (default) or you can have it so that each month lasts 28 days. That's fine, the problem is that no matter how you change the timing, it has zero effect on the first month of your save. If you started in Aug and set the timing so that you had 3X time passage and 2 days for each month, it will not take effect until the following month, so if you might need more time in the first month of the save to get things organized you can forget it! I've lost crops due to this issue. There are many more annoyances that slip my mind at this time, but there are enough to make playing this game aggravating more often then not. I really liked the FS22 version better, it has similar issues, but doesn't seem like it has as many of them as FS25. Since I'm past the time allowed to get a refund I'm stuck with this version. I hope they will get around to dealing with these annoying issues, but I'm not holding my breath since they certainly didn't address them in the FS22 version. Cost wise, I paid 20$ for FS22 and thought it was worth as much as 30$. I paid 50$ for FS25 and think it's worth about 10$. Very disappointing!

review:
Hear me out, the game has gotten a bit better, but still hasn't caught up to older productions of the game by far. Before I go into the negatives, let me say that I am much happier with the performance of the game today than I was a year ago. From helpers to graphics, the game plays so much better than it did. Many kudos to the dev team for the great work on fixing the worst of the performance problems that made me put down a franchise that I have THOUSANDS of hours into. I also want to mention that I DO enjoy many new features that have been added. One of my favorites is the ability to customize the pastures attached to husbandries. That's a feature that I've been dreaming of for many years. Big ups to whoever thought of that!

   With that being said, there is many issues that I don't see being remedied in the future. First of the issues is the paid DLCs/season pass that Giants puts out. In my opinion, There's no real value in buying them at all. Lackluster equipment and maps that don't excite me or my friends, don't really draw my desire to invest. To add context, I pre purchased the game and it included the season one pass. I have not used anything that has come with it. It really seems like a waste of money when I'm constantly looking for better things in the FS25 mod hub, which also has many issues, but I'll get into that later.

    Second, multiplayer is still a gloriously buggy mess. There's no reason that a franchise with this much experience in the game should be having this many problems. With or without mods, the issues are relentless. Examples include weather conditions being different between players, prices in the markets not matching between players, objects not working properly, productions absent/missing from menus, shaders preventing people from joining, and more. The main reason I came back to this game was because my friends with Game Pass wanted to try, and after much frustration, many of them have given up.

   Next issue I've found is the overall lack of what makes this game so great, the mods. If you compare to older titles, you'll see a drastically reduced collection of QUALITY equipment to choose from. When my friends and I play, we are constantly saying how we wish mods from FS19 and FS22 were in this game too. Many great modders have been chased away or rejected for whatever reason, leaving the game empty feeling compared to previous titles. It leaves me wondering if Giants has created massive resistance to mod creators in an effort to cheaply add value to their own paid DLCs. Or maybe it's just because of cross play. Either way, the game feels empty and soulless. But at least we have rice now, right?....

   Lastly, the quality and compatibility of the mods that are offered in the Giants mod hub are much lower than previous games. There's a huge quality control issue in the approval process that I have rarely see in previous games. I constantly find myself troubleshooting or uninstalling mods due to conflicts with much frustration. A big issue that we find is that many mods for some reason use the same controls with little to no ability to remap or work around. Placing buildings becomes a headache when some buildings can be turned on a full axis but others can only be place north to south or east to west. Vital productions and other buildings become eyesores that force you to stop playing because you now have to redesign your perfect layout to compensate for. As an example, most manure heaps can only rotate two directions but most husbandries can rotate however you want. If you have OCD, you are gonna lose your mind playing this game.

  With all that being said, I still keep my recommendation NOT to buy this game. Play it on GamePass if you want to experience the most frustrating addition to the franchise. Buy FS22 or even FS19 if you want to have fun instead. The quality of play and the mods are much better. 

   As a quick note, I used to stream previous versions of this game. I have purchased many copies of FS19 and FS22 and brought many people into this community. Sadly, this game (FS25) has been so rough that I was forced to end my stream for good. It saddens me to see such a great game struggle so hard to be as good as it once was.

I bought this game as premium sorely because FS22 was a nice game, for me.. As it was my first interaction with FS series. Later i learned about their franchise and how this idea works. Business is business, no problems, but if something is valued in certain point over more important, from the consumers perspective, because of greedy approach, then it is not acceptable. Maybe it was the mission all along, who knows.

The money they get from brands are far greater thanks to the popularity of the game. Their focus is obviously to get out as much content as possible and then fix it as they go. They dont have time, or willingness, to test, nor analyze things, because content is out, public is testing, problems can be fixed on the fly, fulfilment for brands is delivered. Money coming in from brand and also from sales = profit. All good. Product is out, problems can be fixed later. 

As for FS25, i understand there might be problems in the start but the game was literally unplayable, unstable and full of errors. On a high end PC it was lagging, stuttering, freezing and crashing from left to right. From a publisher like that, who has years of knowledge and quite frankly the funds, it is not acceptable to even release such a broken game. But why? Well, need to go for the first point again. Its like Intel to release 5% improved CPU every year, just because well, gotta fill those orders for OEM's who want to build "super improved" laptop every year. In this instance, still, the improvement was -50% in some areas. Physics is crap (games which have no direct connection to ground deformation are running circles around a game like Farming Simulator 25, which, ironically, was bragging hard about this new upgraded deformation. Its better than in 22, sure, but given for 2024 release .. it was just another "marketing".

All in all, i am quite disappointed, and its clearly visible from game hours. Only account i have used this fs25 and its 5% max of the time i played fs22 in total.

The reason i did put "not recommending" is a fact that Farming Simulator 22 was a lot more enjoyable game.
In some aspects FS25 feels downgraded, in other its upgraded. Other than somewhat improved physics, graphics, Japanese map, rice interaction, couple new animals - buffalo, goat and a bit differently working production line.. There is not much difference. No more popular used crops from various placed added, which was accessible in FS22 via modded maps. People grow different crops around the world.

Giant as a dev should critically take a close look at their approach, because i understand the game is popular, quite one of a kind (who wants to know why, search and you get some enlighting content), but they seem to live in a bubble, where they think they need to roll out the game for Brands, get the money in (again, business, so not judging) BUT they forget that the game itself must be ready as well.

review:
The design / pacing... -done by a monkey.

The game starts by not telling you what each difficulty does.
Then it tells you to use abilites (which you select with LMB) without telling you to 'activate' its RMB.

Next the tutorial forces you (twice) to RUSH INTO A ROOM and turn on a laptop WHILE ENEMIES ARE NEARBY AND POINTING GUNS AT YOU... - and only once you did that, can you take them out!

The tutorial is HEAVILY scripted and it took me 5 tries to figure out (or rather stubbornly follow) the things i need to do. Its not hard! Its just VERY specific. 

If games like SWAT or XCOM and others like this tought me anything is: NOT to give the enemy a great way to SHOOT ME...  - but that is what the game teaches you.

In 'stage 3' of the tutorial i was refused the option to take cover DESPITE me seeing the enemy behind the next door waiting to rush in. Yes, this had to happen for the ham fisted script, but it is so counter intuitive! 

The enemy who stormed in is used to teach you RETALIATION mechanics. If you get too close the enemy will prioritize you over other targets.(its almost as if good positioning is important). What a piss poor way to explain this to me. It is forced and feels bad- not organic.

--

But... whatever. Its "just" the tutorial and you have to LOOSE THE TUTORIAL mission. Sorta.

You save a hostage, lose a party member which gets kidnapped, and then its back to the police station. Not the SWAT HQ but the police station... because... reasons. 

At the station you get boring cringe dialogue with answers that may been cool in the 90s (at this point i already tuned out since all the dialogue was just so basic and boring) and you learn a few more 'cool moves' with a little more freedom but overall its paint by the numbers.

You go around and shoot up the cops because your pal that was kidnapped came back and TRUST ME BRO WE ARE THE GOOD GUYS AND WE GOTTA GET OUT OF HERE or something.

Then you go to your... idk hidehout? (seriously, NOTHING was established at this point, the game just rushes through! BOAT HOSTAGE POLICE KIDNAPP! TIME PASS DRAMA FREEEDOM FIIIGHHHTERS!)

Its like watching fucking StarWars on 20x speed! You see scenes and stuff but it means NOTHING to you - and again, the cool one liners don't help!

During the shoot out you get "How are you doing?" (remember he was gone for idk years? Though irl it was like 30 seconds) and you can reply: cool. / i get dental / something i already forgot.

urgh...

Anyhow... i was in the hideout and HAD to spend a skillpoint on a skill because level up (yay)

FAR LEFT on the edge of the screen is a character. FAR RIGHT of the screen his/her abilities.
(Why?! This feels very disconnected and they don't use the space for much other then your character who takes like 5% of the space! It feels like selecting skills in the next room, and they COULD have used the space for a visual demonstration of the abilities or something... or just bring them closer to the character!)

I had to chose 1 and give it a perk... i am not ver familiar with those abilities or what is useful later on or if i get to unlock it all over time and a hundred other things! So you read if you want idk hit 1 more target or have a bigger knockback +2 ... 

WHAT DO YOU THINK I USEFUL? Hit +1 target... or knock people back farther?
During the tutorial the entire games gimmick (knocking people out of windows) was done on EASILY 10 of 20 enemies. Something cool, that might happen, is now an ESSENTIAL MECHANIC.

Imagine a game like Overwatch, but Winstons ultimate is now a basic attack!
The game does move from 'abilities to characters' to a game of 'how to remove the most chess pieces' by pushing them back through overly convenient HUGE and badly secured windows!

Why bother learning strength or tactics or items or anything... if there is an automatic win by kicking someone out of the window? (which may be conventiently right there).
And what do you do if there is no window to exploit or door to seal shut hMMMM?

Seriously this might be the dumbest game I played in a while.

---

Just buy ANY OTHER turned based tactical shooter.
The 'fact' these guys are wizzards isn't even that important. 

Shooting someone or spushing someone or even teleporting... - nothing special any other game can do. More importantly: the game sucks ass at telling a story that goes with it!

> boat tutorial
> shoot up your police HQ
> level up
> go to the world map and do 1 of 2 quests!

All in the span of less than 30 minutes! NO PACING.
I doubt i missed much important information since the 'banters' you can go through are 100% skipable and the game made sure i wanted to skip a lot of them...

"OH YOU GOT NO PATIENCE"

>Helldivers: a squad based shooter where picking the right tools is CRUCIAL.
>2+3 most played: Factorio+Satisfactory, where you do nothing but figure out issues.
>165 hrs in Baldurs Gate 3 where i CRAVED to look at everything i could find! (in and out of game)
>5th Company of Heroes.

And don't get me started on my AdvanceWars addicition<.< 

YEAH.....

That is not a patience problem.
That is a BAD GAME problem.

btw: games such as Wandersong or Spiritfarer also have no voice acting and a LOT to read... and i read it... and i won... (and those were fun). Just to brush that off the table too.
Read more darn novels n fanfics than the game has pages worth of freaking code.

review:
The setting of the game is genius and the small stories and dialogues are really fun. The game also plays with stereotypes in Pen and Paper and RPG games. Have you ever seen a traffic wizard? Hilarious :)

Why the negative review then?

Because it is NOT a tactical game. Basically its a puzzle game with some chess-like elements. There is THE solution for many levels that require exact steps each turn. Yes, you have some freedom, but most time freedom leads to subpar results. So you basically solve puzzles the devs created for you, wrapped as a tactical game. And that's simply not what I wanted and how its advertised. For me a tactical game is a game that gives me the freedom to choose my team, my weapons, stealth or not, kills or not. It's definitely not "In Turn 1, you have to position char 1 here and shoot there, char 2 must move exactly here and push that enemy so that in Turn 2 you can....". That's a puzzle. Solving it means to play each move as intended. The little freedom you get are mostly sub variants of exact these moves. The rating of each mission reflects exactly this: how well did you solve the puzzle at it was intended to be played?

Compare this with the complete freedom for Jagged Alliance, XCOM or Shadow Gambit. These are great tactical games that make you think about how YOU want to solve a level/fight. There are no best ways or preferred tactics in these games and thats what make them a tactical game.

Every time I try to play this, I find myself restarting levels over and over to try to optimize them. On the one hand, the game explicitly tells you to not do the challenges it sets out for you, but it also has the optimization conditions sitting in front of you constantly taunting you, plus the end screen that only gives you kudos if you're efficient. Theoretically you'd plan out your actions like a tactical shooter game, but you can't see what enemies will be spawning from which doors or when until you've played through the entire battle once. It just feels so confused and I don't really enjoy it. 

The writing is fun and I like the story, but on a moment to moment basis I'm constantly worrying about whether there's something I could have done better and I don't ever feel like I have enough information to decide if I have.

I honestly don't know how someone could take something as inherently cool as wizards with guns and make it so abysmally horrid, but they found a way. Imagine a bad British comedy from the 60s where every single line comes with a forced pity laugh, and you'll still be taken by surprise by how impressively terrible these characters interact. 

That said, the gameplay is as good as the writing is bad. My advice: wait until this is on sale for $5 or less, and skip all dialog. It plays like every turn based shooter ever.

review:
I didn't like this game, but lots obviously have. It's similar to a number of other mini tac shooting games where everything is broken into mini maps and short engagements and you're rewarded for how quickly/efficiently you clear a stage rather than your tactical approach. 

The writing is pretty good and there is a reasonable story that accompanies the action. It's just kind of dull, there is basically an ideal approach to each level and it requires trial and error to get right. I prefer a more traditional approach like Xcom, where there is value in taking different strategies that you prefer, even if they aren't ideal, but you can still achieve victory rather than being locked into one narrow box.  The engagements are so small and quick, there is no space to build a strategy and plan ahead. The units are also very narrow, each one does something unique so, again, you need to combine them to get the right pattern and outcome. I can see why some would like that, but it's essentially an overdone rock paper scissors game. There is actually a game to like in here: the core puzzle is engaging, not too hard and quite fun to pick apart and that is nearly enough, but...

That could have still worked, there's quite a variety of art and it does what it can within a coherent look, and you only really notice how bad the art is in close up anyway. 

But the characterisation relies heavily on a tone that is, again, jarringly out of place in the game. It feels like every conversation boils down to a character turning to camera and saying "well that just happened!". It's like being trapped at a party by a Londoner who's nowhere near as funny as they think they are.

I got part way into act 3 before I had to leave the party. Maybe your more tolerant of That Guy than I am, after all, the food is good, and the music is banging, but you should at least be aware that he's there. Waiting to comment ironically about the wallpaper. Ugh.

review:
Before you scroll past this negative review, give it a read. I've put about 9 hours into this game, and while it's really quite amazing at the start, it turned into frustration and restriction by the time I stopped playing. What do I mean by that? Well, let me explain. 

Early game is amazing. You have a lot of options, can breach with almost any order of characters you want and still come out of it a bit banged up, but still alive and victorious. The real fun is replaying the levels and finding that "golden idea", that crazy play or daring strategy that'll bag you a perfect victory. But that's where the fun ends, early game when you HAVE that freedom of choice.

Mid and late game is, quite frankly, restrictive. No longer can you survive and clear the level while losing a couple characters along the way. If you want to win the levels in the late game, you need to have the perfect strategy every single time, with little-to-no room for error. This involves a lot of trial and error, rewinding over and over because a character died on your last turn and made the entire rest of the level unwinnable. But you won't know that, you CAN'T know that, until you keep playing for another hour on the same damn level until you inevitably restart from scratch. This isn't fun game design, it's restrictive and demoralizing. I want to be able to approach a level from several different angles, have fun with different strategies and daring plays, not be railroaded into only being able to use the "right" solution halfway into the game.

review:
4/10

Let me start with positives:
From technical point of view game works reasonably well. No major bugs encountered, loading times and performance on Deck are reasonable, and gamepad controls are a bit frustrating, but mostly serviceable (apart from connecting case details on the map bit, having to drag and drop stuff using gamepad is absolutely cursed). Attacks are guaranteed to hit (at least as far as I got in the game) so no RNG screwing you over -- while I can appreciate risk/reward factor of hit chance, it is too often done wrong when other mechanics force you to take low% risks.

First five or so maps are interesting, few battle mechanics are introduced, and you are hyped for what a competent game designers could do with it... And then comes disappointment:

Tactical side of the game is on the level of sokoban, but instead of pushing boxes to slots you push enemies out of windows (sorry, *defenestrate* them, game tries to sound smart/funny by overusing the word far beyond any reasonable amount).
Enemies are basically tackling dummies. There are no ways to sugarcoat it -- they put word "tactical" in title of the game which has basically NO enemy AI. Most of them don't even move, and just wait for you to come into line of site while patiently waiting near window, watching their comrades getting defenestrated. Obvious exception is close-range enemies, which move... only if they can attack you on the same turn. I saw Sokoban clones where boxes had more agency. Or is it supposed to be some kind of political satire, joking on police officers not having free will? With such a lopsided battle allowing player to rewind their actions without any limitations is equivalent of giving a baseball bat to someone who is already kicking tied up and blinded person.

Which leads me to the worst part of the game: writing. All dialogs are overwritten, suffer from neglecting "show, not tell", often retelling what we just saw during gameplay. Excluding those, half of the remaining dialogue are attempts at jokes, which probably should be something in style of Terry Pratchett, but in reality sound more like "smarky" remarks written by a teenager, who has been reading only reddit for the last 5 years. 
Rest of the writing is even worse. Worldbuilding is worse than in freaking Doom (1993) which had lore on one page in manual, in style of Carmack's ""Story in a game is like a story in a (adult) movie. It's expected to be there, but it's not that important.". We are supposedly in post world war 4 world, all countries on the map are different (but shape is retained, suggesting that we are in future of our world), but the society and technological level is basically the same or somewhat lower than modern days, and characters are making references to USPOL left and right. It feels like playing Shadowrun campaign with DM who knows nothing about Shadowrun apart from it being in future but with magic.
Characters are very one-sided, and completely oblivious to their actions ("Gun is more dangerous than anything I can cast" says someone who kills person by smashing them into a wall or throws three people into windows within second -- and don't give me that BS about slow-fall ward -- turns canonically are single second, and if that clown has time to spam wards on all the windows, she can spend it blocking doors instead), to the degree when it gets annoying. 

But, if gameplay loop was good, one would be able to skip the story and enjoy the game, FE:Engage style. Unfortunately, tactically game is as deep as a puddle in the middle of Sahara desert, and optional challenges/confidence are just making you finish level in a suboptimal manner while not really adding any challenge - so no replayability whatsoever, in an unlikely event that you would want to finish your first playthrough.

5/10 "meh" game, I don't understand what people see in it to make it a "masterpiece". And I definitely don't see where the "funny" is that other reviews say, as all the humour boils down to "random quirky potato 'well that was weird' 'what you can do the flibbelidook with the wizard thing?!' 'punchline is something I am not supposed to say in a normal social interaction'" type of Marvel-esque humour. The game sure thinks its writing is good, but it sure feels just a quirky ChatGPT persona just riffing. It has no teeth, no claws, no no setups, proper punchlines, no themes, nothing to say, nothing. Like I was at least expecting a dating-sim mini game or something!

I do like the novel setting thought. AR-Evergreens, flask-grenades, Tome-carriers, etc. But the game doesn't really do anything with the setting. You'd think it would let you play with alchemical bases and the 4 elements like a wizard, but no. Why do they drive cars and trains when they got brooms? Why is necromancy just a "welp, shot you and resurrected you. That just happened"? It's just a new coat of paint for XCOM-likes. The mechanical depth doesn't use the setting in the slightest and makes the quirkiness and novelty of it largely meaningless and wear off quickly.

I liked the puzzles somewhat, I only really started having fun in Act 3 after I got good upgrades on my skill and felt like I was finding my own solutions to the puzzles instead of figuring out the 1 precise set of moves to do. But in act 4 they introduce these really tedious "tank" enemies that require you to optimize and hyper-focus your strategy around 1 character's 1 skill so you can deal damage. It really cleared the first encounter with these, then got so burned out that I never wanted to finish the act, nor the game. And considering how I don't care about the story nor the character, I don't feel any need to see it through.

I didn't hate the game, and I would recommend it if it WASN'T so overrated.

review:
This is a disappointment for me. My expectations were probably too high given the hype and rave reviews.

What it isn't:
- Is it not an XCom-like were you own, equip and develop your team as you see it.
- Is it not a tactics-like RPG with any freedom, exploration or grand adventure.
- Is it not an immersive narrative experience. You are constantly taken out of the story, in and out of missions. Between the training missions, the gamy challenges and achievement-like objectives, you are constantly distracted and prevented from imbibing the narrative and universe.

What it is:
- A series of baked puzzles to solve. Those are not particularly challenging (even with the confidence challenges) and that get stale and repetitive fast. They are often gamy and sometimes only thinly representative of the narrative justification.
- A well written ensemble of quirky & snarky characters that doesn't take itself seriously.
- An underdeveloped but intriguing and distinct universe.
- In the end, it's a game where the player has very low agency and no long term decisions to make or strategy to have. You just read an average and static story, drudgingly unlocking it bit by bit by solving the puzzles like a good dog. I imagine some people feel smart solving the puzzles. I didn't.

What it tries to be but isn't:
- You can feel the desire to be a noir story a la Disco Elysium, with an immersive narrative and engrossing characters, but much detracts from that and it ultimately failed for me.

Pains me to do it, but, after finishing it, this is a thumbs-down.
Why? The writing. It's very funny when dealing with light themes, but when it tries to deal with some heavy stuff, it comes across, for me, as very dissonant. 
And everything beyond the first 20% of the game is heavy themes. It's not that the writing style is bad, but rather that it's mismatched to the story being told.

Also:
- The game is filled with pep-talk containing psychological advice that both rings strange in the writing tone, and is, at most, soap-opera level.

- At the end, a character the squad met two days before gives them insightful personal pep-talk. It is the time for that story beat, to congratulate the player -- but it feels forced, as two days of constant fighting don't make that level of personal knowledge plausible.

- Major plot hole, story spoiler: 
[spoiler]Sorry for the long-winded explanation, but it's multi-dimensional time-travel stuff:
The way to survive the unbeatable Evil Boss is to let your necromancer escape into another dimension through a Death Door she can create. It is explained that people come out of the Death Door 1 hour after they're pushed in. This way, your necromancer comes back to revive the dead squad mates, as she has the power to time-reverse a dead body 1 hour, back when they were alive. Everyone needs to die and get into the Death Door in sight of the Evil Boss, otherwise they won't be seen as dead, and the Evil Boss will keep coming after them. 
So, in the same fight as the other squadmates are killed, the necromancer pops into the Death Door, and comes out 1 hour later. She then time-reverses the squad-mates 1 hour ... and they're alive. They should have been freshly-killed. Even if you allow for some variance, like the Death Door keeping people in a bit less than 1 hour, and necromancy reverting bodies back to a bit more than 1 hour back, they don't say that and, from their discussion planning the whole thing, have no way of knowing if such margins exist.
[/spoiler]

The gameplay kept being relatively easy, and I got some 2/3 of bonus objectives on first try. I skipped some bonus objectives because I found better things to do - for instance, instead of defenestrating 3 people by turn 2, I finished the whole breach in turn 1.
The character power interplay was the main contributor for crisp and fun gameplay, and this remained constant throughout the game.

So, if you don't care about the story, yup, this is still a thumbs-up. 






Original, thumbs-up review:
Outstandingly funny and well-done Squad-Tactics-lite game. Small teams, great gameplay, fully predictable. More Into The Breach than X-COM.

The skills are impactful and creative, they work together well, and the game is surprisingly low-stress. The required objectives are reasonable, while the bonus objectives are quite challenging.

If you've played XCOM, this might be a nice, relaxing, and very funny game. If you haven't, it could be a great entry into the genre.

review:
TL;DR - The games about a 7/10, with the core game play mechanic being the only real selling point. I'm not recommending because I can't in good conscious do so when so many other reviews are just raving about it without talking about it's flaws.

If you're wanting a closer experience to XCOM: Chimera Squad that's still fun and quirky, go play Rogue Waters. It does the same style of gameplay better, is more fun overall, and the black humour is genuinely funny through and through.

Gameplay:
It's hard to not recommend, it IS a good game, but tentatively, that's kind of the problem. The game follows your small team of "Wizards" as they encounter tactical breach situations, which on the surface sounds like you'll be facing some high octane battles as your team ventures into the sprawling compounds you infiltrate. You do not. 

Every mission is basically a short lived puzzle game, with bonus clothing being the reward for finding more stylish or complex methods of defenestration. This wouldn't be so egregious if the boss battles weren't treated the same; most of the bosses simply being a higher hit point chump with the same weakness to windows as every other enemy in the game. Now, to be fair, the actually significant threats you face DO require some tactical gameplay to work over, which makes those particular missions an absolute JOY to play. If those missions had been the operational standard, instead of being the odd battle you see over 2/3 of the way trough the game, I would have whole-heartedly recommended this game to anyone and absolutely raved about it.

As to the writing:
A lot of emphasis is placed on the writing, and honestly, it's kind of canned. The story itself is ok and there's basically two ways to look at it. From a setting POV, the story is cool. It's a clever mix of Magical fantasy elements and Modern aesthetics, complete with some viable technology emerging from the two. If I were to run a modern-fantasy TTRPG, this setting would make an awesome world to play in. Special call out to the DRUID MAFIA. That concept alone sounded so outlandish and is very cool to contemplate.  The story board itself is.. well.. ok. It's not bad, it just isn't good either. It has an extremely copy/pasta feel, like it was ripped right out of a Marvel/DC movie. Each story beat feels more like an excuse to rapidly transit to a new country and beat up people there, with all semblance of planning being treated as a joke. On a tactical level, your wizards have some sound grasp of tactics. On the strategic level, each and every one of them is constantly flailing about and getting lucky about how they proceed to the next area. It's funny the first time, but by the fourth it's lost all the charm and appeal. Seriously, the story makes it feel like the bad guys lost because they're unlucky, not because of YOUR intervention. Zan (the guy on the game's cover) is the biggest casualty in this department, as despite ostensibly having over 25 years of special operations experience (not even counting prior life experiences or general military experience) he's generally portrayed as a semi-competent dotard with half-baked plans rather than the veteran of  of MANY battles (in game lore!!) that he is, with countless portrayals of how those battles play out since he has the ability to ALWAYS SEE HOW HIS AND HIS TEAM'S ACTIONS WILL IMMEDIATELY AFFECT HIS AND OTHER'S FUTURES. Your other characters are generally portrayed in a positive light, with some time dedicated to showing their flaws, but Zan's just doesn't add-up after awhile. The other negative stand out is Dall, your Riot Priest. On the one hand, on a meta level she's hella cool. Home-made power armor made out of a cop car, BIG MFIN' SHIELD SLAPS, tactical teleports! Hands down, awesome kit. Then you look at her aesthetic, and it's just.. too on the nose for our world instead of the game's world. She's a black woman who's class is called the Riot Priest, who wears power armor made out of cop car (I hate making this seem like a negative), wields a flail made out of magically held together spray cans, and the arch-villain of her arc is a rich man leading an ultranationalist and zealous religious police state. If it weren't treated 100% serious in game, I would've thought it a parody, or a look into how it appears from the outside. At one point, you find your enemies as your allies, given a position of trust over your squad, and their numbers feature a POLICE OFFICER. But it's your team who's treated as the expendable, untrustworthy asset.

This brings us to the "Humorous Dialogue":
Honestly, it's good. At first anyways. It starts with some genuinely amusing quips and the odd bit of office rivalry humor, but by the time you've illegally entered your 2nd country, it's gotten stale. It's the same style of joke, the same self-depreciation, the same devaluation of Zan. There's a brief light of hope when Dall learns to relax and you get your fifth teammate but it's short-lived. Basically, if you like Marvel humour, you'll enjoy it. Otherwise it gets old, fast.

The character themes are pretty cool, though.

I'm pretty early in the game, but it's quite easy. There are several bonus objectives that the game tells you you can come back to later to complete (e.g., killing all 5 enemies in the first turn) but the 10-12 bonus objectives I saw were all immediately doable without much fuss. I think in every case I was able to complete them without even taking damage.

There's also some 4th-wall-breaking political signalling pretty early in the game. I'm generally not a fan of paying for a game only to have that game try to recruit me to a political cause.

The characters have such a wide range of powers that it often isn't obvious which character or power to use, however it generally doesn't matter - any choice tends to win. It thus feels much less strategic than Into The Breach, because here you've got overwhelming force and any one of your multitude of powers will work fine. Even if you screw up and a character dies, another can just bring them back to life and health instantly.

I'd hoped the game might be similar to Invisible Inc, however the speed with which levels are finished here and the OP characters makes it much worse.

review:
Nice game. Like others have said, a bit like X-Com but with wizard powers instead of Sci-Fi powers, and with cheaper, indie graphics. The main game cycle involves setting people up to be defenestrated, pushed through extra-dimensional portals, or just pushed off ledges. You can rewind, most of the time, and set up the perfect combos, and that makes it possible to set up some really hairy situations with multiple threats that there's no way to overcome unless you try a few things and rewind many times. Note that you can't rewind between turns, only inside a turn, so it's not that cheaty, it just gives you time to think, just like the wizard power of foresight this mechanic is meant to model would.

The absolutely worst part is the writing. Sorry guys, but the constant wisecracking gets old after the first five lines. I'd like to enjoy the story, which is not light on tropes to be fair, but I find it exhausting reading through the avalanche of bad jokes and you can't go back and re-read earlier text so any interesting story details are lost forever amid all the cracking. It gets worse as the game progresses, too. By Chapter 3 everyone is starting to sound exactly the same, like there's only one character wearing six or seven different peoples' skins and the jokes start to get incoherent. I blame the Marvel Cinematic Universe really. Fuck Deadpool.

Btw, writer, are you listening? It's "Beryllium", not "brellium" and "batrachotoxin" not "batrachatoxin". If you're going to write like a machine gun at least use a spell-checker. Negative review until you correct your spelling.

review:
Missing a lil special sauce. Gameplay is *fine*, but is very much a puzzle game rather than a tactical combat game. I appreciate the difference might be nit-picking for some, but for me I felt like every single encounter had an intended and definite solution, there is no randomness at all (from what I saw). Yes you can "do your own thing" and probably turn out alright, but I often felt like I was doing things in spite of an intended solution.

This isn't x-com, this isn't gears tactics, it's a well crafted puzzle game with a veneer of tactical combat. Kind of like a better Capes.

Humour just doesn't land for me. Tries to be witty, ends up feeling like a marvel film, small talk is everywhere, which is great if you find it funny, I didn't. It reminded me of all those people at school who felt they were funny spouting one liners, nonsequiturs and "dry" humour. It's peak tumblr.

The story itself is pretty mid (from what I gleaned from the first few levels. I didn't care enough to actually keep with it) and is weaved into the game in such a way that even if you wanted to skip it, you'd find it tedious to do so.

Characters felt very one-note, even if their powers were cool, with the first two characters, you have the grizzled veteran harbouring guilt over his past actions and the quirky do gooder who just can't let go. They riff off each other well, but as I said, if you don't enjoy quirky nonsequiturs or dialogue like "I'll take this bullet for you, but you owe me a health pack!" Then it doesn't get better.

It's a promising puzzle game wrapped in a disappointing coat.

I loved Gunpoint. I think their style of writing is still alive and well with TBW. Unfortunately, when half the lines are quippy snark where characters are building off each other, and the plot is relatively basic, it doesn't take much to break immersion and investment in the story with modern politics. There are other problems, narratively - one of the characters can revive everyone else, so it never feels like there are any stakes, even with the opponent having some crazy god powers. If you can overlook a few calls to modern politics, you'll enjoy the game. Personally, I'm downright exhausted about it, so when halfway through the game, it slapped me upside the head, it was very disappointing. If SD makes another game, I'll probably still buy it. I just hope they stick to what they're good at - fun writing - and leave parallels to the real world off the table.

review:
A decent yet generic tactical squad game brought low by embarrassing attempts at witty dialogue in the vain of Rick and Morty, blatant self-insert characters (for example, a furry who has the power to transform into a dog and is the most bad-ass assassin in the world), and low-effort political lecturing which is so incoherent in it's message that, at first, it's hard to even tell which political philosophy the game is attempting to attack, only that the author believes that the IRL followers of said philosophy deserve death. 

Later it becomes clear that the "bad guys" are supposed to be American Republicans who are portrayed as raving super-villains who hold secret Illuminati-style meetings at which they openly admit to being evil racists who want world domination. While there is nothing wrong with having a politically-focused plot, at no point in the entire game is there any attempt at a deep philosophical investigation of the politics at hand. Unfortunately, the game believes that simply writing scenes where republicans admit to being evil somehow qualifies as political dialogue, which makes the story utterly substance-less, tiring, and irrelevant for anyone who does not live in the United States (like myself). Even propaganda would have more effort put into it that this game's story does, as it would actually have the goal of changing peoples minds, rather than the authors clear goal of writing a self-serving fantasy where all of his politics are proven right. Even this would be forgivable if it didn't completely consume the game's plot, which unfortunately it does, with all other story elements effectively being put on hold for 95% of the games runtime whilst we are told about how bad the orange man is, then suddenly coming back to the forefront at the very final level in an an unsatisfying conclusion which serves only to reach the technical requirement of concluding the mystery which at first was portrayed as the driving force behind the narrative. In fact, the evil republicans you spend much of the game fighting are an entirely separate faction to the one which the main nemesis is a member of, making it even more irrelevant to the overarching story, while the main nemesis's faction is also run by an evil sociopathic billionaire hell-bent of world domination, meaning the game somehow manages to have two separate analogies for the evil orange man at the same time. Additionally, this plot swerve into anti-republican slogan chanting suspiciously begins almost immediately after the 2-hour-mark, which conveniently makes it impossible to refund the game once it becomes clear that the games promise of having a "story-driven campaign" will not be met.

TLDR;

The game's story effectively ceases to exist almost exactly two hours into the game. Buy it if you think the pricetag is acceptable for a typical tactical puzzle game. Swerve if you expected a compelling narrative.
