review:
Since purchasing this, almost no new content has been added. Despite this being an "early access" game, it already feels as though it's bordering upon being abandoned. The maps are frankly piss-poor, low effort garbage, with no detail or interest and nothing to facilitate good/interesting gameplay. Each map basically feels like a reskin of the same shitty map that looks as though it was made in under an hour using a game engine from 2005.

There is a ton of AI generated content in this game, and it really shows. Everything about it feels creatively dead/bankrupt. I believe most of the skins available in the game are in some way AI generated, and are equally as uninspired. (And.. for the most part, only available via a ridiculously overpriced year-long subscription to a "Daily Cosmetics Pass" that costs more than double the price of the actual game.)

It honestly feels as though the intention of Prophecy Games was to boil Tribes down to it's absolute core barebones mechanics and absolutely nothing else. They have decided to forgo any actual content or any of the charm/flare present in  of any previous titles in the series. And not only that, but they've chosen to do so with the least amount of cost/effort humanly possible.

Also, the servers are dead. Overall GLOBAL player count averages around 30-35 people, occasionally spiking to 50, maybe 60. And if you live in the wrong timezone? Sorry, you're looking between 5-7 players globally. And if that isn't enough to put you off, Prophecy have done absolutely ZERO to combat people cheating/hacking, so when you do get into a game that has a slightly less awful population (which will universally be populated by people who entirely ignore the gamemode you're playing and just deathmatch until the timer runs out) you'll probably just get ran down by someone aimbotting and/or speed hacking.

Absolute waste of time, do not waste your money.
Tribes is dead.

review:
Instead of making a battlefield-style game like Tribes 2 with broad appeal, the developers in their infinite wisdom have made a fast-paced arena-style game like Tribes: Vengeance. This means there's nothing for you to do in the game if you aren't already good at it.

It's not a bad Tribes game. There just isn't anything to do in the game if you aren't very good at 3D dueling combat or flag capping/chasing.

Past Tribes games had large maps, large bases, vehicles to pilot, an array of deployable items so you could base build, etc. T1/T2 also had mods with much more of these gameplay aspects.

This game has small maps with open flags, small bases, no vehicles, and no way to play a dedicated base building role.

Developers (as usual) don't understand what makes a Tribes game easy or hard, so they have tried to make an easy Tribes game while actually making a hard one.

There are also currently hit detection bugs, but this would be more so expected for early access.

This may be a fun game for veterans of the Tribes series, but it's difficult to recommend it to anybody else at all.

I will probably never see an IP get fumbled as hard as this one did ever again. Extremely tragic to see a series of the most exciting FPS games I've ever played get mismanaged by a company notorious for their ludicrous incompetence when managing projects. 

I really like this game. but it was never in a state to be sold for $20 with the Tribes name attatched to it, as it has about a third of the content of all the previous Tribes games while missing basic functions seen in online computer games since before the first Tribes game (text chat, server browser, ect.). There's no base-oriented gameplay, which is something a huge amount of players from previous games really enjoyed. It is an extremely dumbed down, scaled down, and watered down version of everything associated with the Tribes series, and that's really it's biggest detriment outside of missing basic features and the bots being used to artificially create an active playerbase.

All it really needs is the right amount of love from the right people, and it's been deprived of both and thrown out the window in favor of the next corporate profit venture in the form of a video game (which looks like genuine dogshit, even when put next to pretty much any other game Hi-Rez has to their name which is pretty impressive to me), and there's no mod tools or a level editor and probably won't be anytime soon.

review:
EDIT: Nevermind, don't buy this shit show because apparently the devs abandoned it. 

[h1]Feedback for the Devs[/h1]

Here's a list of everything I think could help improve the game.


[h3]Offline Skirmishes[/h3]
I'd like to experiment with builds and practice against bots, but if the servers are acting funny, it's a bit difficult to engage in it, so please, above all else, add offline support or a LAN option so it doesn't require an internet connection for experimenting/practicing. This is by far my biggest complaint about the game. Everything else, one can give or take, but I think an offline mode is essential.

[h3]Text Chat[/h3]
I don't enjoy being forced to use VGS or voice chat only. Text chat would be greatly appreciated and very helpful.

[h3]Inventory Stations[/h3]
Tribes 2 did it best with inventory stations. Opened up a menu, set the preferred loadouts, customized it and stepped on the inventory pad to receive their changed gear. That was fantastic.

[h3]Free Loadouts[/h3]
In Tribes 1 & 2, you could have a range of weapons you could select, yet only have so many at a time, but you could easily mix and match in between. I liked being able to do that. Tribes 2 also did it best here and I highly recommend bringing that old system back.

[h3]More Deployables[/h3]
As someone who enjoyed playing the building engineer dude who set up turrets, and sneakily deployed inventory stations near enemy bases, that was a lot of fun. I also loved being able to place down different gadgets that would hinder enemy teams abilities such as stealthing/sensor jamming.

Please consider these points, devs. You'll go a long way to making it feel like Tribes even more.

I am a Tribes 2 CTF veteran. I put 110 hours into Tribes 3. I feel I have some legitimacy in talking about how this game stacks up as a Tribes game. There are some bugs and little things that needed tweaking but that isn't the issue here cause the game is a flop and is being discontinued. 

Tribes 3 is too sweaty of a Tribes game to attract casual gamer's that enjoyed Tribes 2 CTF. The large scale sandbox CTF shooter is gone. You get this "Arena CTF" where you are stuck in a box and have to deal with Tribes vets that will slaughter new players in a heartbeat. "Casual" pubs are not particularly fun because you can just spawn in Heavy and shoot mortars at your own gens/flag and not damage your own players or equipment. You get punished for trying to be effective on objectives when playing Offense. If you want to succeed you have to hunt the flag carrier, suicide and repeat. 

This game has no reason to be played for general audiences when they could play Overwatch/CS:GO/Apex/Valorant/CoD etc... 

I still feel Tribes skiing physics has a lot to offer video games but Tribes needs a huge amount of resources to make large scale combat or needs to be rebooted into something else to attract people to the play style. But honestly the market is over saturated with competitive games and Tribes CTF hasn't been relevant since 2002-2003. 

I believe this is the nail in the Tribes coffin. 

Summary : Game is too sweaty to be a casual pub game and doesn't have much to do in it. God bless.

P.S.

If anybody reads this and is still interested in a fun Tribes game you can find us in Discord and come play in Tribes 2 pick up games. The community is a little "mouthy" but they are harmless. The pub scene is not that great right now but who knows it could turn around.

It's also too bad the reward system is lackluster and boring.  Normal gameplay reward cycle without buying the skin pack grants you a handful of skin rewards in the first few levels and then all kinds of titles/emblems/banners after that based on basic gameplay achievements after that, barely any more skins.

I can count on one hand the amount of times I noticed another players skin.  To someone who actually paid for some of these cosmetics in Tribes Ascend it's hilarious watching these guys double dip on such *strong* assets.

Read their statement and decide for yourself if it's worth buying considering the static state of the game, the gameplay of Tribes still holds up and is incredibly fun to those who enjoy it. ***EDIT***
Save your money and buy something else. The game has its moments, however the dying player base alone (70-100 daily players) should be enough to steer clear. Not to mention the devs have stated that this game is being put on the back burner for something else. Unfortunate, but a tribes revival will never happen.

********

This is an extremely stripped down version of tribes. If you are looking for Tribes 2 or even Tribes 2 Ascension, you will be disappointed. There is a feel of competitiveness however it is basically light armor flag runners chasing each other around.

Defensive classes and deployables are essentially worthless. Even more so in a map that has an open flag stand. On maps that have an enclosed flag, defensive classes do a little better but not much.

Maps are smaller and base layouts extremely basic. Base sentries are slow and have bad tracking.

Sniping is nearly impossible, which can be a good or bad thing. Of course you dont want it to be so easy that everyone in the game starts sniping but at least make it challenging instead of impossible. Weapon variations are OK. Mid air kills are always satifying.

Base elements that were essential to destroy in previous versions of tribes are now just optional to destroy. Most 12v ctf games are just basically team deathmatch games, there is no real structure or reason to teamplay and cap flags.

On the upside, skiing and jetpacking are very easy and seamless. This is great for newcomers. The game itself runs fine on the highest settings even on older cards.

There is an in-game store for skins etc, which I have never been a fan of in any game.

A lot of balancing needs to be done.

Overall it shows potential and my hope is that it being early access a lot of features that we've come to love will be implemented further down the line. In order for this game to survive and become popular it needs them.

review:
I get it everyone loves to go fast, but the speed in this game is way too much. You basically have to use explosive weapons because it's nearly impossible to hit with any of the more precision-based weapons. But then you run into the problem that with the explosive weapons most people are moving faster than the projectiles. So the only way to hit with any form of accuracy is to try to time your aim for when they're going to land, or to force them indoors where they cant use their speed by targeting their facilities. At which point it becomes bad in the opposite direction because everyone is using wide aoe explosive weapons, so it's hard to express much skill. The speed meta makes capture the flag so obnoxious. there is one unbeatable strategy to capture the flag: build up as much speed as possible, rocket through the flag at a million miles an hour, and fly away without losing speed. The maps are specifically designed to enable this. Flags on every map are proudly  displayed on the outside of buildings for anyone to grab.If a single person on the enemy team is skilled at this then you're cooked. There is no defense against this. In fact the only time people bother to defend much at all is if someone sabotages the generator. The only thing the generator does nowadays is power the radar, so there's not much point anyway. Everyone is on offense at all times. If you even try to defend people will devote their entire existence to launching mortars from the other side of the map at any defensive tools you place, or they'll just hover around your base shooting at you moving at mach speed until your flag comes back up, at which point they zoom into it at a million miles an hour to repeat the process. Defense is something you do on your way to the offense in this game, and the maps are tiny relative to your speed so you can get back to the base in seconds if you need to.

If there were proper tools to mitigate the speed that would be fine but they've screwed us in that department too. Older tribes games let you customize your builds in a very freeform way with lots of different tools and gadgets and whatnot, but those days are gone. This time, everything is class based. There are 6 classes, 2 for each weight type, and they have 2-3 selections per weapon slot. You have 2-3 weapons per class, plus an ability and a grenade. Half of the selections between classes are "the same gun but bigger/smaller" and there are clear favorites in most slots. All heavies carry a mortar. All classes carry their weight-class version of the spinfusor. No one bothers carrying a sniper rifle. No one carries grenade launchers. No one uses any pistol slot weapon ever. Every pistol-class weapon could cease to exist and no one would care. I'm the only person I've seen using proximity mines, and only when I camp the enemy generator or on a single specific map where the flag is moderately covered so they probably won't get nuked by mortars. Stationary specials are immediately obliterated the moment someone sees them. (they need way more hp to be relevant. 1-2 spinfusor discs will destroy most of them) The destruction of the customization is the thing I'm actually mad about. It's what I loved about tribes. It's why I have hundreds of hours killing bots on the old ps2 game. It made me feel like I was making choices, enacting strategies, really engaging with the battlefield and adjusting tactics to match the situation. This version of the game is just everyone mindlessly flying around at max speed, no counterplay, no choices or tactics, everyone doing the very limited selection of optimal actions on repeat until the the team with the fastest flag capturer wins. I got bored after 3 hours, and there is no progression at all from leveling up aside from getting cosmetics for your player card. The only time I've had much fun in this game is either camping the generator or laughing at speed demons diving the flag only to suicide onto my proximity mines. (this only works on one map where the flag is loosely indoors until the enemy realizes you're camping and start lobbing explosives at the flagstand periodically to clear mines)

Having been a Tribes player since the original first came out, I can't recommend this at this time.

It only took me 2-3 matches to see that this is NOT the game I grew up playing. It's an 'arena mode' version of the original. It's the proof of concept for the basic experience of the first two games.

Gone are the sprawling maps that utilized vehicles, proper base defense, communication, and teamwork that kept people up all night playing in favor of a very watered down experience. 

Maps feel very watered down and basic, the sound (while bringing back some of the classic sound effects) is grating at times, the guns lack *oomph*, the base defenses are inconsequential. Even the skiing, the primary movement mechanic in the game, feels... *off* somehow, like the gravity isn't quite right.

I wouldn't normally be so harsh on it since it's in early access but it is charging money for DLC outfits so all bets are off.

Abysmal player numbers aside, there *is* something here- it's just needs more work, a lot more work. I'm not factoring the developer in this, but from what I've read, maybe I should.

Refund requested, but I'll be keeping my eye on it. I am hopefull the developers will put more effort into capturing what made the original games so much fun to play and make changes accordingly. Time will tell, or maybe I'm just old.

review:
Basically imagine they took the archaic Tribes 2 mechanics and slapped some of the Tribes ascend mechanics on top of it, creating the worst of both worlds. This is coming from someone with 2000+ hours in Ascend, mostly as a capper. Here's what I immediately didn't like.

* Thrust pack barely does anything and just wastes energy, and is on a 15 second cooldown instead of just using whatever energy you have whenever you want.

* Extremely little air control, you basically can't redirect yourself at all in the air, but can with ease by faceplanting whatever hillside you need to, weird design.

* Can't use your pack while you're holding the flag

* no melee :(

* Grenade is no longer ammo based and is also on a 15 second timer.

* When you enable skiiing you automatically thrust forward slightly

* If you land poorly it doesn't matter at all, you still gain speed and don't take any damage

* Clunky movement, basically makes dueling entirely down to who can aim better, movement, prediction, and dodging skill doesn't matter at all. In Ascend you could win a duel from predicting and dodging well. You could use the air and ground in combination to make it harder for your opponent to hit you. In rivals you're basically always a sitting duck vs a sitting duck. Hitting Midairs is a joke because everyones movement is 100% predictable.

* No health regen. Not that this matter much to me, but I prefer having regen, less downtime and more action. No regen just forces you to go back all the time.

* Phase rifle is weird. You have to lead your shot, not hitscan, but also it feels like autoaim when you do land a hit. I never once landed a hit and thought to myself Nice Shot, everytime it was like, did that bullet just bend towards them, how did that hit??

* Bunch of weird "cinematic" video options you will have to immediately turn off. To be honest I think this is the most obvious sign that the developers do not know their audience or game. Motion blur, Adaptive FoV based on speed, camera tilting, etc.

* half the players seem to be bots, but aren't actually distinguished as bots.

* no text chat

Overall just super unimpressed with this game, felt like I was playing an alpha version of Tribes Ascend. I'd rather just have Ascend back than whatever this amalgamation is.

I just don't even.

It's like a CoD phone game milking funds from tweens meets overwatch meets the slide you kept hitting in the park during your childhood.

I get why. There's not as much money to be made in quality games and designs for appreciative, loving, niche audiences. It's just hurtfully sad to see the Tribes name getting dragged through the same mud. Lower quality, lower uniqueness, wider demographic, fingers crossed for some traction on the market, no shame.

But no, really, other people aren't joking when they go on about how this is Tribes: Ascend, but less. There's less of virtually everything.

The one thing that has been increased is the amount of control the player has relative to the motion controls and mechanics. It's easier on the player to make things like that, but it also takes away from the authenticity of the unique Tribes experience. Back when the laws of physics were a thing in games, the player was responsible for going too fast or at too bad an angle. Here, you're not far from just flying in any direction at will like Superman - the only exception being your limited energy, so you can only do so much [i]upward[/i] movement.

Ascend had a LOT of right answers to faults in earlier games. This? This one poured all the polish where it wasn't needed and didn't bother to spread evenly like a half-decent adult. It's just one more body in the pile of, "well, nostalgia cash-in killed [i]that one, too!"[/i]

Tribes 3 takes the movement from the other Tribes games and does an OK job of it, whilst simultaneously making the maps tiny, so travelling skilfully and learning landscapes frankly unimportant now.  It removes all games modes except for CTF, removes all vehicles, simplifies base infrastructure to the point of utter boredom and stops you from being able to fully customise your loadout.  The game is alright at best, but Tribes 1 & 2 were amazing games, and they've almost totally missed what made them special.  Skiing was only a part of the jigsaw puzzle, and reducing map size so thoroughly has crippled even that.

This is a cash-grab.  They give you jet packs and spinfusers so they can call it Tribes, but it's not Tribes.  Avoid.

***5/22/2025 Update***

They abandoned this game.

***5/22/2025 Update***

As I take a break from playing Tribes 3: Rivals, I find myself conflicted. 
The core of this game is really solid, but very much has its roots in Tribes: Ascend. 
For those who do not know, Tribes 3: Rivals is being developed by Prophecy Games, a subsidiary of Hi Rez. Yes, that Hi Rez.


And while there is a solid team behind this game composed of people who have worked on past entries, it's that connection to Hi Rez that I can't really look past.


Tribes: Ascend was not a game that died because it wasn't popular, or due to bad support, or its slow progression, or any reason other than this: It died because Hi Rez wanted it to die. 
The game was well-reviewed, critically acclaimed, and had a healthy player base. That is until July 2013, when they ceased all support for the game and left it to die, citing lackluster financial returns and wanting to better support SMITE as the reason. 


Then as if to rub more salt in the wound they would come back to the game 2 years later and drop a "Out of the Blue" update on the game. This is the literal actual name of the update. "Out of the Blue.” It ended up being an honestly great update that put the game in the best state it had ever been in. But it was bittersweet, given that this was also the signal that this was the LAST update this game would ever receive. From that point on, the game slowly lost its player base until it was ultimately delisted from Steam. 

So that brings us to today: Tribes 3 Rivals is out in early access and seems poised to pick up where Ascend left off.
While the game we have right now is a little sparse on content, the bones here are good. Gone is the insane grind for weapons and gadgets that players of Tribes: Ascend hated. We've got a cross section of familiar locations, classes, and weapons. 

There are no vehicles at the time of this review being written. 
 
There are two modes: Casual 16 vs 16 and Ranked 7 vs 7.
I have yet to get into a ranked match, as most seem to be interested in playing the casual 32 player mode. Hopefully as the early access period progresses and the game releases, the ranked mode will populate better.
Tribes has always pushed boundaries when it comes to huge player counts - the original game was capable of hosting 128 players, and that came out in 1998. Tribes 3 does not do this, tho to be fair neither did Tribes Ascend. 


I would love to see a 64 player mode added to the game one day, but for now the chaos of a fully-populated Tribes match is preserved through smaller map sizes. I would also like to see them reintroduce vehicles and maybe even cross-play at some point.


Outside of the main versus offerings there is also a gun range and a time trial mode to practice your movement - which you will definitely want to consider doing as the game is as fast as it's ever been. 
There have been some nice adjustments to the game just from a quality of life perspective, such as the new drop shadow icon that appears below enemy players. Previously you had to guestimate where they were going to land, this wasn't impossible but this new feature makes it easier than ever to nail those high speed blue plate specials. Or if you're just trying to cut off an enemy's escape you can use it as a guide for where to place those doombringer shells.

There are 6 returning classes: 


The high speed capping/chasing class: Pathfinder.
The lightweight Sentinel defender equipped with the useful Nitro charge to knock the flag off a fleeing player.
The extremely versatile Raider who comes equipped with a standard Spinfusor and semi-auto grenade launcher. This is going to be the bread and butter for anyone who wants to take it to the front line or hang out in midfield and disrupt the enemy team's advance. 
The Technician is back with their ability to quickly repair base assets as well as throw down defensive turrets. They get a similar build to the Raider, however I do feel their importance has been reduced somewhat. *Anyone* can equip a repair tool and effectively do the job of the Technician at the moment. Would like to see some sort of buff come their way. Maybe an extra turret?
     5 & 6. And capping things off, we have the big chungus brothers: The Doombringer and Juggernaut, with very similar weapon loadouts. The big thing separating the two being that Juggernaut is able to passively regenerate health and ammo in addition to their ability to slam into targets for additional damage. 

With the time I've spent with the game, I can confidently say this is an excellent entry in the series just from a pure gameplay standpoint. But I am somewhat worried about history repeating itself. 

The rather expensive cosmetic season passes being prominently featured on the front page and the fact that Hi Rez is still involved (despite hiding behind another developer) are enough reasons to give me pause. 

But if they're committed to bringing this series back and making it as popular as it once was, I'm willing to look past the mismanagement that occurred with Tribes: Ascend.

Tribes deserves to be up there with its peers like Quake and Unreal but has historically been relegated to an after thought both by players and developers alike. Tribes 3: Rivals in its current state is an excellent first start but it's on Prophecy Games and Hi Rez to prove to the playerbase that they’re serious about reviving Tribes. If they can stay away from chasing trends and focus on what made the previous games great, they may have a shot at bringing this once great series back from the self imposed hibernation it was in.

I am disappointed and feel scammed 100%.
DO NOT TRUST ANY NEW GAMES COMING FROM HI-REZ OR ITS STUDIOS.

HOW IS THIS EVEN ALLOWED TO EXIST ON STEAM

HOW ARE THESE THIEVES ALLOWED TO CONTINUE



==================================================

So far so good gameplay-wise. Please dont * this up.

The game is in early access, just keep that in mind. Yes, its a little bare bones at the moment, but content is going to be added along the way. Already we are seeing patches/qol updates. The gameplay is there, it may need to be tweaked here or there, but Tribes itself is something really special...

Anyone who has ever enjoyed an FPS, should at least give Tribes a shot. One of my favorite types of multiplayer games can be played super casually, but also has a ridiculously high skill ceiling. The gameplay loop is simple ctf, but the core of Tribes is mastering the projectiles and movement, and is one of the most fun and entertaining casual AND competitive multiplayer experiences you can have.


Now..

Yes, there are bots in your matches within first few levels of your account, at least that is what it felt like for me. Especially since it was the same system used in Paladins, Hi-Rez's hero shooter. You 100% play with bots until account level 5 in that game. It only equates to maybe 4-6 matches, but it isn't made apparent to the player.

I believe that this is a good system, BUT there is an obvious negative.. newer players get to experience the gameplay and are able to "warm up" to it before hopping into matches with more experienced players. The negative being is that using bots isn't communicated properly.

Right now, everyone slowly comes to the realization as they're playing that 90% of the lobby is bots during their first few matches. When you receive something you aren't expecting, you feel deceived, no matter what the initial intent is. Hey, if the community still isn't ok with bots being in the games, at least give us the option to opt out. If it increases our queue times, well then thats our choice we'd like to make.

The positive note, after a few account levels, you absolutely see human players on a more consistent basis.


So far, no cheaters, its an active game with full lobbies every match, and its fun as hell.


Needs additional basic features that I hope are coming down the line. This stuff seems like the bare minimum for a social competitive experience in a multiplayer game in 2024. Who doesn't like comparing stats with their friends?


Must Adds:


Better tutorial to explain to people what exactly is happening, maybe make a 45 second embeded video as well? Generators? Repairing? Health Orbs? New players need to know what this stuff is.

Text chat with option to mute/squelch.

More stats on separate tabs on post-game screen. Damage done, damage received, and death count for starters. Look at Halo Infinite for an example.

Improved Menus, where are my match history stats, career stats?


Im going to keep adding stuff here as I think of it.

[url= https://www.tribes3rivals.com/news/tribes-3-player-update] She's dead, Jim - "We’re doing our best to support TRIBES 3 with limited updates".[/url]

[i]As a longtime Tribes fan, Rivals leaves me disappointed. Featuring AI art, bots disguised as players, kernel-level drivers via Denuvo, no server browser with only a single game mode (CTF), and finally, two skin passes which cost more than many games out on the market today. Why this isn’t F2P I don’t understand, as there are much more fluid FPS offerings which are.[/i]

[h1]📝 Main Pros, Cons, and Suggestions:[/h1] 
 
🟩 Pros: 

+ Weapon balance is well done
+ Matchmaking was near instant
+ Rewards for completing achievements
+ Cross region gameplay felt fluid (from OCE to NA)
+ Low system resource usage coupled with no performance issues
+ The 365 day skin passes offer over 700 items assuming you win each day, which is much more generous than most other games

🟥 Cons: 

-	Denuvo (kernel-level)
-	No server browser and only a single game mode
-	Custom games list was blank, not sure if a bug or DOA?
-	Narrow in scope and limited by small maps and small team sizes
-	Ridiculous cost for skin passes, considering they are AI generated art 
-	You only receive skins if you win each day despite paying for the skin passes, along with that, they are AI generated

🏷️ Suggestions: 

~ F2P to bring players
~ Add Steam achievements, you already have them in game

[h1]A hollow shell of what Tribes once was[/h1]

I have Tribes 2 and Vengeance in storage, playing both for countless hours over the years. Words cannot express the excitement and nostalgia I felt when I saw Rivals. After playing it however, I am left speechless.

It has jetpacks and skiing, that’s it – The feelings I once had playing Tribes games is lost. Rather than building upon what made the franchise great, the developers delivered a hollow shell of a game, featuring bots and a single game mode (CTF). Further, skin passes have been introduced to try and retain players, because if you want the rewards you paid for, you’ll need to win each day.

While I would love to recommend Tribes 3: Rivals, as I did have fun playing, there are too many cons which I feel cannot be corrected without redesigning core gameplay elements. It has no staying power, the player base is already in decline, and it offers nothing that isn’t in the market already. Nostalgia is a powerful thing, but in this case, that isn’t enough.

All you can do is join auto match making lobby to play a 15 minute ctf game against random players and unidentified bots. How many times are you going to be entertained doing this same little thing over and over?  This feels like the cheap watered down Chinese mobile phone version of Tribes. It's missing 90% of the core features of previous Tribes games that gave it any kind of depth and replayability, and features that have been fundamental in games in general for decades. review:
I caved and bought this game because I have the flu and, despite some issues/misgivings, I had some fun in the free playtests. The thing that made me pull the trigger was reading the recent patch notes and seeing that bots would be clearly labeled and would only fill slots when players leave the game, and voice chat would be enabled by default. The fact that they were addressing these important community concerns made me feel like I could give them money. I failed to notice the part about bots only being identified in ranked mode and that these changes were for a future patch not yet implemented (again I'm sick with the flu).

So I booted it up and jumped into a game. Our team was winning, so I was just having fun trying to hold the midpoint. And it was fun, I was basically just dueling and I was crushing it, which... is unlike me, I'm just not that good at killing rather than being killed, especially because, in these team-based games I like to put more into being a team player than having a reasonable kill/death ratio. But quickly the fun gave way to an uncanny feeling, it felt empty, I was too good, I kept pushing tab, trying to figure out if I was missing where it said I was playing versus bots, the fact that pings are not listed and there's no text chat made it impossible to tell. Am I just in a server with absolute newbies? I'm reading the names of the people in the room with me, are these the names internet players would choose for themselves? I feel paranoid that the world isn't real. Is this a side effect of my fever?

[b]Derealization[/b] is an alteration in the perception of the external world, causing those with the condition to perceive it as unreal, distant, distorted or falsified. The term was famously mentioned in the Bo Burham song "That Funny Feeling".

I went to bed. Before playing again the next day I re-read the patch notes and, sure enough, see that bots are only clearly identified in ranked mode.

So I jump into ranked mode. I'm bad at the game again, great sign that this is real. But, I want to communicate complicated things to my teammates. I don't love voice chat with strangers and besides NOBODY else is talking (I now know this is because VC enabled by default hasn't yet been implemented). Ranked mode is sort of fun, but after a game is over it boots me back to the main screen. No way to communicate joy at winning or heartbreak at losing with those folks. No way to communicate anything, those folks are gone, no way to find them. Were they real? I know they must be but the sense of distance is still there. Before I was dominating bots, now I'm letting down real people, but. Am I letting them down? They can't communicate with me. If they could, what would they ask that I do differently?

The thought I have is that this game feels like Quidditch; sure, there are other roles to play, you can attack the base, attack players, capture the midpoint, but the only one that actually matters for who wins the game is the role of the flag capper, the seeker, the Harry Potter. This one decides who wins the game and exists entirely independent of all other roles.

The game description calls it a "rebirth of the world’s fastest shooter" and I get that they are at least in part referring to the speeds one can get by skiing. But I also think speed and competition are truly what this game is going for. Action as fast as possible, skiing as fast as possible. Capturing the enemy flag is very easy without destroying the enemy base (that would be too slow). This is true of all tasks in the game, none require teamwork or process. You can blow up the enemy generator without defeating any turrets, or running into any players (being good at dueling is fairly unnecessary in this game). But ultimately doesn't matter a ton to the enemy if their generator is destroyed. They can still capture the flag with exactly the same ease. Similarly, you can capture the midpoint without defeating the turrets, and holding the midpoint also seems totally tangential, a distraction from winning rather than a strategy for doing so.

There's no more slow inventory stations, no vehicles. But what would the point of vehicles be? What is the point of bringing a team of heavies to the enemy base when one lone person of any class can do it easily. And what is the point of attacking the enemy base when it does nothing to limit their ability to cap flags or your ability to capture their flag? Turrets are not an impediment to a fast-moving capper, and a capper can still spawn with their perfect loadout even when the teams generator is destroyed. 

Ultimately no part of the game requires teamwork. We see this get brought up as a reason for no text chat, sure there's no ability to communicate complex needs or strategies, but there's no need to. It's nice that in ranked I know my team is real. But... what's the point of their realness? What do we need to communicate about? The best/only thing you can do to ensure victory for your team is to spawn as a light and be good at capping.

I enjoy the mechanics of the movement and the weapons, genuinely, I can see a lot of work went into that and imagine they'll continue to be improved and balanced. But the core gameplay is lacking because I think there is a fundamental misunderstanding of what kind of game Tribes is. It's a game of two teams, with many different roles to fill in order to be victorious (this is why there are different armor classes). It's a slow game, where victory requires multiple steps taken, various roles filled in order to achieve victory. 

Blowing up the enemy generator isn't fun because it’s fun to click on it a bunch, it's fun because it helped my team win. Capping isn't fun because it ends the game and now Griffindor wins, it's fun because we pulled off something together, they counted on me to do it and I did it, or I didn't, and I feel I failed them (stakes). I don't want to be the sole protagonist, I want to be part of a team. I want to build trust with my teammates, and work with strangers who become less strange. I want to be an integral part of the machine that wins, not the singular hero who won alone. 

And you can't really do that in Tribes 3: Quidditch. You can't do it in a game that purposefully obfuscates whether you're playing alone or with others, a game which does not require teamwork and does not support communication, yet still is confoundingly built on the bones of a fundamentally team-based game. 

Also, lastly, in case anyone with any power over the direction of this or any game with similar problems ever reads this. This sense of derealization matters even if you only care about money. Sure it makes the game less fun and less likely to be initially purchased but it also screws up your microtransaction scheme by totally undermining any incentive for buying any cool skins because:

      • What is the point of looking cool if I have the distinct impression that nobody I'm playing with is real? 
      • How do they know that I'm real? 
      • Why do they care that I'm real if the game does not require teamwork (why would they care to notice me at all if I'm not important to them as a teammate)? 
      • But let's say they do think I look cool, how could they let me know without chat?
      • And finally, why would they care to tell me I look cool if when the game ends we are ripped apart and back to a lobby (as one is when playing in 7v7 Ranked, AKA real people mode), unlikely to ever cross paths again?

review:
It's 2024 and I get to play a new Tribes game, is this real life? It is real life, and unfortunately it's more of a nightmare than a dream. 

Tribes 3: Rivals scratches that nostalgic itch I've missed since the 2001 hit Tribes 2. After the initial honeymoon phase ends, you will soon realize that while it's still fun skiing around shooting spinfusors at everything, the game is a shell of it's former sell. 

There's a 16v16 CTF mode,  and a 7v7 competitive CTF mode. That's it. There's no vehicles, the maps are small to medium sized, and the game is missing many core features you may remember for previous titles. No text chat. Voice chat is disabled by default and in 20 hours I've heard 1 other person talking in game. 

That's the entire game. There's nothing to earn in-game, no skins or guns or skills or anything, which is fine; this is how Tribes used to be, but it's 2024 and games have changed. There's a 1 year chest you can buy which gives 1 gun and 1 skin with your first victory every day. But you can't even see what skins are available and there's no way to customize your character beyond these (title/banner aside).

Overall this is a huge disappointment, and I question why release it in this state knowing it could be the early death of this game.

review:
Tribes 3, the latest installment in the renowned Tribes series, endeavors to push boundaries while staying true to its roots. While certain improvements have been made, the game still grapples with significant issues that detract from the overall experience.

One notable improvement in Tribes 3 is the reduced significance of ping, which addresses a longstanding concern in previous titles. However, this step forward is marred by the introduction of client-side hit registration, leading to frequent instances of non-registrations and ghosted hits, particularly for players with higher ping. This undermines the integrity of hit detection, creating frustration and inconsistency in combat encounters.

Unfortunately, the game stumbles significantly in several critical areas:

Combat mechanics, once a cornerstone of the Tribes series, have regressed in Tribes 3. The highly increased ease of hitting opponents diminishes the depth of combat, shifting the focus away from mechanical skill.

Unlike its predecessors, which featured diverse vehicles, game modes, and weapons, Tribes 3 primarily focuses on Capture the Flag (CTF) gameplay, neglecting alternative modes and strategic depth. The absence of vehicles, alongside limited weaponry and the singular focus on CTF, may lead to player boredom over time, as the game lacks the variety and innovation that characterized previous Tribes titles.

The involvement of CEO Erez in development remains problematic. Lacking meaningful experience in game development, Erez's influence has led to misguided decisions, prioritizing short-term player metrics over solid design principles. This approach has resulted in imbalanced gameplay and questionable priorities.

Map design also falls short, deviating from the dynamic landscapes of its predecessors. Instead, players encounter uninspired, flat terrains with sporadic hills, failing to capture the essence of the series' iconic environments.

Moreover, the core elements such as physics and movement mechanics are underwhelming. Skiing and jetpack movement rely heavily on concealed conditional behaviors rather than logical and intuitive principles, resulting in a lack of clarity and coherence in gameplay. Additionally, the introduction of "super abilities" fails to capture the strategic depth of their predecessors, worsening the imbalance within the game dynamics.

Visually, Tribes 3 fails to impress, with subpar framerate performance and lackluster artwork, including recycled assets from other games. The overall presentation feels uninspired and dated.

In terms of gameplay features, Tribes 3 lacks essential social interaction tools. In-game chat is notably absent, depriving players of crucial communication channels and undermining teamwork—a crucial aspect of the series.

Moreover, the presence of bots in public matches detracts from the experience, with a significant portion of players being artificial entities. Lack of transparency regarding bot presence exacerbates the issue, leading to frustrating gameplay experiences.

Even in ranked gameplay, Tribes 3 struggles, with lengthy queue times and a lack of visibility into players' rankings, raising concerns about the game's longevity and player engagement.

Compounding these issues is the subpar server performance, evident in glitchy enemy animations and overall instability, further detracting from the gameplay experience.

This review, crafted by ChatGPT, finds resonance with Tribes 3's heavy utilization of AI artwork.

In conclusion, Tribes 3's potential is hindered by its shortcomings. The future of the Tribes IP hinges on a change in direction. The only viable path forward may be for the IP to be acquired by a more capable developer—one with a clear vision and the expertise to honor the legacy of the franchise while innovating for the future.

review:
** Changed my review to negative because they reduced the 16v16 mode to 12v12 due to it being too "chaotic".  Braindead move.  I'm far outside of the refund window now so I'm advising you to stay away.

Polarizing would be the best term to describe this game.  You've got unhappy veterans of the series who wanted to see the strengths of the original Starsiege: Tribes and Tribes 2 put on display - huge, chaotic wars on equally huge maps filled with vehicles with proxy battles taking place all over various parts of the map.  Then you've got the Tribes: Ascend players who wanted more of that same, fast-paced action which highlights style and impressive skillshots.  You've also got to cater any potential newcomers... if any.

As a veteran of T1 and T2, and someone who played T:A for a dozen or so hours, I would say that Tribes 3 fits somewhere in the middle of the two extremes, and very few players are content.  I played a 16 v 16 match on Raindance, a classic map, which closely encapsulated the feel of the original game.  You had a few players dedicated to light offense, flag cappers and those that played as their tailgunner.  Seldom few who entered the base to claim the generators.  Then, an array of players battling it out in the midfield trying to stop any offensive pushes.  In the back, you had your heavies sitting near the flag and providing artillery strikes from afar.  This one game felt great.  I was sold that all of my experiences would mirror this one.

Sadly, they did not.

Most of the games I've played have devolved into 5-minute stompfests where experienced players can 5-cap a game within  mere minutes.  The solution to this, of course, is to play ranked games - but who seriously wants to do that in a Tribes game?  The 16 v 16 mode is fine, but the maps are too small.  The matches end just as they're getting started (no, extending win criteria won't help).  As some who likes to play heavy midfield, I cannot tell you how easy it is to lob mortar fire and rack up "impressive" scores because of how densely-packed some areas of these maps are.  Fish in a barrel. Other times, players just focused on doing random things, like fighting near the absolute edges of the map.  This would be fine, but remember the restrictive player counts.  These aren't large wars we're fighting like in T1 and T2 where half of the team could be faffing off somewhere and the game remain objective, the entire game is framed around lanes like other contemporary shooters of this era with the old school twist of capture the flag. 

The eSports push for this game isn't the way to go.  It didn't work for Ascend, and not sure why their was decision to place such emphasis on ranked modes with Tribes 3.  It really does seem like there was added emphasis of form over function for this game in early development to try to cater to the streamer/eSports crowd.  The market is saturated.  There are only so many consumers of livestreams, and why would anyone wanted to watch Tribes 3 - a game with a peak of around ~800 players - over games they've been invested in for years?  Yeah, it's very impressive to see high speed midair discs delivered in quick succession.  You know what else is impressive?  Delivering a game capable of holding consistent player counts, fostering a community that actively participates in the betterment of the game, and having a development team that is cognizant of real criticism - capable of weeding out the noise from legitimate concerns or suggestions.

Tribes 3 is a game.  Is it awful?  No, it's a very competent early access shooter, but it does very little to stand out in the sea of other competent but unplayed multiplayer shooters.  The direction of the game seemed to be lost somewhere and it's likely too far in development to make any significant changes, such as the addition of vehicles.  If you're a veteran of the series, this game isn't going to scratch that old itch.  If you're a fan of Tribes: Ascend, this is definitely more your speed.  

Some tenable additions of the game that I'd love to see:
 - Dedicated server browser.  Let us hosts our own servers with our own rulesets and administrators.  The best part of the old games was fostering the community -within- the game.  You made friends and rivals (hee-hee) by... playing the game, not by being loud in the official Discord server.  Yes, I'm aware of the old IRC servers, but times were different back then.

- Larger maps, bigger game modes.  What's written on the tin.  I would like to see much larger maps like Skarabrae fought in 32 v 32 fashion.  They don't even have to be recreations of the old maps, just something larger and more engaging.  Make the battles feel more alive.  Make the players other than the flag capturer feel as if they're contributing to the winning efforts of the game.

 - Less focus on "ranked" play.  Remember the OGL?  Yeah, I do.  It was a league created by players of various games before any of this awful forced matchmaking stuff was a requirement for every game.  When you have player counts this small, ranked gaming splinters the community up to the point where your population will begin to fully dwindle.  It's happened to so many other games, learn from their mistakes.

I don't dislike this game, but it's difficult to recommend to anyone over anything else.  I won't get involved with the drama that surrounds major players of the development studio.  There is plenty of that and it's well-documented all over the place, and yes, a lot of it is alarming toward the future of this title.  I would love to remain cautiously optimistic that this game will receive continued support, launch into full, and be something that sticks around for years to come.  I'll probably pop in once or twice a week to sate that nostalgia (what little this game captures), but moreso, that cathartic feeling when you land that delicious midair disc.

Don't fully screw this one up, Prophecy.  In a time where everyone wants to be on the receiving end of a redemption arc, this could be yours.

--
To any potential new players of the game - yeah, dying sucks.  You're going to do a lot of it, so you best get used to it until you get movement and momentum down.  Focus less on just any one stray opponent fluttering about, and work on your motor skills.  Once you get better at movement, you'll learn to read the momentum of others and place better timed shots.  Best way to learn is by playing.

Update (as of 27 June 2024):
Well there it is! The announcement that T3: Rivals will enter "limited support" as Prophecy (thinly veiled Hi-Rez) Games shifts to their next Early Access title "Ultra Strikers". They don't even have the decency to post it on their Twitter, just on their website and a link in the Discord. Here it is for your reading pleasure: 
https://www.tribes3rivals.com/news/tribes-3-player-update

"...but unfortunately neither game had enough success yet to support the studio and can't be our main development focus right now...". [from 2nd to last paragraph on linked page.]

Maybe if you don't put out a half-assed product you'll find better success. Greedily ripping Honor Ball out only to backpedal later sure didn't help, but neither did your aggressive cosmetic pricing for AI-assisted slop, and neither did having 1 game mode that's honestly the most boring (if classic) that you could feed into the current market of high-paced shooters. 

Of course having Erez Goren at the helm is doing you no favors. He really should analyze what makes better Early Access titles actually better instead of fishing around for an easy cash cow with no soul. My condolences to the devs. Supergiant Games is about the same size as Prophecy and they are absolutely [b] destroying [/b] your asses in EA titles with actual effort put into them. 



Updates (as of 7 April 2024): 
- TDM now has a matchmaking queue (4v4 only and has issues with people dc'ing when losing or just crashing out on startup/lobby join) instead of being custom lobby only. It's a start.
- Honorball has been brought back after 3 weeks likely due to stagnant player numbers in an effort to bolster more mainstream appeal. (It was easily the most popular thing during Feb 2024 playtests). SteamDB player count shows it hasn't helped hardly any so far, but further steps like this might yet salvage this game. 
-- I admit I haven't played Ranked, as I have no interest in it, but I believe CTF is still the only ranked matchmaking queue. Maybe they'll add ranked TDM or something later.
- The vastly overpriced and AI-assisted skin DLC got tweaked to be "first 10 wins each day" earn you drops. Not nearly as bad as on launch, and totally unnecessary to enjoy the game. We take wins where we can get them. 
- Still could use more game modes with larger lobby counts (12v12 or even 10v10 Rabbit would be a lot of fun imo) and with them suddenly bringing Honorball back I suppose there's hope they'll deviate from their roadmap some more and add in more modes. Copium, I know, but hey man I'd like Tribes to thrive instead of die ignominiously. 

I'm not sure if I can recommend the game or not, so I'm leaving it as Do Not Recommend for now - there is still more work that needs to be done to bring this game to its actual potential, but there are steps being taken within the last week or so that show that the game isn't a total lost cause right out the gate.

review:
Is this a Tribes game? Sure, you ski and fly on wide open maps and hit things with projectile weapons. Is it a good one? No. Reviews about nostalgia bait are so obviously bologna I'm convinced they're being paid.

If you took Ascend, took a few classes and weapons out, removed several maps, made the remaining maps smaller and less interesting... You would have Tribes 3: Rivals. That's the honest review of this game without talking about the massive red flags surrounding its development and release. Obviously this is in Early Access and there is a development road map so things are subject to change but we're off to a really bad start and fans of the series have good reason to believe it's not getting better.
Now to speak of those red flags, there's Early Access DAY ONE DLC. On a paid game. This isn't something people writing reviews should just tell people to ignore, although it is funny to watch people writing positive reviews add in their copes. No, it doesn't affect gameplay, but it's a sign of predatory marketing which Hi-Rez is known for.  The DLC doesn't even unlock the skins, you're paying $40 USD to get a skin crate for your first win every day. That's their trick to keep player retention high for a game with such a sad amount of substance to it, especially with how many of us were in the playtests and have seen everything the game has on release (other than some menu polish)
Oh yeah, and don't believe this ISN'T a Hi-Rez game. People will try to sway you from this by saying that the devs of this game, Prophecy, are no longer connected to Hi-Rez and are fully independent. That's the official story the devs would like you to believe. Prophecy's CEO is the Ex-CEO  and founding member of Hi-Rez, who remains on their board of directors and still works with them in business capacities regarding Hi-Rez Ventures. The dev studio is also made up of "ex" Hi-Rez devs. The 2019 "split" from Hi-Rez was only in official capacity, they are VERY MUCH still under that umbrella.  All of this information is available online through LinkedIn and the studios' websites.

review:
TLDR: Wait until the game gets out of Early Access and then wait another few months and reevaluate.

Confused by these reviews? Here's a quick primer:

T1 was released in 1998 and well received.
T2 was released in 2001 and generally well received after some dev and community patching.
TAA was released in 2002 and was T2 on the PS2.
TV is what you watch movies and shows on.
TA was released in 2012 by Hi-rez and abandoned a little more than a year after release for a game called SMITE.
...
~10 years pass
...
Starsiege: Raiders (a looter shooter) was demoed at TwitchCon 2022 and then disappeared.
Starsiege: Deadzone (an extraction shooter) seemingly replaced Raiders, but the Steam listing was 'temporarily' removed in Feb 2023. Google it, you can still see the store listing, you just can't buy or wishlist it.
T3 alpha test was announced and opened in Dec 2023.
SMITE 2 was announced in Jan 2024. Interesting pattern here.
T3 early access in Mar 2024.

There appears to have been some form of FPS development going on at Prophecy since at least 2022.

Hi-rez and Prophecy were founded by someone named Erez. Prophecy spun off from Hi-rez at some point and is purportedly independent, but the studios are across the street from each other.

Tribes games, in general, are high skill floor, high skill ceiling games. The Tribes community, in general, is toxic. Not LoL toxic, but close.

Now, on to the game. There are a number of highly polarizing and concerning issues.

First, the game is lacking most of the features that prior Tribes games have had. Features like a server browser and in-game text chat are not currently in, for dubious reasons. There are no community moderation features, like vote kicking, vote skipping, etc. There are other things missing as well, but I need to keep this under a character count. Some things are understandable from a strictly monetary point of view- adding skinning, mapping, modding, and scripting support means that they can't monetize those kind of features.

Others are less so. They seem determined to make this a small, arena style game, like Valorant or CS2, with small maps, lower player counts (at one point as low as 5v5), no vehicles, and no game mode other than CTF. This is counter to some of the fundamentals that are unique to Tribes. Most Tribes players would agree that speed, skiing, jetpacks, and freedom of movement are the hallmarks of what makes Tribes, Tribes. This game does have some of those hallmarks, but they are hamstrung by the box they are trying to fit the game in. Smaller maps mean that speed isn't as important and freedom of movement/jetpacks are restricted. Low player counts means that engagements are few and far between because you can get away fast and there's no defensive or offensive layering. They even had/have a timer that blows you up if you are airborne too long with the flag. No vehicles and no other game modes means there's very little else to do in the game if you get bored with capping/defending.

They've added bots, which is becoming more commonplace in games, but they are unlabeled here and seemingly ever present. Just watch for 'players' that ruin your grab as they walk the flag off the stand or start humping various terrain features. Be ready for a ton of 5-0 cap out games.

They've used generative AI instead of artists to create content for the game. Some assets from TA appear to have been reused in T3 as well.

They added a fun new game mode that was in the release trailer and then decided to remove it completely to monetize it as a separate game. They didn't remove the footage from the trailer until a couple days before early access started.

The game is/was in 'alpha' and is now in 'early access' but according to the CEO, it is largely feature complete and the only things we can expect are bug/balance fixes, a couple new maps, and a couple new weapons. Doesn't really sound 'alpha' or 'early access' to me.

They've locked the two main Tribes skins behind two separate $40 DLCs. Those DLCs can provide daily skins for a year in addition, but only for the first win of the day, so you have to play and win every day, otherwise you miss out on some. The full, undiscounted price that you will pay to unlock some things and then have 365 days of constant play to unlock the rest is $100. Really trying to kick us in the FOMO. There was also a battle pass system (in an alpha test!) so it seems likely that will be added at some point. At least they haven't added virtual currency. Yet.

They switched anti-cheat from EAC to Denuvo during the playtests, but were clueless (or simply careless) enough to not proactively engage with the community before using something with a name as loaded as Denuvo. For the record, Denuvo anti-cheat (not their anti-tamper/DRM) seems to be a well made and flexible option and you shouldn't solely base any purchasing decision (this game or others) just on it being used as the anti-cheat product. I know because I reached out personally to irdeto (maker of Denuvo products) with my concerns after Prophecy made little to no attempt to respond to community concerns about the change. irdeto had a good and constructive response, in sharp contrast with Prophecy's. After I shared irdeto's response with the community on the subreddit and discord, Prophecy then posted that response to their own website without informing, asking, or attributing to me. I posted it publicly and explicitly got the consent of the individual I was interacting at irdeto, so I'm not too worried about it being out there, but given that they didn't inform, ask, or attribute before posting it gives you an idea of the kind of people they are.

On the topic of people, the founder of Hi-rez and Prophecy, Erez, is a large part of the problem. He's out of touch with gamers in general, passive-aggressive, dismissive in his interactions, and seems determined that *he* knows what everyone else wants best, as indicated by the attempts to use the Starsiege IP for a looter shooter that was about 8 years late, an extraction shooter in a saturated market, and a high speed CTF game on small maps where speed is marginalized. He's not like this all the time, but anyone that thin-skinned and closed-minded should not be interacting with any kind of community, especially not one that is already known for being toxic.

So, the reviews are from a toxic fanbase engaging with a toxic CEO over a game in an underused and frequently abandoned IP that hasn't had a new game released in over 10 years. There's a lot of passion and energy and anger. The CEO has a history of starting up games and then abandoning them. This feels like another thing being thrown at the wall and seeing if it sticks. All indicators point to there being little to no support unless the game does really well, but that just makes this a chicken and egg situation.

My recommendation is to wait. This isn't really T3. It's TA with even fewer features. Call it TA -4. The bones, no not even the bones- an x-ray of the bones of a Tribes game are in it, but it's not worth spending any amount of money or time at the moment. Wait for it to emerge from early access see what kind of game they wind up calling complete.

Updating my review after 20ish hours

- As i said matchamking is a BS system. In a game like tribes you want a server list. 
A matchmaking system only connect the playerbase. A SERVER LIST creates COMMUNITIES. In a game like tribes you want communities, because communities are what keep the game alive.
The devs are so focused on pushing this idea of ​​Esports, in the hope of creating this "make or break" online sensation, like LoL and Overwatch have been, that they don't see these things. So they promote this 7vs7 ranked queue, when the best thing on tribes were the clan vs clan scrimages.
20+ years ago you had 50 vs 50 maps and big clan scrimmages. 20+ years later in the future, with technology several times higher you have 3/4 less of the game and a 7v7 ranked queue. lol ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

- It's a game that unfortunately lacks those elements that made up the first 2 tribes. 
But if we take even just Ascend as a reference it seems like a fairly diluted version.

So you don't have any sort of base gameplay, because bases are mostly 2 rooms, you don't have inventory stations and only engineers can setup one turret, a turret which among other things, has: 
1) a high fire rate
2) good and consistent dps 
3) follows the target like a heat-seeking missile
4) will despawn if the engineer is killed

D-setters were a HUGE part of the game and fortifying a base was an additional mechanic that enriched the game.

- There are no vehicles. You don't need vehicles when you have relatively small maps. Which among other things are maps that were not designed with the idea of ​​an FPS in mind, but are maps built around the skiing mechanic.

- While skiing on T3 is much more enjoyable than TA (at least to my taste) Hirez needs to understand that skiing has NEVER been the ONLY WAY to get around on TRIBES.
You DIDNT'T build speed by skiing, you needed skiing to MAINTAIN the boost you had generated using other mechanics (disk boosting, rocket boosting, nade boosting, spamming jumps on a slope...)
So walking, using the jetpack and the various vehicles had their own importance.

On T3 the jetpacks are not well thought out in relation to the type of armor you are using.
Especially in light armor: you have little flight time with very high energy consumption: damn sometimes from the ground you can't even get to the flag stand

- Hi Rez managed to remove useful functions and many of those cool mechanics that made your jaw drop when others did them to you, but once you learned how to do them, you had HUGE satisfaction:
1) mine + disk, combo. Very useful for oneshotting a light armor or for doing greater damage to a heavy armor (now only heavies can deploy mines,typically around the flag)
2) being able to throw grenades at anytime (during other animations,while shooting...) which allowed you to use nade boosting in the air. (now you either shoot or throw a grenade)
3) the suicide button. Which was extremely useful for making certain flag passes and for quickly respawning, now it's been replaced with "stay still for 10 seconds to respawn" and you can't even respawn if you're flying, you have to touch the ground.
4) Hirez added a self-destruction mechanic if you fly too long with the flag. At this point, take out the jetpacks. 
What's the point of having jetpacks and all that "building momentum" mechanics if I can't use the propulsion I built to fly? After 8 seconds of being in the air, you have to land and ski otherwise you die.
I have the flag and there are 5 or 6 chasing me, I have to: 
a) control the momentum x to ski when I'm on a slope and the jetpack when I'm uphill, 
b) but dont you dare use the jetpack too much because otherwise you explode
c) avoid chainguns, mortars, disks and that STUPID "drop the flag cos i can't MA for shits" granade (the dev introducing that nade into tribes is an idiot)
d) every 8 seconds I am forced to make myself even more vulnerable because I have to ski on the ground to reset the countdown
WHY?
5) Loadout: This is my personal problem. I would like to have the ability to create a loadout with only 2 weapons. And i can't

-  The first to reach 5 points wins.
But why?!
For starters, they use a matchmaking system, so you have a high chance of joining a team that is losing 4 to 1, and with a system like this, a comeback is difficult.
And then you don't even enjoy it, all it takes is 1 good capper and that map is over in a flash.
Was setting the games in such a way that you have 20 minutes per map and at the end of the 20 minutes the team with the most points wins, too much mainstream?

- BOTS: remove bots or at least make them recognizable. I've already ended up in more than one lobby where I was the only living person.
Take away the stupid matchmaking, replace it with a server list and let me join those 2 servers with people if the game population is scarce. You don't have to put me in a matchmaking with fucking bots with plausible names to pass them off as real players: you're wasting my time.
I can tolerate a game having a small playerbase, or a game that isn't successful but still enjoyable to play. But the moment you try to decieve me... here is where I get pissed off .

(Edit)

The more I play this "REMAKE" and realize how pidgin holed I am into nothing but fly by wire CTF or a million people and bots  in a tiny area dueling, the less I hop on. So much so that now I've even uninstalled it as this was a cash grab of a joke by hi-rez aka Erza or whatever they are.

The T1 community is still going strong, they have a chat and play often which you should look into, check discord. You will see how terrible this new title is after that!

I just wish we could get a true remake of T1, still hoping this one grows into that but having talked with others the CEO already blew up in discord and said its not happening and he wants to drop the project and sell it off because of the consumers criticizing his choices on a title that holds die hard fans. Such as AI generated skins, which are behind a pay wall far more expensive then the title, removing game play types, etc.

With it stripped down and altered so much its lost that T1 or even T2 game play, and the only point in remaking a game is to build upon it, not just display its head for shock value and money.

This project gives off the "The CEO didn't listen to anyone on design, rushed dev's, and pushed it out early for $" to it.

Even the less popular T2 with Sierra running it was far better, and I didn't really like T2, I still have my entire original contents of Tribes 1 box set, and threw out T2.


So many people are new to tribes and have no idea what the game really was, most of us are APPAULLED BY THIS MOCKERY and refuse to support it UNLESS its changed to be what it should have in the first place. 




First and foremost....THIS IS STILL IN ALPHA, that being said expect to have things you wish to see built upon because this is a far from finished product. I have some things I will list that I really enjoy, some things I do not enjoy, and things I wish to see worked into the game to give it that OG T1 and T2 feel. 


Positives I can list off the top of my head:

1. The skiing, and overall mechanics of game play is about on par for what I expected, I did however change the key mapping and right away back to my T1 setup and increased the mouse sensitivity and ADS.

2. Graphics are pretty nice, but not overdone, so no causing loss of frame rate, or crashes for me, etc.

3. I actually really enjoy the weapon selection thus far, as well as the fact your not limited to only 3 armor types, but have classes within the 3 armor types. 


Some dislikes:

1. You have so many bots in a match its frustrating to play at times, I would rather play with a 10v10 being short some people and it be a 8v10 losing all the bots. Bots serve a purpose, such as when you simply cant get enough people, or for training, etc. I dislike all the bots, and there are LOTS!

2. The start of each round, hangs up for me, and that's frustrating. By the time I get to move I have people ahead of me and I'm trying to fly past and go cap a flag. 

3. As much as its true to the selection of most weapons, some need improved upon, I tried hitting people with the sniper rifle as I would have with a laser rifle in a T1 match......nope. It sucks, and I instead went to heavy with a mortar. Also you can only zoom in a single time, making the rifle nearly useless across most maps.
Additionally there is the issue of some things still missing "and I hope they are added in" such as a plasma gun, energy pack, ammo pack, so on. I don't care for a "blink" teleport pack, or a jet boost pack that drains ALL of my energy leaving me unable to use my jets when escaping with a flag. Also the boost pack is unusable after you grab the flag, so you have to time your ski and boost just as you head to grab the flag. Just give me an energy pack, its what 90% of 
us ran.

4.The concept that I must run over a health ball someplace across the map randomly instead of having a med kit i can use as needed and then I need to replenish it, is terrible.

Things that I would like to see/improvements:


1. Most of all, bigger maps and more types of play, after six rounds of CTF that end after 5 captures I was bored and stopped playing for awhile.

2. I understand you need to fund the project and pay the devs and all other departments, but the fact we cant have a skin to represent our own tribe, our group of people......   You could make a player ran tribe application, that allows you to submit a few number of skins for approval to be payed for the ability to insert them into the, and only used by those within the tribe. Make it an in game ability to "unlock" that tribes custom skins for use when the leaders have accepted them into the group. This was a similar concept to what Elite Dangerous did for their player made factions, which are inserted into the background simulation, I put over 2k hours into that game in less then my first year.....and have 6+ accounts. I feel limiting us to such a serious extent is harmful to the concept of the game, its a group of tight knit confederacies flying across the galaxy and battling it out for supremacy. 

3. More then 16v16.....come on..l...arge bases, underground/large underground bases, high floating air bases, and large bases you have to force into with real team work, as well as defend. Not just a fly and ski by shot across the map CTF. We want different modes of play, challenges, the ability to be more creative and work together in multiple aspects of play, across multiple types of maps.

4.Vehicles, T1, T2, TV.....vehicles.....sure you new kids on the block might not know what your missing from the old titles.....but we do and we want you to experience how much more can be brought to this game.

5. This brings me to a large point that I'm sad about, everything is now locked away and only a dev can do anything. No map editor for custom crazy maps, you wont have a map that's so large and things that you can interact with now. No skeet shooting range where you can blow up power armor dummy's, duel whilst bouncing from tiny piller to tiny piller so high in the air a fall is certain death. No built in IRC chat where you can host a room specific to your tribe, get news on matches and upcoming game patches/content via the TSN room "Tribes Shoutcast Network". No talking to Bytor and his lovable IRC helper, Shazbot. You cant make your own reticle and toss that BMP. file into the folder and have a reticle that works better for YOU, your stuck with whatever a dev decides. So much of the custom art for weapon and armor skins will never exist because skins are a pay wall, you cannot create your tribes personal skin, or just be creative. You will never see custom dope sound packs from players for players "THIS IS MY BOOM STICK!" either because of this. I don't think they will ever give us the freedom to build upon this game, to make it into what the community built together with T1. 



All in all I have my fingers, toes, heck, I'd cross things I cant mention on here.....that they don't botch this title and as I continue to watch the alpha develop, I will be looking for a lot of these things. I can tell you now, that it needs more content, and its missing a lot of the freedom that made the groups of tribes within the game, so fun.

I played a lot of the early beta test, and I thought "Wow, I really really like tribes, tribes ascend was cool but then Hi-Rez killed it with awful decision/monetization/balancing choices. I sure hope this new tribes game will learn from those mistakes." Now here we are, "early access" release and it's like a skim skim milk version of tribes ascend. It's still Hi-Rez, I don't care if they say "Prophecy Games", Erez is in charge and yet again he made a million terrible choices to ruin the chances of tribes coming back as a fun series. Behold:

Fun new game mode? Cut honorball out of the game and attempt to release it as a separate game to money grub even harder. 
Tribe Skins? That default game feature for the last 4 tribes games where you got to rep with cool skins per team like Diamond Sword and Blood eagle? How about those awesome per class skins that T:A had to add that extra style and uniqueness for the player? Sorry consumer, those are paid DLC now. 
Want to play with real people? Sorry IDIOT, here's bots in every casual match. They even went the extra mile and tried to name the bots psuedo-player names so people would have a harder time figuring out if it was a real player or not.
Art team? How about we touch up some AI generated slop. That's like art right? I don't even feel like i'm playing a real tribes game. It's sterile, milquetoast, no personality. You had all of the announcer voice lines and VGS from Ascend and yet refuse to use any of it. The maps have 0 intrigue, all of that amazing art over tribes history gets ignored in favor of the blandest possible UE assets.
Want to text chat? lol. lmao even. How dare you even ask?
All of the QoL features from previous games are still missing, tons of weapons from past titles,  vehicles shown in the initial preview now mysteriously gone, no melee attack, missing classes, missing perks, no rearm stations, just little glowing health nuggets for you to slow down and grab, we still have flag drag, a 200 MPH speed cap, all of the feedback from the beta tests clearly fell on deaf ears.
It's sad that tribes has to be owned by the worst possible person. Erez, if you're reading this there's a reason almost every single one of your games has failed miserably after you manage to squeeze every ounce of goodwill out of it. You truly have no idea what a fun good video game looks like, and now I get to watch you kick tribe's mangled corpse around for a little longer while you try and justify your "new" honorball title.
Oh yeah, and they even partnered with a crypto scam as well during the beta. Completely forgot lmao
