review:
Edit Sept 23, 2024:  Tribes 3 is really cool, and I initially gave it a positive review since everybody was already sh*ting all over it's early iterations and I wanted to see it succeed.  But at this point, it ultimately still feels like a glorified demo.  It has a ton of potential and the devs clearly worked their as*es off, but the guy in charge at Prophecy already had the team pull the plug on development.  He is extremely immature, angry, reactive, and has lashed out at the community instead of embracing them or taking their criticism to heart.  He can never seem to figure out what game he wants the team to work on, and seems to be desperately looking to chase his own "Fortnite," infinite money glitch, so this game was abandoned for another.  

Instead of refunding players after ending support for the initial release, or trying to rescue the remaining possibility of a player base by making the game free to play, they offered up discount codes for cosmetics in their future games to make up for support being cut; one of those games already being abandoned as well.  

I can't recommend purchasing any games from Prophecy or anything Erez has anything to do with if you have any expectations for support to last longer than 6 months at a time.  The only hope now is to pass Tribes 3 onto the community with mapping and modding tools so they can take it from here, as has been done with the rest of the Tribes franchise. 

If you want to play the classic Tribes games, they are all available as freeware and have small but active communities.  If you've never played a Tribes game before, I highly recommend playing the Tribes Vengeance single player campaign as a tutorial.  

I may change this review back to positive if there's another update down the road, or if there are mapping and modding tools made available, but I highly doubt that's going to happen.  

_________________

Original review:  

DISCLAIMER:  As of launch, March 12th 2024, the first 5 matches you play will be against bots.  After that you will enter the main player queue.  No, you are not crazy, and the game is not a desert of bots.  This has confused a lot of new players since according to the discord, Prophecy believes they don't need to say anything about the bots, so I'm passing this knowledge onto you to avoid confusion.  

I'm giving this a thumbs up based on how hard the devs worked on this game.  I feel through alpha testing they really worked hard on making this work as best as they could.  Yeah the leadership at Prophecy has come under harsh criticism, but the devs themselves earned my small handful of dollerydoos.  

This is absolutely a Tribes game, but it's set from the ground up to be friendly to new players.  Yes it lacks the features of the average Tribes game, but it solves the biggest problems of past Tribes games and player retention by making movement much more efficient and projectile inheritance adjustable.  

Yes, they added in micro-transactions.  No, you don't have to buy them.  I just bought the $17.99 version and I'm content with what we have so far, and as an early access title I'm quite impressed.  

At the end of the day, if T3 gets nothing but negative reviews then hi-rez-phecy won't be adding more fixes or content.  I say give it a chance!

review:
Edit 11/24: It shouldn't be legal for this game to still be on sale with $80 of DLC.

This game has been super rushed out, under baked, with bare bones game modes and leadership that doesn't seem to be in this game for the long run.

I've put about 150 hours into this game playing nearly every play test since testing started in early December, was on a winning tournament team, and I've played a few of the older tribes games but not religiously so I've been adjacent to this community for awhile.

I've been excited for a new Tribes game for a few years now feeling the nostalgia of playing Ascend ten years ago. So I'm very excited for a new Tribes and honestly want to see this game become something. These play tests have felt very good and introduced a new game mode called Honorball that was very, very good and has the potential to bring a lot of new players to the game. I haven't even cared much for the fact that allot of things from previous games weren't making a return. The new guy in charge of developing this game has basically said that they have absolutely no intention of bringing back old, expected features, like 32v32 and vehicles.

But issues keep coming up and it's getting very hard to defend this game even if I desire to do so. First that big game mode that everyone is exited about? It's disappeared. Rumor had it that it would be becoming an entirely separate game, but the community, really did not want that. So where did it go? It wasn't a particularity buggy game mode or super unbalanced. It actually felt really good. Are we going to have to spend another $20 to play Honorball as a separate game?

There is also a deathmatch game mode, but it is hidden away in custom lobbies, no quick play, and there was a mercenary/kill confirmed kind of gamemode that was tested but didn't make it to early access.

So, the game has released with only one game mode, CTF, and personally it's what I want to play the most, but I know that this game mode has a high skill cap and often new players really don't like it.

Next, the last couple of play tests have absolutely been infested with bots to fill out match sizes. This games biggest game mode is 16v16 and they are struggling to fill those. I haven't played since release but it sounds like that is still a problem and I'll soon go check it out for myself.

The last play test they quietly introduced AI art for kill cam banners and player Icons. #1 I don't understand why modern games want to make their own Icons and stuff when they can just let players use their steam/xbox/whatever Icons. This is already just silly to not let people bring their own player icons. #2 I simply can't in good faith support stuff with AI art in it. And #3 the devs initially claimed that this art would be a placeholder and was traced over (which is not what it looks like). Quickly the head of the company went to discord to joke on people complaining about the AI generated art and the devs refused to elaborate if this art was actually temporary or if it would be removed for the early access release. It was not. On their road map they claim they'll be doing another art update during March. So hopefully in a month it'll be gone. As a side note, the winning teams of the draft tournament got AI generated looking trophies for player Icons. Thanks I guess.

Finally is the very cool decision to open this early access game with $80 of micro transactions that puts a paywall behind basic skins for the two main factions in Tribes (Diamond Swords and Blood Eagles). The best analogue that I can think up for this is if a new Halo was released, and you could only play as a UNSC Marine if you bought the base game. If you wanted to play as a Spartan, that is a $40 DLC. And if you wanted to play as an elite, that is a SEPARATE $40 DLC. I've seen a lot of people trying to defend this decision on Discord and I seriously cannot understand how people can't see this as any thing other than a cash grab on the border of becoming a straight up scam...

I really do hope this game can become a successful part of the tribes franchise with a healthy modern competitive scene, but from what I've seen from the leadership and monetization of this game, it's dangerously close to just being a paycheck for some company. I've been religiously recommending this game to my friends who I know have been into games like titanfall, and stuff like valorant and overwatch's competitive scenes. And I have had pretty positive responses. But these last play tests, and this early access release, have me worried that I'm humiliating myself by promoting this game.



Oh also I forgot about the orbital strike thing. Why was that even conceived and put into the game? It just punishes people for capping certain kinds of routes. Like on Katabatic, you can hit a fast right to left or back to front route were you can just dunk the flag from the opposing flag stand. Why would you want to just straight up be punished for being able to pull that off? Seems like good, positive game design. It has no real benefits to chasers and even as a chaser seeing a carrier get hit with it is just real silly and meaningless.

P.S. Just an update that maybe a little petty, but I would like to point out that the executive head of this game, Erez, left the discord server for Tribes 3 on it's launch day after being fairly active in that community throughout most of play testing. kinda sus, but also he was not doing a good job at promoting or providing players with confidence in his game.

Edit: Prophecy has opened up testing for a new game. 

The empty and vague road map the devs released for Tribes 3 claimed there would be a new map in April. It's May, with no communication about said map. No other solid items are on that road map. Considering how low player counts are and considering this companies owners history with abandoning games and disdain towards Tribes fans, I say it'll be safe to assume Tribes 3 wont be getting another major update. Erez has found a new product full of asset flips (and certainly ai generated trash) to initially make some launch money with and abandon to slowly rot with time. Almost all Hi-Rez products had similar fates, and Prophecy will continue the tradition.

There's a dedicated competitive community that I'm kinda apart of. I'm glad it exists.

review:
It feels like the ghost of Tribes, not a successor. You boot the game, finish the tutorial, and then look at what could easily be a mobile game. Details are sparse, quality sparser, and you're immediately greeted by your "Daily" panel that instructs you to buy a 40$ dlc. There is nothing to unlock, no skins to gain, and no weapons to earn. There is nothing but the gameplay unless you pay MORE money. This game is, without a doubt, modeled after F2P games. It looks empty and soulless. 

Then you play it, and remember exactly why you even hazarded the 20$ to try it. It's fun, it's fast, and man it feels great when you snipe people mid air with the spinfusor. But then you play another match, then another, and the luster wears thin. This is not the Tribes you once loved and adored; poured thousands of hours into and woke up early to play just one more match before leaving the house. It's all bitesized and shallow. Everything is there where it should be, yet the spark is lacking to ignite what should have been an inferno of nostalgic joy. 

There's something so viscerally disgusting about charging 20$ for a game that has 80$ of DLC day 1 into Early Access. It makes my skin crawl. The cherry on top is that you don't even actually get your rewards after purchase, but instead must win day after day to slowly unlock things. You are rationed your 40$ treats. I could almost see it if it were setup to where all the DLC + game would be 60$. I wouldn't like it, but I could see it, right? But that's not the case. If you want EVERYTHING in this game, it's 100$. A game modeled after a F2P game. If there were at least SOME skins to unlock for free, sure. You paid for the game, after all. But no. 

There's nothing. 

This is, in a word, soulless. Empty. A shell of what it should, could, or would have been given a different guiding hand. What a shame.

review:
[h1]Too Many Red Flags For Me.[/h1]


After the history with T:A and the dev team going somewhat indie, I really want to support them and give this game a chance. However, I cannot in good conscience recommend the game at this time as there are too many red flags to warrant a $20 purchase.



These choices are as follows:

- The game is extremely barebones. CTF is the only gamemode and there are no vehicles and a very limited amount of utility weapons. While skiing around is fun and the gamemode is very solid, it can get boring quick. If Prophecy wants to innovate with this franchise, they are doing it wrong.

- While there are two new maps coming and A whole new weapon in April, the roadmap for this game does not say anything about adding new features such as new gamemodes, vehicles, or utility weapons. For the most part, it seems like what you see is what you get on v1.0. It is very disheartening to know that all of the fun features that were in T1, T2, or T:A will not be present on release day, and that a game that was released in the 90s on day one will feature more content than one released now.

- AI-generated content for cosmetics and assets. While it is mostly used for reference, it is dull and lifeless. I don't really look forward to getting a new banner when it looks ugly and messy.

- There are a ton of predatory design philosophies that are taken from games like Fortnite. There is of course the $60 price tag for the cosmetic "Ultimate Edition", but one design choice is to have players dropped in a match with bots for their first few rounds without telling them. That way they are not discouraged, can frag some people, and keep playing. This is an awful decision because it only keep players around short-term. They will be shocked to find their way of playing does not work in real matches, and will die constantly before winning again. This will make or break many players, and will frustrate veterans that are tricked into playing against robots rather than real people.

- Denuvo Anti-cheat required to activate the game, which has a history of causing performance issues as well as being consumer unfriendly by acting as DRM in addition to Steam. It is still up to debate whether Denuvo causes major performance issues (I have not seen any yet). Regardless, Prophecy Games placed Denuvo in their game right before Early Access without prior knowledge or feedback from players.



If you are not convinced and would purchase this game, I hope you enjoy. I had requested a refund and will be enjoying the original Starseige: Tribes.



Sidenote: I have played this game more often in beta playtests, about 15 hours or so. The hours played currently do not reflect how often I have played this game. Not much has changed since the playtests as of this moment.

review:
This is a long review, but the tl;dr is don't waste your money or your time. No matter what you're looking out of tribes, this ain't it. This will barely even scratch the itch, and there are much better ways to relive your glory days of Tribes than dropping money on this game that's going to be dead in a month or two.

Also most players you meet in-game are going to be bots that the game doesn't tell you are bots.

Don't let the time fool you. I've played this game for about 20 hours between the playtest and demo.

UPDATE: People think I want this game to fail. But this review is more about the fact that the game is destined to fail. And I think it's really scummy to pretend that if enough people send their thoughts and prayers (and cash), they can change the reality.

---

Tribes is a story about a dev team catching lightning in a bottle in 1998, and then a collection of stories of people who feel the need to change every parameter until the game is made in their own image, by which point it's become a can of shit that gives you a static shock when you try to open it. This is Story #10 in that long-running series.

The story of Tribes 3 Rivals starts on a single premise: it would have been "easy" for them to just make Tribes Ascend 2 instead. And it probably would've sold pretty well. As I understand it, Tribes Ascend still had an active community up to making a severe balance change "Out of the Blue" and most people who had stuck with the game to that point basically just wanted the old version of the game back. It wouldn't have been my kind of Tribes, but it would've at least been the kind of game where I can go in and shoot at people for a few hours a week. I might have paid like $10 for that?

Instead, they tried to take the "hard" route, making an e-sports Tribes CTF game. A game where you zip around at 200mph, grabbing flags off the stands while making epic stops on people trying to take your flag. High speed, high octane gameplay where the elite players always seem to know where they should position themselves. So here's the problem. If Hi-Rez Studios (or whatever they call themselves now) made their e-sports CTF game perfectly, would it even be successful in this day and age? What do you do to make it successful? How do you actually sell people on the idea? Well, they haven't figured that out either. Buying up a bunch of sponsored streams isn't going to cut it, because most players will take one look at it and decide it's way too hard to get into, no matter how easy they try to make every aspect of the game. Ironically, even the veteran players they're trying to court need to be convinced to buy into the game, because they all have their own Tribes games to play. It would take a very good case to get them to abandon literal decades of experience on their respective games to pick up something that plays completely differently.

Of course it didn't even matter, because Hi-Rez's new version of e-sports Tribes CTF is garbage. Even the veterans to which they tried to appeal instantly knew something was wrong with this game when Hi-Rez was insistent on making it a 5v5. That tiny player count is not a Tribes game most veterans play on purpose; it's a sideshow meant to please people in the dying days of a Tribes game when you can no longer manage to fill a server. While they were eventually argued up to 7v7 for their e-sports mode over the course of the playtest, Hi-Rez has brought this level of ignorance to literally every aspect of the game, and has been much less willing to budge on any other decision they've made.

You can read lots of reviews about this game and see hundreds upon hundreds of the game's problems, and you should quickly realize to stay the hell away. But in the interest of adding actual content to this review, here's a short list:
- The original button binds are completely different from any Tribes game before it for basically no reason
- Projectiles move way too fast and remove most of the precision that the series is known for in favor of "twitch" combat
- Most of the maps just have a hundred tiny fucking bumps instead of big hills. Again. This developer is fucking obsessed with flat levels that have random bumps here and there.
- You can go way too fast off a tiny fucking bump and/or the game's "Go Fast" button, almost hitting your armor's built-in speed limits with little effort
- Players can literally teleport through the flag to grab it without ever touching the stand, making defense even more impossible for newer players
- There is no in-game chat, just the canned chat messages (VGS)
- They make heavy balance changes on a weekly basis and you can't keep anything straight from one week to the next
- There is a plan to remove every non-CTF gametype from the game and try to sell each one as a different game
- As a live service game, there are no dedicated servers, no way to do any modding of the game, etc.
- They ban people from their Discord for pointing out any of these issues and the fact that they stopped taking feedback a very long time ago

Some of this might seem like nitpicking. But the most important thing to note is that player turnover is so bad in this game that, even when the game was a free playtest, they had to add bots to fill out servers. When people called them out and said they would rather those slots be empty, they went all-in on obfuscating the bots, removing every UI element that showed you they were bots, changing their names to make them look like names players would actually use. But even when they have names like dildojackhammer, the bots are blatantly obvious, from the way they run into walls and stay there, to the way they suddenly become crack shots if you somehow enter their field of vision, to the way they just suddenly disappear in the middle of combat when someone new joins the game. It makes sense they would hide this, because if all you want out of Tribes is to fight bots so you can get a feel for the series (or relive past glory without all the work), some subsection of Tribes 2 or Vengeance definitely has you covered.

And now, a game that couldn't get enough players to fill servers when it was free... will cost money out of your pocket. Are you sure you want to pull that trigger? And will the developer continue to support it after they have your money? Did I mention that the developer's last game (Starsiege: Deadzone) was shut down after a few months when it didn't get the kind of numbers they were looking for? And that this game's free demo didn't even reach a THIRD of that game's peak? And they're already looking forward to making their next game instead of bothering to support this one? And that this "next game" was originally a side mode in this game's playtest until they realized they weren't going to break even on this game?

Dynamix had three years with the Tribes series, and made two unforgettable games which are still being played, with a modding scene that extended them far beyond what the developers ever intended. Even when these games were new and the skill level of the average player was low, people still understood how special these games were. Since these lofty peaks, the Tribes series has been passed around and treated like garbage, with mediocre games entering and leaving the public consciousness within months. Hi-Rez Studios has held onto the Tribes license for over a decade, and it's become blatantly obvious that their best days are behind them (if they ever had "best days" to begin with). This game is not fun, and it is not satisfying to play. If the fat lady were singing any harder than she is right now, the glass house this game was cast from would instantly shatter.

Do not give them any more of your time. Do not give them any more of your money. Do not continue this abusive relationship. Tribes is little more than a fleeting memory, a zombie shambling on in a world where it should've been laid to rest somewhere between 10 to 20 years ago, when the ideas ran out.

review:
I love Chernobylite, I 100% the first game, beat it several times, studied the entire story, fell in love with the characters, custom made a physical version of the OST, and created many things inspired off it. I loved it so much that multiple of my friends fell in love with it too from watching me play or hearing me talk about it for months. 

When I heard there was a second game coming out and that it would be co-op, me and my friend immediately wishlisted it. I got the game on release day and played the prologue, but ultimately waited for him to also get the game. He did recently, and so we started playing it.

Booting it up was no problem, although i did experience several GPU failures while trying to get past the first fighting area on the ship. The animations are oddly smooth and uncanny, the mouth visemes look like the characters are overexaggerating their speech, the alpha mapping looks like static. These aren't massive problems, but some things really broke the immersion and feel of the game, like: The map being unrealistic to the Zone, and not just something being moved a little ways away, but some buildings entirely in the wrong places even though the first game prided itself on being so accurate, it feels like a far cry from what it was. The NPCs talk like robots, pronouncing character names wrong, the most notable that I've encountered is Tarakan being pronounced "tear-a-can"?? The voices feel off too, that is NOT what Black Stalker sounded like in the first game. The combat isn't horrible, but it feels sometimes like the game is way too easy and then way too hard. The first boss atop of Prip'yat hospital was really buggy and could 2 shot me, but a gang of raiders I could head shot without them even getting to aggro onto me? The melee combat feels wonky too, sometimes enemies deal inconsistent damage, or I get stun locked by 5 projectiles and 2 Chernohosts ganging on me. The Zone doesn't feel as correct as the first game. I enjoy the open world aspect, but it could definitely be made better with missions or side missions or random events occuring as you run from point A to point B. The story is completely lost on me, I don't really understand anything going on, I have no attachment to any of the characters, they feel shoe-horned, not introduced.

To become friends with Sashko, Mikhail, Tarakan, Olga, and even partially Olivier, you had to earn it. You did missions that would help them, you would talk to them directly and learn about them, they would teach you, help you, do more than just sit at base. The base felt like a home, we all had to put in our own work and together get the materials to survive. Now, I talk to Sonya, she doesn't face me while talking to me, then I get given a task 1000 meters away, so I run there, do it, run back, and mission complete. I also don't understand why I can't just go do something, why do I have to talk to Black Stalker for something? Why is Black Stalker called that in the tablet if we only know him as Igor? Why do people say "ku-mu-nuck" instead of how it should be pronounced naturally? 

I have many opinions and views on this game, it works better on its own, not as a sequel. It feels like Fallout 4 instead of Metro or STALKER, like the original game. It feels like the devs tried to do too much extra and lost its roots in the process. I pray to god the devs read this and this becomes a No Man's Sky scenario: horrible launch, amazing a few years later. If I could help the development process, I would. I just hope it returns to a survival game with proper story and emotional attachment instead of a glorified Fallout.

I don't recommend it right now, although down the line it may be better to play.

自从用上RPG，BOSS的设计便失去了应有的挑战性与平衡性。当前游戏在优化方面存在明显不足，例如显卡负载过高、模型定位异常、骨骼动画疑似非原创、过场动画交互失效等问题频发。此外，某些软体怪物的建模质量粗糙，视觉效果甚至不及上世纪90年代的作品。在技术飞速发展的2025年，建议相关开发团队重视美术资源与引擎技术的升级，以提升整体游戏品质。

Since the adoption of RPGS, the design of bosses has lost its due challenge and balance. The current game has obvious deficiencies in optimization, such as frequent problems like excessive graphics card load, abnormal model positioning, suspected non-original skeletal animations, and ineffective cutscene interaction. Furthermore, the modeling quality of some soft monsters is rough, and the visual effects are even inferior to those of works from the 1990s. In the year 2025, when technology is advancing at a rapid pace, it is recommended that relevant development teams attach importance to the upgrading of art resources and engine technology to enhance the overall quality of the game.

review:
The game clearly has a lot things going on and you can understand that a great potential is there but it suffers in aspects that are somewhat common both in AAA titles and indie as well.

1. No clear vision of what the game wants to be. Developers say that this is not Stalker and it aims to be a survival horror with base building and that is respectable. Well frankly i cant feel any horror or special atmosphere since the game feels more like a Simcity in exclusion zone with the bonus that you can see your world from first or third pov camera. Too much expanded base building, i mean come on i even set up electrical lanes for the base what more can i say? Add a water pipe system and you got Simcity there. Feels like it is there to make the game feel more content rich, something like Assassins Creed with the countless brain dead side quests to i dont know collect 123123 feathers from the building roofs for the achievement or to be 100% in your game completion bar.

2. Optimization is really bad like in the majority of UE5 games, Stalker 2 included while the graphical outcome is something that doesnt justify this at all. It is really disappointing to see things like these and from the other hand you play free mods like Improved Weapons Pack OR Anomaly Custom and see projects like IX Ray and Open Xray which have improved a 20y old graphical engine offering respectable graphics with good performance and most important of all IMMERSION.

3. Gunplay and melee combat feel really strange. Melee weapons feel like World of Warcraft which means that you hit with a bludgeon weapon and the whole feeling of you hitting and the enemy receive the hit is like i dont know Minecraft. Gunplay is even worse. Taking the example of Improved Weapon Pack modpack for Stalker i shoot with the shotgun and MAN it feels that i actually shoot with a shotgun. Shooting with a shotgun or AK here feels like shooting Nerf from Temu.

The ingredients are here for a really good game in the Exclusion Zone but right now even after the 5th August big patch i would advice people to wait for the final product OR 1 year later in the EA.

Not recommended.

review:
oh I've mixed feelings on this.... but I'm thumbing it up.

For early access it's alright and it shows a lot of promise. I'm not captivated or blown away - but I didn't bounce of it as much as I expected. Performance started out as acceptable with the occasional bottleneck in the open world (I'm assuming the game is loading in assets and might be happier on an SSD?) although it seemed to get worse the further I progressed in the game. 

In terms of story the idea of factions trapped under a Chernobyllite dome duking it out with mutants works for me and I'm easily won over by open worlds. Exploration, surviving and finding your way is fun. Or at least it should be. 

There's a lot here I'm unsure about.  I haven't put a lot of hours into the game - so I may have missed things somewhere. But so far...

There doesn't seem to be a lot to do outside of missions. The original gave you a map with a specific objective (retrieve ammo, meds, whatever) with the option to pick up resources on the way. With a larger map there's the invitation to explore and players need to be rewarded for going off the beaten track. An open world which is just a backdrop to trundle between story missions is wasted. We need to be able to rummage around and discover things for ourselves. Add to that I've come across the occasional scrap between mutants and humans - I'm guessing these are are scripted (which is fine)- but I'd like to discover characters outside the main story somewhere in the Zone (perhaps occasionally giving me something to do which may annoy, or woo, a faction along with a reward). And there's many a building that *looks* interesting from the outside - and that's as far as it goes, because once it you get closer you find the entrances boarded up.

This is a lot more combat heavy. The original impressed that combat was something best to be avoided, or low key and tactical.  This fully embraces slugging it out in melee and firefights, and it's easy to run into a mob of chernobylite riddled mutants and get into a tussle. The inclusion of 'bullet sponge' enemies (thankfully going to be addressed) was a wrong move and contributed to much frustration in the early game - having to take one down for things to open up. There is a tension... I miss the slower pace of the original where you felt vulnerable in the face of opposition. EZ throws plenty of mutants at you, but then the game starts to feel a bit too hack & slash (or point & shoot). It becomes less of a tense encounter, which if to do the original justice - is how it should feel, and more of hacking/gunning through a mob of enemies to get to your objective.  

I'm intrigued by the RPG elements, winning over faction members to develop specific skills, watching relationships change based on decisions made during missions and having skill checks in the open world. From what I've seen so far this looks promising (although watching your character attempt a skill, and using a probability mechanic to determine success rather than having it blocked off altogether if your stat isn't high enough would work better for me).  

There isn't the sense of battling "against the Zone" - so improved survival mechanics will be welcome. At the moment I'm collecting resources to expand my base - in the original I was able to decide who ate, who ate less, and who went to bed hungry whilst being worried about who would up sticks and simply walk out on me.  

For the atmosphere - again I'm mixed. The original had the sense of weirdness "breaking in", here it's taken everything over with some weird Chernoyblite winged beastie encountered in the first area of the game. This is tough-- it changes the tone but in the same vein I don't think it would have worked to have remade the first game (a'la Stalker). It's less a continuation of the story, more of a development of the concept... what would happen if Chernobyilite was harnessed on a commercial scale? It's taking some time to grow on me.

On the picky side, I'm not won over by the modelling of the main character... when downing bad guys / mutants lets have an option to autoloot... having to hold down a button to crouch is slightly annoying  (because the delay is just long enough to irritate me)- and am I the only one who found the English voices a little jarring?

Despite all this, I've kind of enjoyed it so far.  Reading the updates from the devs I'm excited. There's a lot of passion going into this and I'm confident they'll iron out the quirks and rework this into something on par with the first game. I'll stick with it and looking forward to the August update. 

i7-10700F
GTX 4060
32 GB RAM

Megapatch 3: 1 hour in after restart. Removal of the class system I think was a wise move. Enjoying the open world atmosphere although there seems to be a bit too much open space at the moment (although I've found a bunker which I need a charge to open, so that looks interesting). Some of the monster animations seem clunky when there's several on screen - which is annoying as things were fine pre-patch.

Megapatch 4: Sorry to write this. I realise its EA but I don't always have the patience. Crashed straight to desktop as soon as I used a teleporter. Frame-generation looks to tank the game (at least on my rig). Load times are slow, textures take while to load in. Inventory menu access is sluggish. Could be because I'm running off a HDD - but with 32GB and a 4060 GTX where performance was fine on MP3 and earlier builds this is a disappointment. Think I'll shelve this one for now. There's no fun starting/tweaking/restarting a game in the hope it'll be playable on the next launch.

review:
Chernobylite 2... So, as a backer for both the original Chernobylite and now its sequel, Chernobylite 2, I was super hyped for this early access release. I even got to play the "pre-launch" version, which actually ran a bit better overall. Honestly, though, that excitement's been a bit tough to hold onto. This review's coming out a bit late because when the game first launched, I just couldn't play it – the performance issues were really rough.

Fast forward almost three months, and while the game is technically playable now, it's still pretty rough around the edges when it comes to performance. It's a real bummer, honestly, because I had such high hopes for it.

Diving into the actual gameplay, it's a bit of a mixed bag. The melee combat feels like it's trying to be a bit like Dark Souls but maybe missed some of the key ingredients, and everything feels really fast-paced. As for gunplay, it's okay, but it just doesn't have that satisfying, weighty feel that made shooting in the first Chernobylite so great.

The classes are decent, though many of them do feel a bit similar. I have to give a huge shoutout to the Chernomancer, though – that one is genuinely unique and a ton of fun! It's basically your magic-user but with all these cool mutant abilities, which is a really fresh idea.

So, even though I haven't been able to sink a ton of hours into it yet, I wanted to share my initial thoughts for anyone considering picking it up. Right now, in its current state, I'd probably suggest holding off for a bit.

The game feels like it's trying too hard to be Elden Ring, when it really should be leaning into a STALKER 2-style experience. I'm hoping for a shift in direction at some point, aiming for more of a shooter RPG vibe, much like STALKER.

However, I really do believe in Farm 51. They've shown a great commitment to their games in the past, and I'm optimistic that they know what they're doing. I have a strong feeling that in about six months or more, this game could really transform into something special. So, if you're interested, I'd highly recommend adding it to your wishlist and checking back on it later in the year.

As a big fan of the STALKER series, this franchise means a lot to me. I'm really looking forward to seeing how Farm 51 continues to develop the game in the coming years, and I'll definitely be updating this review as things progress!

review:
This game in NOT the original Chernobylite game that you likely first fell in love with.  That gritty action game that was immersive and compelling in its game play.

Before you go clicking the purchase button and spending your money only to have buyer's regret, read through the below and check out the online reviews about the direction the developer has decided to on this venture.

Currently very disappointed in how the game currently stands. I understand we're early access, but the controls and feel of the game world are horrible compared to the original game. Why is the PDA so big and taking up so much space on the screen when not minimised? It seems like a cool idea a dev came up with and that they haven't had someone give them honest feedback to scrap it. Put the data elsewhere in components on the screen and axe the PDA.

I'm spending more time staring at the PDA in the bottom corner of the screen than the world around me. I don't want to play the PDA game. I want to play the amazing Chernobylite game in the amazing Chernobylite world.

PDA map...why doesn't it zoom in and out?

Coming back to the point again: get rid of the PDA. Why do I need it up to scan the world around me? I've got perception, that's my skill, not the PDA's skill. I want to stop looking at the PDA and start looking at the world. Let me scan the world independent of the PDA, highlight or mark the items in the world around me, and then also maybe have them on a smaller zoomable mini map tucked away in the top-right corner of the screen.

When first starting the game the default mouse speed was set extremely slow. Fixed by going into settings.

The first couple of hours playing were visually horrible. Why was everything so close to the POV of the character? Found the field of vision setting, but even at max its still a bit too close.

The character models feel like they're based on late 1990's code and modelling, just up scaled. Not lifelike or fluid.

The voice acting... The voice actors come across like they're reading individual lines into a microphone in a room on their own, not actually speaking dynamically with another person. The dialogue between characters is so...halting. It's not fluid and breaks any sense of immersion. Again, it feels like late 1990's technology.

Text windows on the Build Your Base screen take up way too much space and stick around needlessly. Why can't I zoom in and out? This is a part of the overall problem that is a pattern in the game so far. Too much clutter. Not enough immersion and realism.

After building a room and attempting to place a workbench in that room, the screen is again taken up by way too many things leaving way too little of the screen open to see the room and the item that you're trying to place in it.

Can't leave the Build Your Base screen if you've got a large room selected but not placed due to rocks in the way.  Hit ESC to leave the interface?  You get a popup asking you to ACCEPT or DECLINE the error message preventing you from leaving the interface.  Neither option lets you leave Build Your Base....you just get left with the same unplaced room and stuck in the interface.

Using a workbench: why isn't ESC a default key to exit the workbench screen alongside the displayed odd choice of the TAB key? TAB isn't a game standard choice for exiting screens, if you're going to use it, at least keep ESC as a secondary exit key. ESC should get you out of every single screen that you are in while playing the game.

Same problem with skipping conversation lines of dialogue. Why is ENTER your choice of key bind here? Why are users taking their hand off the mouse to move to the keyboard and hit ENTER? The SPACE key should be default, or at least a secondary key. Left hand is already at the standard WASD home location, that leaves the thumb to readily hit the SPACE key to skid dialogue lines quickly.

Attribute screen: you need to be able to click an attribute to lock it in so you can go down and scroll through the explanation text window. Currently you have to try and carefully weave your mouse pointer around other items to get down to scroll the text window without inadvertently changing it to a different item.

Systems and quests aren't thoroughly tested to be intuitive and error free.  During Night Activities in learning how to build an extractor the steps are clunky and at the end you're audibly prompted to return to the base, but attempting to leave has the stalker appear out of no where saying you can't leave....why?  I dunno, no quest info on the screen, but apparently you need to talk to him before leaving and him automatically stopping you from leaving apparently isn't a good enough time for him to just say what he has to say.  Again, the close camera distance made this quest annoying trying to place pipes or a power line especially with all the things taking up screen space.  Looking at you needless PDA and over-sized quest text that never goes away...

Combat just feels sluggish and awkward. The original game was gritty and realistic and so far the in game experience feels like a child's game for pre-teens for combat. Fights seem...episodic not natural or a part of the world.

In 3rd person, you can strafe while holding down aim for a ranged weapon...but not a melee weapon? Blocking is bound to the right mouse button instead of aiming like with a ranged weapon. A better solution is needed. Normally a modifier like SHIFT or another key would let you strafe, but I haven't found a modifier key to strafe in 3rd person melee....I just wobble around inefficiently trying to line up shots. 3rd person melee is needlessly frustrating. Where is the elegance of the original game?

3rd person combat has none of the gritty realism of the original game. Why? Why was this changed? Melee in first person leaves odd disorientation after multiple swings. Where did the enemy go? Why did my camera angle change?

Getting melee'd through the wall of a cargo container needs to get fixed.

I selected the gun based class. I want to play as a sniper and a gun-based character...but here I am playing a mindless melee character by default due to the limitation of too little ammo and guns just not matching up. I didn't want to play like this, why am I being funnelled into swinging a melee weapon when the game asked me how I wanted to play? Cater the in-game experience to the class chosen by the player.

Typos in the on screen text display of NPC audio conversations need to be fixed. Igor needs to use the word "he'll" not "heill."

Going to the map screen by hitting "M" needs to center the location of the mouse pointer. Currently if you've been turning and then press "M" the map screen will slide all the way to the left or the right until you manually center your mouse in away from the edge of the screen.

I understand you're in EA, but these are really core components that are key to user experience and immersion. Why has the game strayed so far from the original game's design and mechanics? There's a reason that it was successful and fun to play. It feels like the development team may be working with a yes-man culture where everyone is possibly being too polite and not enough honest discussions are being had or encouraged to be brutal on pet code projects or sunken resources into code that is simply not good.

This is not the original Chernobylite game deepened and uplifted into a better version of the first game.  This is a scrapping of the original and a rewrite from the bottom up, having not held true to the original game play experience....which is why users are on this Steam page hoping for more of the same...only better.

review:
I do honestly want to like this game. I loved the first game, and was so excited about a sequel that I did back the kickstarter. Chernobylite 2 leaves me......confused.

Overall the game is fine? I love exploring the exclusion zone, I love that Igor is around to guide us......and thats really it. It's not even that the rest of the game is bad. Heck I can see why some enjoy a lot of its elements. But if you want a true sequel to the first game, this really isn't that.

Combat is now souls-like, clearly with the melee combat in mind, but that means gunplay and the, admittedly interesting gauntlets suffer a bit to get it all to work. The slow, methodical combat in from the first game is now just mindlessly blitzing almost anything you see. 

The Main character almost feels like he was originally meant to be a custom voiceless character before getting shoehorned in for a personal story element, but all that does imo is force you to play as the most generic, boring SoB i've seen in a game. The first game had a very personal story for Igor but it was well implemented into the overarching narrative about him finding his wife using information you grab about the Chernobyl Disaster. Generic Man (legit can't remember his name) has a wife, and she's left him for a decent enough reason, and that's all I remember about the guy. I think scrapping a pre made character in favour for a custom one would do wonders for the game. Focus the story on the world you're stuck in without the need for side bits about a very unlikeable MC.

Base Building is fine. Feels a little bare bones right now but I can assume there will be more added and the feature fleshed out in the future. In fact, all my other complaints can be attributed to early access, and I wouldn't normally be too critical about that. I mean I left NMRIH2 a positive review cause it feels good under the EA jank. But the fundamentals built into Chernobylite 2, that probably can't/won't see much change at all, really sour the overall experience for me. 

Maybe in the future I'll look at this game favourably, but right now, I'm left very confused and admittedly a little sour.

Extremely upset with the state of this game. It is in no way ready for even early release. This is a $40 beta test. Cool premise, good graphics when they don't glitch out, poor optimization, and just overflowing with bugs. Add to your wishlist and follow but DO NOT PURCHASE at this time!

I don't usually post a negative review but this is horrible...especially since I decided to do a couple of the rifts tonight and did not earn ANYTHING! None of my loot, none of my exp, absolutely zero benefit. 

Highly disappointed to this point. 


RE:BUGS BUGS BUGS
Doesn't look bad, but this is definitely rushed to release.

1. Loot and other objects fall through the ground. This especially occurs in the port area on the sandy areas, when crossing bridges and over tunnels, and when there is an underground facility below where you are fighting or scanning.

2. When going through portals, your clothing glitches over your face and head making first person untenable to proceed. The only way to correct is to force a new loading. Unfortunately this is happening often in the "Breach" portion of the game that does not allow saving and reloading. Had to quit the game and start over multiple times. Very annoying.

3. Storage is extremely limited early on. Either storage needs to be increased or the scrapping of items needs to be available very very early.

4. When placing benches a "snap to" option with a grid would be nice...please!

5. Melee combat is ridiculously buggy...you can be in a fight and swing until you stamina is gone and get zero hits...but the enemy can be swinging all over the place and nearly kill you with 1 hit.

6. EXP gain needs to be worked on. After 5 days in game, following the story and doing a little exploring but not much, only enough experience to gain two stat points. This is much to slow for how quickly the enemy and gear requirements climb.

7. Goes along with #6 but the amount of locked areas that you will have to try and remember to come back to and pick up what every is behind the door you need 12 strength or the crystals that need 15 psyche to get past etc.etc. is really really annoying. I don't want to have to revisit every single place I went to following the story just to see if these crates have anything useful in them. And when they don't have useful items for my current level whenever I get enough points to actually access them people will just not bother.

8. REALLY REALLY should use the same voice on characters...following the story, get immersed, and then the same dialog with the same character suddenly has a different voice...way to break the story telling.

Probably more things as I continue playing but wanted to start a list...I'll keep adding here.

review:
What a shame. The first Chernobylite was a great game. The atmosphere and dark and gritty gameplay made for a nice mix of survival FPS and horror, with a base building element. I have absolutely no idea what would compel the developers to stray so far away from what made the first Chernobylite so great, but here we are. I even replayed the first game in preparation for this one when I saw it was releasing in a couple months only to be extremely disappointed.

The devs changed basically everything about the game for this, and from the very start of the game where you get to test the 3 'classes' it feels like an awfully made futuristic ubisoft shovelware clone. It's truly unbelievable as I loved the first game and was really looking forward to this one, but from what I can see, this game takes almost nothing from the first game, which wouldn't be an issue if the game was halfway decent.
	
There are now 6 classes, which specialize in melee, firearms, and chernobylite(magic), or a mix of the 3. They also changed the combat system to one that IMO resembles a mix of skyrim and a wannabe dark souls. Basically braindead AI that spam attacks you and you can block or dodge. Obviously the hitboxes are pretty bad and the game is sadly easy even on hard difficulty because you can just spam dodge and during the dodge animation you're unable to get hit, even if the shot goes straight through you. The NPCs and ESPECIALLY the player model look absolutely horrendus, they literally look and move like aliens who are pretending to be humans. It also seems like they picked and chose what lines would be voice acted by your character and others. I was 5 hours into the game and my character started talking in an unmistakably AI generated voice, and then 5 minutes later his normal voice comes back. review:
Let this intro serve as not just a warning to potential buyers but a message to the developers and also provide some context for my early access review:

Chernobylite was my GOTY for 2021 until Inscryption dropped and stole the gold. Get Even was a fantastic story driven stealth shooter with a really cool gameplay hook as well. The Farm 51 always approach their games with a clear vision and the final result is every time something unique and worthwhile. However, Chernobylite 2 SHOULD ONLY BE PLAYED/PURCHASED by those of you interested in supporting the devs during early access either financially or by playing and providing your own unique feedback. There are just too many issues both technical and gameplay related that will only serve to frustrate players. To sum it up as simply as possible: this game makes a terrible first impression which combined with the Early Access tag can bury a game. Pros and Cons incoming. Cons will include genuine feedback but I will add any additional feedback after the list of cons.

PROS:
- Choice between 1st and 3rd person perspective allows players to choose their preferred method of play 
- Voice acting is nearly on par with previous games from the devs (although some of the dialogue sounds like placeholder AI, which shouldn't be looked at as a con for Early Access, please stop chewing on your keyboard)
- Base building is even better and more expansive than the first game and I can only imagine what a fully decked out base would look like (seriously addicting)
- Melee combat is surprisingly smooth and feels not only functional but a viable way to approach many combat encounters. Although the input queue will definitely trip up some of the button spammers out there (I played in 1st person).
- Worldbuilding is strong and plays off the foundation set by the first game very well.
- Great OST, on par with the first in terms of tone and style. Not sure if it's the same composer as the first game, but there is a reason I bought the OST for the first one and I will buy this one as well if it lives up to that in the end.

CONS
- Tons of graphical issues. You name it and the game probably has it. I don't mind this stuff for Early Access, but it reaches a point where your immersion is just obliterated making it nearly impossible to really stay in the game.
- Some key rebinding doesn't actually work, which combined with inconsistent tutorialization can make it difficult to figure out what some buttons do. Seriously, during the tutorial section when you're trying out the classes (which ends up being basically meaningless when you make your class choice) I thought I was doing something incorrectly because the NPC kept saying I was doing something wrong no matter what I did during the encounter which made me second guess how the weapons actually worked.
- Deeper distinction between classes (which may or may not come later in the game). The RPG choices presented to certain classes don't seem very interesting or intuitive. And it looks like any class can use basically any gear with no penalty? 
- There is very little feedback for anything that you do outside of swinging a melee weapon. I didn't even know I leveled until I got back to the base because there is no sound or music or fanfare whatsoever. For how absurdly overbearing the UI can be, the fact that it didn't tell me I had leveled in any meaningful way just felt so strange.
- Speaking of UI, somehow the building elements from the first game (building stations like healing, ammo crafting, etc.) were made more difficult because of how little of your screen you can actually utilize when placing a station. If there is a button to minimize or remove UI during that process I didn't see it (and I'm willing to just be dumb on this one) but the fact that either wasn't obvious, or just set as the default is incredibly frustrating. This was exacerbated further by the incredibly poor lighting in the base itself. I don't mind low lighting when you're out exploring (in the first game especially it made for some incredibly tense moments), but for the building stuff, you should either just have better visibility by default OR the building should just be moved into the base building menu as well. Other than porting over the elements from the first game for the sake of ease, I can't imagine why this wasn't just a change that was made in general.
- This is probably my biggest criticism of the game and I don't think it is necessarily an Early Access issue so please take special noteL The enemy types are far too varied mechanically to look so similar. The ones that shoot look like the ones that swing look like the ones that punch. I don't mind them all looking so similar, it makes sense in the lore and it would be weird to change it too much, but something has to be considered. If you're standing in green grass near trees and a Chernobylite deposit with 4 or 5 Chernohosts that all look identical but you can't tell which one is firing at you while another one swings, that's just not a good approach to enemy design. There are far too many examples of this done right to fail this hard.

I may update my review with additional feedback when there are major changes, but as it stands I may not come back until 1.0 so I can experience the world and story as intended and not with so many issues. I have no doubt whatsoever that the final product can absolutely be one of the best RPGs on Steam. Even in its current state (2 days into Early Access) it is superior to mainstream garbage like Starfield, But I want newcomers to get the best that the team at The Farm 51 are capable of. So in the meantime, I would recommend either replaying OR playing for the first time the original Chernobylite. A fantastic game from fantastic developers and by the time you get through that one, the second one might be in a more acceptable state.

review:
This game is really weird to me. The first game was really cool and I really enjoyed it. It was a awesome blend of Sci-fi, horror, mystery, exploration and atmosphere. It had RPG elements and base building elements but those werent really the focus. 

Chernobylite 2 however... it's like they removed everything that made the first game so cool and doubled down on all the stuff that wasn't. This feels like a wonky fantasy fallout game or something. The environments look cool, but the gameplay itself is just so boring. The story so far, is just not interesting. 

Collecting loot in games is not exciting for me. The first Chernobylite there was something calming and almost hypnotizing about using the scanner and going and finding the loot you needed. Chernobylite 2 feels like any other RPG loot system. Just kill stuff spam Loot All and have inventory full of random items. Looting was in the first game as well, but it was different. This feels like its way more of a focus. It just feels like a medicore RPG game now instead of this cool scifi / horror story. 

I thought the first game did a good job on balancing the action  and the horror. And there were times when Chernobylite 1 was actuallly pretty scary. Chernobylite 2 is the exact opposite in this regard. It's just mindless run and shoot pack of RPG mobs that have health bars. They even have axes and shields and shit. You can even cast spells its like wtf... Like, Igor passed out in some green gas and is having a fever dream. Thats what this feels like.

The AI voicelines become more and more frequent the further I got. Also apparently the "dismantle" skill (alternative to selling your hard earned loot) is only learned from a SCIENTIST faction member, so god help you if you choose to assist the Mercs/Mutants at the start of the game you will be unable to dismantle items for some time until you meet them later in the game. Voice acting seemed off for me, in the sense that some lines just felt robotic and not spoken like a human. I noticed that AI was used for translations so perhaps this has something to do with it? This jarring voice acting was coupled with some weird animations, most notably for me is the sprinting animation in third person which for lack of better way of saying it, looks goofy.

Combat was okay, it played kind of like a generic third person shooter (was considering first person mode but got a warning this was experimental?) and while I'm sure it gets more interesting later the issues I did have made me ultimately put this down and refund for now.

I understand that this game is still in early access, so I'm willing to be gracious about some of the things I've experienced.

This is a very middle-of-the-road game as far as simulators go. Obviously, with full automation unlocked, there isn't much to do but turn your brain off and occasionally buy products to restock your concessions. Honestly, this isn't a huge issue for me; though, I understand some peoples' frustrations with a lack of further game play.

My biggest gripe with this game is the sheer amount of AI generated content. Again, I understand that it's in early access, and I do hope that the AI content will eventually be replaced; however, if the devs intend to leave or expand the AI content beyond what it already is, it reeks of laziness and an easy cash grab. There are a small handful of movie titles where it's obvious that the devs crafted original scenes using the assets they had, which stand out as better content than the AI generated loops. I know it isn't cheap or easy to create original content, but it would at least justify the price paid for the game, overall, if there was more thought and effort put into it beyond the AI.

For me, the game is a solid 5 out of 10. I don't love it. I don't hate it. I'm interested to see what more may come, but I'm not holding my breath for a miracle.

review:
Even in its Early Access phase, this game fails to deliver any value commensurate with its price. From the very beginning to the end, the game balance is severely flawed, making it virtually impossible to enjoy any aspect of gameplay.

* A message for the developers and my own reflections are included at the end of this review.

[h2]Expectations vs. Reality in a Movie Theater Management Simulator[/h2]
Movie Selection
Although the game is marketed as a movie theater management simulator, the option to choose which movie to screen is merely superficial. The films available are actually AI-generated content created by others, and the original credits remain intact. This lack of originality and disregard for creative ownership is a major drawback.

[h2]Hiring Staff and Delegating Tasks[/h2]
The concept of hiring staff to manage screenings and operations sounds promising at first. However, once you delegate these tasks, you as the player are left with nothing substantial to do other than watching a simulation. The interactive and engaging aspects are completely lost, reducing the experience to a monotonous series of automated tasks.

[h2]Lackluster Expansion and Repetitive 3D Graphics[/h2]

While there is a feature to expand your theater, the core gameplay itself barely changes. You’re just repeating the same dull tasks: assigning seats, selling snacks, cleaning, and dealing with troublesome customers. On top of that, scheduling essentially boils down to deciding how to fill a 14-hour daily slot. In the early stages, you’re stuck with three- or four-hour films that aren’t very popular, but before long, you can easily license far more popular one-hour films, so there’s virtually no strategic depth in planning your schedule.

I only watch around 70 movies a year myself, but I still think there were better ways to simplify this concept into a game. For example, rather than limiting movies to a single genre, they could’ve introduced multiple genres and given users different preferences. If all I want to do is run a money-making simulation, I might as well play a clicker game instead of something branded as a simulation game. There’s also an option to place arcade machines, but they just sit there unused.

The short animation of loading popcorn is the only thing that feels even slightly cute, and overall, the experience boils down to tedious routine work.

[h2]Additional Grievances[/h2]
[h3]Bizarre Beverage Skill Check[/h3]
The game includes a skill check related to beverages that seems tacked on without any meaningful integration, leaving one to question whether the developer even played the game themselves.

[h3]Tedious Cleaning Mechanics[/h3]
Cleaning is unnecessarily cumbersome as the dirt on the floors does not disappear with a long press; you have to click repeatedly, which only adds to the frustration.

[h3]Rigid Object Placement and Poor Quality[/h3]
Objects can only be placed in predetermined positions, stripping away any sense of creative freedom. The overall quality is so low that it feels as if a novice student, armed with generative AI and readily available online content, hastily assembled this crude simulation software.

[h3]Mostly Positive?[/h3]
Don’t be misled by the current user reviews. As of February 28, 2025, 83% of the 154 posted reviews are marked as positive, but the unlock rates for achievements that should be easily attainable in this game are only a few percent. For example, only 3.5% of players have earned the basic “Hire One Employee” achievement, and an ostensibly easy goal like “Achieve 100% Customer Satisfaction” also has a similarly low unlock rate.

Furthermore, the customer satisfaction score fluctuates wildly during film screenings. It appears that instead of calculating an average among everyone in the theater, the game uses the satisfaction of only those who have just finished watching a movie—likely a bug.

[h3]Final Thoughts[/h3]
In all honesty, it appears that the developers lack sufficient experience in actually playing and refining a game—or they are simply understaffed, leading to inadequate quality assurance. Having played a fair number of indie games, I can confidently say that this is not a game at all, but rather a shoddy simulation software produced by a small-scale company. For a price tag of around $10, there is no justifiable value here, especially when compared to the wealth of far more engaging titles available. Save your money and look elsewhere.

[b]Note: This review was summarized and translated from my rough notes using generative AI.[/b]

Unfortunately, it seems generative AI still isn’t quite ready for game QA testing. While Claude 3.7 Sonnet appears to be getting better at playing Pokémon, thorough QA testing apparently still requires human effort. I'm sure the developers eagerly await the day AI can fully handle QA tasks—and frankly, so do I.

Making a game is incredibly difficult. I’ve dabbled in it myself, and I’ve spoken with friends who work full-time in game development. I also write code for data analysis, but the volume of code and techniques used in game development are on a whole different level. Even with that in mind, this is just terrible.

I understand how hard you must have worked to try to make it good. And no matter how much you push your limits, hearing comments like mine must feel demoralizing.
However, I believe the developer must not forget their own inner “user” perspective. Don’t betray yourself.

Have you had many people playtest it? I’m not sure how many hours they’ve spent playing, but please have as many people as possible try your prototype and sincerely take their feedback into account.
A movie theater simulator is a great concept, and I was excited at first. I was also thrilled that you could choose from so many movies. But the footage includes credits that can easily be traced back to the original creators if you dig a little. Since it’s generated by AI, the question of whether it’s subject to copyright varies by country and era. Maybe keeping the credits is more ethical. Still, as a creator, why not at least use AI-generated content you’ve created yourself?

I do understand the game’s system. However, even if the idea is good, it will lack potential to grow—both as code and as a game—if it’s based on random spur-of-the-moment ideas or sloppy design.

I noticed that the developer of this game responded only to negative reviews, sometimes asking, “What is the reason for your negative rating?” That’s why I wrote this detailed explanation here. My intention isn’t to be hostile, but rather to encourage the developer to take user criticism seriously—not to brush it off with superficial questions—and to engage with users humbly.

I truly hope this game becomes something genuinely worthwhile.

To conclude wait to purchase its got a long way to go to be worth the price even if on a sale. I intend on refunding and comming back once its had some updates as this needed more time in the oven before releasing even into early access.

[h1]The "over the top" positive reviews, not correct [/h1]

Current reviews are not truly honest because they do not address fundamental issues with this game. Has to be internal or people just being nice to get some review understanding. 

We are here to save your money and interest, not provide information that would be otherwise unhelpful to the team developing the game.
We would rather be honest, provide feedback, assist with corrections, and expose our passion or lack thereof for their work, rather than boost sales for a fundamentally flawed game.
Fun at first, but replayability will not be there once you do it all, unless they add lots more.
The gruel, without flow, running yourself ragged because you can't hire help for the departments you have, is the killer. 

Who wants to run day after day with a lottery labor pool of applicants?

Too many problems in design, as previously stated, driving our team bananas. 

Was enjoyable for the first five minutes, then when things got going.. good lord... just want to stop playing.

The only analogy... proverbial... "How many times do you need to be punched in the face before relocating your entire presence, before you have enough?" 
Well, I just went 10 rounds with Mike Tyson, in our analogy, and four of six of us feel nothing but regret. Games are made to be fun, challenging, satisfying, emotionally connected to a character or environment, and never regret.

The amount of bugs that are present, lack of content, design, fundamental issues, in the short play durability/replay ability, ect.
Don't get us wrong, its a fun little game for $7 or under, a dollar more is pushing it so get it on sale if you must but you will refund after an hour unless they are all hands on deck making HUGE development, time-consuming, well planned changes.

[h1]In closing:[/h1]
Fair price for $7, while on sale at best. Not a penny more.

[h1]Our opinion to grow the game:[/h1]
Get a white board.
Plan Where you are starting  a character from and where you want the user at, by X stage, Y stage, Z stage...ect.
More movies, content all around, movie theater immersion, possibly IMAX theaters, more items in food sales (That you fill one side sensibly), better movie ads (cardboard cutouts to fill empty space in theater, especially for HUGE releases. 
Just a QOL improvement, not keeping everything to unlock since you stopped making content and could not spare any to give you an immersive environment.
Advertising you can put in previews of upcoming movies or products... on screen before the feature... for advertising sales... on and on... can make this fantastic.

[h1]Major bugs and annoyances:[/h1]

Buy a concession stand puts popcorn on one side... drink on another with no organization or consequential placement that should fill one side of the theater than the other.

Employees for hire, do not give you choice of hiring positions that you need. Its horrible.
FOUR DAYS and not one person to help concessions running from ticketing to drinks to popcorn or CLEANING! Too much to enjoy.

Some English, some possibly Polish or Italian. No Frutia? There is only popcorn and drinks offered for the start so whatever.. more bad complaints from patrons entering just banging you up in rep... so sad.

Customers saying they did not ask for the time you gave them tickets for, yet they will give you bad reviews if you place them in their time slot at 7 pm when they bought there tickets at 8 am the same day.?? Don't understand that... imagine how we feel trying to explain it.
 
If you sell them a ticket on the time requested, sometimes penalized.

Put them in the time now that they asked for, per requested but prior person penalized you for something... you get a second penalized and it keeps in a chain reaction, with saying did not ask for the time. WTF! 
So if you get one, expect a second right after apparently. Never ending because never tested.

Put them in the row they wanted, but not the exact seat because they were taken... stupid... penalized. GRRR!

In the early game, people stand in lobby instead of sitting in the theater, eating snacks, waiting for previews and movie to start. 
NOPE... lets throw trash on the movie theater floor, when you sell NOTHING, and then again in the stadium as if they smuggled in popcorn and a buffet. I mean come on... that is lazy. Pure nonsense.
Critical... not really... this is basic stuff that should have been caught if properly tested, designed with an ounce of common sense or better said... love.

[b]Our rating all things considered:[/b]
[h1]5.4 out of 10[/h1]

Great idea, poorly designed and executed. 
Fixes we are sure may or may not happen... we will check back when they happen and keep you all posted accordingly. This one.... certainly won't get a Oscar.

review:
Could have been a fun and cozy game if they wouldn't limit you so much. Let me explain.

You can gather furniture and take it back to your warehouse. You can also do this with things like wall pieces, windows, doors and even the bricks and wood the house is build with. And in the beginning I started gathering as much as I could. But here's the limiting thing: You can't really do anything with it.

Yes, there are orders you can complete but the bigger ones don't really make sense. There are three different rarities and a lot of different items you can collect, so you always miss a few of the items to fill a bigger order, so you end up doing the smaller ones. And yes, there is a trader that takes items from you but you can only sell 1 or 2 to him a day since as soon as you put more into the truck the discount he expects rises to 80% and you get less money for more goods, which is just absurd.

The contracts you get usually involve destroying the entire house so destroying everything, including the furniture, is a better way to make some money since you can collect the garbage into bags that you then can take back to recycle, getting you money at the end of the day. And you can't even upgrade the trash bags or how many you can carry so you end up just running back and forth a lot.

And thus the game is just way too repetitive: Destroy everything, gather trash, get trash to warehouse to recycle, repeat.

Warehouse: You can't choose where things like loading/unloading zones are, which means you have to design your warehouse around being able to move the entire shelf closer to you to fill an order and then move it back.

Orders: Honestly the most infuriating thing about this game! Truly unhinged requests for things like 15 small windows... there is one small window every 2-3 houses, meaning it would take 50-60 jobs to complete that one request. You also end up having to maintain stocks of things you don't want, like a 20 dollar lamp, because the orders need a 20 dollar lamp to go with their 29 walls and premium television.

Upgrades: None of the upgrades to your character really matter; things get slightly faster, but it does nothing to alleviate the exhaustion you feel after taking apart your 90th dresser. The exosuit is probably the best one, but I can't use the sprint because you can't remap the key.

Vehicles: The difference between the first three vehicles is almost nonexistent, and the final two are better but still aren't wide enough to really allow you to stack things properly, and for some reason you can pay to upgrade your warehouse to hold more vehicles, which seems pointless.

Destruction: There is no wrong way to do this; almost every contract has you destroy the entire house, and there are no repercussions for collapsing it on yourself or leaving the electrical and water hooked up. There was an opportunity here to play with hazards, but it's completely ignored. The destruction does feel fun, but you'll dread it because of my next point:

Recycling: This is the longest part of every job, and there is NO way to upgrade your bag size or carry capacity or to buy a garbage truck or improve this element whatsoever. Some houses are like 30+ bags, and you need to deal with each one of them individually on both the gathering side and the unloading side.

The wrecking ball: It's way too expensive. A really good contract pays maybe 1300 dollars, and the wrecking ball is half that! (600) It also isn't hard to take down a house without it; it's the difference between doing it by hand for about 3 minutes or doing it with the wrecking ball for about 1 minute and then still having to clean up the area by hand.

Overall this game was a good concept, but it was poorly executed. I wish I had kept better track of my 3 hours so I could have returned it.

review:
This game is SUCH a cool idea, it could be one of the most amazing sim games on the market, but it needs a lot more care and attention to detail before it gets there.  My main issues are:

1) Severe lack of content.  I was so excited when I saw that permits require 10, 20, etc jobs completed - to me that implied that there WERE 10 or 20 jobs to do... but the reality is there are barely 5, you just regenerate a list of the exact same jobs every day.  Same title, same house, same tasks, same job, and you're going to have to keep doing them over and over again to expand your permit.  By the third time doing the exact same job, I was pretty bored and over it.  There's also just WAY too few items and item types to make it interesting.  I love the idea of pulling everything out of the houses that could be valuable, but after a couple of jobs it's just the exact same furniture, same chairs, same hippo statue, and it gets boring fast.

2) No progression.  There are a handful of "tool upgrades" but for some completely incomprehensible reason YOU CAN'T UPGRADE YOUR SLEDGEHAMMER..  OR YOUR TRASH BAG! Why?!?  And the tool upgrades there are aren't really satisfying. There should be a lot more room for upgrades and gear changes that allow for customizing based on how you like to play.

3) Jank tsunami.  Obviously, you always expect a little jank in your sim games, it's part of the charm! But this one sadly takes it way too far - graphical issues left and right, including objects disappearing from the warehouse, trees and other things clipping right into my van, walls/garbage/items getting stuck in weird places during demolition - it all comes together to make it feel more frustrating than fun.

Ultimately, I'm going to keep this one in my library because I do see the devs have been pushing out updates, and I hope that with a little more care they can make this game the awesome experience it really could be.  But for now, can't recommend it.
