review:
Currently feels still like too much of a tech demo and not enough like a game.

From limited experience and a lot of youtube, my issues are:
1) Control scheme needs to be looked at again. Why not left click for nearly everything (incl pick up objects when you have your hands out)? Why not have a different button for doors so that you can open stuff whilst holding it? Esc in computer should escape, not menu. 
2) Buggy noises and textures.
3) Cannot move dismantleable furniture but this stuff can still be destroyed when you destroy a nearby wall (tutorial bed exploded from nearby wall). No way to prevent that except dismantle bed and remake, PITA.
4) Exploding rubble. Rubble from demolished walls is extremely volatile and breaks stuff very easily (brick wall in tutorial exploded and destroyed the light fixture).
5) Unclear how best to remove all wood slats from the wooden walls. Half the time it ends up collapsing and breaking.
6) In general, game play is still quite shallow. Deconstructing a house should include utilities (wiring, plumbing, gas, etc). You should be penalised for how much 'trash' you create, thereby incentivising proper deconstruction. Different material types would also be good and better sales of items to third parties. Random orders right now feels to RNG. Would like to see incentives for roof dismantling - metal roofs? Would be good to also have to jackhammer concrete base etc to completely remove the building.
6) Pallets for reclaimed items should be on shelves or something. No one would store stuff like that. Also, should probably have the option to scrap stuff for raw materials cost. Maybe different sized pallets for different stuff.
7) Object placement in trucks is jank. Free 3d rotation would be nice and better valid placement checks. Adding multiple plasterboard to the tiny truck is not viable even if you don't take anything else! Chair stacking FTW!
8) Stuff inside houses is too RNG. Trailer should not contain premium etc. More 'types' of furniture would be good (common, uncommon, etc etc), also premium should be high value, is currently meh?
9) Starting warehouse is actually quite big? If stuff is tuned, could start off with a crappy storage box or something and grow.
10) Order a skip (trash truck) to the site?

Has potential though depending on what the developers do. Will revisit in a few months.

review:
If you're thinking about getting this game, download the demo and play it through a few times until you're bored because there really isn't much more content that's worth it outside of the demo itself. 

This game was initially a lot of fun, it felt like there were clear objectives and lots to look forward to, but it feels like I've reached mid-game about 10 hours in, and there's no real urge to see it to completion. It's repetitive. 

The idea of the game is neat, but what it really lacks is any sort of tangible progression or end state. Later game contracts are made arbitrarily harder by implementing a "day-tax" penalty and making the contract 200km away. Being able to only sell collected items as part of bundles means you spend hours painstakingly collecting items that likely never get sold and just take up space in your warehouse. Overall, the upgrades just feel like something to waste money on to flesh out the maybe 5-10 hours of gameplay this game has than something that makes any tangible difference. 

90% of your in game time will be spent fighting the punishing mechanics of trying to fit items into your van. You can see the silhouette, you can see that it fits, but the hit markers won't let you place anything. This is especially frustrating when the later-game contracts take 2 hours each way to get to and you have to make numerous trips. 

Overall, fun at first, but if I had to do it all over again I'd wait for this game to go on sale for $5, play it on a rainy Sunday, then forget about it.

review:
There's some 200.000 games on Steam right now. You could be exploring faraway galaxies, leading vast armies, saving a beautiful dragon from a horrible princess, you could be building magnificent cities, or perhaps entire civilizations that will stand the test of time. You could be securing the future of your royal dynasty by getting to know your sister better. You could be a master assassin, or an ancient vampire, heck you could run around and cause mischief as a goat. Either of those would be more fun than what the devs, appropriately named Incubator, are expecting you to spend your limited time on this planet on. 

This game lures you in with a promise of explosive action - something that could help lower your cortisol levels after a stressful day job. Instead, it offers an exciting opportunity to do a second job in your free time. Indeed, the Destruction tag in this mostly refers to your sanity. You get half a dozen tools in this game - screwdrivers, saws, you name it. And all of them but one you can upgrade many times. The one you can't is the sledgehammer. You nominally have it, yes, but the game goes out of its way to discourage your using it. That's because it wants you to spent 10 minutes carefully dismantling a wardrobe - one screw at a time - because you can then sell it for more than the entire contract's worth... And the wrecking ball? Well, it costs $600 to rent one, when the contract to wreck the house pays... that's right, $600. Mic drop.

I endured this game as much as I can and now I think I can say this game sucks. I got the last permit, upgraded tools and warehouse and bought the big truck, but I did most of it just for the sake of it and see until the end if the game gets any interesting with new permits and more item space.

1- It's a high when you first get into business, then it's downward spiral. There is no joy in this game, you can get more satisfaction and joy if you actually deconstructed a building yourself. Really, really boring.

2- There is no music, no story, no end goal, nothing. Intro starts like you are on a revenge mission, you have a story, a target. But nope. After the tutorial you are on your own and only thing you see is the mission descriptions. No secrets, no easter eggs, no fun. You just go through the same dozen of houses over and over and over and over...

3- There are some concepts they tried, like customer types, but it's shallow as a pool of piss. You can't set a quality for your products, you have to collect EVERYTHING or you miss the most profitable contracts because that wealthy customer wants a premium TV, a premium couch, coupled with some stupid common walls or bricks. You can't just focus on most valuable items, unlike what game tells you at the beginning.

4- That cool wrecking ball in trailer? It's not free, you can't buy it, you have to pay a hefty amount at the beginning of the mission to use it and it's not cheap at all.

5- Game has a lot of jank. Not only a couple of assets, whole second floor doesn't even collapse if you start hitting the bottom floor first. You will get used to see floating pieces everywhere.

6- IF they implemented a "set item" system to contracts, that would improve the experience. Like, you see 8-pieces-premium kitchen set, well, tough luck, you sell each piece randomly. But if you could get a bonus for set items like chairs and tables, bed and wardrobe, TV and coach whatever, that would be great. But of course, it's way beyond the bubble of thought of these devs obviously.

7- I mean, that's pretty much it for this game. There is nothing even exciting to complain about. It's THAT boring, shallow, poorly implemented and isn't rewarding. Stare at a wall instead.

review:
I originally bought this game, in the blind, because I love Ship Graveyard Simulator 2 so much, and was hoping this would be a building version of that. I assume I'm not alone in that, but am sad to report that this is not that.

After a frustrating Tutorial experience, I decided to 100% the first level before writing my review, and ultimately have decided that this game is more not fun than fun, hence the thumbs down. Will you like this game? Maybe. I don't know. I'll detail below what the game entails, so you can decide if it sounds fun or not.

First, this is not a Deconstruction Simulator game. At least not primarily. That comes like fourth.

1st - It's a van loading/unloading simulator - Every plank, every piece of drywall, every piece of furniture, every bucket of small items, etc. must be manually loaded into your van, in a maddening game of wobbly-physics Tetris. And then, when something is sticking out just a little too far, and you try to close the doors, they will almost close, and then fly back open, so you can play Tetris some more. Then, once you finally get the load in and doors closed (of which you will have many many runs/loads per job), you get to unload everything in your warehouse! Every plank, every piece of drywall, every piece of furniture, etc. I hate this. Then, when it comes time to sell off everything you've stockpiled, yay, you get to load it all up again in the buyer's van! So you've now loaded/unloaded every single piece of everything, no less than three times, before you can get it out of your life. Did I mention I hate this?

2nd - It's an inventory management game - Very few games handle inventory management well, and this is not one of them. It's usually a necessary bummer, but this game tries to make it the secondary game loop. Once you get everything to your warehouse, you have to sort it all into the correct shelves, like a HomeDepot worker stocking the lumber yard. Then, once my warehouse was full (after just one job), I couldn't sell any of it off because I still didn't have all of the items in any of the available client orders, so I guess I was just expected to start the second job with a full warehouse and start dumping stuff anywhere there was space, since my shelves were full?

3rd - It's an IKEA furniture disassembly simulator - You spend more time taking apart all the different furniture pieces than you do the house. I will say, it is very satisfying how each piece of furniture auto-packages itself into a new IKEA box after disassembly.

4th - It's a deconstruction simulator, which should really only be called a wall removal simulator - The ceiling and floors are just bashed with a hammer and thrown in the trash. It's only the walls that are taken apart and salvaged.

Lastly, this game has chosen punishment over reward. It charges you for gas. It charges you rent. When you complete a level, you don't get paid (immediately), but rather you invoice the customer and have to wait. If you break something you shouldn't, you get docked for it (why not instead reward a player who doesn't damage anything?). This realism isn't fun. I play games to NOT think about bills. Don't give me game bills.



Wish List
- Let me carry more than 1 piece of drywall at a time. Loading/Unloading a stack of 50 sheets (3 times), one-by-one, is not a fun game mechanic.
- You currently have to wiggle your mouse to use many of the tools. I don't want to wiggle my mouse, I want to click once and hold. This isn't a VR game.
- Let me just sell off the stuff I salvaged. What am I supposed to do when the warehouse is full and there aren't any fullfillable orders?
- Let me just chuck everything into the truck. If there must be a capacity system (volume? weight?) so be it, but I never ever want to stack anything in these ridiculous physics simulators. I hate it. It is not fun. It is what your game is, and shouldn't be.
- The game runs hotter than an American Eagle jeans ad. Needs more optimization.

review:
[i]TLDR will be at the bottom for those who want to skip the reading[/i]

[h1] Deconstruction Sim Review [/h1]

[i]This Game has some [b][u]AMAZING[/u][/b] Potential. However that means there's currently [u]LOTS[/u] of improvements needed. I want to preface with saying that I REALLY like this game, and WANT to make it the most enjoyable experience I can. so let's start off with the core premise of the game.[/i] 

[h3]Deconstruction.[/h3]

The ENTIRE game is about demolition, yet a majority of the time you are dismantling objects because customers want to save stuff or because there's a premium item you want to save to sell later, the only downside is. You can't. You see, you can only sell items with random contracts, these contracts decide which of the items you can sell to them, only problem is, most of the time it's something you don't have. in my playthrough so far, I have almost 200 pieces of beams/wood that I salvaged from houses, but not 1 of them has sold yet, because there are no contracts for them. If there where  ways to sell items individually, for the price that the scanner claims then it would improve the gameplay but a LOT. In my opinion, I feel like the scanner should have more uses [b]LIKE[/b] selling the items you click on [b][u]ONLY[/u][/b] in the warehouse.

[h3]Optimization[/h3]

The game runs fairly solid on my PC, but I'm an outlier as I have a fairly beefy setup, so why am I talking about this? because the game TANKS due to the amount of entities while dismantling houses. I have a 3090ti and top of the line CPU and I will tank down to less than 30fps when the wrecking ball hits the houses due to all the debris flying. if the amount of entities could be lowered or some more time spent on optimizing the game, I believe it could honestly make for a fun and engaging time. However, in its current state, the FPS drops make it difficult to want to keep destroying houses.

[h3]Economy[/h3]

Okay, this is my biggest gripe so far. I haven't delved TOO deep into the game yet, but the prices of items compared to what each contract pays is ridiculous. It takes three to four contracts + rubble from those same contracts, to gain MAYBE 3-4K. This is a problem, due to the cost of tools, which you have to buy [i]INDIVIDUALLY[/i] may I add. increasing each upgrade until you max out the tools. That of which ranges from 1.5-2k [b]PER TOOL[/b]. Not to mention upgrading you vehicle which you then need to spend 1K to unlock the Garage, then 3-4K for the next Van, on top of buying new permits to unlock better contracts. Also, why is the wrecking ball $600 to rent when a contract only gains me $200??. The only thing I found that works is to not even bother with the warehouse mechanic and just destroy [b]EVERYTHING[/b] and sell the ruble. it's saves time and gains me Guaranteed income compared to selling items. This, by the way, includes stuff like, walls, bricks, wood, windows, doors, etc. just destroy them all and you'll make more money than individually selling them.

[h3]Warehouse[/h3]

As stated before, I fail to see a reason to engage with the warehouse at all. sure, you can take the time to dismantle items,w store them in your van/truck, and store them in the warehouse, but at the end of the day, you rarely sell items you have. my warehouse is FULL will walls, bricks, wood, windows and various premium items and I can't get contracts to sell them to save me. it makes the entire premise of the warehouse pointless, you're better off just adding a dump truck to the game and a landfill to sell rubble as that's more profitable than taking the time to take a cabinet apart, piece by piece and storing it to sell whenever the games lets you. In my opinion, I feel like this mechanic needs to be looked at and reworked to make us WANT to fill it up and sell things, but at this point in time, it just feels pointless.

[h3]Vehicles[/h3]

Im just gonna say it. why do I have to buy a garage in order to buy better vehicles? why can't I just sell the starter van and replace it with new vehicles? it's stupid and a waste of money to HAVE to buy a garage to THEN buy a new truck. it's unnecessary.

[h3]Closing words[/h3]\

There is still plenty I want to say about this game, and I may even be wrong about much of it, like the economy and warehouse functionality, but I just can't seem to enjoy these premises. The amount you make is minute compared to what you spend to upgrade. The warehouse feels pointless and just another cash dump to upgrade. And the game's performance, while good, tanks when too many things break or are destroyed at a time. I believe this game can become amazing, and I enjoyed my time playing it, but it needs to improve and touch on some of these issues because it causes it to feel stale and hollow. you can only destroy the same house, store the same items, and play Tetris in your van so much before you get bored and leave.


[h3]TLDR[/h3] 

This game can become a great demolition game, the physics and contract system are fun but carry a lot of issues like performance hits, and entity overloading causing game crashes, the warehouse feels empty and pointless leading to no reason to fill it up. Contracts rarely asks for items you DO have, and selling the rubble from houses makes more income than selling items individually. This game has plenty of issues but if worked on and optimized, even reworking some systems, can become a great  game to play. At it's current state [u]DO NOT[/u] recommend the game.

review:
I enjoy this game! I want to recommend it! I really do! It's SO close!!!

There are plenty of reviews that rightfully point out the game's glitches. The developers seem to be on top of things and I don't doubt a future update will flip this thumb around. Seriously, if there was a maybe thumb, I'd do that. Alas, Steam be Steam.

The game, at its core, has three issues that hold it back more than even the glitches.
 
The first might be a minor or major issue depending on who you are. While the beginning hints at some kind of story or narrative to encourage you to continue growing your business, this kind of just vanishes after the tutorial. While this isn't a deal breaker, it does make any failures of the game's other systems stand out all the more blatantly.

The second is the gameplay loop. The overall flow is: Go to site, collect as many materials/valuables as you can, break everything else, clean up, go home, sell what you brought back. The primary issue with the loop is that the "sell what you brought back" portion lags far slower that you are going to be getting materials and valuables. You sell the items in the form of requests that are fully random both in how close to full value the item is, how many items they want, and what kind they want. That means that you will VERY quickly accumulate a ton of inventory and seriously struggle to get rid of anything.

To clarify why this becomes a problem, let's say you treat a home like a Buffalo and carefully break down everything you can and bring back everything you can as I started doing early on.  If you get unlucky, you might never seem to get a request for lumber and even if you do it will only be for one particular kind meaning you will accumulate a ton of one specific size that you can never seem to get rid of. All of the items you can bring back and sell have this problem and you could go several in game days of nothing only to have one order asking for a ton of stuff but they just HAPPEN to be asking for the ONE thing you don't have and there's no assurance that the next few contracts you do will have what they are asking for. So you just end up accumulating more junk hoping desperately you are hording the right stuff.

The third is probably the biggest disappointment: Lack of hazards. Hardspace: Shipbreaker is probably the abject best example of how to handle games focused on deconstruction and has a feature that easily puts it ahead of the rest are hazards. As you are working, you actively have to consider what you are tearing apart and how. Without hazards, games centered on deconstruction inevitably just boil down to a very monotonous cycle where you smash stuff until it falls over. There's no fear of being under the roof as it collapses, no pipes you need to close off, and, heck, you can literally smash the power bank that provides the building electricity hard enough to make it explode into sparks and nothing happens.

The third point is honestly the biggest elephant in the room for me. Ironically, Ship Graveyard Simulator 1 had this exact same problem and even the sequel doesn't really utilize hazards enough to be a huge challenge. As it stands, the most efficient method of playing this game is to recover any item people want, smash the two edge planks holding walls up until all of the walls come down, pack up the mess, and leave. Without any risk to smashing buildings apart like a maniac, the game just turns into one of those rage rooms where you smash stuff to let off steam.

Great fun in the flesh. Digitally, it gets dull very quickly when you realize everything you smash just feels the same.

review:
I am still waiting for the game to be in what I'd consider a playable state before continuing. Here are the larger issues I've seen reported recently. I make no claims as to the accuracy or completeness of this list. There are a number of other minor and visual issues as well such as garage doors respawning, chimneys not falling when buildings collapse, furniture models / shadows getting messed up in the warehouse, trees clipping through vans, etc.

* Items falling through customer van on travel, then unable to be picked up (10/5/25)
* Items (rarely) disappearing when placing in van (10/5/25)
* Relaxed-mode turning off randomly (10/6/25)
* Destroyed entire house, only 92% completion shown (10/5/25, is this just visual?)
* Furniture pallets (maybe also non-furniture?) disappearing from warehouse (10/4/25)
* Various racks (cardboard, windows, wood) disappearing and/or partially falling through warehouse floor (10/5/25)
* Items disappearing from site on travel (120cm drywall, 150cm beams reported 10/6/25)
* Partially completed pallets / boxes disappearing from site (10/5/25)
* Pending money lost on reloading save before end of day (10/3/25)
* Cannot fulfill some orders even with correct item / rarity (10/5/25, maybe different items with the same name?)

--------------------------------------

I really like this game so far, but I can't recommend it in it's current state. I hope the bugs detailed below are fixed soon and I will amend my review afterward. Dev communication so far has been excellent in both the Steam forums and Discord (though I'd like to see a known-issues list), so I do have hope.

Unfortunately, there is a bug which is completely killing my enjoyment where items can despawn when you leave the job site. The game is designed such that you have to leave and return multiple times in order to finish unless, maybe, you destroy literally everything, so I can't see any way to avoid this unless you are much better than I am at figuring out what will fit in the van by eyeballing it.

The first time this happened to me, another player let me know on Discord they had previously reported this issue (he had an early access key) and it seemed to happen to items you left near the delivery van. However, after starting over (I had lost a customer-requested item and didn't want to lose the reputation), I had multiple items disappear from inside the house. Brick pallets are apparently especially susceptible to this, though I had at least four other different types of items disappear, so it's not limited to them.

There are a couple other more minor bugs related to game settings. When I quit the game, all of my settings were reset and I had to redo them. Other people report this happening whenever they try to confirm the settings with the hotkey. (The workaround is to just exit the settings menu and select to save them that way instead.) Also, some people have reported that various difficulty settings (which are not modifiable after the prologue) are resetting mid-game.

People also report progress-stopping bugs in the prologue and crashing, but I didn't experience them.

This isn't a bug per se, but I'd also really like a way to rotate items in all three dimensions. In particular, there is no way to lay an item flat. For example, drywall can either be set down at an extreme angle or at a low angle, but if you want to slide it in into the truck on top of a refrigerator, you're out of luck. With as much work as they seem to have put into the collision boxes and physics, and with van-tetris being kind of fun in general, it's strange how difficult it is just to put something into a space which is obviously large enough to accommodate it. It would also be nice if there was a way to "nudge" items without having to pick them up and completely reposition them. Also, items tend to bounce around like they're made of Styrofoam when you place them too close to the van walls, which is strange since the game won't let you place things where there are collisions.

Beyond that, I was really enjoying the game so far, though I was only on the first mission post-tutorial. Disassembling items is a bit annoying and that's a little surprising since it seems like the optimal way to play in the early game is already to destroy almost everything and thus bypass the tools. This is because the starter van is just far too small for anything else to make sense due to fuel costs unless the job site is extremely close to the warehouse. This may change later with a large truck, faster tools and more expensive items, but I'm not there yet.

Destroying stuff is fun in general, though it does feel like it takes maybe too many hits with the sledge. This may be something that gets upgraded later, I'm not sure.

When picking up items like wood planks or bricks, and when placing them onto pallets, i would like to be able to hold down the button instead of having to press the button repeatedly. My RSI will thank you for making this change. :D

The warehouse is a really cool idea and it's fun to store things there. I don't know yet how I feel about the "orders" system where you look for people wanting things you have. It feels a little convoluted and game-y. I'd rather hold an auction or build a house or something.

Performance is great for me with a 3060ti and 5600x. With high settings, default FoV and DLSS 4 (the game comes with DLSS 3 but I updated it via DLSS Swapper) DLSS: Balanced is giving me 55-65 FPS in 1440p, which I'm doubling to 110 with Lossless Scaling while still having some GPU room to spare. I haven't noticed any hitching, though I wouldn't expect to since the game takes place in relatively small areas with a loading screen between them.

I'd also like to note that I think the price is extremely reasonable and much less than the community had been expecting pre-launch. If the aforementioned bugs are resolved, this is an easy game to recommend.

review:
This game is advertised as an open world survival game with with base-building that has PVP elements. Once you play it long enough to see the core of this game (meaning the part that has replay value) it is 100% PVP. You can't advance at all in this game without doing PVP missions which consist of repeatedly visiting the same 5 buildings to loot the same boxes 100+ times to collect the items you need to build basic benches or complete the storyline quests on the "PVE" island. The pve island is equally limited with a few locations to visit but once you've been there and looted materials there is literally no benefit to ever going back...unless you enjoy wasting ammo. In addition the base-building in this game is EXTREMELY limited. You can only build with thatch and unless you want to spend 150 hours going on the same extration mission over and over you won't be able to build any benches to put in your grass house. You end up living in a grass hut full of storage boxes, unless you want to build several grass huts full of storage boxes. Overall it gets old pretty fast. 
I feel like for people who are looking for a straight up PVP game with some interesting side-quests on a home island it would be good. It should be advertised as such. For players looking for base-building, crafting, or open world exploration this is a huge dissappointment.

review:
Nice game, good concept of PvPvE, so people who are not professional players/youtubers can actually enjoy PvP. That said, game has couple of caviats:
 - quests are a bit lackluster, and could use a bit better narration
 - gunplay is a bit stiff, especially in close-quarters, very often gun/bow misses in point blank where enemy is in your face, like hiena
 - level design is good but it needs polish in multiple places (e.g. rocks with 90 degrees edges)
 - match-making is often stuck on retrieving server information
 - enemies have night-vision and can see through foliage, they very often also hide behind bushes to shoots you (AI would need to be seriously improved in general)
 - balancing is lacking, e.g. hiena can eat your 50 DR metal armour in 2-3 bites
 - many other bugs

And as a side note, if devs want to avoid for their game to end like Marauders, they need to work on option to start match when there are no other players around.

In general, promising title, but not yet there to be playable longterm.

Edit (02.01.2026):
I have changed my opinion to negative. After the last changes, it is obvious the game is not going in good direction. Couple of reasons for this are:
 - one of survivors vanished
 - trade recipes changed for worse (e.g. you could exchange bottle of water for 35 ammo, now it is ripe coconuts)
 - running still feels wonky or even worse, and your character runs couople of meters and is already out of breath
 - situation with health and armour was bad, now is even worse. basically 3 hits from hiena kill player with 30% armor

I've played this game for over 150 hours.

The games playability is akin to the thatchet structures you can build in the game; it has it’s limits, you can easily shoot holes through it, and it goes up in flames very easily.

As much as I enjoyed playing this game in early access the problem is the current coding does not allow peace of mind. The whole premise of this game is to grind pvp, score loot, secure loot then repeat. You can protect your loot and base from countless hordes of hyenas or raiders, but you can’t protect it from the developers when they release patches. The community is the only thing that makes this game enjoyable and in truth I’m not sure how many people will be left if their bases are destroyed and hard earned resources/gear vanish every time a new patch is released.

And yes there will be those to quickly point out this is an Early Access game. And yes they are correct, it is, but even early access games like 7 Days to Die, Minecraft, etc. you could still play and gather resources without the fear of losing everything when you sign back in (or in the case of 7 Days to Die they at least warn you of potential release effects).
--
Quick update:

Save yourself the time and money and do not purchase this game if you're looking for a competitive extraction shooter. The game has become essentially become Kindergarten Cop with the PVE update. One team runs around killing everything and other teams swarm upon the kills to get loot before anyone else.

If that's not a good enough reason for you, then please be concerned about the alarming amount of bugs in game equivalent only to the number of bugs that swarm from hives on Pioneer Island. Don't get me started on the ticketing system by the Devs to help assist.. in the words of Tiger King, "I called for help twice, and not a 'f*** you', what do you need or nothing.

At this point I'm just gonna bite the bullet and buy Arc Raiders

review: You're stranded on this island and are forced to go on these "expeditions" in order to obtain better loot and progress with the story. If you die on these expeditions, you lose everything you brought with you. Here's the thing though: enemy difficulty seems to increase the longer you play and is not based on how well-equipped you are when you arrive at the expedition island. So, each time you die, you eventually reach a point where you literally can't obtain new things because the enemies become too difficult to fight because you've lost your weapons. It'd be better if you only lost what you obtained on the expedition, not what you brought with you. And difficulty should be dynamically adjusted based on the weapons you have on you. Players should be able to have the choice to only play against AI on the expedition island. There needs to be a keep inventory on death setting when playing solo. Any game that relies on forced PVP is bound to die out if solo players are at such a disadvantage that the game progression becomes softlocked two hours in. Let solo players join games of other Solo players without providing a game code. If that were possible, the expedition island might be possible to survive long enough to get the needed items to progress on our PVE islands. 

Right now the game is far too challenging and impossible to play. I already requested a refund which was denied because I had played 3 hours, 2 of those hours were spent with the game open while I tried to find online how to make it stop kicking me from the expedition island every 3-4 minutes. 

Great concept for a survival game but the Devs need to listen to feedback and remove forced PVP or provide an alternate method of getting required game items for solo players.

review:
I went into Lost Rift hoping for a solid mix of survival, base building, and PvPvE expeditions. 
The concept is there, but in its current state it feels more like “Early Mess” than Early Access.

The good:

*The core idea is interesting: build a base on your island, then venture out on expeditions that mix PvE and PvP tension.

*When it works, the base building system is satisfying.

*Atmosphere and weather effects can look great on good hardware.

*There are occasional chaotic moments (storms, raids, surprise encounters) that feel genuinely exciting.

The bad:

*Performance is rough. FPS drops, stuttering, crashes, and even graphics settings resetting themselves are common.

*Bugs everywhere: falling through floors, ziplines not working, infinite expedition loops, textures breaking, loading screens that never end.

*The colour palette was made by an autistic genius - mostly it works, but when you look closer, it's like a play-doh mash-up of ugly brown in many places.

*Multiplayer is unstable, with frequent disconnects and issues joining friends.

*The map punishes you if you don’t build your base on the “everyone builds here” private island. Any other spot puts you at a serious disadvantage for resources and safety.

*Progression and balance are inconsistent: sometimes you’re far too weak, sometimes enemies are trivial, often it just feels uneven.

*Memory leak - the more you play, the worse it gets, until it's unplayable.

*Core systems feel unpolished — crafting, loot, hazards, and building collision logic all need serious work.

*Swimming is bugged - when you swim, you lose stamina, when you have 0 stamina, you start drowning and losing HP. You cannot dive and loot is on the sea floor.

Verdict:
At its best, Lost Rift shows flashes of the game it wants to be. But right now, it’s hard to enjoy when the experience is dominated by crashes, bugs, and design choices that punish experimentation. It might get there someday, but at this point it feels like you’re paying to beta test an idea that’s still too unstable to be fun.

Not recommended in its current state.

P.S.
Bots positively reviewing the game are not helping. ('nice game, buy' , 'nice!!!!' , 'buy now' etc.)

review:
I'm giving the game a negative review for PvPvE.

But first, I want to highlight the game's good points:
- An aesthetic approach and a setting that immediately draws you in.
- Truly breathtaking weather changes, some of the most beautiful I've ever seen.
- A pretty good taste of the depth of field, which draws you in and makes you want to discover the mysteries that the universe has to offer ahead.
- The art direction highlights different eras, but also shows a desire to stand out.

In terms of survival mechanics, it's fairly classic for the genre in terms of crafting and building. Nothing breathtaking, but it does the job very well.

Next comes the PvPvE part. I should point out that I am a solo player and will only be talking about my own experience, so as a newbie, I progress through the universe with the help of an NPC who acts as a tutorial and helps you understand the basics and get started. You follow along until this same NPC sends you to the western island. You are told to get ready, and off you go to this island to collect the components you need to progress in this tutorial quest (at least that's what the NPC tells you). Well, I shouldn't have. I find myself alone on an island teeming with creatures and hordes of bandits, but also two teams of five people armed to the teeth. I looked pretty pathetic with my old bow and arrow. I realised straight away that this adventure wasn't for a lone character, so I exercised the utmost discretion, avoiding hot spots as best I could. I gathered what I could, which wasn't much. Once at the extraction point, I got a rude awakening when an opposing team was there to greet me. I fled and died in a riverbed due to lack of energy. (Sad ending) Worse still, I lost everything I had crafted for my character. I felt like I had been literally punished by the game for wanting to explore and follow the tutorial.

In my opinion, this is a major point that needs to be reviewed and changed: the approach to this PvPvE world. It should be clearly defined as optional and, in any case, should not impact your solo play. Or at least it should be a completely different quest and narrative line. I stopped playing immediately after this humiliation and preferred to ask for a refund. I'm waiting to see significant changes and to be sure that I can enjoy the entire game solo, and why not PvPvE, but against a match-up that corresponds to your numerical strength. 1 vs. 10+ an NPC army is not fair.

Still the game seems promising and deserve to be tried. It's just not my type of gaming I seek for now.

review:
Ever wanted the strange lovechild of Tarkov and Grounded on a Far Cry-ish island? On paper, that’s Lost Rift.  Ocean ambience as far as the eye can see, with a weird sci-fi Bermuda Triangle multiverse... thing, happening in the background.

Crafting is pretty decent, with some nice QOL touches for making sure your buildings are exactly the way you want them, minus some very picky utility items that simply REFUSE to build if you don't have proper flooring.  Base building being removed from the PvP feature is also a huge win, no worrying about chronically online children raiding your base while you sleep.  (Looking at you, RUST.)

However, the charm, especially for Solo players, wears after the first hour as the island turns insanely hostile: mobs respawn before you reach your corpse, TTK is 1–2 gunshots or hyena bites, and those hyenas beeline past raiders straight to you. I did five corpse runs in a row and felt the fun evaporate as I was spending more time trying to recover lost loot than making any meaningful progress in the game loop.  

Verdict:  

Pros: 
-Decent Building system
-Nice QOL touches in some areas
-Base building separate from PvP

Cons: 
-Punishing solo balance (Especially with the chance of being matched against larger groups in PvP)
-Overtuned Damage
-Fiddly placement rules
-Weak VO/Dialogue for the Lore
-Always online even in Single Player Mode
-PvE Island is incredibly small, content being stretched in EA by PvP mode

Score: 6/10  Not worth it yet.  Maybe after some more tuning and content drops.

(In response to the developer post, it's highly unlikely I'll repurchase this game unless a member of my crew buys it.  It's just not in a place where a solo player could enjoy it, but I'll keep an eye out for updates, especially if there's a mode where I can fully enjoy a complete PvE experience.)

Want to like this but the bugs are actually game breaking. Past the return mark at this point, 8.6 hours at time of review. Otherwise I would def refund. 

Its not that its a bad game. Has its issues sure but its fun and has a lot of charm. The problem is, twice now, I have lost control of the plane. First time: near complete lost of input. Had to reboot game to fix. Second time: the reduce throttle button started pausing the game for some reason. These cause the plane crash, which cause loss of money supplies or even mission failure. As the only time the game saves is when you dock, rebooting the game to fix this loses progress. The better your plane becomes, the longer you'll be out before you need to dock, the more time you'll lose.

I've noticed these events seem to happen just after a scripted event occurs. This is the type of bug that simply cant be ignored to give a positive review. Tragically many posts seem to say the devs are MIA. So, I doubt it'll get any fix but its mine forever now... guess Ill keep trying to finish it.

To be clear, there are many other gripes I have with this game. Yet, there is a lot of good to combat them. I will not be going over any as there is no real point. In other words, its not the only issues but taking the good vs the bad, it WOULD be a positive review if the above issues were fixed.

Absolutely know they dropped support for the game after most of the bugs were fixed. 

Most of the time, it works and does what it's advertised but when you get to a good mid level plane, completely loses steam. Most of the mods for the plane don't make sense or were not really thought out really. There's also a few characters that have annoying little quirks with them. Some can't go fast and could pass out while going at high speed. Some have a nagging mother that periodically floods your radio with useless embarrassing info about the character. Some see things at night and you can't use them at night or they cause more problems. Pointless mechanic that just ruins the fun. 

The variety of the enemies also is not so entertaining. At some point I got a few mods that allowed me to knock em out pretty quickly but you sacrifice storage so you're doing more flying than you should unless you gather a plane that has storage but now your plane sucks at fighting. I get why they put it in there but you don't even know what parts you equipped until you buy it so when you use it you suddenly realize that it sucks or doesn't suit you and you wasted components to get it. 

Overall I don't support people buying this even if it's at a discount because at some point someone will do it better and I am still shocked it lasted a few years before the devs dropped it.

review:
+++ Novel and unique gameplay mechanic
+++ Challenging and interesting side missions
+++ Good aircraft customization options

--- Samey, repetitive feeling to the game world
--- Irrelevant minigames
--- Use of generative AI

While the concept and the idea are wonderful on paper, the execution is marred by a constant feeling that the end result has been underbaked and spread too thin. Gathering ingredients for brewing recipes is a fun (albeit quickly repetitive) experience, combat can be an imprecise and needlessly long-winded affair, and most everything else feels like an afterthought that doesn't belong and should've been sacrificed in favor of dialing in the core mechanics. AI-generated voice acting delivers the coup de grâce on a title that got overambitious for its own resources, leading to a hollow sensations in all 25 hours of its playtime. This title would've fared much better with a more focused design centered on the essentials. As it stands now, it functions only to fuel a wistful daydream of "what could've been..."

review:
This is an amazing game with a few small and one big issue. The art style is amazing, unique and vibrant. Whilst I would like more plane customisation, what is there right now is fun to play with and definitely adequate, and I like the aerial combat mechanics and boss weak points. The brewing minigame is fun, although that does lead me into my first issue, which is that the water ingredients can be hard to spot.

By far my biggest issue with this game is the AI voices. They are flat, soulless, genuinely quite terrible. They struggle to convey any kind of emotion, and strip most of my interest for dialogue. Having actual VAs would immeasurably improve this game.

Whilst I do have that issue with the AI voices, it is an exceptionally good game in all other areas, and I would recommend picking it up if you're looking for a more unique flying game.

review:
I'd love to recommend this game because it can be so much fun, but there is a litany of issues. They haven't updated it with any meaningful content maybe ever (they added some plane parts but they kind of suck for the most part). The plane parts should be focused towards a specific thing so you can build your plane to either harvest wheat, or tree resources, or bomb resources. It also falls short in combat where you need either a fast plane or a strong plane and they both suck against specific enemies even if you build toward combat. The game play loop is enjoyable to me and i could play this for hours if they added more end game content. The pirates are pretty unmanageable if you leave them on since you only have so much time in a day to collect resources and make brews. I hope this isn't an abandoned game, but it feels like they're doing the BARE MINIMUM to make it feel like it isn't. A lot of people bring up the ai voices and yeah they are bad, but really this game isn't a story driven dialogue game.

Overall this has potential to be a great game, but it feels like the updates they do are few and far between (not to mention they include almost no new content apart from plane parts). Really fun, but should probably be about 10$ since it's about 10 hours of content and VERY stale after that.

Game just doesn't respect your time. 

Fast traveling between already unlocked islands is an incredibly expensive upgrade so prepare for minutes of just flying in a straight line to/from your destination. Parts to customize your plane must be repurchased each time. Realize you dislike what you just brought? Well you better have extra cash to swap back to the old one. This makes experimenting with new parts and plane designs, what should be the game's bread and butter, an expensive slog.

Don't get me wrong the art direction of Brew Barons is great. It's a playable world of seaplanes and sky pirates which we all imagined watching Porco Rosso. But the systems that should support gameplay actively detract from it and everything is weighed down by minutes of monotonous travel between bouts of actually playing the game.

I want to like this game.  I so badly want to like this game, but I can not stand playing it. 
 Visuals are amazing, I love aviation, the general style of the game and concept is amazing.  Game handles/controls better than I expected, not amazing, but better than some games have handled aircraft. 

I just hate everything in the game revolving around Brewing which is sadly one of the game's core themes.   It's grind and generally just too annoying to actually make the game fun. I tried again today after taking a pause to see if the game got improved.. still can not stomach the brewery.  

Flying, and doing stuff in the plane the best part of the game, not baby sitting a Brewery.   

If the game was more than just Brewing, like say you could be a mail carrier, fly cargo, and do far more than just be a Brewer.  Get hired to hunt down some sky pirates.  Something more open ended like say Steambot Chronicles was on the PS2 which this game interestingly reminds me a lot of..   Perhaps I could like the game. 

But since don't like farming ingredients for brewing, don't like how orders are handled, dislike generally crafting the brews themselves.  It was neat the first few times I did it and wore of VERY quickly.   This "Grind" element shouldn't be in a flying game personally.   At least not in this context, a darn farmer should be making the ingredients not me stealing it from them.  It's my bar, other people should be doing this stuff for me. lol

I just want to fly in this amazingly beautiful world with lots of sky pirates.   If it was more Sandbox like and I got to choose what I wanted to do, not be handcuffed to a darn bar, it would be so much better of a game.   Sadly I know that can not change because well it's Brew Barons, Brewing is at the core of the game. 

I honestly rather drop bombs and blow up every bar in the game than have to brew another beer.  That is after less than 3 hours of playing.

The whole harvesting by shooting at stuff is also a bit silly. This becomes old quickly and I feel like it could have been implemented differently.

As it stands, it's a okay game with a really interesting graphics style and decent flight mechanics, that doesn't quite live up to its potential. You might have some fun with this one, but as far as combat flight games go there are better options out there.

review:
TLDR: This is not a Crimson Skies Game, if you're here for that or for a prop-plane dogfight game, this is not it. There are better alternatives. If you are here for an ok brewery management game with planes then this game is ok but still needs some tweaking and improvements. If the developers continue to improve the game in the future i will change the review.

After 27 hours of play, completing the main "story" and getting all the achievements i cannot honestly recommend this game for people who are looking for a Crimson Skies like game. This game is a brewery management game with planes and pirates.

Pros:
- Beautiful Coastal environments
- Flight controls with mouse and keyboard is ok (similar to warthunder)
- Brewing and delivering is fun
- Resource collection and exploring by air is a nice concept

Cons:
- Quality of life is not good: NO FAST TRAVEL (There is a high speed travel upgrade but its expensive in early and mid game), can only buy certain ingredients from merchants (would have liked to be able to buy emergency ingredients), cannot adjust camera when customizing plane (at least i didn't see any option to), Character missions have no checkpoint and if you crash you pay for the repairs (Last "story" mission has though, so a bit confused), No ability to pin map and have pin show up in compass or HUD, and many many more.
- Some or most of the buyable Plane Parts have either redundant abilities or abilities that aren't worth it due to their negative effects.
- Some good looking plane parts are tied to said redundant abilities, which means you can't look cool and have a good plane at the same time. 
- Combat in the Light plane is painful, you get shredded by enemy fire and your dmg per bolt is less. A heavy plane is needed to not get shredded easily and still deal ok dmg, but you're a flying truck.
- Enemies are chased away after being defeated, not destroyed. After spending 15 - 20 mins fighting a giant zeppelin it flies away and comes back later to mess with you....again...(there is an option to switch off pirates or make them less numerous)
- You start of with actual water guns and water bombs. Is there an upgrade to actual guns? Nope. You know whats even funnier? The pirates get machine guns and cannons to shoot at the player. Even the CIVILIANS get guns to shoot at pirates during a certain mission. (This pissed me off on a personal level)
- Tutorial can be more expansive, had to figure out how to collect ingredient underwater, only knew underwater ingredients existed because of the ornament that literally points it out to the player while flying.
- salvaging minigame can become very frustrating due to large number of hostile marine life.

Honestly If the game were to allow players to get good looking plane parts and then choose what ability to put on them i would be less disappointed, if they made it possible to use actual firearms and bombs to take out pirate bosses permanently this would've been a positive review.

review:
To expand on my previous review: 

The game has a number of pros: 

-Good flight controls with mouse and keyboard, easy to grasp and intuitive (like war thunder controls all in all) 

-Great style while not hyperfocused on graphic fidelity or "hyper-realism", good artistic vision on display 

-Overall nice brewing and mission management, not too tedious but sometimes hampered by QOL issues 

-Bossfights with kind of nice mechanics, no "shoot till it dies" over and over again, fun for the most part 

Sadly, there are a number of cons, some of these seem to be very specific to my setup or may be just personal preference: 

-Lack/No Quality of life, there is no fast travel (only a super fast flying functionality that is sort of weird and propels your plane to thousands of knots, which makes slowing down and landing at your destination weird and a hassle), some UI functionality is weirdly restrictive (not being able to pin contract specific information when in the brewing process, only before) and a few minor other issues (some side-jobs not allowing you to quit once you start them) 

-Bugs/Savegame Issues, I personally crashed and corrupted my savegames multiple times so far, all crashes in the middle of play, sometimes in the tutorial, sometimes in missions, sometimes in the hangar, everytime so far, the game was completely bricked subsequently, checking wether or not the game folder was set as read only has helped somewhat but ultimately not completely fixed the problem and had me reinstalling multiple times 

-AI "voice acting", a minor gripe, but the voices sound annyoing, dull and overall not like a human should, another QOL would be the ability to turn of character voices, as they can get annoying, constantly giving the same "hard landing", "soft landing", "the plane is damaged" input when you already know that is the case, also a lot of dialogue seems rather harsh/rude with character almost calling you an idiot (personal preference, but not my thing) 

-Pirates and Combat, while the flight controls are nice, fighting pirate planes is a hassle, all of their planes seem to be "gunships", shooting at you with turrets while circling over and over again, your own light plane is usually not quite fast enough to engage them and takes damage so easily while dishing out almost none, you are better off using the heavy planes, which have the turning circle of a large freighter and are about as agile, there are a few modifications that eliviate these issues somewhat (specific gun turrets of your own, special wings or bodies for more agility or speed) but all of these come with a number of draw-backs that require you to either have specific builds for fighting and farming, to refit your plane every time you want to do something else or just deal with a sub-par jack-of-no-trades plane, that somehow has to make due

-Cost and Money, upgrades cost money to buy for the first time, so far expected, they also cost money to install, not too bad either, however everytime you want to switch around a part, it costs money again, there is no quick switching for specific missions, all customization is a monetary investement that can come back to haunt you later on, this in turn makes the previous issue of having to customize your plane for every issue way worse, as you now have to sink a substantial amount of money into either keeping around a number of planes or refitting everytime you dont want to deal with the issues of a sub-par do-it-all build

-Visuals, while the artstyle and also plane-design is great overall, there are some issues (IMO) with it, for the "rendering" or "shading" or whatever you want to call it, the game often times seems somewhat cheap or as if relying on pre-made shaders that really do not serve it well, either oversaturating and blinding you with washed out light effects cranked up to 11 or understating so hard, the nights tend to seem dull and way too bright at the same time, this sadly also hampers the gameplay-loop as often times under-water ingredients are almost impossible to spot or so indistinctly rendered/drawn, that they outright disappear 
As for the planes, the customization is limited and often times dictated by function rather than style, as a number of bodies or wings or swimmers have horrible or outright redundant stats, that would make most optically pleasing builds either bad or not usefull (this is an issue that might be fixed by future expansion of content/building parts) 

Overall, a great idea, solid in terms of graphics and control of your aircraft, with a lot lacking in bug fixing and gameplay-loop. 

Looking forward to when it finds its spot as a game.

review:
This game has a neat concept and is interesting. As a Crimson Skies fan I had to see if it could scratch that itch. The flying is almost there, but I'm sad to say that the rest of it needs work. It feels like it just lacks a lot of polish and I would expect to see that before I feel like I can recommend it and give a thumbs up review, but when that is said this is definitely a game I'd suggest keeping an eye on.

- The negative sides include bad controller support that is unintuitive to use with the UI (which is also kind of rough when using keyboard and mouse). Also if you want to use a controller you need to connect it before starting the game because otherwise it assumes you are playing with keyboard and mouse, which makes the controller layout for the analogue sticks really weird as it tries to work as a mouse cursor mid-flight.

- The voices are so bad that I almost wish they had left them out and the dialogue is uninspired. 

- The pacing is terrible and a lot of mechanics (while they might be fun) needs better explaining or better tutorials. The game feels very grindy when gathering ingredients for the brewery, but I will admit that I like the idea of gathering materials for brewing and selling. It just feels too slow in progress currently. The game lets you design your own bottles and I even created a label that I imported into the game. Sadly it's difficult to tell the bottles apart in your inventory as you only really see them when you create them or sell them to a bar.

Again, this is a game that I really want to recommend because it's doing some really interesting stuff. It just needs a good bit of polish and maybe another attempt at voice acting before I give it a thumbs up.

Gameplay wise you'll find there's a bit more emphasis on the gathering aspects of the game when it comes to making most of your income and pleasing other folks in the setting.  I think it's a terribly fun way to tie yourself to the world and the resources it has to offer, and the brewing minigame is plenty fun to keep you occupied while you're grounded!  Ingredients are collected through various methods involving your plane, from shooting fruits from trees, to running your plane through fields of wheat; all methods have a nice balance of risk to reward, more or less.  Plenty of players have pointed out the tedium of water bombing ingredients, and it's something I've noticed as well.  Apparently the devs are quite active on improving the game over time, so I expect some balancing to be done at some point in the future.

UI/UX is a little clunky as well, as others have noted.  It works well enough, but I've found myself getting the cursor "caught" on certain buttons and elements of the UI, and sometimes it's difficult to tell where your cursor will end up if you're using a controller.  Mouse and Keyboard cursor inputs through the UI can also be a hassle, and I've found it generally easier to just default to a controller.  Again, this is something many are suggesting will be addressed by the dev team as they're bolstered by the initial sales and feedback.  Outside of these quibbles, though, I feel like the piloting controls respond as I'd expect they would from an arcade flying game, so it gets a pass where it matters the most!

Updated as of 2026: The devs have added an AI disclaimer of using AI to generate speech in the game, when, in reality, there was far more that AI had been used to generate in this game like portraits and dialogue.

At this point, I'm completely against having AI in any component of a game's development, no matter the size of the team or scope of the game.

review:
Too much going on and too little time.
The demo didn't make this seem too ambitious. But in execution, this wasn't a very fun experience overall.

Starting with the pros, it has a great art style, great world and concept for that matter. Exploring the map was fun, it left me jaw dropped because of how gorgeous and well crafted it is. The scale too was impressive. The fact the islands were only part of the map is another big surprise. And it’s well optimized. 

But the cons are many, I got 10 hours through on Medium Difficulty, done over 30 contracts, discovered over 6 new islands. And this is where it falls apart essentially.

Story, doesn’t really have much of one? It’s really just exploration, brews, and pirates. Each character has their own backstory which is nice I suppose. 

By far the most cons come from the gameplay. From the start, the tutorial is very brief and as a result leaves you in the dark. I’m on the autism spectrum and have learning difficulties and this game was way too overwhelming in some areas. Tutorials after the start though were non-existent. I found myself having to go to the controls to figure out how to do things, even things tied to the gameplay that you’re not told about.

The plane controls were odd? It felt different to other games, I used mouse controlled here though I am used to keyboard, find mouse a bit more precise. It’s the way the plane moves, it feels slow and feels like it’s not very well polished… regardless of the upgrades that come later.

The brewing aspect would have been fun if, you didn’t have to pick up every recipe through exploration/experimentation, and be able to reset a brew you finished in case of a mistake, as before a patch this didn’t have a quality of life to show the contracts.

Contracts I feel mixed on. They’re straightforward with what they want and you have to deliver a higher quality to sell, the higher the quality the more the money. Problem is, this ties to recipes again, and has many secrets it seems to achieve the best quality. So the start of the game feels extremely slow, I was only able to get speed upgrades for my plane in my 8th hour roughly.

The bar is strange too, the fact you can’t serve every drink you make at a profit, not to mention it not making much profit at that. It feels overly complicated in that aspect too. Probably scratches an itch for those who like managing stuff. Not for me though.

The hangar is by far one of the most bizarre choices. This game at this point I realize prioritises realism over fiction… because there’s friction everywhere. And I mean, everywhere. Dink your plane a bit? You can’t move much anymore, and have to pay a portion of your gold. Want to harvest more wheat? Replace your wing entirely for gold and if you want to go back, pay gold. Catalogue is also very overwhelming to look at with so much text. Also the stats for the plane too. 

The Roster system is a bit complicated too. And finnicky in terms of UI. Forgot to mention, the UI is very finnicky. Sometimes pressing tabs in menus doesn’t do anything. 

Exploration whilst it has its pros, it all seems to be a bit of a memory game. But the ingredient gathering is arguably one of the worst aspects of it. The winching minigame is annoying in itself (not to mention rare even when exploring multiple islands). I never really enjoyed gathering ingredients, which can also be very bugged too. Like the suction radius when gathering them is extremely small. Some ingredients are just hard to spot like Whispywheat, which I had no clue on how to get until I asked in the community. But this type of ingredient is a pain too because of how slow it is to gather. Getting to it is a problem in itself. Then there’s underwater ingredients which despite how easy it is to spot ingredients on land and air, it was impossible to see underwater until you’re close by and at day time. There’s no indicator on where these ingredients are so you have no idea where to drop water bombs on then. Also the waterbomb crosshair is very bugged. It isn’t landing where the crosshair is, the crosshair keeps glitching out, and it doesn’t always dislodge ingredients… 

Combat, well, what little I did of it, was just a pain. First I found a plane that was marked for me to take down… shot it for over 5 minutes with water bolts and it wasn’t going down. So I don’t know what that was about. Second, found pirates harvesting from an island. They sent out planes to fight me which luckily were fairly easy to take down, but this giant plane was not. As there was no obvious way to dodge attacks (Other than the top one where the gun fires everywhere, where you just go beneath it). And it seemed to have a massive health pool as well, but got shot down before I was able to see how much I could damage it. My third encounter was on an island opposite where they had an airship. I turned away because I knew this was pointless. But things got worse. All the friendly islands got invaded by pirates with, submarines. This was even more of a pain than the first two. Because there were no obvious weakspots, had no clue what to aim at. I was getting missiles thrown at me, with the only way to take them down being to shoot them. Then the submarines disappeared when I was shooting them (Submerged I guess) only to reappear, then I get shot down before I could even get an angle on them, and now the island is held hostage. 

New contract? What’s this abo- what the hell is Caramel Carrot? Seriously, why am I getting contracts for ingredients I not only can’t get to, but have no recipes for? I get there’s a deadline for accepting contracts and delivering them, but I don’t get why there’s contracts for things I don’t have or have not discovered yet. 

But by far the most baffling thing to me is the withholding of information which ties to everything. This ties to pretty much everything on the list. There’s nobody to say “Hey, you got a contract for X ingredient? You can find that in X by flying into the streams.” Or “This plane is heavily armoured, you might need to come back another time.” This paired with the gameplay loop of going out to get ingredients, deliver everything even, just makes things so arbitrary and tedious. I would have been happy if this was even a 8 hour game with a linear story and a lot of quality of life options.

Small but annoying things:
I sometimes lost brews when transporting them (All safe landings where unsafe can leave damage or lose brews/ingredients)
Gathering of water is tedious.
Island boosting upgrade which is useful, unfortunately has the caveat of you looking to look at a logo in the sky… and it also doesn’t trigger all the time. Not sure if it’s because of distance or what?
Which reminds me, water bolt and water bomb’s distance is quite underwhelming. It would have been great to have an upgrade at least to make these hit from further away. 

If it isn’t obvious by this point, I don’t recommend. I was really looking forward to playing this game. And the first few hours were great, but I Immediately noticed these issues when they first appeared. Plus if I need to use the internet to play the game for me… is it really playing at all? I’m really frustrated, probably having a meltdown without realizing it. If a lot of these issues are patched I might consider coming back, but I don’t really have any hope at this point. I was having a bad day as of writing this too.

A mish-mash of solid concepts do not form together to make a good game.

While the artstyle and general 'vibe' of it seemed pretty great to me, and I was a vibe fan of the concept, the game just doesn't fit together that well.

The voice acting is distractedly dreadful, and I'd genuinely prefer none at all, since this isn't exactly a game that needs it, basically all the dialogue is poorly written and confusing, which works with a poor UI to make the game feel unnecessarily clunky.

The gameplay, honestly, is one of its worst sins. Don't even bother playing it with a controller. But if you use a mouse, you'll find the main thing that attracted me; It's clearly SUPPOSED to feel somewhat like Warthunder, but with an oddly weighty and slow style of handling, it feels outright awful to try and manuever your plane, with the game encouraging you to always go just a little slower than you'd be comfortable with. There's practically no sense of inertia, and gathering resources is tedious, and feels more or less like something that was slapped on to justify the game's resource system.

Also, there's the elephant in the room of the game's AI voice acting. I only found out about it shortly before I wrote this- It's choppy and sounds particularly weird, but at the same time, it feels like other parts of the game- The dialogue in particular, also used ML with how damned clunky it seems to be. I feel it must be restarted that this just... Adds up to something far, far worse than the sum of its parts. 

It's a shame too, since on the surface this game is made up of pretty much everything I SHOULD enjoy, but it just falls at the first hurdle.

review:
TL;DR: A frilly artstyle and concept isn't enough to save this game riddled with bugs, bad controls, awful AI Voices, and frustrating mechanics. Highly recommend avoiding this game. 2/5 stars

I really wanted to like this game. It has a lot going for it with a fun concept, beautiful artstyle, and great customization.

Unfortunately, they clearly spent too much time on the art design, and not enough time on the gameplay. This genuinely  has some of the worst flying I've ever experienced in a game. To begin with, they clearly never tested controller support because the default settings has the sensitivity set to the moon. So after wasting time trying to get it to a playable sensitivity, you find out that the game despite saying Full Controller Support, does not show controller prompts, so back to searching through menus to find the controller layout.

And after all that, you finally take off for the first time and you find out that your plane controllers like a brick. It feels like I'm playing QWOP with a plane with how unwieldy the controls are. There are multiple points where you need fairly precise controls otherwise you end up wasting a bunch of time having to backtrack to grab resources. 

In my short time playing the game I encountered several infuriating bugs like menus not working and not being able to talk to characters. Not being to talk to the characters was honestly a blessing because this game uses awful grating AI-generated voices which sound off and constantly take me out of the scene.

I very rarely give games such a short chance, especially a game like this which I really want to enjoy. But it became abundantly clear that this game is bad, and I don't want to invest my time further and try to convince myself some enjoyment could be buried here. Avoid this game, unless you need to fulfill your perverted curiosity for bad games.

review:
Edit with more playtime: Unfortunately the game has been getting worse, not better, with patches. I routinely get bugs that result in progress wipes, freeze controls, and now I cannot finish the final mission because the game soft-locks during the final boss fight. I regret ever buying it.

TLDR: Although the game has a solid base, it needs some more time to cook. Check it again in a few months maybe.

Ok, so the base game is pretty simple: you fly around and collect ingredients to turn into alcoholic beverages that you sell to scattered bars. The base gameplay is good, with a satisfying (although sometimes wonky) flight model, reasonable difficulty (most of the time), a beautiful setting and interesting characters. Flying around in this game is just fun, and checking out the different islands is nice. The characters all have different missions that add some variety to the basic gameplay loop, and different traits that make different builds for different missions worthwhile to explore.

But... the game really needs some time to go through balancing, bug fixing and content adding. I'm finding plenty of bugs and although the developers are quick about putting out patches this is stuff that should have been fixed a while ago. Gathering ingredients can be hit or miss, with those you shoot taking no time at all while those on farms you have to bomb or scythe are pure, tedious frustration. The enemies are, for the most part, just window dressing, they never really come after you, just hang around flying in circles and taking shots at you with their turrets. Some of the boss battles are interesting even if the objective is unclear, but others are awful; I can into a submarine that wouldn't let me leave the island until I defeated it, turning a quick flight out to pick up some ingredients into a tedious boss battle in a plane built for ingredient gathering. The game is a long series of this, with plenty of fun mixed in with frustration from poor design choices and bugs that will take a while to settle.

Finally, the game has a weird inconsistent "gentle" vibe to it. On one hand, it's literally called Brew Barons and you deliver hard liquor to bars, but there is a screen before the game that oh no the developers don't condone drinking. But one pair of characters' mission is to fly drunk around and cause property damage...? You shoot water bolts at the enemies and they're never defeated, just run away, while the pirates are clearly some sort of smog-spewing Captain Planet C-villains, but there is a clear drumbeat of military stuff going on in the game and the whole ingredient gathering is very violent. It feels like they switched directions mid-stream and it makes for a lot of jarring moments.

I really wanted to like this game, I really did... I can handle some of the bugs, but I can't handle over 30 minutes fights against bosses that realistically can't down you but have such small hitboxes that you can't hit them either. When none of your weapons do ANY damage unless its in the couple of pixels wide weak spot and the planes seem to have a mind of their own with an incredibly unreliable sensitivity on a flight stick (as in sometimes a light touch does nothing, and sometimes it gets you 90 degrees straight up) it's just not enjoyable... and it's not like you can just avoid all combat, enemies will start to take over unless you kick em back.

The main mechanic of the game, the flying, feels poorly designed.
- If you use any rudder or elevator AT ALL, your speed tanks. Not sure if this is supposed to be more percentage based, but at the moment of writing this, you loose just as much speed at 1% rudder as you do at full.
- Speed feels off in more ways than one. I know you're literally flying a boat, but when the speedometer shows 350 KNOTS (which is faster than some fighter planes in WWII) and you still feel like you're moving slow, then I'm not sure what is going on.
- On the note of speed, the faster you go the more rotation you gain while using your control surfaces. Probably realistic, but playing on a controller was hard on its own. Not sure what playing on keyboard would be like as I didn't dare try. Maybe cutting down on the input curve for the rotation speed would help the player?
- The boost is cool, but you literally lose control of your aircraft while doing so. If you make the mistake of pulling up while boosting, you might just enter a perpetual loop that you cannot escape. I crashed a couple of times like this with different pilots.
- Overall, I felt like the flying became a second thought over all the other strange and offputting mechanics in the game. I'm glad I never got into a dogfight. I doubt I would be able to do anything of note.

I have a few gripes about the UI as well.
- It feels largely unintuitive and is clunky to get around. I started using the controller to get around, but quickly realized it was nearly impossible to figure out which button the game was focusing on.
- Even with mouse and keyboard I had to press some buttons multiple times in order for them to do something. Was this due to the controller having a button selected somehow?
- Inventory management was fine, but left something to be desired. You have so little space in your plane, you can fit a few apples and a few grapes in there, which you can bring back to make brews with, but overall I felt like going back and forth 3 times to make one batch is too much with how the flying feels.

* I cannot say this for sure, but the VOs almost sound like AI? It sounds a bit unnatural sometimes. Not hating on the VOs at all if that's not the case. It's mostly the end of some of the sentences where the tone sounds weird. *


Overall, all I can say is this. In the current state of the game, if you're looking for a nice flight based exploration game, this is not it. If they fixed the controls and feel of the plane, then perhaps.

Let me get one thing right out of the way. This may be a negative review, but I absolutely LOVE The Brew Barons. I just love the version of The Brew Barons that will be on Steam in about a month or two from now. Unfortunately this game is a buggy buggy mess in its current launch version. But hey, the game was made by a total of TWO peoples. So i can give them a little slack, and hope that all of these issues get ironed out and soon (so I can change this to the "Positive" review it really deserves)

In it's current state, the UI does not play well with controller users and has a bunch of general issues. The basic brewing mechanics have bugs that can just make your whole shipment disappear or make you lose all of the ingredients you harvested. There's all kinds of weird issues with pausing the game and trying to access various menus. My plane likes to just randomly crash for no reason as well. 

I'm also not super impressed with the boss battles. The general dogfights are solid enough, but Boss battles can take days of in-game time. And they are required in order to make certain deliveries. There's no way around them. So if you get unlucky enough to get a delivery in an occupied island, you have to fight not just one, but occasionally two bosses. And the actual combat is not hard at all. It's just so slow and takes forever.

So with all of those reasons for the negative review, let just follow up by saying, that I as a very longtime Studio Ghibli fanatic, feel that the three of these folks (two developers and a composer), have managed to create something that feels more true to the core spirit of Miyazaki and his peers than any video game to come before. Even the music resonates Joe Hisaishi's more adventurous moods, and the writing and general tone of the game are so dead-on Ghibli, it's literally insane! Like both Ni-No Kuni games, despite being "produced" by Ghibli and multiple studios with thousands of people, felt less true to Ghibli, than Brew Barons does. But, they have also created their own world, that feels unique from those of Miyazaki and Takahata, etc. I'm jusy going to patiently wait until the game that was promised is here, then I'll revisit this review.
